docs.title: Where next
docs.text:
• Quickstart

    The platform end to end: make dev, make seed, then fit, inspect and score from the browser. About ten minutes.

  • Your first model in Python

    Build a labelled dataset, write a spec, fit it, forecast a new store and see the typed errors that protect you. About ten minutes.

  • Runs and executors

    Submit the same work as runs to the in-process executor: the protocol the platform's executors implement.

  • Concepts

    Dims and policies, stages and context tails, representations, bundles.

  • Port a model

    Bring your own PyMC, scikit-learn or hand-written model.

docs.title: Runs and executors
docs.text:
fit_spec and score_bundle are plain functions. The platform does the same work as runs: JSON-only submissions handed to an executor, which reports progress as events and returns a status that is the source of truth. The in-process executor implements that protocol inside your Python process, so notebooks, tests and the platform's local-process and docker executors share one code path.

sequenceDiagram
    participant You as Notebook / API
    participant Ex as Executor
    participant H as Harness (fit_spec / score_bundle)
    You->>Ex: submit(RunSubmit{kind: fit, payload: spec}, nonce)
    Ex->>H: resolve dataset refs, fit
    H-->>Ex: progress events
    Ex-->>You: event stream (state, progress, complete)
    You->>Ex: wait(handle) → SUCCEEDED
    You->>Ex: submit(RunSubmit{kind: score, payload: request + bundle})
    Ex->>H: score_bundle
    Ex-->>You: result: xr.DataTree

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
The executor resolves the dataset:// references in specs and requests through a resolver. Here it is a mapping to in-memory datasets; the built-in tabular plugin ships the store-demand data and spec used below.

import asyncio

from mapi_plugin_tabular.datasets import (
    STORE_DEMAND_SCHEMA,
    STORE_DEMAND_SPEC_YAML,
    store_demand_dataset,
)
from mapi_sdk import InprocExecutor
from mapi_spec.executor import ExecState, RunEventType, RunKind, RunSubmit

history = store_demand_dataset(stores=4, skus=2, weeks=60, seed=1)
recent = history.isel(week=slice(-8, None))  # a window of fitted weeks to re-score

executor = InprocExecutor(
    # dataset refs in specs and requests resolve to in-memory datasets
    resolver={
        "dataset://retail/store_sku_weekly@latest": history,
        "dataset://retail/last_8_weeks@v1": recent,
    },
)
print(executor.caps().isolation.name)  # NONE: your own code, in your own process

docs.title: Submit, wait, score
docs.text:
async def main() -> None:
    fit = await executor.submit(
        RunSubmit(
            run_id="fit-001",
            kind=RunKind.FIT,
            payload={
                "spec": STORE_DEMAND_SPEC_YAML,
                "raw_schema": STORE_DEMAND_SCHEMA.model_dump(mode="json"),
            },
        ),
        nonce="nonce-fit-0001",  # resubmitting the same nonce returns the same run
    )
    status = await executor.wait(fit, timeout=300)
    print(status.state)  # succeeded
    for event in executor.events(fit):  # the same event stream a cloud run will produce
        if event.type is RunEventType.PROGRESS:
            print(event.seq, event.payload.get("message"))  # 2 validated the spec and the data

    executor.put_bundle("store-demand@1", executor.result(fit))
    score = await executor.submit(
        RunSubmit(
            run_id="score-001",
            kind=RunKind.SCORE,
            payload={
                "bundle": "store-demand@1",
                "request": {
                    "apiVersion": "mapi/v1",
                    "kind": "ScoreRequest",
                    "model": "endpoint://retail/store-demand-xgb",
                    "mode": "predict",
                    "data": "dataset://retail/last_8_weeks@v1",
                },
            },
        ),
        nonce="nonce-score-0001",
    )
    assert (await executor.wait(score, timeout=300)).state is ExecState.SUCCEEDED
    tree = executor.result(score)  # an xr.DataTree, exactly what score_bundle returns
    print(dict(tree["summary"].to_dataset()["y_hat"].sizes))
    # {'stat': 3, 'store_id': 4, 'sku': 2, 'week': 8}


asyncio.run(main())  # in Jupyter: `await main()`

succeeded
2 validated the spec and the data
3 split the data
4 fitted quantile model 1
5 persisting the fitted estimators
6 fitted on the training data
7 evaluated the holdout through the score path
8 fitted quantile model 1
9 persisting the fitted estimators
10 fit complete
{'stat': 3, 'store_id': 4, 'sku': 2, 'week': 8}

What to notice:

  • Payloads are JSON. The spec travels as YAML text or a dict, the raw schema as a dict, and data only as references. This is exactly what the API will store and what a sandboxed runner will receive.
  • Submissions are idempotent. Re-submitting with the same nonce returns the same handle, so a retried API call never starts a second fit. adopt(nonce) finds a run after a restart.
  • Status is the source of truth. Events are for progress bars; status() and wait() decide whether a run succeeded. Failures come back as RFC 7807 problems with a stable code.
  • Cancellation is cooperative. cancel(handle) is checked between pipeline phases and inside long fits.

docs.title: Isolation levels
docs.text:
Every executor declares how strongly it isolates a run, and the platform refuses to send untrusted code to an executor that is not strong enough.

Executor Isolation For Status InprocExecutor NONE Notebooks, tests, your own trusted code available Local process / Docker PROCESS / GVISOR Local platform, CI v0.2 Cloud Run Jobs (gen2) MICROVM Hosted runs, one fresh sandbox per run v0.3

Never run untrusted code in-process

The in-process executor runs plugins with your permissions in your interpreter. It is for code you wrote or trust. Public plugins only ever run in the sandboxed executors.

See the roadmap for the sandbox design.

docs.title: Your first model
docs.text:
In this walkthrough you fit a demand model for three stores and two products, forecast the next four weeks (including a store that has not opened yet) and see the errors that stop dishonest answers. Everything runs in a notebook cell by cell; the complete script is docs/snippets/quickstart.py and the test suite runs it on every change.

flowchart LR
    D["1. Labelled data<br/><code>xr.Dataset</code>"] --> S["2. Schema<br/>dims, roles, policies"]
    S --> P["3. Spec<br/>pipeline + model"]
    P --> V["4. Static check<br/>no data touched"]
    V --> F["5. Fit<br/>evaluate, then refit"]
    F --> SC["6. Score<br/>forecast, new store"]
    SC --> B["7. Bundle<br/>write, read, verify"]

docs.title: 1. Labelled data
docs.text:
Your data is an xr.Dataset: every variable has named dims and every dim has coordinates (labels). Nothing downstream depends on the order of stores or products.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import xarray as xr

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
stores = ["north", "south", "east"]
skus = ["apples", "pears"]
weeks = pd.date_range("2025-01-05", periods=52, freq="W-SUN")
shape = (len(stores), len(skus), len(weeks))

price = 3.0 * np.exp(rng.normal(0.0, 0.1, shape))
promo = (rng.uniform(size=shape) < 0.2).astype(float)
units = rng.poisson(np.exp(2.5 - 1.2 * np.log(price / 3.0) + 0.5 * promo)).astype(float)

dims = ("store", "sku", "week")
data = xr.Dataset(
    {"units_sold": (dims, units), "price": (dims, price), "promo": (dims, promo)},
    coords={"store": stores, "sku": skus, "week": weeks},
)

Coming from pandas?

A long DataFrame with one row per store, sku and week becomes this dataset with df.set_index(["store", "sku", "week"]).to_xarray().

docs.title: 2. Describe it with a schema
docs.text:
A DataSchema says what each dim is and what may happen to it when you score:

from mapi_spec import DataSchema

schema = DataSchema.model_validate(
    {
        "dims": {
            # a store we have never seen may be scored: it gets the pooled prediction
            "store": {"kind": "categorical", "policy": "new_levels", "new_level_strategy": "pooled"},
            # the product range is fixed: an unknown sku is an error
            "sku": {"kind": "categorical", "policy": "fixed"},
            # time extends into the future, one Sunday-ending week at a time
            "week": {"kind": "time", "policy": "extend", "freq": "W-SUN"},
        },
        "vars": {
            "units_sold": {"dims": list(dims), "dtype": "float64", "role": "target"},
            "price": {
                "dims": list(dims),
                "dtype": "float64",
                "role": "covariate",
                "units": "EUR",
                "future_required": True,  # a forecast must say what the price will be
            },
            "promo": {
                "dims": list(dims),
                "dtype": "float64",
                "role": "covariate",
                "future_required": True,
            },
        },
    }
)
Dim Policy At score time store new_levels (pooled) Unseen stores are allowed and get the pooled prediction sku fixed Only the fitted products; anything else is UNSEEN_LEVELS week extend New weeks must continue the fitted range without gaps

If you skip the schema, mapi_sdk.infer_schema(data, targets=[...]) drafts one: time dims become extend, everything else fixed.

docs.title: 3. Write the spec
docs.text:
A ModelSpec names the dataset, binds your names to the model's canonical names, picks a train/holdout split, lists the preprocessing steps and chooses the model.

from mapi_spec import load_model_spec

spec = load_model_spec("""
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: fruit-demand, project: quickstart}
data:
  dataset: dataset://quickstart/fruit_weekly@latest
  bind:                                   # canonical name: your name
    dims: {store: store, sku: sku, time: week}
    vars: {y: units_sold, price: price, promo: promo}
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: time, last: 8}
pipeline:
  - {id: cal,  use: core.calendar@^1, with: {along: time, features: [week_of_year]}}
  - {id: logy, use: core.log1p@^1,    with: {vars: [y]}}
model:
  use: tabular.regressor@^1
  settings:
    estimator: {kind: xgboost.XGBRegressor, params: {n_estimators: 60, max_depth: 3}}
    rows: [store, sku, time]
    coord_features: {store: category, sku: category}
  fit: {seed: 7}
evaluate: {metrics: [rmse, mape, coverage_80]}
""")
  • bind maps canonical names (what steps and models use) onto your dataset's names. Outputs come back under your names.
  • core.calendar adds week-of-year features; core.log1p models log(1 + units) and is inverted automatically on the way out.
  • tabular.regressor is a built-in quantile model (xgboost underneath) whose rows are stacked from the labelled dims; store and sku become categorical features.

docs.title: 4. Check it before fitting
docs.text:
The same static check the API runs before accepting a job: no data is read, and it takes milliseconds.

from mapi_sdk import default_registry
from mapi_spec import validate_spec

registry = default_registry()  # every installed step, model and plot (entry points)
check = validate_spec(spec, registry.catalog(), schema)
print(check.ok)  # True: names, dims, settings, split stage and leakage all check out
print(check.resolved.model.resolved)  # tabular.regressor@1.0.0 (the semver range, pinned)

A typo in a variable name, a split on a dim that does not exist yet, or a stateful step before the split would be reported here, each with a stable code and a JSON pointer such as /pipeline/1/with/vars/0.

docs.title: 5. Fit
docs.text:
from mapi_sdk import fit_spec

bundle = fit_spec(spec, data, registry=registry, raw_schema=schema)
print(bundle.metrics.values)  # holdout metrics, in units sold: {'rmse': ..., 'mape': ..., ...}
print(bundle.metrics.n_holdout)  # 48 cells: 3 stores x 2 skus x 8 weeks

With the default fit.mode: evaluate_then_refit, fit_spec:

  1. fits every stateful step and the model on the first 44 weeks;
  2. scores the last 8 weeks through the score path, exactly like a forecast, and computes rmse, mape and coverage_80 in units sold (the log1p is undone);
  3. refits on all 52 weeks, so a forecast starts from the latest data, and links the evaluation fit in the bundle.

docs.title: 6. Forecast, including a new store
docs.text:
Supply the plan for the next four weeks: prices and promotions are future_required, the target is not needed. west has never been seen.

from mapi_sdk import score_bundle

future_weeks = pd.date_range(weeks[-1] + pd.Timedelta(weeks=1), periods=4, freq="W-SUN")
plan = xr.Dataset(
    {
        "price": (dims, np.full((4, 2, 4), 2.9)),
        "promo": (dims, np.zeros((4, 2, 4))),
    },
    # "west" opens next month: the model has never seen it
    coords={"store": [*stores, "west"], "sku": skus, "week": future_weeks},
)

forecast = score_bundle(
    bundle,
    """
    apiVersion: mapi/v1
    kind: ScoreRequest
    model: endpoint://quickstart/fruit-demand
    mode: forecast
    horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}
    output: {summary: [median, q10, q90]}
    """,
    plan,
    registry=registry,
)
summary = forecast["summary"].to_dataset()
print(summary["y_hat"].dims)  # ('stat', 'store', 'sku', 'week'), in your names
print(summary["y_hat"].sel(stat="median", store="west").values.round(1))
print(forecast.attrs["representation"])  # quantiles: what this model's uncertainty is
print(forecast.attrs["output_space"])  # {"y_hat": "raw"}: log1p undone, back in units sold
print(forecast.attrs["issues"])  # an info notice: 1 new level of 'store' uses 'pooled'

The result is an xr.DataTree. summary holds the statistics you asked for along a stat dim, with your dim names restored. Its attributes tell you how to read it:

Attribute Value here Meaning representation quantiles Per-cell quantiles: you can read them, not add them up output_space {"y_hat": "raw"} Inverted through every value step back to the raw data's space issues UNSEEN_LEVELS (info) west was scored with the pooled strategy

docs.title: 7. The errors that protect you
docs.text:
These requests fail before any model code runs, each with a stable code:

from mapi_spec import ErrorCode, MapiError


def try_score(request_yaml: str, payload: xr.Dataset) -> ErrorCode:
    try:
        score_bundle(bundle, request_yaml, payload, registry=registry)
    except MapiError as err:
        print(err.code, "-", err)
        return err.code
    raise AssertionError("expected a typed error")


FORECAST = """
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ScoreRequest
model: endpoint://quickstart/fruit-demand
mode: forecast
horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}
"""

# 1. a forecast without next month's promotions: promo is future_required
code_1 = try_score(FORECAST, plan.drop_vars("promo"))

# 2. quantiles are per cell, so "total over all stores" would be a made-up number
code_2 = try_score(FORECAST + "output: {aggregate: {over: [store]}}\n", plan)

# 3. a product outside the fitted range: sku is a fixed dim
code_3 = try_score(FORECAST, plan.assign_coords(sku=["apples", "kiwis"]))

MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE - forecasting needs future values of ['promo'] at stage 'raw'
CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED - cannot aggregate 'quantiles' output: Quantiles are marginal per cell; summing quantiles is not a quantile of the sum.
UNSEEN_LEVELS - 1 level(s) of 'sku' were not seen at fit and the dim's policy is 'fixed'

So how do I get a total over stores?

Use a model whose representation supports it. sklearn.tabular_bootstrap returns joint draws, which can be summed per draw, and Bayesian models return posterior draws. See Representations.

docs.title: 8. Save and reload the bundle
docs.text:
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from mapi_sdk import Bundle

out = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "fruit-demand-v1"
manifest = bundle.write(out)
print(sorted(p.name for p in out.iterdir()))
# ['bundle.zarr.zip', 'diagnostics.json', 'evaluation', 'manifest.json', 'metrics.json',
#  'plots.json']  - `evaluation/` is the train-only fit that produced the holdout metrics

again = Bundle.read(out, registry)  # every file's size and hashes are verified here
assert again.bundle_id == bundle.bundle_id

A bundle holds the spec, the binding, every step's state and context tail, the model's fitted groups and native artifacts (here: the xgboost model as JSON), and a manifest with the size, CRC32C, MD5 and SHA-256 of every file. Nothing is pickled. See Bundles.

docs.title: The whole script
docs.text:
docs/snippets/quickstart.py 
"""Getting started: fit and score a labelled demand model in a notebook.

Every section between ``--8<--`` markers is included verbatim in the docs, and
``conformance/tests/test_docs_snippets.py`` runs this file top to bottom.
"""

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import xarray as xr

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
stores = ["north", "south", "east"]
skus = ["apples", "pears"]
weeks = pd.date_range("2025-01-05", periods=52, freq="W-SUN")
shape = (len(stores), len(skus), len(weeks))

price = 3.0 * np.exp(rng.normal(0.0, 0.1, shape))
promo = (rng.uniform(size=shape) < 0.2).astype(float)
units = rng.poisson(np.exp(2.5 - 1.2 * np.log(price / 3.0) + 0.5 * promo)).astype(float)

dims = ("store", "sku", "week")
data = xr.Dataset(
    {"units_sold": (dims, units), "price": (dims, price), "promo": (dims, promo)},
    coords={"store": stores, "sku": skus, "week": weeks},
)

from mapi_spec import DataSchema

schema = DataSchema.model_validate(
    {
        "dims": {
            # a store we have never seen may be scored: it gets the pooled prediction
            "store": {"kind": "categorical", "policy": "new_levels", "new_level_strategy": "pooled"},
            # the product range is fixed: an unknown sku is an error
            "sku": {"kind": "categorical", "policy": "fixed"},
            # time extends into the future, one Sunday-ending week at a time
            "week": {"kind": "time", "policy": "extend", "freq": "W-SUN"},
        },
        "vars": {
            "units_sold": {"dims": list(dims), "dtype": "float64", "role": "target"},
            "price": {
                "dims": list(dims),
                "dtype": "float64",
                "role": "covariate",
                "units": "EUR",
                "future_required": True,  # a forecast must say what the price will be
            },
            "promo": {
                "dims": list(dims),
                "dtype": "float64",
                "role": "covariate",
                "future_required": True,
            },
        },
    }
)

from mapi_spec import load_model_spec

spec = load_model_spec("""
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: fruit-demand, project: quickstart}
data:
  dataset: dataset://quickstart/fruit_weekly@latest
  bind:                                   # canonical name: your name
    dims: {store: store, sku: sku, time: week}
    vars: {y: units_sold, price: price, promo: promo}
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: time, last: 8}
pipeline:
  - {id: cal,  use: core.calendar@^1, with: {along: time, features: [week_of_year]}}
  - {id: logy, use: core.log1p@^1,    with: {vars: [y]}}
model:
  use: tabular.regressor@^1
  settings:
    estimator: {kind: xgboost.XGBRegressor, params: {n_estimators: 60, max_depth: 3}}
    rows: [store, sku, time]
    coord_features: {store: category, sku: category}
  fit: {seed: 7}
evaluate: {metrics: [rmse, mape, coverage_80]}
""")

from mapi_sdk import default_registry
from mapi_spec import validate_spec

registry = default_registry()  # every installed step, model and plot (entry points)
check = validate_spec(spec, registry.catalog(), schema)
print(check.ok)  # True: names, dims, settings, split stage and leakage all check out
print(check.resolved.model.resolved)  # tabular.regressor@1.0.0 (the semver range, pinned)
assert check.ok, check.errors

from mapi_sdk import fit_spec

bundle = fit_spec(spec, data, registry=registry, raw_schema=schema)
print(bundle.metrics.values)  # holdout metrics, in units sold: {'rmse': ..., 'mape': ..., ...}
print(bundle.metrics.n_holdout)  # 48 cells: 3 stores x 2 skus x 8 weeks
assert set(bundle.metrics.values) == {"rmse", "mape", "coverage_80"}
assert bundle.metrics.n_holdout == 48

from mapi_sdk import score_bundle

future_weeks = pd.date_range(weeks[-1] + pd.Timedelta(weeks=1), periods=4, freq="W-SUN")
plan = xr.Dataset(
    {
        "price": (dims, np.full((4, 2, 4), 2.9)),
        "promo": (dims, np.zeros((4, 2, 4))),
    },
    # "west" opens next month: the model has never seen it
    coords={"store": [*stores, "west"], "sku": skus, "week": future_weeks},
)

forecast = score_bundle(
    bundle,
    """
    apiVersion: mapi/v1
    kind: ScoreRequest
    model: endpoint://quickstart/fruit-demand
    mode: forecast
    horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}
    output: {summary: [median, q10, q90]}
    """,
    plan,
    registry=registry,
)
summary = forecast["summary"].to_dataset()
print(summary["y_hat"].dims)  # ('stat', 'store', 'sku', 'week'), in your names
print(summary["y_hat"].sel(stat="median", store="west").values.round(1))
print(forecast.attrs["representation"])  # quantiles: what this model's uncertainty is
print(forecast.attrs["output_space"])  # {"y_hat": "raw"}: log1p undone, back in units sold
print(forecast.attrs["issues"])  # an info notice: 1 new level of 'store' uses 'pooled'
assert set(summary["store"].values) == {"north", "south", "east", "west"}
assert summary.sizes["week"] == 4

from mapi_spec import ErrorCode, MapiError


def try_score(request_yaml: str, payload: xr.Dataset) -> ErrorCode:
    try:
        score_bundle(bundle, request_yaml, payload, registry=registry)
    except MapiError as err:
        print(err.code, "-", err)
        return err.code
    raise AssertionError("expected a typed error")


FORECAST = """
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ScoreRequest
model: endpoint://quickstart/fruit-demand
mode: forecast
horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}
"""

# 1. a forecast without next month's promotions: promo is future_required
code_1 = try_score(FORECAST, plan.drop_vars("promo"))

# 2. quantiles are per cell, so "total over all stores" would be a made-up number
code_2 = try_score(FORECAST + "output: {aggregate: {over: [store]}}\n", plan)

# 3. a product outside the fitted range: sku is a fixed dim
code_3 = try_score(FORECAST, plan.assign_coords(sku=["apples", "kiwis"]))
assert code_1 is ErrorCode.MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE
assert code_2 is ErrorCode.CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED
assert code_3 is ErrorCode.UNSEEN_LEVELS

from mapi_sdk import CoordPlan
from mapi_spec import load_score_request, validate_score_request

# What the API stores next to a model version: JSON only, no arrays, no plugin code.
meta = CoordPlan(load_score_request(FORECAST), bundle.resolved, bundle.fit_coords).metadata()
print(f"{len(meta.model_dump_json()) / 1024:.0f} KiB of metadata")

request = load_score_request(FORECAST + "output: {summary: [hdi_90], draws: 100}\n")
for issue in validate_score_request(request, meta):  # no data, no model: milliseconds
    print(issue.code, issue.pointer, "-", issue.message)
# MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE /data - forecasting needs future values of ['price', 'promo'] ...
# CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED /output/draws - draws were requested but the model's
#                                        representation is 'quantiles'
# CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED /output/summary/0 - summary 'hdi_90' cannot be computed from
#                                            'quantiles' output
assert any(
    i.code is ErrorCode.CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED for i in validate_score_request(request, meta)
)

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from mapi_sdk import Bundle

out = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "fruit-demand-v1"
manifest = bundle.write(out)
print(sorted(p.name for p in out.iterdir()))
# ['bundle.zarr.zip', 'diagnostics.json', 'evaluation', 'manifest.json', 'metrics.json',
#  'plots.json']  - `evaluation/` is the train-only fit that produced the holdout metrics

again = Bundle.read(out, registry)  # every file's size and hashes are verified here
assert again.bundle_id == bundle.bundle_id

print(manifest.role, manifest.plugin["id"], manifest.spec_hash[:19])
# production tabular.regressor sha256:...
print(manifest.files["bundle.zarr.zip"])  # size, crc32c, md5 (GCS forms) and sha256
print(manifest.lineage["evaluation_bundle"])  # the train-only fit behind the metrics

tree = again.to_tree()  # the whole bundle as one xr.DataTree
print(sorted(tree.children))
# ['binding', 'fit_coords', 'model', 'native', 'preprocess', 'schema', 'spec']
print(sorted(tree["preprocess"].children))  # ['cal', 'logy']: one node per step
assert {"model", "preprocess", "native", "spec"} <= set(tree.children)

docs.title: Quickstart: zero to first model in 10 minutes v0.2
docs.text:
You will start the platform on your own machine, load a demo dataset, fit a hierarchical geo marketing-mix model from the web app, read its scorecard and plots, and score an 8-week forecast. No Docker and no cloud account are needed: PostgreSQL is embedded and object storage is a local emulator of Google Cloud Storage.

Step What happens Time on a laptop 1. Install Python and JavaScript dependencies 2–5 min the first time 2. Start the stack Database, object store, API, worker, web app, plot sandbox about 10 s 3. Load the demo Three datasets and a model spec, through the API about 40 s 4. Fit from the browser A sandboxed fit run, followed live 20–60 s 5. Inspect Scorecard, diagnostics, plots, provenance – 6. Score An 8-week forecast with the fitted preprocessing replayed about 10 s

We ran exactly these steps on a fresh clone while writing this page: from make dev to a scored forecast took under three minutes. The screenshots below come from that run.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• macOS or Linux, about 2 GB of free disk space;
  • uv (it installs Python 3.12 for you if needed);
  • Node.js 22 or newer with pnpm (corepack enable provides the pinned pnpm version);
  • git, and jq and curl if you want to follow the HTTP examples later.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
git clone <repository-url> modeling-api
cd modeling-api
make install          # uv sync --all-packages, then pnpm install

make install puts every Python package of the workspace into .venv and the web app's dependencies into node_modules. Nothing is installed globally.

docs.title: 2. Start the stack
docs.text:
make dev

make dev runs every service in the foreground, each output line prefixed with its name, and prints all 6 services up when it is ready. Leave it running; Ctrl+C stops everything. The first start also queues a sandboxed describe run that exports the catalog of installed models and steps; it finishes in a few seconds.

Service Address Web app http://127.0.0.1:5173 API http://127.0.0.1:8000 (OpenAPI document at /openapi.json) Plot sandbox (a separate origin, on purpose) http://127.0.0.1:5174 GCS shim (signed URLs point here) http://127.0.0.1:4443

Port 8000 (or any other) already taken?

Export the matching variable before make dev, and in every other shell you use:

export MAPI_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18000
export MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:14443
export MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:15173
export MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:15174

make dev, make seed, the CLI, the Python client and the web app all read the same variables. This page was produced on exactly these ports. Troubleshooting has more.

docs.title: 3. Load the demo
docs.text:
In a second shell:

make seed

API http://127.0.0.1:8000 is ok (version 0.2.0)
uploading eu_media_daily (17 KiB) ...
  dataset://default/eu_media_daily@v1 ready
uploading fx_daily (17 KiB) ...
  dataset://default/fx_daily@v1 ready
uploading holidays_eu (7 KiB) ...
  dataset://default/holidays_eu@v1 ready
spec spec://default/eu-geo-mmm@r1: valid

make seed talks to the public API only. For each table it asks for a signed upload URL, sends the file straight to object storage, and starts a sandboxed ingest run that opens the file, checks it against its schema and stores an immutable, content-addressed version. Then it saves the model spec and validates it.

The data is the conformance corpus' E33 example: 30 weeks of daily spend per market and channel and daily revenue per market for NL, DE and UK (UK in GBP), an FX table and a holiday calendar.

Scoring needs the spend you plan for the coming weeks. Upload it with the CLI:

uv run python scripts/seed.py --export demo/     # the demo tables, score payloads and spec
uv run mapi datasets upload demo/eu_media_future.zarr.zip --name eu_media_future

docs.title: 4. Fit from the browser
docs.text:
Open http://127.0.0.1:5173, go to Build and click the eu-geo-mmm row.

The editor validated the spec on the server as it opened: every dataset:// reference, every step and the model settings resolve, and the panel on the right shows what each pipeline step does to the data. The split into training and holdout weeks sits after the weekly step, because a week only exists from that stage on.

Press Fit. The run page follows the run over server-sent events:

  • Starting the sandbox: the run's supervisor read its one-time bootstrap object and deleted it before any model code started.
  • DEV_MODE_ISOLATION is expected on a laptop: the local executor cannot run the model code as a separate user. Containers and the cloud executor can.
  • The progress bar and message come straight from the sampler.

The spec uses tiny sampler settings, so the fit takes well under a minute (the first one on a new machine also compiles PyTensor code). When it succeeds the platform checks every file the run wrote against the storage's own checksums, copies the files where runs cannot reach them and signs a manifest. Press Inspect model://default/eu-geo-mmm@v1.

docs.title: 5. Inspect the model
docs.text:
The scorecard flags R-hat and effective sample size: two chains of 100 draws are not enough to converge, and each warning says what to do about it. The metrics come from the 8 holdout weeks, scored through the same code path a forecast uses, before the model was refitted on all the data (fit.mode: evaluate_then_refit).

Open Plots → Contribution by channel:

Every plot is a Vega-Lite or Plotly spec that the server sanitized, rendered inside an <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts"> served from the plot sandbox's own origin. Provenance shows the signed manifest, every stored object with its generation, and the lineage.

docs.title: 6. Score a forecast
docs.text:
Press Score (top right). The form only offers the modes this model supports.

  1. Keep mode forecast, horizon dim time and 8 periods.
  2. Set Input data to dataset://default/eu_media_future@v1.
  3. Leave the fx side table at the version the fit used; it covers the forecast weeks.
  4. Press Score.

Nothing was refitted: the run replayed the fitted preprocessing (currency conversion, weekly resampling, scaling, and the last weeks of spend each market carries into the adstock) and inverted the result back to weekly EUR. The result's output_space says so.

docs.title: Stop, and start again later
docs.text:
make stop             # or Ctrl-C in the make dev shell
make dev              # everything you loaded is still there (.local/)
make clean-local      # delete the local database and objects, start from scratch

docs.title: Where next
docs.text:
• Tour every page of the web app

    Datasets and CSV mapping, revisions and dry-runs, run controls, the data tree, counterfactuals.

  • Do the same from the command line

    mapi datasets upload, mapi fit --remote @, mapi score, --json for scripts.

  • Or from Python

    mapi_client.Client: uploads, live events, model versions and xr.DataTree results.

  • Understand what just happened

    The control plane, the run sandbox, storage integrity and the event path.

docs.title: The command line v0.2
docs.text:
mapi (package mapi-cli, Apache-2.0) works in two places:

  • locally, without any server: scaffold a spec, check it, fit it and score it in your own Python process with the installed plugins (new, check, fit, score, catalog, plugin, spec);
  • remotely, against the HTTP API of a running platform: upload datasets, fit, follow runs and score model versions (datasets, runs, and --remote on check, fit, score and catalog).

Every command and option is listed in the generated CLI reference. The examples on this page are scripts that the test suite runs: the local ones in the default suite, the remote ones in make e2e.

Running the commands

make install puts mapi into the workspace environment. Either activate it (source .venv/bin/activate) or prefix every command with uv run (uv run mapi --help).

docs.title: Without a server
docs.text:
Scaffold a spec from a template. --with-data also writes the matching conformance fixture's sample data (it needs the mapi-conformance package, which the workspace has):

mapi new tabular -o spec.yaml --with-data     # an XGBoost demand model plus its sample data
Template What it is Conformance fixture geo-mmm Hierarchical geo MMM (weekly EUR, adstock, saturation) E33 forecast HSGP trend and seasonality forecast C08 tabular XGBoost demand with quantile uncertainty xgb_store_demand glm Hierarchical GLM, long layout E02

Check it statically against the installed plugins and the data's schema. --stages prints the schema after every pipeline step; the exit status is 1 when there are errors, so it works in CI:

mapi check spec.yaml --data data.zarr.zip --stages

Fit in-process. The bundle (zarr zip, sidecars, plots, metrics and the evaluation bundle of evaluate_then_refit) goes to bundles/<name>/; --side-table NAME=PATH supplies side tables:

mapi fit spec.yaml --data data.zarr.zip       # in-process: writes bundles/<name>/
ls bundles/tabular

mapi score request.yaml --bundle bundles/<name> --data future.zarr.zip -o result.zarr.zip scores a local bundle with a ScoreRequest document.

Local means trusted

Local fit and score import and run the plugins in your own process (isolation NONE), exactly like a notebook. Use them with code and data you trust. On the platform, the same work runs in a sandbox.

Inspect the catalog of installed plugins, and upgrade spec documents across apiVersions:

mapi catalog models
mapi --json catalog steps | jq -r '.steps[].id' | head -n 5
mapi spec upgrade spec.yaml --check           # exit 0: already the current apiVersion

mapi plugin init NAME scaffolds a plugin package (model, entry point, contract-kit tests) and mapi plugin test NAME runs its tests; see Write a plugin.

docs.title: Against a running platform
docs.text: Start the stack first (make dev, then make seed; see the quickstart).

docs.title: Choosing the API
docs.text:
Every remote command resolves the API the same way as the Python client, first match wins:

  1. --url and --token (global options, before the command: mapi --url http://… runs ls);
  2. MAPI_URL (falling back to MAPI_API_URL, the name make dev uses), MAPI_TOKEN and MAPI_PROFILE;
  3. the selected profile in ~/.config/mapi/config.toml ($MAPI_CONFIG or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mapi/config.toml if set);
  4. http://127.0.0.1:8000.
# ~/.config/mapi/config.toml
profile = "local"

[profiles.local]
url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"

[profiles.other-ports]
url = "http://127.0.0.1:18000"
timeout = 60

mapi config show prints the resolved URL and profile and where each value came from (never the token); mapi config path prints the file's location. --remote @ on check, fit, score and catalog means "the configured API"; --remote URL overrides it for one command.

Tokens

v0.2 is single-tenant and has no authentication: the API listens on 127.0.0.1 only. The client already sends MAPI_TOKEN as a bearer token, and refuses to send it over plain HTTP to anything but a loopback address. OIDC and scoped tokens arrive with multi-tenancy in v0.3.

docs.title: Upload data
docs.text:
mapi datasets upload creates the dataset if it does not exist, sends the file to the signed URL the API returns, starts the sandboxed ingest run and waits until the version is ready. CSV and Parquet files need --mapping mapping.yaml, an IngestMapping with the column of each dim and variable:

python scripts/seed.py --export demo/      # the E33 tables, score payloads and spec
mapi datasets upload demo/eu_media_future.zarr.zip --name eu_media_future
mapi datasets ls

docs.title: Fit and follow
docs.text:
mapi fit SPEC --remote @ creates the spec (or adds a revision when the text changed), submits a fit run and follows its event stream until it ends, printing warnings, diagnostics and metrics as they arrive. --no-wait returns after submitting; mapi runs watch RUN follows any run later.

mapi check demo/eu-geo-mmm.yaml --remote @   # the server's static validation
mapi fit demo/eu-geo-mmm.yaml --remote @     # create or revise the spec, fit, follow
mapi runs ls --kind fit --limit 3

mapi runs cancel RUN requests cancellation, and mapi runs retry RUN --resource-class L starts a new run from a failed one.

docs.title: Score
docs.text:
cat > forecast.yaml <<'EOF'
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ScoreRequest
model: model://default/eu-geo-mmm@latest
mode: forecast
horizon: {dim: time, periods: 8}
data: dataset://default/eu_media_future@latest
side_tables: {fx: dataset://default/fx_daily@latest}
output: {kind: expected, summary: [mean, hdi_90]}
EOF
# the CLI has no `models` command yet: take the model id and version from the API
MODEL=$(curl -s "${MAPI_API_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:8000}/v1/models" \
  | jq -c '.items[] | select(.name == "eu-geo-mmm")')
mapi score forecast.yaml --remote @ --model "$(jq -r .id <<<"$MODEL")" \
  --version "$(jq -r .latest_version <<<"$MODEL")" -o forecast.zarr.zip

mapi score --remote @ sends Prefer: wait=60 (change it with --wait), follows the run if it takes longer, prints the outputs with their sizes and CRC32C, and with -o downloads the result tree, checking it against that CRC32C.

docs.title: Scripting with --json
docs.text:
--json (a global option) prints one JSON document on stdout instead of tables; runs watch --json prints one JSON event per line. Errors become {"error": {...}} with exit status 1, and usage errors exit with 2.

RUN=$(mapi --json runs ls --kind score --limit 1 | jq -r '.[0].id')
mapi --json runs get "$RUN" | jq '{state, attempt, kind}'
mapi runs logs "$RUN" | tail -n 5

Text that came from the server, a plugin or a run log is printed with ANSI and control sequences removed, so a hostile log line cannot rewrite your terminal.

docs.title: mapi serve
docs.text: mapi serve runs mapi-server dev: database migrations, then the API and the orchestrator in one process, with an embedded PostgreSQL unless DATABASE_URL is set and an in-process GCS shim unless one already listens at MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT. It is the smallest way to get an API for the CLI or the client. For the web app as well, use make dev (Local deployment).

docs.title: Conformance corpus
docs.text:
The corpus is how the platform defines "supported": a set of small, realistic modelling problems (ports of pymc-challenges and of the plan's examples) that must keep working, end to end, on every change. Each fixture goes through exactly what a user's model goes through:

  1. validate – the spec is checked statically against the step, model and plot catalogs, as the API does before accepting a run;
  2. fit – a fit run on the in-process executor, honouring fit.mode (evaluate_then_refit included);
  3. score – every request in score_requests.yaml as a score run; requests that must fail are checked for their typed error code (HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT, UNSEEN_LEVELS, ...);
  4. evaluate – the holdout scored through the score path; the metrics must equal the ones computed at fit time;
  5. contract – the full check_model contract kit;
  6. plots – the spec's outputs.plots rendered from real outputs;
  7. expectations – the fixture's own checks (recovered effects, terminal state, ...).

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
python -m mapi_conformance list
python -m mapi_conformance run                         # every fixture at size tiny
python -m mapi_conformance run --fixture e24 --fixture c08
python -m mapi_conformance run --size full --json corpus.json
make conformance                                       # the same as `run` at size tiny
make conformance FIXTURE=e33                           # one fixture
make conformance-full                                  # every fixture at size full
python -m mapi_conformance list --deferred             # plus the plan fixtures not ported yet

The runner prints one row per fixture and exits non-zero if any step failed:

fixture           model                           validate  fit  score   evaluate  contract  plots   expectations  ...  result
----------------  ------------------------------  --------  ---  ------  --------  --------  ------  ------------       ------
e02               tabular.hierarchical_glm@1.0.0  ok        ok   ok 6/6  ok        ok 13/13  ok 2/2  ok                 PASS
c08               ts.hsgp_trend@1.0.0             ok        ok   ok 6/6  ok        ok 13/13  ok 3/3  ok                 PASS
e24               ts.gaussian_hmm@1.0.0           ok        ok   ok 5/5  ok        ok 15/15  ok 2/2  ok                 PASS
xgb_store_demand  tabular.regressor@1.0.0         ok        ok   ok 6/6  ok        ok 16/16  ok 3/3  ok                 PASS
e33               mmm.hierarchical_geo@1.3.0      ok        ok   ok 5/5  ok        ok 16/16  ok 4/4  ok                 PASS
pymc_marketing    mmm.pymc_marketing@1.0.0        ok        ok   ok 4/4  ok        ok 16/16  ok 2/2  ok                 PASS

--size tiny (the default, used by pytest -m conformance) keeps data small and MCMC short; --size full uses the spec's own fit settings and larger data.

docs.title: Through a running stack
docs.text:
The default runner skips the control plane. --stack drives the same fixtures through the API of a running stack (make dev), as a user does: spec → ingest → fit → score.

  1. The data, side tables and score payloads are uploaded as dataset versions (signed PUT, then a sandboxed ingest run).
  2. The spec, pointed at the uploads, is validated, created and fitted through the dispatcher, the runner and FINALIZING.
  3. Every score request runs against the registered model. An expected typed error may come from the failed run or from the API refusing the request up front.
  4. The holdout metrics and stored plots are checked on the model version.
  5. The bundle is downloaded through signed URLs with every hash verified, and goes through the fixture's check_fit.
python -m mapi_conformance run --stack http://127.0.0.1:8000 --fixture e33 --fixture xgb_store_demand
uv run pytest -m e2e tests/e2e/test_corpus_stack.py   # E33, xgboost and sklearn (`make e2e`)

The contract kit does not run in this mode; it needs the plugin in-process.

docs.title: The fixtures
docs.text: Fixture Model Exercises e02 tabular.hierarchical_glm long layout, shuffled county labels, hyperprior new counties, LOO, CRN counterfactual c08 ts.hsgp_trend sentinel codes, max_extension from anticipated coords, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT, contiguity e24 ts.gaussian_hmm padded + mask, terminal state, forecast and filter, relabelling, invalid LOO xgb_store_demand tabular.regressor pooled new stores, quantile aggregation refused, future-required covariates sklearn_store_demand sklearn.tabular_conformal the same panel with plain scikit-learn (histogram boosting, skops): split-conformal intervals, interval aggregation refused, pooled new stores e33 mmm.hierarchical_geo FX (supplied) and holiday (pinned) side tables, split after resample, per-market lag context, new market from the hyperprior, weekly EUR plan via inputs_stage, CRN counterfactual (intervention and baseline-vs-scenario), derived quantities in EUR pymc_marketing mmm.pymc_marketing a model that owns scaling, carry-over and units; a scoring window equals the same weeks of the full series

docs.title: Deferred
docs.text:
The plan's corpus also lists fixtures that need plugins or run kinds that do not exist yet. They are listed in mapi_conformance.fixtures.DEFERRED with the reason, and a test keeps the plan's list, the fixtures and the deferrals in step:

Plan fixture Waits for E13 state-space a state-space plugin with the filter mode (vetted plugins, M4) E84-lite choice panel a discrete-choice plugin (M4) E82-slim GP Bayesian optimisation the recommend mode and Campaign runs (M6) E45 a plugin for its model (vetted plugins, M4)

docs.title: Porting time
docs.text:
The M0 exit criteria ask for the porting time of every fixture (target: under one day each, model plugin plus fixture). It measures human effort, so it cannot be derived from the code or from commit timestamps; record it here when a fixture is ported or re-ported.

Fixture Porting time Recorded e02 not measured yet – c08 not measured yet – e24 not measured yet – xgb_store_demand not measured yet – sklearn_store_demand not measured yet – e33 not measured yet – pymc_marketing not measured yet –

docs.title: Add a fixture
docs.text:
Create a package conformance/src/mapi_conformance/fixtures/<id>/ and list <id> in fixtures/__init__.py.

data.py generates the data:

def generate(seed: int = 0, size: str = "tiny") -> tuple[xr.Dataset, dict[str, xr.Dataset]]:
    """The dataset and its side tables (name -> dataset)."""

def schema() -> DataSchema:            # optional: the raw schema (else inferred)
    ...

def payload_new_store(data, seed, size) -> xr.Dataset:   # optional payload builders
    ...

spec.yaml is an ordinary ModelSpec with the fit settings of a full run.

score_requests.yaml lists the requests to score. apiVersion, kind and model are filled in for you:

- name: forecast_with_new_store
  request: {mode: forecast, horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}}
  payload: new_store          # none | fit_data | "tail:<n>" | a payload_<name> builder
  drop_targets: true          # remove target variables from the payload (default)
  side_tables: true           # pass the fixture's side tables to the run (default)
  expect: {vars: [y_hat], sizes: {week: 4}, issues: [UNSEEN_LEVELS], groups: [summary]}
- name: quantiles_are_not_summed
  request: {mode: forecast, horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}, output: {aggregate: {over: [store_id]}}}
  payload: new_store
  expect_error: CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED

expectations.py (optional) adds fixture-specific checks; raise AssertionError to fail:

TINY_FIT = {"tune": 150, "draws": 100, "chains": 2}       # fit overrides at size tiny
TINY_SETTINGS = {"m": 20}                                  # model-settings overrides
MODEL_CHECKS = None                                        # or a subset of check_model checks

def check_fit(bundle, data): ...
def check_score(name, tree, bundle, data): ...
def check_evaluate(tree, bundle, data): ...

A hook that declares a keyword ctx parameter also receives a FixtureContext: the seed, size, registry, side tables and results, the trees of the score requests that succeeded before this one. Use it to compare requests, as E33 does when it checks that a weekly EUR plan forecasts exactly what the raw daily path forecasts:

def check_score(name, tree, bundle, data, *, ctx):
    if name == "weekly_eur_plan" and "forecast_8w" in ctx.results:
        ...

A side table with score_policy: supplied must be named in each score request that replays its step (request.side_tables); the runner supplies the data under that name.

From Python, mapi_conformance.run_fixture("e24") returns a FixtureReport and run_corpus() a CorpusReport with .table() and .to_json().

docs.title: Your first model in the web app v0.2
docs.text:
This guide fits a hierarchical geo marketing-mix model (the corpus' E33 example) on the local stack and then uses it, entirely from the browser:

  1. upload daily spend and revenue per market and channel, an FX table and a holiday table;
  2. paste the model spec into the editor and let it validate as you type;
  3. fit it and follow the sampler live;
  4. read the sanity scorecard, the posterior predictive check and the channel decomposition;
  5. score an 8-week forecast, a market the model has never seen, and a weekly budget in EUR.

It takes about ten minutes, most of it reading. The fit itself uses tiny sampler settings and finishes in under a minute on a laptop.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Start the stack and leave it running (Local development):

make install
make dev                      # PostgreSQL, GCS shim, API, worker, web app, plot sandbox
open http://127.0.0.1:5173

Port 8000 taken?

Move the API with export MAPI_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8010 before make dev. Every other command in this guide (make seed, make e2e) reads the same variable. The other three ports move the same way; see Port conflicts.

This guide clicks through every step, including the uploads. For the short path (make seed loads the data and the spec for you) see the quickstart; for every page of the app, The Expert web app.

Then write the demo files to a folder. Nothing is uploaded yet:

uv run python scripts/seed.py --export demo/
File What it is Upload it as eu_media_daily.zarr.zip 30 weeks of daily spend_local(market, channel, date) and revenue_local(market, date) for NL, DE and UK (UK in GBP) eu_media_daily fx_daily.zarr.zip Daily EUR per GBP, covering the fit window and the forecast horizon fx_daily holidays_eu.zarr.zip A daily holiday indicator holidays_eu eu_media_future.zarr.zip Planned daily spend for the 8 weeks after the data (no revenue) eu_media_future eu_media_future_fr.zarr.zip The same weeks plus FR, a market the model has not seen eu_media_future_fr eu_media_weekly_plan.zarr.zip A planner's budget: weekly spend in EUR eu_media_weekly_plan eu_media_window.zarr.zip The last four weeks of the data, for counterfactuals eu_media_window eu-geo-mmm.yaml The model spec, pointing at dataset://default/<name>@latest (paste it)

make seed does steps 1 and 2 for you through the HTTP API. This guide clicks through them.

docs.title: 1. Upload the data
docs.text:
Open Datasets → New dataset, name it eu_media_daily and create it. The upload panel opens: choose eu_media_daily.zarr.zip and press Upload and ingest. The browser sends the file straight to object storage through a signed URL; a sandboxed ingest run then opens it, checks it and stores an immutable, content-addressed version. The page refreshes on its own until the version is ready.

The schema came with the file: market allows new levels at score time (with a hyperprior), channel is fixed, and date may be extended into the future. revenue_local is the target, spend_local is spend, both in local currency. A CSV upload would ask you for the same mapping column by column.

Repeat for the other six files, using the names in the table above.

docs.title: 2. Write and validate the spec
docs.text:
Open Build → New spec, select everything in the editor and paste eu-geo-mmm.yaml. The editor validates as you type: the server resolves every dataset:// reference and step, checks the settings and propagates the schema through the pipeline without running anything. Problems appear as squiggles at the exact YAML path.

The pipeline panel shows what each step does to the data. to_eur converts both spend and revenue to EUR with the fx side table, weekly resamples days to weeks (only from this stage on does a week exist, so the train/holdout split sits right after it), and scale_spend, scale_y and lags learn state from the training weeks only. Open Schema after this step on any card to see the variables and dims at that stage.

Press Save spec. The spec becomes revision r1 of spec://default/eu-geo-mmm. (If you ran make seed before, that name is taken: change metadata.name first, or open the seeded spec under Build instead.)

docs.title: 3. Fit it
docs.text:
Press Fit. The run page follows the run over server-sent events:

  • Starting the sandbox: the run's supervisor read its one-time bootstrap object and deleted it, so the credentials it held are gone before any model code runs.
  • DEV_MODE_ISOLATION is expected on a laptop: the local executor cannot drop to a separate user for the model code. Containers and Cloud Run do.
  • The progress bar and message come straight from the sampler (chain 1/2: sampling 39/100).

fit.mode: evaluate_then_refit makes the run fit the training weeks, score the 8 holdout weeks through the normal scoring path, then refit on all the data, so the model you use has seen the latest weeks while its metrics are honest. When the run succeeds, the platform checks every file the run claims to have written against the storage's own checksums, copies them where the run cannot reach, and signs a manifest. Press Inspect model://default/eu-geo-mmm@v1.

docs.title: 4. Inspect the model
docs.text:
The Overview tab opens on the sanity scorecard, the holdout metrics and what the model can do.

With 2 chains of 100 draws the sampler has not converged: R-hat above 1.01 and fewer than 200 effective samples are flagged as warnings, each with a suggested action. That is the point of the tiny settings; raise tune and draws (and use more chains) for a model you mean to use. Diagnostics lists the same checks per variable.

Plots has the recipes the spec asked for. Every plot renders inside an <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts"> served from a separate origin (port 5174), so even a malicious plot spec could not read the app, its cookies or your data.

Fit and forecast compares the model's predictions for the holdout weeks with what happened: the line is the median, the bands are the 50% and 90% intervals, the dots are the actual weekly EUR revenue.

Contribution by component splits revenue over time into the baseline, each channel, seasonality and holidays, in EUR, with the totals and their uncertainty below. Response curves shows what an extra euro of spend returns per channel, and Sampler convergence has the trace and rank plots behind the scorecard. Provenance shows the signed manifest, every stored object with its generation, and the lineage: data and side table versions, spec hash, plugin, seed and library versions.

docs.title: 5. Score it
docs.text:
Press Score. The form only offers what this model supports, and the fitted preprocessing is replayed exactly: nothing is refitted.

An 8-week forecast. Keep mode forecast with 8 periods along time, set Input data to dataset://default/eu_media_future@v1 and press Score. The fx side table defaults to the one the fit used; it covers the horizon, so the planned local-currency spend can be converted to EUR. The result shows a fan per market, then the outputs: the result tree (score.zarr.zip), its summary as a table, and a quick chart you can re-plot by any column.

A new market. Score again with dataset://default/eu_media_future_fr@v1. FR was never seen in training; its effects are drawn from the hierarchical prior over markets, so its band is visibly wider than the others'. The result's issues record an UNSEEN_LEVELS note saying so.

A weekly plan in EUR. Planners think in weekly euros, not daily local currency. Set Inputs enter at stage to weekly and Input data to dataset://default/eu_media_weekly_plan@v1. The request enters the pipeline after to_eur and weekly, so no FX table is needed. Because this plan is the same spend as the daily file, the forecast is identical to the first one, which is exactly what replaying the preprocessing promises.

A counterfactual. Choose mode counterfactual, set Input data to dataset://default/eu_media_window@v1, add an intervention spend_local where channel=tv, multiply by 1.2, choose Predictive output and set Draws to 100 (with 0 draws you get the means, but not the uncertainty of the change). The result holds the baseline, the scenario and their difference, computed with common random numbers so the delta is not drowned in sampling noise.

docs.title: What was checked along the way
docs.text:
The same flow runs as two automated suites against the running stack (make e2e):

  • tests/e2e/test_m1_stack.py drives it through the Python client. It also verifies the manifest signature, that every bundle object sits in the bundles bucket at its signed generation, that the bundle reads back with all hashes intact, that the bootstrap object is gone, and that forged run events are refused.
  • apps/web/e2e/m1-flow.e2e.spec.ts clicks through the pages above with Playwright and checks that the plot frame is an opaque origin with no access to its parent.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Marketing-mix models: the model, its priors, derived quantities and budget plots.
  • Spec format and the steps used here.
  • Web app and plot sandbox: every page and how plots are isolated.

docs.title: The HTTP API v0.2
docs.text:
Everything the web app, the CLI and the Python client do is a call to the versioned /v1 HTTP API. This guide does the main flow with curl and jq, so you can see every request. The script is docs/snippets/http_tour.sh; make e2e runs it against a live stack. The outputs below are from one of those runs, shortened.

Where What HTTP API reference Conventions, errors, pagination, idempotency, SSE and every endpoint with its DTOs OpenAPI explorer The OpenAPI 3.1 document, browsable, with every schema and example GET /openapi.json on a running API The same document, served by the API itself Error codes Every stable error code and its HTTP status

Start the stack and load the demo first: make dev, make seed, uv run python scripts/seed.py --export demo/ and uv run mapi datasets upload demo/eu_media_future.zarr.zip --name eu_media_future (see the quickstart).

docs.title: Health and the catalog
docs.text:
API=${MAPI_API_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:8000}
curl -s "$API/readyz" | jq -c '{status, version, checks: .checks | map_values(.status)}'
curl -s "$API/v1/catalog/models" \
  | jq -r '.items[].manifest | "\(.id)@\(.version)  \(.capabilities.representation)"'

{"status":"ok","version":"0.2.0","checks":{"postgres":"ok","object_store":"ok","catalog":"ok"}}
mmm.hierarchical_geo@1.3.0  draws
mmm.pymc_marketing@1.0.0  draws
sklearn.tabular_bootstrap@1.0.0  draws
…
ts.hsgp_trend@1.0.0  draws

/healthz says the process is alive; /readyz checks PostgreSQL, the object store and the catalog, and answers 503 with the same body when one is not ready. The catalog is what the runner image provides, exported by a sandboxed describe run; specs are validated against it.

docs.title: Upload a CSV
docs.text:
Data never passes through the API. You create a dataset, ask for an upload session, and PUT the bytes to the signed URL it returns:

DS=$(curl -s "$API/v1/datasets?limit=200" | jq -r '.items[] | select(.name == "weekly_sales") | .id')
if [ -z "$DS" ]; then
  DS=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/v1/datasets" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"name": "weekly_sales", "description": "a CSV upload from the HTTP guide"}' | jq -r .id)
fi
echo "dataset $DS"
printf 'week,sales\n2026-01-04,120\n2026-01-11,131\n2026-01-18,127\n2026-01-25,140\n' > sales.csv
SIZE=$(wc -c < sales.csv | tr -d ' ')
UP=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/v1/datasets/$DS/uploads" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"filename\": \"sales.csv\", \"content_type\": \"text/csv\", \"size_bytes\": $SIZE}")
HEADERS=()  # the signed URL binds these headers: send them exactly
while IFS= read -r h; do HEADERS+=(-H "$h"); done \
  < <(jq -r '.upload.headers | to_entries[] | "\(.key): \(.value)"' <<<"$UP")
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'PUT %{http_code}\n' -X PUT "${HEADERS[@]}" \
  --data-binary @sales.csv "$(jq -r .upload.url <<<"$UP")"

dataset ds_01m4zy65cdbxtaa4vgsvpeb4rt
PUT 200

The URL is a V4-style signed URL for one object in the quarantine bucket, valid for an hour. Send the headers from upload.headers exactly, because they are part of the signature: content-type must be the one you declared, x-goog-content-length-range caps the size at size_bytes, and x-goog-if-generation-match: 0 makes the object write-once, so a second PUT to the same URL is rejected.

Then turn the upload into a dataset version. For CSV and Parquet the mapping names the column of every dim and variable, with its kind, score-time policy and role:

MAPPING='{
  "format": "csv",
  "dims": {"week": {"column": "week", "spec": {"kind": "time", "policy": "extend", "freq": "W-SUN"}}},
  "vars": {"sales": {"column": "sales", "role": "target", "units": "units"}}
}'
DV=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/v1/datasets/$DS/versions" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d "{\"upload_id\": $(jq .id <<<"$UP"), \"mapping\": $MAPPING}")
V=$(jq -r .version <<<"$DV")
STATUS=ingesting
while [ "$STATUS" = ingesting ]; do  # a sandboxed ingest run parses and checks the file
  sleep 1
  STATUS=$(curl -s "$API/v1/datasets/$DS/versions/$V" | jq -r '.status // "ingesting"')
done
curl -s "$API/v1/datasets/$DS/versions/$V" | jq '{ref, status, dims: .data_schema.dims | keys}'

{
  "ref": "dataset://default/weekly_sales@v1",
  "status": "ready",
  "dims": ["week"]
}

POST …/versions answers 202 with the version in status ingesting and the id of the sandboxed ingest run that parses the file. It accepts an Idempotency-Key: a retried request with the same key and body returns the same version instead of ingesting twice.

docs.title: Validate and fit a spec
docs.text:
jq -Rs '{yaml: .}' demo/eu-geo-mmm.yaml \
  | curl -s -X POST "$API/v1/specs:validate" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @- \
  | jq '{valid, issues: [.issues[] | {code, pointer}], stages: [.stages[] | .name]}'

{
  "valid": true,
  "issues": [],
  "stages": ["raw", "to_eur", "weekly", "scale_spend", "scale_y", "lags", "season", "hols"]
}

POST /v1/specs:validate answers 200 even for an invalid spec: the verdict is in valid and every problem is in issues with its code and JSON pointer. Non-2xx statuses are kept for requests that cannot be validated at all (unparseable YAML, too large).

SPEC=$(curl -s "$API/v1/specs?limit=200" | jq -c '.items[] | select(.name == "eu-geo-mmm")')
RUN=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/v1/runs" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d "{\"kind\": \"fit\", \"spec_id\": $(jq .id <<<"$SPEC"), \"revision\": $(jq .latest_revision <<<"$SPEC")}" \
  | jq -r .id)
echo "run $RUN"

POST /v1/runs answers 201 with the run in state created or queued. The same Idempotency-Key with the same body answers 200 with the same run; with a different body, 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Generate one key per user intent and reuse it on retries.

docs.title: Follow the run
docs.text:
# server-sent events: a snapshot, the persisted events, live progress, then `end`
curl -sN -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' "$API/v1/runs/$RUN/events" | grep '^event:' | uniq -c
curl -s "$API/v1/runs/$RUN" | jq '{state, output_model_version_id}'

   3 event: snapshot
   1 event: state
   1 event: warning
   2 event: state
   6 event: progress
   1 event: state
   5 event: diagnostic
   3 event: metric
   1 event: state
   1 event: complete
   1 event: state
   2 event: snapshot
   1 event: end
{
  "state": "succeeded",
  "output_model_version_id": "mv_01m4zy6yc82qy97jzjmv9phv1j"
}

With Accept: text/event-stream the events endpoint is a live stream: a snapshot of the run first, then the persisted events (each with an id:), live progress and log frames (no id, never replayed), a fresh snapshot on every state change, and end when the run is terminal, after which the server closes the stream. Reconnect with Last-Event-ID: <id> to resume exactly after the last persisted event. Without that Accept header the same URL returns the persisted events as a JSON page. See Run events.

docs.title: Read the model version
docs.text:
MODEL=$(curl -s "$API/v1/models?limit=200" | jq -c '.items[] | select(.name == "eu-geo-mmm")')
M=$(jq -r .id <<<"$MODEL")
MV=$(jq -r .latest_version <<<"$MODEL")
curl -s "$API/v1/models/$M/versions/$MV" \
  | jq '{ref, scorecard: .scorecard.overall, metrics, signed: .manifest.signature.alg}'

{
  "ref": "model://default/eu-geo-mmm@v1",
  "scorecard": "warn",
  "metrics": {"mape": 7.59, "elpd_loo": 183.47, "coverage_90": 0.875},
  "signed": "KMS-EC-P256-SHA256"
}

GET …/artifacts/{name} returns a signed GET URL for any bundle object or ui/ view. It is minted only after the server has verified the version's signed manifest; each link is pinned to an object generation, supports HTTP Range requests and expires after 15 minutes.

docs.title: Score
docs.text:
RES=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/v1/models/$M/versions/$MV:score" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Prefer: wait=60' -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"request": {
        "apiVersion": "mapi/v1", "kind": "ScoreRequest",
        "model": "model://default/eu-geo-mmm@latest",
        "mode": "forecast",
        "horizon": {"dim": "time", "periods": 8},
        "data": "dataset://default/eu_media_future@latest",
        "side_tables": {"fx": "dataset://default/fx_daily@latest"}}}')
jq '{done, state: .run.state, outputs: [.outputs[] | {name, size, crc32c}]}' <<<"$RES"
curl -s "$(jq -r '.outputs[] | select(.name == "result.json") | .url' <<<"$RES")" \
  | jq '{mode, representation, output_space}'

{
  "done": true,
  "state": "succeeded",
  "outputs": [
    {"name": "plots.json", "size": 4122, "crc32c": "d8PGZA=="},
    {"name": "result.json", "size": 406, "crc32c": "PonvmQ=="},
    {"name": "score.zarr.zip", "size": 9396, "crc32c": "Uwymhw=="},
    {"name": "ui/summary.arrow", "size": 27266, "crc32c": "hxiS8w=="}
  ]
}
{
  "mode": "forecast",
  "representation": "draws",
  "output_space": {"contributions": "weekly", "y_hat": "weekly"}
}

Prefer: wait=60 holds the request until the score run finishes (at most 60 seconds) and answers 200 with done: true and signed links to the outputs. If it takes longer the answer is 202 with done: false: repeat the request with the same Idempotency-Key to get the same run's result, or follow the run. The response header Preference-Applied says which wait the server used. Over HTTP the ScoreRequest needs its apiVersion and kind (the Python client fills them in).

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
curl -s -X POST "$API/v1/models/$M/versions/$MV:score" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"request": {"apiVersion": "mapi/v1", "kind": "ScoreRequest",
       "model": "model://default/eu-geo-mmm@latest", "mode": "filter",
       "data": "dataset://default/eu_media_future@latest"}}' | jq '{status, code, detail}'

{
  "status": 422,
  "code": "MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED",
  "detail": "validation failed with 2 errors; first at /mode: model 'mmm.hierarchical_geo@1.3.0' does not support mode 'filter'"
}

Every error is an RFC 7807 problem document (application/problem+json) with a stable code, an HTTP status, and every individual problem in errors[] with a JSON pointer. Tracebacks and plugin messages only ever appear in an untrusted_text field; render them as text. The score request above was rejected statically: no run was created.

docs.title: Other clients
docs.text: The OpenAPI document is generated from the server itself (apps/web/scripts/gen_openapi.py writes apps/web/openapi.json, and CI fails if it drifts), so any OpenAPI generator produces a typed client. The web app's TypeScript client is generated that way (openapi-typescript and openapi-fetch). For Python, use mapi_client.

docs.title: Marketing-mix models
docs.text:
mapi-plugin-mmm ships two marketing-mix models (MMMs) as built-in plugins:

Plugin What it is Use it when mmm.hierarchical_geo A hierarchical geo MMM written for the platform (PyMC) You have several markets, want new markets and budgets scored honestly, and want response curves and marginal costs in your own currency mmm.pymc_marketing An adapter around pymc-marketing's MMM You already use pymc-marketing and want its model behind the platform: versioned bundles, forecasts, counterfactuals and plots

Both are registered through the mapi.models entry point, so a spec only has to name them: use: mmm.hierarchical_geo@^1.3.

docs.title: From daily spend in local currency to weekly EUR decisions
docs.text:
A typical European media dataset is daily, per market and channel, in each market's own currency. The platform's preprocessing turns that into the weekly EUR panel the model fits, and remembers every learned step so scoring replays exactly the same work:

apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: eu-geo-mmm, project: growth}
data:
  dataset: dataset://growth/eu_media_daily@latest
  side_tables:
    fx:       {ref: dataset://growth/fx_daily@latest, score_policy: supplied}
    holidays: {ref: dataset://shared/holidays_eu@v3, score_policy: pinned}
  bind:
    dims: {geo: market, channel: channel, time: date}
    vars: {y: revenue_local, spend: spend_local}
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: time, last: 8, after_step: weekly}   # weeks exist after `weekly`
pipeline:
  - id: to_eur
    use: core.fx_convert@^1
    with: {vars: [y, spend], table: fx, table_along: date, currency_dim: geo,
           currencies: {UK: GBP}, default_currency: EUR}
  - {id: weekly,      use: core.resample@^1,   with: {dim: time, freq: W-SUN, how: sum}}
  - {id: scale_spend, use: core.mean_scale@^1, with: {vars: [spend], over: [time], unseen_levels: pooled}}
  - {id: scale_y,     use: core.mean_scale@^1, with: {vars: [y], over: [time], unseen_levels: pooled}}
  - {id: lags,        use: core.lag_tensor@^1, with: {vars: [spend], along: time, within: [geo], l_max: 6, pad: first}}
  - {id: season,      use: core.fourier@^1,    with: {along: time, period: 52.18, order: 3, out: fourier}}
  - {id: hols,        use: core.holidays@^1,   with: {table: holidays, table_along: date, along: time}}
model:
  use: mmm.hierarchical_geo@^1.3
  settings:
    pooling: partial
    adstock: {kind: geometric, l_max: 6}
    saturation: {kind: logistic}
    priors:
      beta_channel: {distribution: HalfNormal, sigma: 1.0, dims: [channel]}
      lam:          {distribution: Gamma, alpha: 3, beta: 1, dims: [channel]}
  fit: {mode: evaluate_then_refit, engine: nutpie, tune: 1000, draws: 1000, chains: 4, seed: 7}
outputs:
  derived: [contributions, response_curves, marginal_cost]
  plots: [core.ppc_fan, core.convergence, mmm.decomposition, mmm.response_curves]
evaluate: {metrics: [elpd_loo, coverage_90, mape]}

What the platform does with this, without a line of model code:

  • Binding. Your names (market, revenue_local) become the model's canonical names (geo, y) and are reversed on every output.
  • Split at the right stage. The holdout is the last 8 weeks, cut after resampling, so no partial week leaks into training.
  • Evaluate, then refit. The model is fitted on the training weeks, scored on the holdout through the scoring path (the same code a forecast uses), then refitted on all weeks so forecasts start from the latest data.
  • Context. lag_tensor stores each market's last weeks of spend; a forecast prepends them, so carry-over from last month's TV burst reaches next month's sales.
  • Original units. Predictions and contributions come back in weekly EUR: the scaling steps are inverted, and the inversion stops at the weekly resample (daily values cannot be recovered from weekly sums). Every output says so in its output_space and units attributes.

A runnable version of this spec, scaled down, ships as mapi_plugin_mmm.examples.E33_SPEC_YAML, together with a simulator (e33_dataset) whose true parameters are known.

docs.title: The model
docs.text:
For geo g, channel c and week t (model units: the target and spend are mean-scaled):

adstock   a[g,c,t] = sum_l spend[g,c,t,l] * w[c,l]          w = alpha**l (normalised)
saturate  s[g,c,t] = (1 - exp(-lam[c] a)) / (1 + exp(-lam[c] a))
effects   beta[g,c] = beta_channel[c] * exp(beta_sigma[c] * z[g,c])     partial pooling
mean      mu[g,t]  = intercept[g] + sum_c beta[g,c] s[g,c,t] + controls[g,t]
target    y[g,t]  ~ Normal(mu[g,t], sigma)

intercept[g] is a hierarchical effect over geos, and every other numeric variable along time (Fourier terms, holidays, prices…) is a control with one coefficient per feature.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Level Default Meaning pooling basic partial partial shares channel effects across geos; complete uses one effect for all geos; none estimates each geo separately (and then new geos cannot be scored) adstock.kind basic geometric geometric decays from the spend week; delayed peaks after theta weeks saturation.kind basic logistic logistic, hill or none (linear) centred advanced false Centred parameterisation of geo effects; non-centred samples better with few geos adstock.l_max advanced from the data Must equal the lag_tensor l_max adstock.normalize advanced true Lag weights sum to one, so a constant spend has steady-state adstock equal to the spend priors advanced see below Prior overrides by parameter controls advanced auto Control variables (default: every other numeric variable along time) grid advanced 0–2× in 21 steps The spend-multiplier grid of the response curves

Guided mode shows the basic settings only; every field carries x-ui-level in the manifest's JSON Schema.

docs.title: Priors
docs.text:
Priors use pymc-marketing's dict form: a distribution, numeric parameters and the canonical dims the parameter varies over.

Parameter Support Default Meaning intercept real Normal(0.5, 0.5) Population mean of the geo intercepts intercept_sigma positive HalfNormal(0.25) Spread of the geo intercepts beta_channel positive HalfNormal(1) per channel Typical channel effect at full saturation beta_sigma positive HalfNormal(0.3) per channel How much a channel's effect varies across geos alpha unit interval Beta(1, 3) per channel Weekly adstock decay theta positive HalfNormal(2) per channel Delayed adstock: weeks to the peak lam positive Gamma(3, 1) per channel Logistic saturation rate slope, half positive Gamma(3, 2), Gamma(2, 2) Hill curve gamma_control real Normal(0, 0.5) Each control feature's coefficient sigma positive HalfNormal(0.5) Observation noise

The allow-list covers Normal, StudentT, Laplace, HalfNormal, HalfStudentT, HalfCauchy, Exponential, Gamma, InverseGamma, LogNormal, Weibull, Beta, Uniform and TruncatedNormal. A prior whose support does not fit its parameter (a Normal media effect, a HalfNormal adstock decay) is rejected when the spec is validated, before anything runs. A list-valued parameter gives one value per label:

priors:
  lam: {distribution: Gamma, alpha: [3, 2, 2], beta: 1, dims: [channel]}

docs.title: Scoring
docs.text:
Score requests work like for every other model; these are the ones MMM users need most.

ForecastA new marketA weekly EUR planWhat if 
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ScoreRequest
model: endpoint://growth/eu-geo-mmm-prod
mode: forecast
horizon: {dim: time, periods: 8}
side_tables: {fx: dataset://growth/fx_daily@latest}    # fx is `supplied` at score time
output: {kind: expected, summary: [mean, hdi_90], draws: 200}

Send daily spend in local currency for the next 8 weeks; get weekly EUR revenue.

Add a market the model has never seen (FR). Its intercept and channel effects are drawn from the fitted hyperpriors for every posterior draw, so its forecast is honest about what the model does not know: wider than a fitted market's. The response carries an UNSEEN_LEVELS notice.

mode: forecast
horizon: {dim: time, periods: 8}
inputs_stage: weekly          # enter after fx conversion and resampling

Planners and optimisers send weekly EUR budgets (spend_local(market, channel, date) on W-SUN weeks) instead of inventing daily local-currency spend. No FX table is needed: the steps that use it are skipped. The forecast equals the raw-data path for the same spend.

mode: counterfactual
interventions: [{var: spend_local, sel: {channel: tv}, multiply: 1.2}]
output: {kind: predictive, draws: 200}

The scenario and the baseline share their noise (common random numbers), so the delta group shows the effect of the change, not sampling noise. Only the treated channel's contribution moves.

Every score returns y_hat and contributions(component, geo, time): one component per channel, baseline and one per control. They add up to y_hat.

docs.title: Derived quantities: what a Guided report reads
docs.text:
Ask for them in outputs.derived; they are computed once, at fit, over the first outputs.ui_draws posterior draws, and stored in the bundle in original units:

  • contributions: channel_contribution(sample, channel, geo, time), baseline and one variable per control, over the fit window. mmm.decomposition plots them.
  • response_curves: contribution(sample, channel, multiplier, geo), the total contribution over the fit window when a channel's spend is scaled by the multiplier, plus the EUR spend on every grid point. mmm.response_curves and mmm.marginal_cost plot them, and Guided-mode what-if sliders interpolate them per draw: instant, and the uncertainty bands stay joint.
  • marginal_cost: the extra EUR of spend needed for one extra EUR of revenue at current spend (and its inverse, marginal ROI), per geo and per channel.

docs.title: Optimising budgets
docs.text:
mmm.hierarchical_geo declares decision: true. Its objective scores a budget per posterior draw:

import xarray as xr
from mapi_plugin_mmm import HierarchicalGeoMMM
from mapi_sdk.models import ScoreContext

budget = xr.Dataset(
    {"spend": ("channel", [40_000.0, 25_000.0, 10_000.0])},
    coords={"channel": ["tv", "search", "social"]},
    attrs={"periods": 13},                       # EUR per week, for a quarter
)
value = HierarchicalGeoMMM().objective(bundle.model, budget, ScoreContext())
value.dims   # ('chain', 'draw'): expected revenue of the plan, per draw

Budgets are in original units (EUR per week here) and so is the result; this uses the unit conversions cached with response_curves, so request that derived quantity (or pass attrs={"units": "model"} to work in model units). A channel budget is split across geos by each geo's share of that channel's spend; pass spend(geo, channel) to set it yourself. The value assumes the spend is sustained long enough for carry-over to settle (steady state).

docs.title: The pymc-marketing adapter
docs.text:
mmm.pymc_marketing runs pymc_marketing.mmm.MMM (version 1.2, on PyMC 6). pymc-marketing scales the data, carries spend over and reports original units itself, so the adapter declares owns: [scaling, carryover, inverse_units] and the platform steps aside:

  • keep scaling and lag steps out of the pipeline (currency conversion, resampling and holidays are fine);
  • scoring prepends the last l_max fit weeks before any window, so a four-week window scores exactly like the same weeks of the full series;
  • outputs are labelled model-owned; holdout metrics are not inverted a second time.
model:
  use: mmm.pymc_marketing@^1
  settings:
    dims: [geo]                    # panel dims besides time and channel
    adstock: {l_max: 4}
    saturation: {kind: logistic}
    controls: [holiday]
    yearly_seasonality: 2
  fit: {engine: nutpie, tune: 1000, draws: 1000, chains: 4}

Bundles never contain pickle: the adapter stores the posterior, pymc-marketing's fit_data and its JSON model description, and rebuilds the model through pymc-marketing's own loading path when it scores. Markets are a fixed dim for this adapter: pymc-marketing cannot score a market it has not seen.

docs.title: Trust, but verify
docs.text: Both plugins pass the SDK contract kit (mapi_sdk.testing.check_model): bundle round trips, shuffled and subset markets, typed errors, the holdout scored through the same path as a forecast, additive contributions. The conformance corpus runs both through the whole spec → fit → score path, and a parameter-recovery test fits simulated data with known adstock, saturation and channel effects and checks they come back (adstock decay within 0.1, EUR contributions within 20%).

docs.title: Plots: recipes, templates and safe sharing
docs.text:
