Every model you fit gets a set of standard plots for free: data overview, convergence, posterior predictive checks, a fit-and-forecast fan, decomposition, scenario comparisons and more. Plots are Vega-Lite (or Plotly for 3D, maps and animation) wrapped in a small envelope called a PlotSpec. The data travels next to the spec as named Arrow tables — never as a URL — and every plot passes a sanitizer before anyone sees it.

uv add "mapi-plots[recipes]"   # recipes + Altair/Plotly helpers (runner images, notebooks)
uv add mapi-plots              # sanitizer and templates only (JSON in, JSON out)

`core.ppc_fan`: model estimate, 50% and 90% bands, actual values and the end of the training data, one panel per market.

docs.title: Render a recipe in a notebook
docs.text:
A recipe is a function from a fitted bundle or a score output to a PlotSpec:

from mapi_plots.examples import example_inputs
from mapi_plots.recipes import get_recipe

inputs = example_inputs()  # synthetic bundle/score trees for every recipe (xarray only)
data, options = inputs["core.ppc_fan"]
plot = get_recipe("core.ppc_fan").render(data, **options)

print(plot.kind, plot.persona)  # vega-lite both
print(sorted(plot.datasets))  # named Arrow tables travel next to the spec, never as URLs
print(plot.caption_plain[:60], "...")

Inputs are flexible: an xr.DataTree (bundle or score output), an xr.Dataset, or a plain {"group": Dataset} mapping. Recipes find their groups at the root, under model/ (bundles) or anywhere in the tree. Options are validated; an unknown option or a missing group raises a typed RecipeDataError (SCHEMA_INVALID) that says what was expected.

Every plot carries:

  • persona — guided (analysts), expert (data scientists) or both;
  • caption_plain — a plain-language reading of the chart with the actual numbers ("The scenario changes total revenue by 184 (90% interval 139 to 251) compared with the baseline. Probability of an increase: 100%.");
  • provenance — the recipe and version, the bundle id and a timestamp.

Try every recipe without a model

mapi_plots.examples.example_inputs() returns synthetic bundle and score trees for every recipe, built with xarray only:

for recipe_id, (data, options) in example_inputs().items():
    rendered = get_recipe(recipe_id).render(data, **options)
    print(f"{recipe_id:28} {rendered.kind:10} {rendered.persona}")

docs.title: The standard catalog
docs.text:
Recipe What it shows Reads core.data_overview Each variable over time per group, a missingness heatmap, group sizes raw data / observed_data core.prior_predictive Datasets the model generates before seeing data vs your data, plus a prior fan prior_predictive, observed_data core.convergence R-hat and ESS per parameter, a table of the worst, trace and rank plots, divergences posterior, sample_stats core.posterior_forest Median, 50% and 94% HDI per parameter, one panel per variable posterior core.ppc Predictive densities vs observed, PIT histogram, interval coverage posterior_predictive, observed_data core.ppc_fan Fit + forecast fan with the train/forecast split line draws or summary, observed core.fit_vs_actual Predicted against actual with R² and MAPE predictions + observed core.residuals_over_time Actual minus predicted over time predictions + observed core.decomposition Stacked contributions over time and each component's total share contributions core.model_comparison elpd per model and the difference to the best (PSIS-LOO table or WAIC) comparison, or one child per model with log_likelihood core.counterfactual Scenario vs baseline over time and the distribution of the total change draws/summary, baseline/…, delta/… core.decision_distribution Distribution of a decision objective per option and P(best) decision/objective

The marketing-mix pack (mmm.*) adds response curves with current spend marked, marginal cost (or marginal ROI) per channel, a budget-plan comparison and a channel decomposition. The tabular pack (ml.*) adds ml.feature_importance: ranked tree importances, or signed coefficients for linear estimators, read from the groups the scikit-learn and xgboost plugins store in their bundles.

Recipes respect each output's representation: they sum joint draws when a dim has to go, but never add up quantiles or intervals — a summary with an extra dim asks you to request an aggregated output instead (summed means are shown without a band). Predicted-vs-actual and residual plots never need a total, so they compare such summaries cell by cell (one dot or line per store × sku, coloured by the facet dim).

docs.title: Bring your own chart
docs.text:
Build with Altair or Plotly as usual, then wrap it:

import altair as alt
import pandas as pd
from mapi_plots import from_altair

frame = pd.DataFrame({"week": pd.date_range("2026-01-04", periods=6, freq="W-SUN"),
                      "revenue": [10.0, 12.5, 11.0, 14.2, 15.1, 13.8]})
chart = alt.Chart(frame).mark_line().encode(x="week:T", y="revenue:Q")
mine = from_altair(chart, id="acme.revenue", caption_plain="Weekly revenue.")
print(list(mine.datasets))  # the inline data became a named dataset

import plotly.express as px
from mapi_plots import from_plotly

fig = px.scatter(frame, x="week", y="revenue")
theirs = from_plotly(fig, id="acme.scatter")  # typed arrays -> named Arrow datasets
print(list(theirs.datasets))  # one dataset per trace, referenced as {"$ref": "trace0.y"}
  • from_altair moves Altair's inline data (and any data.values) into named Arrow datasets and rewrites the references; named data (alt.Data(name="pts")) is filled from datasets={"pts": frame}.
  • from_plotly decodes plotly.py 6 typed arrays ({"dtype": "f8", "bdata": ...}) into Arrow datasets, one per trace, and binds them with {"$ref": "trace0.y"}. The default plotly.py template is dropped (the renderer themes plots) unless keep_template=True.

Both run the sanitizer and raise a SanitizeError if the chart breaks a rule. from_plotly also strips HTML from the strings it moves into datasets (see below).

Colours and dark mode. An explicit mark colour wins over any theme, so the platform recipes draw only with mapi_plots.palette (for example OBSERVED, ESTIMATE, BAND, ALERT). In dark mode the plot sandbox swaps each palette colour for its dark variant; every stroke, dot and text colour keeps at least 3:1 contrast on both card backgrounds. Use the palette in your own charts to get the same behaviour. Any other colour is drawn as written in both themes.

docs.title: Role- and dim-bound templates
docs.text:
A template binds channels to roles and dims instead of one model's variable names, so a "target over time, one line per geo" plot applies to every model of a family:

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import xarray as xr
from mapi_plots.recipes import builtin_templates, render_template

weekly = xr.Dataset(
    {"revenue": (("geo", "time"), np.random.default_rng(0).gamma(20.0, 50.0, (3, 12)),
                 {"role": "target", "units": "EUR"})},
    coords={"geo": ["DE", "FR", "UK"], "time": pd.date_range("2026-01-04", periods=12, freq="W-SUN")},
)
tmpl = builtin_templates()["tmpl.target_over_time"]
print(tmpl.bindings)  # x="dim:time", y="role:target", color="dim:geo" - no variable names
chart = render_template(tmpl, weekly)  # the schema is inferred; roles come from attrs
one_market = render_template(tmpl, weekly.sel(geo="DE", drop=True), optional=["color"])

Inside a template spec, {"$bind": "y"} becomes a Vega-Lite field definition and "{{y}}" (also {{y.field}}, {{y.type}}, {{y.title}}) is replaced by the bound name. Binding kinds are dim:, role:, var:, coord: and stat: (a summary statistic such as stat:hdi_90_lower). The JSON-only half, mapi_plots.templates.apply_template, runs in the API to check that a saved template applies to a model before anything is rendered.

docs.title: What the sanitizer allows
docs.text:
Plots run in an isolated iframe on a separate origin, but the server checks every plot first:

Rejected Why url data (anywhere, including lookups and topojson) data must be referenced by name; no fetching href encodings and mark properties no navigation out of the plot image marks, url channels, layout.images / image traces with non-data: sources no external fetches (only base64 PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP) Tile-map traces and subplots (scattermap, choroplethmap, densitymap, layout.map) tiles come from third-party servers; use scattergeo/choropleth __proto__, constructor, prototype keys or field paths prototype pollution javascript:, data:text/html, SVG data URIs, CSS url() in any string script and fetch vectors Vega expressions outside a small allow-list of functions, method calls, window/document/fetch, computed member names expression sandbox escapes Custom format types, Plotly network options (topojsonURL, showLink, ...) code and network hooks Anything that does not match the pinned Vega-Lite v6.4.1 / plotly.js 4.1.1 schemas unknown keys are where exploits hide

Plotly text keeps only <b>, <i>, <br>, <sub> and <sup> (plus <extra> in hover templates); everything else is stripped and reported as a change. The server never decodes Arrow, so text that from_plotly moves into a dataset (text, hovertext, category labels) is stripped and scanned on the sandbox side during conversion; the plot iframe must still treat dataset strings as untrusted and re-strip them before handing them to plotly.js. Vega renders dataset strings as text (and the iframe's tooltip handler escapes them). Method args of Plotly buttons and sliders are checked in both the {attr: value} and positional [attr, value] forms, and usermeta.embedOptions is rejected in Vega-Lite specs. Specs are capped in size, depth, node count and string length. See the plots reference for the full rule list and error codes.

from mapi_plots import check_plot, sanitize_plot
from mapi_plots.sanitize import SanitizeError

hostile = {
    "id": "evil.chart",
    "title": "Totally normal chart",
    "kind": "vega-lite",
    "spec": {
        "data": {"url": "https://attacker.example/steal.json"},  # fetches are not allowed
        "mark": "point",
        "encoding": {"href": {"field": "link"}},  # neither is navigation
    },
}
try:
    sanitize_plot(hostile)
except SanitizeError as err:
    print(err.code, sorted(rule.value for rule in err.rules))  # PLOT_UNSAFE ['href', 'url_data']

for issue in check_plot(hostile):  # editor-friendly: every problem, never raises
    print(issue.pointer, "-", issue.message)
# /spec/data/url - data must be referenced by dataset name, never by URL
# /spec/encoding/href - href links are not allowed in plots
# /spec/$schema - added $schema

docs.title: Write a step or a model plugin
docs.text: A plugin author writes very little: a step implements fit/transform (and inverse when it can); a model implements fit/score. The platform owns everything around them — binding, splits, context tails, coordinates, inverse transforms, summaries and bundles. The contract kit tells you, before anyone else runs your code, whether you followed the rules.

docs.title: A preprocessing step
docs.text:
from typing import ClassVar

from mapi_sdk import Step, StepContext, StepSettings, StepState
from mapi_spec import StepKind
from pydantic import Field, JsonValue


class ScaleSettings(StepSettings):
    vars: list[str]
    over: list[str] = Field(default=[])  # plain defaults: the exported JSON Schema keeps them
    unseen_levels: str = "error"  # error | pooled | fill: what a new level's scale becomes
    fill_value: float = 1.0  # the scale used by 'fill'


class ScaleStep(Step[ScaleSettings, StepState]):
    """Divide each variable by its mean absolute value over `over` (learned on train)."""

    id = "acme.scale"
    version = "1.0.0"
    kind = StepKind.VALUE
    Settings = ScaleSettings
    State = StepState  # stateful: fitted on the training data only
    invertible = True
    var_params = ("vars",)  # settings that name variables ...
    dim_params = ("over",)  # ... and dims, so the control plane can check them
    unseen_levels_param = "unseen_levels"
    effect_template: ClassVar[dict[str, JsonValue]] = {  # static: how the schema changes
        "template_params": ["vars"],
        "updates": {"{*vars as v}": {"units": "1"}},
    }
    summary = "Divide by the mean absolute value over the named dims"  # catalog and UI text
    summary_plain = "Puts each series on a comparable scale"

    def fit(self, ds: xr.Dataset, s: ScaleSettings, ctx: StepContext) -> StepState:
        return StepState(arrays=xr.Dataset({f"scale__{v}": abs(ds[v]).mean(s.over) for v in s.vars}))

    def _scale(self, v: str, ds: xr.Dataset, s: ScaleSettings, st: StepState, ctx: StepContext):
        state = st.array(f"scale__{v}")
        return ctx.align_state(state, ds, s.unseen_levels, fill_value=s.fill_value)

    def transform(self, ds, s, st, ctx):  # never learns; skips absent vars (the target at score)
        return ds.assign({v: ds[v] / self._scale(v, ds, s, st, ctx) for v in s.vars if v in ds})

    def inverse(self, ds, s, st, ctx):
        return ds.assign({v: ds[v] * self._scale(v, ds, s, st, ctx) for v in s.vars if v in ds})

The rules:

  • transform never learns. transform(train, fit(train)) must equal the fit-time output, and a subset of the data must transform to the same subset of the output.
  • Reductions name the dims they reduce over; state stays labelled by the rest.
  • Steps that look back (lags, rolling windows) declare context_template ({"along": "{along}", "n": "{max:lags}", "within": "{within}"}). The platform stores the last n rows per group at the step's input and prepends them at score time.
  • Unseen levels go through ctx.align_state(state, ds, policy).
  • effect_template must describe the real output schema — the control plane validates specs with it and never imports your code.

docs.title: A model
docs.text:
from mapi_sdk import PREDICTIONS, CustomModel, FitOutput, ModelSettings, new_level_mask
from mapi_spec import Capabilities, DataSchema, Representation


class BaselineSettings(ModelSettings):
    ridge: float = 1e-6


class GeoBaseline(CustomModel[BaselineSettings]):
    """y = intercept[geo] + beta * spend, by least squares (point predictions)."""

    id = "acme.geo_baseline"
    version = "1.0.0"
    Settings = BaselineSettings
    capabilities = Capabilities(
        inference="point",
        representation=Representation.POINT,
        score_modes=frozenset({"predict", "forecast", "evaluate"}),
    )
    # the data contract the model needs, in canonical names (a DataSchema, or a
    # DataSchemaTemplate whose names come from settings)
    schema_template = DataSchema.model_validate(
        {
            "dims": {
                "geo": {"kind": "categorical", "policy": "new_levels", "new_level_strategy": "pooled"},
                "time": {"kind": "time", "policy": "extend"},
            },
            "vars": {
                "y": {"dims": ["geo", "time"], "dtype": "float64", "role": "target"},
                "spend": {"dims": ["geo", "time"], "dtype": "float64", "role": "covariate"},
            },
        }
    )
    outputs: ClassVar[dict] = {"y_hat": {"dims": ["geo", "time"], "units_of": "y"}}
    pad_extend = False  # time is not indexed by position

    def fit(self, ds, s, cfg, ctx):
        g, t = ds.sizes["geo"], ds.sizes["time"]
        x = np.concatenate(
            [np.repeat(np.eye(g), t, axis=0), ds["spend"].values.reshape(-1, 1)], axis=1
        )
        coef = np.linalg.solve(x.T @ x + s.ridge * np.eye(g + 1), x.T @ ds["y"].values.ravel())
        params = xr.Dataset(
            {"intercept": ("geo", coef[:g]), "beta": coef[g]}, coords={"geo": ds["geo"].values}
        )
        return FitOutput(groups={"params": params})

    def score(self, fitted, ds, req, ctx):
        # `ds` arrives canonicalised: fit order, unseen geos appended and flagged
        p = fitted.group("params")
        new = new_level_mask(ds, "geo")
        known = p["intercept"].reindex(geo=ds["geo"].values)
        pooled = 0.0 if ctx.strategy("geo") == "zero" else float(p["intercept"].mean())
        intercept = xr.where(new, pooled, known.fillna(pooled))
        y_hat = (intercept + p["beta"] * ds["spend"]).transpose("geo", "time")
        return xr.DataTree.from_dict({PREDICTIONS: xr.Dataset({"y_hat": y_hat})})

outputs lists every variable score returns with its dims (representation dims such as chain/draw or quantile may be left out). When the data dims depend on settings, add "dims_of": "y": the output then also carries every dim of that input variable in the resolved schema (for example the sklearn models' settings.rows).

FitOutput.native is for safe native formats only (skops, xgboost JSON, safetensors). Pickle is rejected when a bundle is written and when it is read.

docs.title: Run the contract kit
docs.text:
mapi-sdk installs a pytest plugin, so the fixtures are available in any test suite:

import pytest
from mapi_sdk.testing import ModelFixture, toy  # toy: small reference steps and models


@pytest.mark.mapi_contract
def test_step_follows_the_contract(mapi_check_step, mapi_panel):
    data, _fx = mapi_panel  # a daily market x channel panel and its FX side table
    report = mapi_check_step(
        toy.ScaleStep, data, {"vars": ["spend_local"], "over": ["date"], "unseen_levels": "pooled"}
    )
    assert report.ok, report.summary()


SPEC = """
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: toy, project: demo}
data:
  dataset: dataset://demo/panel@latest
  bind: {dims: {geo: market, time: date}, vars: {y: revenue_local, spend: spend_local}}
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: time, last: 14}
model: {use: toy.linear@^1, fit: {seed: 1}}
evaluate: {metrics: [rmse]}
"""


@pytest.mark.mapi_contract
def test_model_follows_the_contract(mapi_check_model, mapi_panel, mapi_toy_registry):
    data, _fx = mapi_panel
    fixture = ModelFixture(spec=SPEC, data=data, registry=mapi_toy_registry)
    report = mapi_check_model(toy.LinearModel, fixture)  # raises ContractViolation on failure
    assert report.ok

check_step checks the exported catalog entry, deterministic fitting, a pure and deterministic transform, that transform never learns, the state's bundle round trip, that the declared schema effect matches the real output, that a missing target is tolerated, the inverse round trip, context-window equivalence and every unseen-level policy.

check_model fits the fixture and checks the bundle round trip (and that it has no pickle), shuffled and subset scoring, new-level policies, the typed errors of every dim policy (gaps and out-of-range coordinates on datetime and integer extend dims, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT past max_extension, MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE for a forecast without a future-required variable, RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED for a horizon longer than a target lag), unsupported modes, context-window equivalence, that the evaluation metrics are reproduced by the score path, output units (including outputs that inherit the target's units), that every returned prediction is declared in outputs with matching dims, legal aggregation, additive contributions, seed determinism, that the manifest's plots render and pass the sanitizer, and — when the manifest declares fast_score — that fast scoring matches exact scoring within MCSE. That last check calls the plugin's check_fast_score(fitted, ds, *, seed) hook; PyMCModel provides it.

A failed check raises ContractViolation with a readable report:

contract kit: step acme.scale@1.0.0
  [PASS] catalog_entry: exported acme.scale@1.0.0
  [FAIL] transform_never_learns: AssertionError: ...

mapi_sdk.testing.toy holds small, real reference implementations (scale, log1p, lag, resample, Fourier, FX steps; point, draws and quantile models) to copy from.

docs.title: Port a model in 15 minutes
docs.text:
You have a model that works in a notebook. This guide turns it into a plugin that the platform can fit, score on new data, forecast, version and plot, and proves it with the contract kit. You write the statistics; the platform writes everything around them.

flowchart LR
    A["0–3 min<br/><b>Pick a base class</b>"] --> B["3–6 min<br/><b>Declare the data contract</b>"]
    B --> C["6–11 min<br/><b>Write build / estimator / fit+score</b>"]
    C --> D["11–13 min<br/><b>Write a tiny spec</b>"]
    D --> E["13–15 min<br/><b>Run the contract kit</b>"]

docs.title: What you write, what you get
docs.text:
You write The platform does PyMCModel build(ds, settings, ctx) -> pm.Model Engines (nutpie, PyMC with resumable segments, MAP, ADVI), convergence diagnostics, rebuild-and-predict scoring, new levels from the hyperprior, common-random-number counterfactuals, fast scoring SklearnModel estimator(settings) Stacking labelled dims into rows and features, coordinate features, safe persistence (skops / xgboost JSON), quantile / bootstrap / conformal uncertainty, pooled new levels, contributions CustomModel fit(...) and score(...) Binding, preprocessing, splits, context tails, coordinate canonicalisation, inverse transforms, summaries, bundles

All three get, for free: validated settings with JSON Schemas, static spec validation, evaluate-then-refit, CoordPlan checks, representation-aware summaries, plots and bundles.

docs.title: 1. Pick a base class (0–3 min)
docs.text:
• Your model is a PyMC model → mapi_pymc.PyMCModel.
  • Your model is an sklearn or xgboost estimator on a design matrix → mapi_sklearn.SklearnModel (or the quantile, bootstrap, conformal or classifier variants).
  • Anything else (statsmodels, JAX, a Kalman filter, closed-form maths) → mapi_sdk.CustomModel.

docs.title: 2. Declare the data contract (3–6 min)
docs.text:
Write down, in canonical names, the dims and variables your model needs and what may happen to each dim at score time. This is the model's schema_template. Users bind their own dataset names onto it in the spec.

Three questions per dim

Can a score request bring a new level (a new county, store, market)? Then new_levels, with a strategy. Does it grow at forecast time (time, observations)? Then extend. Otherwise fixed.

docs.title: 3. Write the model (6–11 min)
docs.text:
PyMCscikit-learn / xgboostCustom 
from typing import Any, ClassVar

import pymc as pm
import xarray as xr
from mapi_pymc import BuildContext, PyMCModel
from mapi_pymc.examples import RADON_SCHEMA  # dims obs (extend) + county (new_levels)
from mapi_sdk import ModelSettings
from mapi_spec import Capabilities, Representation
from pydantic import Field


class RadonSettings(ModelSettings):
    beta_sigma: float = Field(1.0, gt=0)


class Radon(PyMCModel[RadonSettings]):
    """log radon ~ Normal(a[county] + b * floor, sigma), with partially pooled a."""

    id = "acme.radon"
    version = "1.0.0"
    Settings = RadonSettings
    capabilities = Capabilities(
        inference="mcmc",
        representation=Representation.DRAWS,
        score_modes=frozenset({"predict", "counterfactual", "evaluate"}),
    )
    schema_template = RADON_SCHEMA
    outputs: ClassVar[dict[str, Any]] = {"y": {"dims": ["obs"], "units_of": "y"}}
    expected: ClassVar[dict[str, str]] = {"y": "mu"}  # output -> Deterministic for E[y]
    pad_extend = False  # long layout: no positional time axis

    def build(self, ds: xr.Dataset, s: RadonSettings, ctx: BuildContext) -> pm.Model:
        with pm.Model(coords=ctx.coords()) as model:
            floor = ctx.data("floor")
            county = ctx.data("county_idx")
            a = ctx.hier_effect("a", "county")  # new counties come from the hyperprior
            b = pm.Normal("b", 0.0, s.beta_sigma)
            mu = pm.Deterministic("mu", a[county] + b * floor, dims="obs")
            sigma = pm.HalfNormal("sigma", 1.0)
            pm.Normal("y", mu, sigma, observed=ctx.observed("y"), dims="obs")
        return model

The ctx helpers are what make scoring work without you thinking about it:

Helper Why you use it ctx.coords() The model's coords; at score time includes new levels ctx.data(name) A pm.Data over the training values at fit and the score values at score time (the model is rebuilt) ctx.observed(name) The target at fit; a placeholder at score time (never imputed) ctx.hier_effect(name, dim) A partially pooled effect whose new levels are drawn from the hyperprior per posterior draw ctx.position(dim) 0, 1, 2, … along an extend dim, continued into the forecast horizon

expected names the Deterministic that is the expected value of each output, so output.kind: expected returns it without observation noise.

from typing import ClassVar

from mapi_sklearn import PointSettings, SklearnModel, capabilities_for
from mapi_spec import Capabilities
from sklearn.linear_model import Ridge


class LinearDemand(SklearnModel[PointSettings]):
    id = "t.acme.linear_demand"
    version = "1.0.0"
    capabilities: ClassVar[Capabilities] = capabilities_for("none").model_copy(
        update={"contribution_scale": "additive"}  # a linear model decomposes exactly
    )

    def estimator(self, s: PointSettings) -> Ridge:
        return Ridge(alpha=0.5)  # must be exactly an allow-listed class

estimator() returns an allow-listed estimator instance (or a {kind, params} mapping). Subclasses and parameters outside the estimator's params model are rejected, so the bundle can always be loaded safely. Rows, columns and coordinate features are settings, not code: see Tabular models.

from mapi_sdk import PREDICTIONS, CustomModel, FitOutput, ModelSettings, new_level_mask
from mapi_spec import Capabilities, DataSchema, Representation


class BaselineSettings(ModelSettings):
    ridge: float = 1e-6


class GeoBaseline(CustomModel[BaselineSettings]):
    """y = intercept[geo] + beta * spend, by least squares (point predictions)."""

    id = "acme.geo_baseline"
    version = "1.0.0"
    Settings = BaselineSettings
    capabilities = Capabilities(
        inference="point",
        representation=Representation.POINT,
        score_modes=frozenset({"predict", "forecast", "evaluate"}),
    )
    # the data contract the model needs, in canonical names (a DataSchema, or a
    # DataSchemaTemplate whose names come from settings)
    schema_template = DataSchema.model_validate(
        {
            "dims": {
                "geo": {"kind": "categorical", "policy": "new_levels", "new_level_strategy": "pooled"},
                "time": {"kind": "time", "policy": "extend"},
            },
            "vars": {
                "y": {"dims": ["geo", "time"], "dtype": "float64", "role": "target"},
                "spend": {"dims": ["geo", "time"], "dtype": "float64", "role": "covariate"},
            },
        }
    )
    outputs: ClassVar[dict] = {"y_hat": {"dims": ["geo", "time"], "units_of": "y"}}
    pad_extend = False  # time is not indexed by position

    def fit(self, ds, s, cfg, ctx):
        g, t = ds.sizes["geo"], ds.sizes["time"]
        x = np.concatenate(
            [np.repeat(np.eye(g), t, axis=0), ds["spend"].values.reshape(-1, 1)], axis=1
        )
        coef = np.linalg.solve(x.T @ x + s.ridge * np.eye(g + 1), x.T @ ds["y"].values.ravel())
        params = xr.Dataset(
            {"intercept": ("geo", coef[:g]), "beta": coef[g]}, coords={"geo": ds["geo"].values}
        )
        return FitOutput(groups={"params": params})

    def score(self, fitted, ds, req, ctx):
        # `ds` arrives canonicalised: fit order, unseen geos appended and flagged
        p = fitted.group("params")
        new = new_level_mask(ds, "geo")
        known = p["intercept"].reindex(geo=ds["geo"].values)
        pooled = 0.0 if ctx.strategy("geo") == "zero" else float(p["intercept"].mean())
        intercept = xr.where(new, pooled, known.fillna(pooled))
        y_hat = (intercept + p["beta"] * ds["spend"]).transpose("geo", "time")
        return xr.DataTree.from_dict({PREDICTIONS: xr.Dataset({"y_hat": y_hat})})

The rules for score:

  • the dataset arrives canonicalised: fit order, new levels appended and flagged by <dim>__is_new (new_level_mask(ds, dim)), so position-indexed parameters line up;
  • return an xr.DataTree with a predictions group in your declared representation;
  • never look at targets in the payload (evaluate mode passes them for metrics, not for you).

FitOutput.groups uses ArviZ group names (posterior, sample_stats, …), learned holds small JSON, and native holds bytes in a safe format only (skops, xgboost JSON, safetensors). Pickle is rejected.

docs.title: 4. Write a tiny spec (11–13 min)
docs.text:
The spec the contract kit fits. Keep it small and fast: few draws, few trees.

PyMCCustom (with a step) 
from mapi_pymc.examples import radon_dataset
from mapi_sdk import Registry
from mapi_sdk.testing import ModelFixture, check_model

SPEC = """
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: radon, project: demo}
data: {dataset: dataset://demo/radon@latest}
model:
  use: acme.radon@^1
  fit: {mode: train_only, engine: pymc, tune: 100, draws: 100, chains: 2, seed: 3}
"""
report = check_model(
    Radon, ModelFixture(spec=SPEC, data=radon_dataset(), raw_schema=RADON_SCHEMA, registry=Registry())
)
print(report.summary())

from mapi_sdk import default_registry
from mapi_sdk.testing import ModelFixture, check_model

registry = default_registry().copy()
registry.register(ScaleStep)  # the model is registered by check_model itself

SPEC = """
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: acme-baseline, project: demo}
data:
  dataset: dataset://demo/sales@latest
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: time, last: 6}
pipeline:
  - {id: scale, use: acme.scale@^1, with: {vars: [spend], over: [time], unseen_levels: pooled}}
model:
  use: acme.geo_baseline@^1
  fit: {seed: 1}
evaluate: {metrics: [rmse, mape]}
"""
raw_schema = infer_schema(data, targets=["y"], policies={"geo": "new_levels"})
report = check_model(
    GeoBaseline,
    ModelFixture(spec=SPEC, data=data, raw_schema=raw_schema, registry=registry),
)
print(report.summary())
# contract kit: model acme.geo_baseline@1.0.0
#   [PASS] fit: ...
#   [PASS] bundle_roundtrip_no_pickle: ...
#   [PASS] shuffled_scoring: ...
#   ...

docs.title: 5. Run the contract kit (13–15 min)
docs.text:
check_model fits your fixture and then tries to break your plugin the way real users will:

contract kit: model acme.geo_baseline@1.0.0
  [PASS] manifest: acme.geo_baseline@1.0.0 (point)
  [PASS] fit: bundle ef4100375dbb, metrics ['mape', 'rmse']
  [PASS] bundle_roundtrip_no_pickle: scores match after write/read
  [PASS] shuffled_scoring: shuffled ['geo']
  [PASS] subset_scoring: subset of 'geo'
  [PASS] new_level_policies: geo: new level scored (pooled)
  [PASS] extend_typed_errors: raised NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION; raised COORD_NOT_ALLOWED
  [PASS] unsupported_mode: raised MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED
  [PASS] context_window_equivalence: holdout via stored context == in-sample full series
  [PASS] evaluate_path_equals_score_path: metrics ['rmse', 'mape'] reproduced through the score path
  [PASS] output_space_and_units: y_hat in raw (None)
  [PASS] representation_aggregation: point aggregation over 'geo' allowed
  [SKIP] additive_contributions: contribution_scale is not additive
  [PASS] seed_determinism: same seed, same fit and scores
Check What it proves bundle_roundtrip_no_pickle Scores are identical after writing and reading the bundle, and nothing in it is pickle shuffled_scoring, subset_scoring Reordered labels and subsets give the same answers for the same cells new_level_policies Every strategy your dims declare works (or raises UNSEEN_LEVELS when it should) extend_typed_errors Gaps and out-of-range time labels raise typed errors unsupported_mode Undeclared modes are refused context_window_equivalence Scoring the last training periods as a forecast equals the in-sample result evaluate_path_equals_score_path The holdout metrics are reproduced through the normal score path output_space_and_units Outputs are inverted and labelled with units and output space representation_aggregation Aggregations are allowed or refused according to the representation additive_contributions Declared-additive contributions sum to the prediction seed_determinism The same seed gives the same fit and scores, when the plugin claims it

A failed check raises ContractViolation with the report (pass raise_on_failure=False to get the report instead).
