docs.title: Bonus: a preprocessing step
docs.text:
Steps follow the same pattern: settings, an optional state, fit / transform / inverse, and a static effect_template that tells the control plane how the schema changes.

from typing import ClassVar

from mapi_sdk import Step, StepContext, StepSettings, StepState
from mapi_spec import StepKind
from pydantic import Field, JsonValue


class ScaleSettings(StepSettings):
    vars: list[str]
    over: list[str] = Field(default=[])  # plain defaults: the exported JSON Schema keeps them
    unseen_levels: str = "error"  # error | pooled | fill: what a new level's scale becomes
    fill_value: float = 1.0  # the scale used by 'fill'


class ScaleStep(Step[ScaleSettings, StepState]):
    """Divide each variable by its mean absolute value over `over` (learned on train)."""

    id = "acme.scale"
    version = "1.0.0"
    kind = StepKind.VALUE
    Settings = ScaleSettings
    State = StepState  # stateful: fitted on the training data only
    invertible = True
    var_params = ("vars",)  # settings that name variables ...
    dim_params = ("over",)  # ... and dims, so the control plane can check them
    unseen_levels_param = "unseen_levels"
    effect_template: ClassVar[dict[str, JsonValue]] = {  # static: how the schema changes
        "template_params": ["vars"],
        "updates": {"{*vars as v}": {"units": "1"}},
    }
    summary = "Divide by the mean absolute value over the named dims"  # catalog and UI text
    summary_plain = "Puts each series on a comparable scale"

    def fit(self, ds: xr.Dataset, s: ScaleSettings, ctx: StepContext) -> StepState:
        return StepState(arrays=xr.Dataset({f"scale__{v}": abs(ds[v]).mean(s.over) for v in s.vars}))

    def _scale(self, v: str, ds: xr.Dataset, s: ScaleSettings, st: StepState, ctx: StepContext):
        state = st.array(f"scale__{v}")
        return ctx.align_state(state, ds, s.unseen_levels, fill_value=s.fill_value)

    def transform(self, ds, s, st, ctx):  # never learns; skips absent vars (the target at score)
        return ds.assign({v: ds[v] / self._scale(v, ds, s, st, ctx) for v in s.vars if v in ds})

    def inverse(self, ds, s, st, ctx):
        return ds.assign({v: ds[v] * self._scale(v, ds, s, st, ctx) for v in s.vars if v in ds})

from mapi_sdk import infer_schema
from mapi_sdk.testing import check_step

report = check_step(
    ScaleStep,
    data,
    {"vars": ["spend"], "over": ["time"], "unseen_levels": "pooled"},
    schema=infer_schema(data, targets=["y"]),
)
print(report.summary())
# contract kit: step acme.scale@1.0.0
#   [PASS] catalog_entry: exported acme.scale@1.0.0
#   [PASS] transform_never_learns: ...
#   ...

The step kit checks the exported catalog entry, deterministic and pure fitting, that transform never learns, the state's bundle round trip, that the declared schema effect matches the real output, that a missing target is tolerated, the inverse round trip, context-window equivalence for look-back steps, and every unseen-level policy. More in Write a step or model plugin.

docs.title: Ship it
docs.text:
Register your plugins through entry points in your package's pyproject.toml; the value may be a class, a tuple of classes or a function that returns them:

[project.entry-points."mapi.models"]
acme = "acme_models.plugins:PLUGINS"      # PLUGINS = (Radon, GeoBaseline)

[project.entry-points."mapi.steps"]
acme = "acme_models.steps:STEPS"          # STEPS = (ScaleStep,)

mapi_sdk.default_registry() then finds them, and so will the platform's runner images.

Checklist

  • schema_template in canonical names, with honest dim policies
  • capabilities: representation, score modes, contribution scale
  • outputs with units_of, so results come back in the user's units
  • settings as a ModelSettings subclass with defaults and descriptions (they become the form in the UI)
  • a tiny spec and check_model passing in CI
  • no pickle: native artifacts as skops, xgboost JSON or safetensors

See the full worked guides: PyMC, scikit-learn and xgboost, steps and custom models.

docs.title: Bring a PyMC model
docs.text: With mapi_pymc.PyMCModel you write one method, build(), that returns a pm.Model. The platform fits it with the engine named in the spec, keeps the ArviZ groups you ask for, turns convergence checks into scorecard items, and predicts by rebuilding your model on new data: new geos, forecast horizons, counterfactual scenarios. You never handle coordinates, pm.set_data or posterior bookkeeping yourself.

docs.title: A hierarchical model in 30 lines
docs.text:
This is the classic radon model (varying intercepts by county) in long layout. obs rows carry a county_idx that points into the county coordinate.

from typing import Any, ClassVar

import pymc as pm
import xarray as xr
from mapi_pymc import BuildContext, PyMCModel
from mapi_pymc.examples import RADON_SCHEMA  # dims obs (extend) + county (new_levels)
from mapi_sdk import ModelSettings
from mapi_spec import Capabilities, Representation
from pydantic import Field


class RadonSettings(ModelSettings):
    beta_sigma: float = Field(1.0, gt=0)


class Radon(PyMCModel[RadonSettings]):
    """log radon ~ Normal(a[county] + b * floor, sigma), with partially pooled a."""

    id = "acme.radon"
    version = "1.0.0"
    Settings = RadonSettings
    capabilities = Capabilities(
        inference="mcmc",
        representation=Representation.DRAWS,
        score_modes=frozenset({"predict", "counterfactual", "evaluate"}),
    )
    schema_template = RADON_SCHEMA
    outputs: ClassVar[dict[str, Any]] = {"y": {"dims": ["obs"], "units_of": "y"}}
    expected: ClassVar[dict[str, str]] = {"y": "mu"}  # output -> Deterministic for E[y]
    pad_extend = False  # long layout: no positional time axis

    def build(self, ds: xr.Dataset, s: RadonSettings, ctx: BuildContext) -> pm.Model:
        with pm.Model(coords=ctx.coords()) as model:
            floor = ctx.data("floor")
            county = ctx.data("county_idx")
            a = ctx.hier_effect("a", "county")  # new counties come from the hyperprior
            b = pm.Normal("b", 0.0, s.beta_sigma)
            mu = pm.Deterministic("mu", a[county] + b * floor, dims="obs")
            sigma = pm.HalfNormal("sigma", 1.0)
            pm.Normal("y", mu, sigma, observed=ctx.observed("y"), dims="obs")
        return model

A runnable version, with synthetic data, ships as mapi_pymc.examples.RadonModel.

docs.title: What the ctx helpers do
docs.text:
Helper At fit At score ctx.coords() the data's labels adds <dim>__fit and <dim>__new when unseen levels arrive ctx.data(name) pm.Data over the training values pm.Data over the score values (the model is rebuilt) ctx.observed(name) the target a zero placeholder of the right shape (never imputed) ctx.hier_effect(name, dim) name ~ Normal(mu, sigma) over dim (non-centred by default) fit levels from the posterior, then name__new for unseen levels ctx.position(dim) 0, 1, 2, … along an extend dim the same positions continued into the horizon ctx.anticipated_coords fit labels plus max_extension future labels the same

New levels follow the dim's new_level_strategy:

  • hyperprior: every posterior draw gets a fresh level mu + sigma * z from the fitted hyperprior. The noise z is frozen per seed, so scoring twice returns the same answer.
  • pooled: the population mean mu.
  • zero: 0.
  • error: the request is rejected with UNSEEN_LEVELS.

If your model indexes a plain parameter by a new_levels dim (pm.Normal("a", dims="county")), scoring a new county fails with a clear UNSEEN_LEVELS error that points you at ctx.hier_effect.

docs.title: Choosing an engine
docs.text:
Set model.fit.engine in the spec:

Engine What you get nutpie (default) Fast NUTS with parallel chains. It is not bit-for-bit reproducible from a seed. pymc PyMC's NUTS, reproducible from a seed, with segmented sampling. map pm.find_MAP: one point (1 chain, 1 draw). advi Mean-field ADVI. tune is the number of optimisation steps (default 10,000). pathfinder Pathfinder from pymc-extras, when installed in the image. numpyro, blackjax PyMC's JAX bridges, when installed in the image. 
model:
  use: acme.radon@^1
  fit:
    engine: pymc
    tune: 1000
    draws: 2000
    chains: 4
    seed: 20261014
    checkpoint: {every_draws: 500}      # segmented sampling
    keep: {log_likelihood: true, posterior_predictive: {thin: 4}}
    prior_predictive: {draws: 500}

The opt-in groups are:

  • prior and prior_predictive (prior_predictive: {draws: N});
  • log_likelihood, which LOO and WAIC need;
  • a thinned posterior_predictive.

The bundle always holds posterior, sample_stats, observed_data and constant_data.

docs.title: Segmented sampling and checkpoints
docs.text:
With engine: pymc and checkpoint.every_draws, the sampler tunes once and then draws in chunks. After each chunk it writes a checkpoint with three things:

  • the draws so far;
  • every chain's position;
  • the full sampler state (step size, mass matrix and random state), encoded as JSON, never pickled.

If a run is interrupted and retried, it resumes where the last chunk ended. The result is identical to an uninterrupted run.

nutpie cannot export its adaptation state, so its checkpoints are snapshots. They hold the draws so far, which is enough for a partial result, but a retry starts sampling again.

Every engine reports progress for each chain ("chain 2/4: sampling 150/500, 0 divergences").

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
Each MCMC fit adds these items to the sanity scorecard, each with an expert message, a plain-language message and a suggested action:

  • RHAT: rank-normalised split r̂ below 1.01;
  • ESS_BULK and ESS_TAIL: at least 100 effective draws per chain;
  • DIVERGENCES;
  • TREE_DEPTH.

docs.title: Expected vs predictive, and counterfactuals
docs.text:
output.kind: expected returns the Deterministic you named in expected (no observation noise). output.kind: predictive returns draws of the observed variable.

Predictive draws use common random numbers: y = F⁻¹(U) with uniforms U frozen by the seed and the cell. In a counterfactual (mode: counterfactual with interventions), the scenario and the baseline therefore share their noise. The delta then reflects only the intervention, not two independent noise draws. Distributions without an inverse CDF (Poisson, negative binomial) fall back to the seeded sampler stream, and the output's noise attribute records which method was used.

docs.title: Fast scoring with a FrozenPredictor
docs.text:
Declare a FrozenPredictorSpec and the platform can compile one PyTensor function that evaluates your responses for many inputs and scenarios at once. Use it for response curves and what-if grids:

import numpy as np
import xarray as xr
from mapi_pymc.examples import RADON_SCHEMA, RADON_SPEC_YAML, RadonModel, radon_dataset
from mapi_pymc.testing import check_fast_score
from mapi_sdk import Registry, fit_spec

registry = Registry()
registry.register(RadonModel)  # declares fast_score_spec = FrozenPredictorSpec(
#                                  response_exprs={"y": "mu"}, input_vars=["floor"])
data = radon_dataset()
bundle = fit_spec(RADON_SPEC_YAML, data, registry=registry, raw_schema=RADON_SCHEMA)

model = RadonModel()
predictor = model.frozen_predictor(bundle.model, data, num_samples=200, seed=1)
floors = xr.DataArray(
    np.outer([0.0, 0.5, 1.0], np.ones(data.sizes["obs"])),
    dims=["scenario", "obs"],
    coords={"scenario": ["basement", "mixed", "ground floor"]},
)
grid = predictor.predict({"floor": floors})  # one compiled call for every scenario
print(grid["y"].dims)  # ('sample', 'scenario', 'obs')

report = check_fast_score(model, bundle.model, data)  # fast path == exact path within MCSE
print(report.ok)  # True

The contract check mapi_pymc.testing.check_fast_score(plugin, fitted, ds) confirms that the fast path agrees with exact scoring within Monte Carlo error.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
Use the SDK contract kit:

from mapi_pymc.examples import radon_dataset
from mapi_sdk import Registry
from mapi_sdk.testing import ModelFixture, check_model

SPEC = """
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: radon, project: demo}
data: {dataset: dataset://demo/radon@latest}
model:
  use: acme.radon@^1
  fit: {mode: train_only, engine: pymc, tune: 100, draws: 100, chains: 2, seed: 3}
"""
report = check_model(
    Radon, ModelFixture(spec=SPEC, data=radon_dataset(), raw_schema=RADON_SCHEMA, registry=Registry())
)
print(report.summary())

Keep test fits tiny (tune: 100, draws: 100, chains: 2, engine: pymc) so they are fast and reproducible.

docs.title: The Python client v0.2
docs.text:
mapi-client (mapi_client, Apache-2.0) is a typed client for the /v1 HTTP API, built on httpx. Every request and response is a Pydantic model from mapi_spec.api, the same models the server uses, so a typo in a field name fails in your editor, not in production. Errors come back as mapi_spec.errors.MapiError subclasses with the server's stable error code.

It is the client the mapi CLI, make seed and the end-to-end tests use. This page walks through one script, docs/snippets/client_tour.py, which make e2e runs against a live stack; the outputs shown come from running it (shortened in places).

uv add mapi-client              # or, for xr.Dataset uploads and xr.DataTree results:
uv add "mapi-client[xarray]"

In the workspace both are already installed. The examples need a running stack and the demo files: make dev, then uv run python scripts/seed.py --export demo/.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
from mapi_client import Client

api = Client()  # MAPI_URL / MAPI_API_URL, a profile, or http://127.0.0.1:8000
health = api.ready()
print(api.config.base_url, health.status, health.version)

http://127.0.0.1:8000 ok 0.2.0

Client() resolves its settings like the CLI: arguments (Client("http://…", token=…)), then MAPI_URL (or MAPI_API_URL), MAPI_TOKEN and MAPI_PROFILE, then a profile in ~/.config/mapi/config.toml, then http://127.0.0.1:8000. api.config.sources says where each value came from. Use the client as a context manager (with Client() as api:) or call close().

docs.title: Upload data
docs.text:
versions = {}
for name in ("eu_media_daily", "fx_daily", "holidays_eu", "eu_media_future"):
    versions[name] = api.datasets.upload(f"demo/{name}.zarr.zip", dataset=name)
    print(versions[name].ref, versions[name].status.value, versions[name].sha256[:19])

dataset://default/eu_media_daily@v2 ready sha256:0073129ba8ee
dataset://default/fx_daily@v2 ready sha256:7f27db4a2ac4
dataset://default/holidays_eu@v2 ready sha256:11abf028d5f5
dataset://default/eu_media_future@v2 ready sha256:2db88e1af79d

datasets.upload does the whole dance: it creates the dataset if the name is new, opens an upload session, PUTs the bytes to the signed URL (without sending your API credentials there), starts the sandboxed ingest run with a fresh idempotency key, and waits until the version is ready, raising the ingest's error if it fails. It accepts a path, bytes, or an xr.Dataset (with the xarray extra). CSV and Parquet files need a mapping=IngestMapping(…); zarr zips and netCDF files describe themselves.

The version carries the schema the ingest run checked:

schema = versions["eu_media_daily"].data_schema  # the DataSchema the ingest run checked
print({dim: spec.policy.value for dim, spec in schema.dims.items()})
print({var: spec.role.value for var, spec in schema.vars.items()})

{'date': 'extend', 'market': 'new_levels', 'channel': 'fixed'}
{'spend_local': 'spend', 'revenue_local': 'target'}

docs.title: Validate a spec
docs.text:
with open("demo/eu-geo-mmm.yaml", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    spec_yaml = fh.read()

check = api.specs.validate(spec_yaml)
print("valid" if check.valid else [(i.code, i.pointer) for i in check.issues])
for stage in check.stages:  # the schema after every pipeline step, and where the split is
    if stage.data_schema is not None:
        print(stage.name, sorted(stage.data_schema.dims), "<- split" if stage.split else "")

valid
raw ['channel', 'geo', 'time']
to_eur ['channel', 'geo', 'time']
weekly ['channel', 'geo', 'time'] <- split
scale_spend ['channel', 'geo', 'time']
scale_y ['channel', 'geo', 'time']
lags ['channel', 'geo', 'lag', 'time']
season ['channel', 'fourier_mode', 'geo', 'lag', 'time']
hols ['channel', 'fourier_mode', 'geo', 'lag', 'time']

Validation is synchronous and static: the server never imports plugin code. It returns every issue at once with a JSON pointer (/pipeline/2/with/over), plus the schema at every stage, here in the dataset's canonical names (geo, time) after binding.

docs.title: Fit and follow the run
docs.text:
from mapi_client import RunEnd, RunEventFrame, RunLiveFrame

revision = api.specs.upsert(spec_yaml)  # creates the spec, or adds a revision if it changed
run = api.runs.fit(revision.spec_id, revision.revision)

for item in api.runs.stream_events(run.id):  # SSE; resumes with Last-Event-ID
    match item:
        case RunLiveFrame(name="progress", event=event):  # live only, never replayed
            print("  ", event.payload.get("message"))
        case RunEventFrame(name=name, event=event):  # persisted, with an event id
            p = event.payload  # state, warning, diagnostic, metric, complete, error
            print(name, p.get("code") or p.get("name") or "", p.get("message") or p.get("value"))
        case RunEnd(run=final):  # the stream closes after this frame
            print("end:", final.state.value)

run = api.runs.wait(run.id, raise_on_failure=True)
print(run.state.value, run.output_model_version_id)

state  bootstrap object read and deleted
warning DEV_MODE_ISOLATION worker isolation is reduced (development mode): …
state  downloading the dataset
state  fitting the pipeline and the model
   validated the spec and the data
   chain 1/2: tuning 116/150, 0 divergences
   chain 2/2: sampling 31/100, 0 divergences
   evaluated the holdout through the score path
state  rendering plots and views
diagnostic RHAT 1.0488798610868963
…
metric mape 7.589774995896182
state  uploading outputs
complete  None
state  complete manifest uploaded
end: succeeded
succeeded mv_01m4zxxfd6xbmbmnv1byrxenf3

runs.stream_events follows the server-sent event stream and yields four kinds of items:

Item When Notes RunSnapshot First, and after every state change The full Run RunEventFrame Persisted events: state, warning, diagnostic, metric, checkpoint, complete, error Has an id; replayed after a reconnect RunLiveFrame progress and log Live only, never replayed RunEnd Once, when the run is terminal The stream then closes

A dropped connection is resumed with Last-Event-ID, so no persisted event is lost or repeated. runs.wait polls instead (with backoff) and, with raise_on_failure=True, raises the run's error; runs.logs(run_id) pages through the captured output.

docs.title: Inspect the model version
docs.text:
model = next(m for m in api.models.list() if m.name == "eu-geo-mmm")
mv = api.models.version(model.id, model.latest_version)
print(mv.ref, mv.scorecard.overall if mv.scorecard else None)  # pass | warn | fail
print(mv.metrics)
for item in mv.scorecard.items if mv.scorecard else []:
    print(f"{item.status:4} {item.code}: {item.message_plain}")

model://default/eu-geo-mmm@v4 warn
{'mape': 7.589774995896182, 'elpd_loo': 183.46594271421736, 'coverage_90': 0.875}
warn RHAT: The independent sampling runs disagree about 'beta_sigma', so its estimates are not reliable yet.
warn ESS_BULK: There is too little independent information about 'beta_channel' (about 53 effective draws) for stable averages.
warn ESS_TAIL: There is too little independent information about 'gamma_control' (about 35 effective draws) for stable intervals.
pass DIVERGENCES: The sampler explored the model without running into trouble.
warn PARETO_K_HIGH: Some data points strongly influence the model, so the leave-one-out score is only approximate.

A ModelVersion also carries the signed manifest, the diagnostics, the capabilities, the lineage and the list of artifacts. Download any of them:

metrics = api.models.download(model.id, mv.version, "metrics.json")  # bytes, CRC32C-checked
api.models.download(model.id, mv.version, "bundle.zarr.zip", dest="eu-geo-mmm.zarr.zip")

The API checks the manifest's signature before minting the short-lived signed URL, and the client checks the download against the CRC32C and size the object store computed. mapi_sdk.bundle.Bundle opens the downloaded bundle.zarr.zip in a notebook.

docs.title: Score
docs.text:
result = api.models.score(
    model.id,
    mv.version,
    {
        "model": mv.ref,
        "mode": "forecast",
        "horizon": {"dim": "time", "periods": 8},
        "data": "dataset://default/eu_media_future@latest",
        "side_tables": {"fx": "dataset://default/fx_daily@latest"},  # score_policy: supplied
        "output": {"kind": "expected", "summary": ["mean", "hdi_90"]},
    },
)
print(result.run.state.value, [link.name for link in result.outputs])
summary = result.tree["summary"]  # an xr.DataTree (needs the `xarray` extra)
print(result.tree.attrs["output_space"])  # {"y_hat": "weekly", ...}: weekly EUR, inverted
print(summary["y_hat"].sel(stat="mean", market="NL").round(0).values)

succeeded ['plots.json', 'result.json', 'score.zarr.zip', 'ui/summary.arrow']
{"contributions": "weekly", "y_hat": "weekly"}
[69720. 60339. 61101. 60544. 63529. 64553. 61885. 60652.]

models.score sends the request with Prefer: wait=60. If the run is not done by then, it repeats the same request with the same idempotency key: the server answers with the one run it already created, so a slow score never turns into two runs. With the xarray extra the result tree is downloaded and checked into result.tree.

The request is a ScoreRequest as a dict, a YAML string or the Pydantic model. apiVersion and kind are filled in for you.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
from mapi_spec.errors import MapiError, ModeNotSupported

request = {
    "model": mv.ref,
    "mode": "forecast",
    "horizon": {"dim": "time", "periods": 8},
    "data": "dataset://default/eu_media_future@latest",
}
try:  # the fx side table has `score_policy: supplied`, and this request does not supply it
    api.models.score(model.id, mv.version, request)
except MapiError as err:
    print(err.code, err)  # SIDE_TABLE_COVERAGE, with a JSON pointer: /side_tables/fx

try:  # this model cannot filter (that is for state-space models)
    api.models.score(model.id, mv.version, {**request, "mode": "filter"})
except ModeNotSupported as err:
    print(err.code)  # MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED, raised before any run is created

SIDE_TABLE_COVERAGE validation failed with 1 error; first at /side_tables/fx: side table 'fx' has score_policy 'supplied' and must be provided for stage 'raw'
MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED

Every RFC 7807 problem from the server becomes a MapiError (or a subclass such as ModeNotSupported, ValidationFailed, CoordPlanError, QuotaExceeded, IntegrityFailure) with the stable code, the HTTP status, the JSON pointer and the individual issues. Both requests above failed during static checks, before any run was created. Transport failures raise mapi_client.TransportError; responses the client cannot parse raise UnexpectedResponse.

Idempotent calls (GETs, and POSTs with an idempotency key) are retried on 429, 502, 503, 504 and connection errors, honouring Retry-After (ClientConfig.max_retries, default 2).

docs.title: Async
docs.text:
AsyncClient has the same resources and arguments; calls are awaited and lists are iterated with async for:

import asyncio

from mapi_client import AsyncClient


async def recent_fits(n: int = 3) -> list[str]:
    async with AsyncClient() as aapi:  # same resources and arguments, awaited
        found: list[str] = []
        async for run in aapi.runs.list(kind="fit", limit=n):  # follows next_cursor lazily
            found.append(f"{run.id} {run.state.value}")
            if len(found) == n:
                break
        return found


print(asyncio.run(recent_fits()))

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
Resource Calls projects list, get catalog get, models, model, steps, plots, schema datasets create, list, get, find, ensure, create_upload, create_version, versions, version, wait_version, upload, artifact, download specs validate, create, list, get, find, revise, upsert, revisions, revision, dry_run runs create, fit, get, list, wait, stream_events, events, logs, plots, cancel, resume, retry models list, get, versions, version, artifact, download, score plots list, get, validate

List calls return lazy paginators that follow next_cursor. api.health() and api.ready() call /healthz and /readyz. The DTOs are documented in mapi_spec and the endpoints in the HTTP API reference.

docs.title: Tabular models with scikit-learn and xgboost
docs.text: mapi-sklearn turns any allow-listed scikit-learn or xgboost estimator into a full modeling-api plugin. You describe which dims are samples and which variables are features; the platform stacks your labelled xr.Dataset into a design matrix, fits, persists safely, and at score time rebuilds exactly the same columns, handles new stores and forecast horizons, and unstacks predictions back to labelled arrays — with honest uncertainty.

docs.title: The plugins
docs.text:
The uncertainty kind decides the output representation, which in turn decides which summaries and aggregations are valid. Each kind is its own plugin:

Plugin Representation What y_hat holds Aggregate over cells? sklearn.tabular_regressor point point prediction (+ contributions) linear only, flagged sklearn.tabular_quantiles quantiles conditional quantiles (quantile, ...) no sklearn.tabular_bootstrap draws one joint draw per bootstrap replicate (chain, draw, ...) yes, any sklearn.tabular_conformal interval (bound=[lower, upper, point], ...), attr alpha no sklearn.tabular_classifier point probability of the positive class linear only, flagged

Why conformal is an interval, not draws

A split-conformal interval guarantees per-cell coverage (P(y in interval) >= 1 - alpha). It is not a distribution, so summing intervals across stores or weeks would claim a coverage nobody measured. The platform rejects such aggregations with CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED. If you need totals, use sklearn.tabular_bootstrap, whose draws are joint.

docs.title: A store-demand forecast
docs.text:
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: store-demand-xgb, project: retail}
data:
  dataset: dataset://retail/store_sku_weekly@latest
  bind:
    dims: {store: store_id, sku: sku, time: week}
    vars: {y: units_sold, price: price, promo: promo_flag}
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: time, last: 12}
pipeline:
  - {id: imp,   use: core.impute@^1,   with: {vars: [price], method: ffill, along: time, within: [store, sku]}}
  - {id: plags, use: core.lag@^1,      with: {vars: [promo], along: time, within: [store, sku], lags: [1, 2]}}
  - {id: cal,   use: core.calendar@^1, with: {along: time, features: [week_of_year, month]}}
  - {id: logy,  use: core.log1p@^1,    with: {vars: [y]}}
model:
  use: sklearn.tabular_quantiles@^1
  settings:
    estimator: {kind: xgboost.XGBRegressor, params: {n_estimators: 600, max_depth: 6, learning_rate: 0.05}}
    rows: [store, sku, time]                  # dims stacked into samples
    columns: {roles: [covariate]}             # which variables become features
    coord_features: {store: category, sku: category}
    uncertainty: {kind: quantile, quantiles: [0.1, 0.5, 0.9]}
    forecast_strategy: direct
  fit: {seed: 7, mode: evaluate_then_refit}
evaluate: {metrics: [rmse, mape, coverage_80]}
execution: {resource_class: S, timeout: 10m}

What happens:

  1. The holdout (last 12 weeks) is scored through the score path, using context tails from the training weeks, and rmse, mape and coverage_80 are computed in units sold (the log1p is inverted; quantiles map exactly through monotone transforms).
  2. The model is refitted on all weeks; the bundle stores the xgboost model as JSON.
  3. A forecast request supplies future prices and promotions; lags are rebuilt from the stored tail, and the platform checks the weeks continue the fitted range without gaps.
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ScoreRequest
model: endpoint://retail/store-demand-xgb
mode: forecast
horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}
data: dataset://retail/plan_next_4_weeks
output: {summary: [median, q10, q90]}

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Setting Default Meaning estimator — {kind, params} from the allow-list below (required for the built-in plugins) target y canonical name of the target variable rows — dims stacked into samples; every row dim of the target time_dim / time_kind time / time the row dim that extends at forecast time and its kind (time, integer, index; none when no row dim extends) columns {roles: [covariate, media, spend, control, exposure]} feature variables by role, or an explicit vars list; exclude removes names coord_features {} encode row-dim labels as features: category, onehot, ordinal, numeric new_levels pooled what an unseen level of a row dim becomes: pooled, zero or error pooled_max_levels 256 pool over at most this many (most frequent) fitted levels weight, mask — sample-weight variable; boolean mask of usable cells forecast_strategy direct recursive is rejected with RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED in v1 retransform median point predictions through a non-linear inverse (log1p): median or Duan smearing contributions auto point/bootstrap plugins: auto, exact, zeroing, none n_jobs 1 estimator threads (kept at 1 by default for bit-reproducible fits)

Variables with dims beyond rows become one column per label — spend(store, channel, time) with rows [store, time] gives spend[tv], spend[search]. Variables missing a row dim (calendar features over time only) are broadcast. Rows with a missing target, a non-positive weight, mask false or (for estimators without native missing-value support) a missing feature are left out of training and reported in a ROWS_DROPPED diagnostic.

docs.title: Coordinate features
docs.text:
• category — integer codes declared natively to xgboost and to HistGradientBoostingRegressor (up to 254 levels); one-hot for every other estimator.
  • onehot — one 0/1 column per fitted level.
  • ordinal — the level's position as a number (for ordered dims).
  • numeric — the label itself: numbers as-is, datetimes as days since the first fitted label.

docs.title: Estimators
docs.text:
Kind Task Quantiles Missing values Categories Stored as sklearn.LinearRegression regression — — one-hot skops sklearn.Ridge, sklearn.Lasso, sklearn.ElasticNet regression — — one-hot skops sklearn.QuantileRegressor regression one model per level — one-hot skops sklearn.RandomForestRegressor regression — — one-hot skops sklearn.GradientBoostingRegressor regression one model per level — one-hot skops sklearn.HistGradientBoostingRegressor regression one model per level native native skops xgboost.XGBRegressor regression one native multi-quantile model native native xgboost JSON sklearn.LogisticRegression, sklearn.RandomForestClassifier, xgboost.XGBClassifier binary classification — xgboost only xgboost only skops / JSON

Every kind has a bounded Pydantic params model (extra="forbid"). Parameters the platform owns — seeds, threads, categorical declarations, and the loss/objective an uncertainty kind needs — are not settable; for example sklearn.tabular_quantiles sets xgboost's objective: reg:quantileerror itself and rejects a conflicting one. Because the params models are a discriminated union, the control plane validates them statically: a max_depth: -1 is rejected with a JSON pointer before any run starts.

docs.title: Uncertainty
docs.text:
Quantiles. xgboost fits all levels at once; quantile-capable sklearn estimators fit one model per level. Crossing quantiles are sorted (monotone rearrangement, which never increases pinball loss) and the fraction of crossing rows is reported as QUANTILE_CROSSING. When you leave output.summary unset, the default (median, q5, q95) adapts to your grid — with [0.1, 0.5, 0.9] you get median, q10, q90. Explicitly requested levels outside the grid are an error: quantiles are interpolated, never extrapolated.

Bootstrap. n replicates refit the estimator on resampled rows — or, with by: store, on resampled whole stores (a cluster bootstrap that keeps within-store dependence). expected outputs are the replicate predictions; predictive outputs add an out-of-bag residual per cell. Draws are joint, so totals over stores, counterfactual deltas and any summary are valid.

Split conformal. A calibration fraction is held out — by default the most recent weeks (calibration_by: last), which mimics forecasting; random picks rows at random. The radius is the ceil((n+1)(1-alpha))-th smallest absolute calibration residual; too small a calibration set for the requested alpha is a SETTINGS_INVALID error rather than an infinite interval. refit: true refits the point model on all rows afterwards (sharper, but the finite-sample guarantee then holds only approximately).

docs.title: New stores, skus and markets
docs.text:
When score data contains a label of a row dim that was not seen at fit, the dim's effective policy decides (the tighter of the data's policy and the plugin's new_levels):

  • pooled — the prediction is the training-frequency-weighted average of the predictions the row would get under each fitted level. For a linear model with one-hot features this equals predicting with the average encoding; quantiles and interval bounds are averaged (Vincentisation); bootstrap draws are averaged per draw so they stay joint.
  • zero — the level contributes nothing: all one-hot columns are 0, category codes are missing (estimators with native missing-value support).
  • error (or a fixed dim) — UNSEEN_LEVELS before anything runs.

docs.title: Contributions
docs.text:
Point and bootstrap plugins can return contributions(component, ...) next to y_hat:

  • exact (linear estimators; the default with contributions: auto) — intercept plus coef × x per column, with a coordinate feature's one-hot columns summed into one component. Components add up to the prediction exactly.
  • zeroing (any estimator) — counterfactual zeroing: baseline is the prediction with every feature at zero, each feature's contribution is the drop when only it is zeroed, and interaction holds the remainder so the components still add up. These are labelled counterfactual_zeroing and are not Shapley values (SHAP is out of scope for v1).

Contributions are additive in model space (output: {units: model}). Through a non-linear inverse such as log1p the per-component inverse is not a decomposition; request model units when you want the parts to add up.

docs.title: Persistence and safety
docs.text:
Fitted estimators are stored in the bundle's /native group — never pickled:

  • scikit-learn estimators with skops. Loading lists the file's types first and refuses anything outside that estimator's allow-list (for example a random forest may contain sklearn.tree._tree.Tree, a ridge regression nothing extra); the loaded object must be exactly the expected class.
  • xgboost models as the booster's JSON document.

The bundle manifest records size, CRC32C, MD5 and SHA-256 of every file, and the contract kit checks that no pickle-like entry exists.

docs.title: Write your own sklearn plugin
docs.text:
Implement estimator() and pick a base class for the representation you want:

from typing import ClassVar

from mapi_sklearn import PointSettings, SklearnModel, capabilities_for
from mapi_spec import Capabilities
from sklearn.linear_model import Ridge


class LinearDemand(SklearnModel[PointSettings]):
    id = "t.acme.linear_demand"
    version = "1.0.0"
    capabilities: ClassVar[Capabilities] = capabilities_for("none").model_copy(
        update={"contribution_scale": "additive"}  # a linear model decomposes exactly
    )

    def estimator(self, s: PointSettings) -> Ridge:
        return Ridge(alpha=0.5)  # must be exactly an allow-listed class

estimator() may return an allow-listed instance, a {kind, params} mapping or a choice model; subclasses of estimators and parameters outside the params model are rejected. Base classes: SklearnModel (point), SklearnQuantileModel, SklearnBootstrapModel, SklearnConformalModel, SklearnClassifier.

Run the contract kit on synthetic data before you publish:

from mapi_sdk.testing import ModelFixture, check_model
from mapi_sklearn.testing import demand_dataset, demand_registry, demand_schema, demand_spec

data = demand_dataset()  # a store x sku x week demand panel
report = check_model(
    LinearDemand,
    ModelFixture(
        spec=demand_spec("t.acme.linear_demand@^1", {"estimator": None}),
        data=data,
        raw_schema=demand_schema(data),
        registry=demand_registry(),
    ),
)
print(report.summary())
# ... [PASS] additive_contributions: contributions sum to 'y_hat' ...

docs.title: Limits in v1
docs.text:
• Forecasting is direct only: future features must be supplied or derived by the pipeline.
  • Classification is binary.
  • Row dims other than time_dim are declared categorical, so integer-labelled groups (numeric store ids) need string labels.
  • Contributions are not available for quantile or conformal plugins.

docs.title: Forecasting and sequential models
docs.text: Time is where most modelling platforms quietly cut corners: a forecast that silently runs past what the model can represent, a state-space model that restarts from scratch at every score, a holdout scored without the history it depends on. modeling-api makes each of these explicit and checks them before any compute is spent.

docs.title: Horizons are part of the contract
docs.text:
A time dim declares its policy extend and, optionally, a max_extension: how far past the fitted range a forecast may go without a refit. The control plane checks every score request against it from metadata alone:

apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ScoreRequest
model: endpoint://climate/mauna-loa-co2
mode: forecast
horizon: {dim: t, periods: 30}

{"code": "HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT", "status": 409,
 "detail": "horizon of 30 exceeds the 24 periods this fit supports along 't'; a refit is required"}

Models that need a bounded domain take it from the same place. ts.hsgp_trend sizes its Hilbert-space GP from ctx.anticipated_coords (the fitted labels plus max_extension future labels), so the basis it evaluates at a forecast month is exactly the basis it was fitted with:

dom = HSGPDomain.from_positions(positions_of(ctx.anticipated_coords["t"]), s.c)
phi = hsgp_basis(dom.scale(ctx.position("t")), s.m, dom.L)   # same at fit and at score

Score payloads must also continue the fitted range without gaps (NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION) and may not start before it (COORD_NOT_ALLOWED).

docs.title: Evaluate the way you will forecast
docs.text: With fit.mode: evaluate_then_refit (the default for promotable models) the platform fits on the training window, scores the holdout through the score path (with the context and state from training only), records the metrics, then refits on everything so forecasts start from the latest data. The production bundle links the evaluation bundle and its metrics.

docs.title: Sequential models keep a terminal state
docs.text:
Hidden Markov models, Kalman filters and particle filters summarise the past in a state. They store it in a plugin-owned terminal_state group and read it at score time instead of replaying history. ts.gaussian_hmm stores the filtered state distribution at the last fitted step, alpha_T(chain, draw, animal, state):

  • forecast propagates it: P(z_{T+h}) = alpha_T · A^h, per posterior draw;
  • filter continues the forward filter over new observations and returns an updated terminal_state group, so filtering six new steps at once or in two batches of three gives the same state.
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ScoreRequest
model: endpoint://ecology/animal-tracks-hmm
mode: filter
data: dataset://ecology/tracks_live@v1

The result has predictions (one-step-ahead y_hat and filtered state_prob) and a terminal_state group with attrs.step set to the last filtered step.

docs.title: Missing values and sentinels
docs.text:
Raw series often encode gaps as numbers (-99.99). Declare the code in the schema (missing_sentinel) and turn it into NaN with core.replace_sentinel; models that support gaps (such as ts.hsgp_trend) leave those periods out of the likelihood and still predict them.

See Built-in models for every setting, and the Conformance corpus for the fixtures (c08, e24) that keep this behaviour tested.

docs.title: The Expert web app v0.2
docs.text:
The web app is the Expert-mode front end of the platform: data scientists upload data, write and validate specs, fit them, inspect the fitted models and score them, all against the same /v1 HTTP API that the CLI and the Python client use. Nothing the app does is privileged: every button is one or two API calls.

This page walks through every page in navigation order. The screenshots come from the quickstart stack; make dev serves the app at http://127.0.0.1:5173.

Guided mode arrives in v0.4

The Guided / Expert switch in the header already exists, but Guided mode is a preview of the task flow that analysts will get in v0.4. Both modes edit the same ModelSpec.

docs.title: The shell
docs.text:
Element What it does Sidebar Home, Datasets, Build, Runs, Models, Score and Catalog; Settings at the bottom. Collapse (Cmd+B) narrows it to icons. Jump to… (Cmd+K or /) A command palette: go to any page, start a new spec, switch the theme, or paste an id (run_…, mdl_…, ds_…, spc_…) to open it. API connected Polls GET /readyz: green when PostgreSQL, the object store and the catalog are ready, amber (API degraded) or red (API unreachable) otherwise. It links to Settings, which shows each check. Guided / Expert The persona switch (remembered in this browser). Display icon Light, dark or system theme. ? The keyboard shortcuts. Single keys work when no text field has focus: G then H Home, D Datasets, B Build, R Runs, M Models, S Score, C Catalog, , Settings.

Text that came from a run or a plugin (log lines, tracebacks, warning messages, plot captions) is always rendered as plain text, with ANSI escapes and control and bidi characters removed. It is labelled untrusted output where it appears.

docs.title: Home
docs.text:
The landing page answers "is anything happening, and does anything need me?":

  • Running (the heading says Nothing running when idle): active runs with their live progress bars;
  • Needs attention: failed, stalled or partial runs among the latest 50, each linking to its run page;
  • Recently finished: the latest runs of every kind with their state and input;
  • Models: registered models with their latest version;
  • Start something: write a spec from the geo MMM template, upload a dataset, browse the catalog. Upload data and New spec do the same from the header.

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
A dataset is a named collection of immutable versions. New dataset asks for a name (lowercase letters, digits, _ and -) and an optional description, then opens the upload panel.

Uploading. Pick a file:

  • a zarr zip (.zarr.zip) or netCDF (.nc) file is self-describing: its dims, coordinates and, if present, its mapi_schema attribute (roles, policies, units) are used as they are;
  • a CSV file is previewed in your browser (it is never parsed by the server) and you map each column: a dim with its kind (time, categorical, …), its score-time policy (fixed, extend, new_levels) and frequency, or a variable with its role (target, spend, covariate, …), units and missing-value rule. Parquet files are mapped the same way, without the local preview.

Upload and ingest sends the file straight to object storage through a signed PUT URL (the API never sees the bytes), then starts a sandboxed ingest run. The page refreshes until the version is ready, or shows the ingest's issues in plain language ("3 markets are missing 2 weeks in March").

A version page has five tabs:

Tab Shows Schema Dims with kind, score-time policy, frequency and new-level strategy; variables with dims, dtype, role, units and missing-value rule Coordinates Each dim's coordinate range and values, searchable when there are many Missingness A heatmap of missing values per variable along the time dim, rendered in the plot sandbox Preview The first rows, as the ingest run wrote them (preview.json) About The content hash, size, the ingest run, when it was created and the version message

dataset://default/eu_media_daily@v1 (the copy button next to the title) is the reference that specs and score requests use. @latest resolves to the newest ready version when a run is submitted, and the run records which one it got.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
Build lists the specs with their latest revision and whether it is valid. New spec opens the editor on the geo MMM template.

The editor is Monaco with YAML support bound to the server's modelspec.json schema, so it completes keys and documents fields on hover. As you type (and on Cmd+Enter) the spec is sent to POST /v1/specs:validate: the server resolves every dataset:// reference, step and model plugin, checks the settings against the plugin's sanitized JSON Schema, and propagates the data schema through the pipeline using each step's exported schema effect. Problems appear as squiggles at the exact YAML path and in the Issues tab, with their error code (LEAKAGE_RISK, SCHEMA_INVALID, …). The badge under the title says valid or how many errors there are.

The right-hand panel:

Tab Shows Pipeline The raw data after binding, then one card per step: its plugin and version, what kind of step it is (reshape, value, feature), whether it learns state and is invertible, the dims it adds or changes, the context tail it keeps for scoring, and Schema after this step. The Train / holdout split marker sits where data.split.after_step puts it. Issues Every validation issue with its code, JSON pointer and message Revisions Every saved revision, with its message; pick two to see a diff

The buttons:

  • Save revision (Cmd+S) stores the text as a new immutable revision (r1, r2, …) with the optional message. Invalid revisions can be saved too, so work in progress is never lost; they cannot be fitted.
  • Dry-run starts a sandboxed validate run of the saved revision: it checks the real data array by array against the spec, fits the pipeline on it (not the model) and records the schema at every stage. Use it when a step's effect is dynamic, or when the static check passes and you want to know the data really fits.
  • Fit submits a fit run of the saved revision and opens its run page.

docs.title: Runs
docs.text: Every ingest, describe, dry-run, fit and score is a run. The list filters by state and kind and updates live.

docs.title: Run detail
docs.text:
The run page subscribes to the run's server-sent event stream (Live next to the state) and resumes where it stopped after a disconnect.

  • Progress: the current phase (Starting the sandbox, Loading inputs, Fitting, Rendering plots, Uploading outputs, …), the latest message from the runner (for a PyMC fit, the chain, draw and divergence counts) and a progress bar. No progress reported recently appears when a run goes quiet for longer than expected; the run is marked stalled, which is a warning, not a failure: the executor's own status decides whether the run is alive.
  • Logs: the stdout and stderr the supervisor captured from the worker (capped and stripped), with All / stdout / stderr / system filters, a text filter and Follow.
  • Details: timestamps, the spec revision, model version or dataset it ran on, the spec hash, the run it retried, and its cost (Not metered locally).
  • Events: every persisted event, including the DEV_MODE_ISOLATION warning on a laptop, diagnostics and metrics.

Actions: Cancel (any active run; checkpointed fits stop as partial), Resume (a partial run continues from its checkpoints as a new attempt) and Retry (a new run from a failed one; after RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED the dialog suggests the next resource class). A succeeded fit links to its model version: Inspect model://default/eu-geo-mmm@v1.

docs.title: Models
docs.text: Models lists every model (one per spec name) and the model page lists its versions. Each successful fit registers a new version after the platform has verified the run's outputs and signed the bundle manifest. The version page has six tabs and a Score button.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Scorecard rolls the diagnostics up into pass, warn and fail items, each with a plain-language message, the metric and its threshold, and a suggested action. Metrics are the holdout metrics the spec asked for (evaluate.metrics), computed by scoring the holdout through the normal scoring path before the refit. Capabilities are the plugin's: score modes, representation (draws, quantiles, interval, point, moments), how contributions combine, what preprocessing the model owns, and whether results are deterministic for a seed.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text: One row per check and variable, sortable and filterable: R-hat, bulk and tail ESS, divergences, Pareto k, or "LOO invalid" with the plugin's reason.

docs.title: Plots
docs.text:
The plot recipes the spec listed in outputs.plots, rendered from the bundle's precomputed plot data. Each card says which recipe made it (core.ppc_fan@1.0.0) and in which library (vega-lite or plotly), with a plain-language caption.

Every plot, first-party included, renders inside an <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts"> served from the plot sandbox's own origin (port 5174 locally). The specs were checked by the server's sanitizer when the run finished and again on every read, and the sandbox refuses URL data, links, external images and tile maps before any charting library runs. The two windows talk only through a small, validated postMessage protocol. See Web app and plot sandbox.

docs.title: Data tree
docs.text: A browser over the bundle's ui/tree_index.json: every group of the fitted bundle (binding, fit_coords per stage, model/posterior, sample_stats, log_likelihood, preprocess/<step>/{arrays,context}, derived/…) with its variables, dims, shapes, units and attributes. It reads the index only; the arrays stay in the bundle, which you can download from Provenance or with the client.

docs.title: Preprocessing
docs.text: A heatmap of each step's learned state (for example scale(geo, channel)), read from the bundle's ui/preprocess.json view: every step in order with its resolved plugin, whether it is stateful, its learned JSON and its numeric state arrays (larger arrays are listed as omitted). The full state is also browsable under preprocess/ in Data tree.

docs.title: Provenance
docs.text:
• Signature: the bundle manifest's signature (EC P-256 locally, standing in for Cloud KMS), the spec, data and catalog hashes it binds, and its status. The server checks it, the tenant and every object generation before it hands out any download link.
  • Lineage: the fit run and attempt, plugin and version, engine and seed, executor and resource class, dataset and side-table versions, the evaluation bundle it was refitted from, and the library versions in the runner.
  • Bundle objects: every stored object with its size, CRC32C and generation; each can be opened or downloaded through a short-lived signed URL, and the download is checked against that CRC32C.

docs.title: Score
docs.text:
Pick a model and version (or arrive from a model page). The form is built from the model's capabilities, so it only offers what the model can do, and the server checks the request statically before any run starts.

Field Meaning Mode predict, forecast, counterfactual, simulate, evaluate (and filter for state-space models), as the plugin declares Horizon dim, Periods For forecast: how far to extend the time-like dim past the fitted range Inputs enter at stage Where the request's data enters the pipeline: raw (the dataset's own units), or a later stage such as weekly, to send weekly EUR spend directly. Steps before the stage are skipped, and so are their side tables. Input data A dataset:// reference (Upload creates one): future spend for a forecast, a new market, or a window of past data for a counterfactual Scenario data A changed copy of the input data; counterfactuals compare it with the input Side tables Tables with score_policy: supplied (here fx) default to the version the fit used and must cover the scored dates; pinned tables are replayed from the fit Interventions Change a variable on selected coordinates: spend_local where channel=tv, multiply by 1.2 Quantity Expected (the mean response) or Predictive (with observation noise) Units, Names Original units (inverted back through the pipeline) or model space; your dataset's names or the plugin's canonical names Summaries, Draws Which summaries to return (mean, median, sd, hdi_50, hdi_90, quantiles), and how many joint draws (0 returns summaries only; counterfactual deltas need draws to show their uncertainty) Variables, Seed Restrict the outputs; fix the seed for reproducible draws

Score sends POST /v1/models/{id}/versions/{v}:score with Prefer: wait=30 and an idempotency key, then follows the run.

Results shows the run's own plots (a forecast fan per market, or the scenario against the baseline for a counterfactual), the outputs with their sizes and signed links (score.zarr.zip is the full xr.DataTree, ui/summary.arrow the summary table), the summary as a table with one row per coordinate and one column per statistic, and a quick chart you can re-plot by any column. A market the model has not seen, like FR above, is drawn from the fitted hierarchy, so its band is wider; the result's issues say so.

docs.title: Catalog
docs.text: What the runner image provides, as exported by its sandboxed describe run and identified by its digest: Models (inference, representation, score modes, base image), Steps (kind, whether it learns state, invertibility, summary) and Plots (recipe, title, audience and the bundle groups it needs). Click a row for its full entry. Specs can only use what is listed here. The same data is in the generated catalogs.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Appearance and Mode are stored in this browser. Connection shows the API and plot sandbox the app was built for (VITE_API_BASE, VITE_PLOTS_ORIGIN), the server and contract versions, and the latency of each readiness check.

docs.title: Guided
docs.text: The six tasks an analyst will follow in v0.4: choose a template, answer questions about the data, enter beliefs as ROI ranges, run, read the report and scorecard, try what-if scenarios. Today the page explains them and links back to Expert mode.

docs.title: Where next
docs.text:
• Your first model in the web app: the E33 demo clicked through from upload to counterfactual.
  • Web app and plot sandbox: build variables, the API client and the security headers.
  • Security model: what the sandbox and the plot iframe protect against, locally and in production.

docs.title: Deployment v0.2
docs.text:
v0.2 runs the whole platform on one machine, single-tenant. The two supported ways start the same services on the same ports, so URLs, the CLI, the Python client and the tests work with either.

Local, without Docker Docker Compose Google Cloud Command make dev make docker-build && make compose-up – PostgreSQL embedded (pgserver) or your DATABASE_URL the official postgres:16 image Cloud SQL Object storage the GCS shim, in .local/gcs the GCS shim image, in a volume Cloud Storage Runs execute as mapi-runner subprocesses of the worker subprocesses of the worker container, or one container per run Cloud Run Jobs, one fresh sandbox per run Code your working tree, with hot reload the container images the same images Use it for development, demos, the end-to-end tests checking the production images end to end v0.3 
flowchart LR
    browser(("browser")) -->|":5173"| web["web app"]
    browser -->|":5174"| plots["plot sandbox<br/>(separate origin)"]
    browser -->|":8000 /v1"| api
    browser -->|":4443 signed URLs"| shim
    cli["mapi CLI ·<br/>Python client"] -->|"/v1"| api
    api["api<br/>(mapi-server api)"] --> pg[("PostgreSQL")]
    api --> shim["GCS shim"]
    worker["worker<br/>(dispatcher · reconciler ·<br/>finalizer · events)"] --> pg
    worker --> shim
    worker -->|"starts"| runner["mapi-runner<br/>supervisor + worker"]
    runner -->|"signed URLs only"| shim

Whichever you choose:

  • It is single-tenant and has no authentication. The API listens on 127.0.0.1, and compose publishes every port on 127.0.0.1 only. Do not expose a v0.2 stack to untrusted networks; see the security model.
  • State is the database plus the object store. Back up both (.local/pg and .local/gcs locally; the pgdata and gcsdata volumes under compose), and the bundle signing key (.local/keys/) if you want existing model versions to stay downloadable.
  • Migrations run first. make dev and compose both run mapi-server migrate before the API and the worker start, and stop if it fails.

docs.title: In this section
docs.text:
• Local, without Docker: what make dev starts, everyday commands, working on one component, where state lives.
  • Docker Compose: the compose stack, its network layout and the executor choice.
  • Container images: the six images, how they are built and the guards that keep them honest.
  • Configuration reference: every environment variable.
  • Troubleshooting: port conflicts and everything else.

docs.title: Configuration reference v0.2
docs.text:
Every component is configured through environment variables; no component reads a config file except the CLI and the Python client (~/.config/mapi/config.toml) and Docker Compose (.env). This page lists every MAPI_* variable in the code base, grouped by who reads it. A test (conformance/tests/test_docs_platform.py) scans the source tree and fails when a variable is missing here, and the full server settings table is generated from the code.

The short version

For a local stack you only ever need the four addresses, and only when a port is taken: MAPI_API_URL, MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT, MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN and MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN. Export the same values in every shell that runs make dev, make seed, make e2e, mapi or the Python client. Troubleshooting has an example.

docs.title: Topology (every component)
docs.text:
These come from mapi_spec.localdev.LocalDev, the one contract the API, worker, runner, GCS shim, make dev, make seed, the end-to-end tests and (through VITE_*) the web app share, so they cannot disagree about where things are.

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_ENV local Environment name; buckets are mapi-{env}-quarantine, -bootstrap, -runs, -bundles, -data DATABASE_URL (or MAPI_DATABASE_URL) unset A postgresql:// URL. Unset: make dev and mapi serve start an embedded PostgreSQL 16 (pgserver) in $MAPI_DATA_DIR/pg MAPI_API_URL http://127.0.0.1:8000 Where the API listens and is reached. make dev derives the API's host and port from it MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT http://127.0.0.1:4443 The object store (the GCS shim). Signed URLs point here MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN http://127.0.0.1:5173 The web app's origin. The API and the shim allow it for CORS MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN http://127.0.0.1:5174 The plot sandbox's origin. Must differ from MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN: every component refuses a configuration where they are equal MAPI_DATA_DIR .local Local state: pg/, gcs/ (objects and the shim's keys), keys/ (the bundle-signing key), executions/, dev/

docs.title: mapi-server (API and worker)
docs.text:
mapi-server api, worker, migrate and dev read mapi_server.settings.Settings: each field is the variable MAPI_<FIELD>. Besides the topology above:

Identity and API

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_PROFILE single-tenant single-tenant or multi-tenant. The local-process executor refuses multi-tenant MAPI_TENANT_ID, MAPI_PROJECT_ID default The single tenant and project of an M1 install MAPI_API_HOST, MAPI_API_PORT 127.0.0.1, 8000 Bind address of mapi-server api when started without --host/--port MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS 127.0.0.1,localhost,api Host header values the API answers (comma-separated; the host of MAPI_API_URL is always allowed; * turns the check off). The DNS-rebinding guard of the unauthenticated M1 API MAPI_DEBUG false Put tracebacks into problem documents' untrusted_text. Never in production MAPI_LOG_LEVEL info debug, info, warning or error MAPI_INTERNAL_TOKEN unset If set, POST /internal/events (simulated Pub/Sub pushes) requires this bearer token MAPI_SSE_HEARTBEAT_S 15 Seconds between : keepalive comments on event streams MAPI_SSE_POLL_S 5 Fallback poll of an event stream when no PostgreSQL NOTIFY arrives MAPI_MAX_SIDECAR_BYTES 8 MiB Largest JSON sidecar (plots.json, diagnostics.json, …) the control plane will parse

MAPI_PROFILE means two things

The CLI and the Python client read MAPI_PROFILE as the name of a config-file profile; the server reads it as the deployment profile. Do not export a client profile name in a shell that starts make dev or mapi-server: the server refuses any value other than single-tenant or multi-tenant.

Database

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_DB_POOL_SIZE 10 Connections per process (plus as many overflow connections) MAPI_DB_ECHO false Log every SQL statement

Object storage

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_OBJECT_STORE shim shim (the GCS shim at MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT) or memory (tests only) MAPI_GCS_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT The base URL put into signed URLs, when browsers or containers reach the shim under another host name MAPI_GCS_ROOT $MAPI_DATA_DIR/gcs The shim's state directory; the server reads the principals' key files under _shim/keys/ MAPI_GCS_KEY_FILE $MAPI_GCS_ROOT/_shim/keys/control.json Key file of the control plane's principal MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN from exec.json Bearer token of the shim's exec principal, handed to local runs (local executors only, never in the cloud)

Executors

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_EXECUTOR local-process local-process, docker or docker-gvisor MAPI_RUNNER_COMMAND mapi-runner next to the interpreter The supervisor's command line (shell-quoted) for local-process MAPI_EXECUTOR_WORKDIR $MAPI_DATA_DIR/executions Per-run scratch of the local executor MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGE mapi/base-bayes:<version> Runner image of the docker executors for runs without a mapped plugin (ingest, describe) MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGES mmm, tabular: base-bayes; sklearn: base-ml; ts: base-forecast Plugin namespace to runner image (JSON), tagged with the workspace version MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK none The run containers' network: container:<gcs-shim container> or an internal network that contains only the shim. none is refused while the bootstrap URL is HTTP MAPI_DOCKER_RUNTIME_GVISOR runsc The OCI runtime of docker-gvisor MAPI_CANCEL_GRACE_S 10 Seconds between SIGTERM and SIGKILL when a run is cancelled

Dispatcher and reconciler

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_DISPATCH_RATE_PER_MINUTE, MAPI_DISPATCH_BURST 180, 10 Token bucket in front of the executor (Cloud Run's jobs.run quota) MAPI_DISPATCH_BATCH, MAPI_DISPATCH_POLL_S 10, 1 Queued runs leased per pass, and the pause between passes MAPI_DISPATCH_LEASE_S 120 How long a dispatcher's lease on a run lasts MAPI_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_S 10 The reconciler's level-triggered loop MAPI_STALL_INTERVALS 15 A run is stalled (a warning) after this many progress intervals of silence MAPI_COMPLETE_EVENT_GRACE_S 60 How long to wait for a run's complete event after the executor reports an exit MAPI_LOST_EXECUTION_GRACE_S 60 How long an execution may be missing from the executor before the attempt is lost MAPI_DEADLINE_GRACE_S 60 Slack after a run's timeout before the reconciler stops it MAPI_MAX_INFRA_RETRIES 2 Automatic retries after infrastructure failures MAPI_AUTO_RETRY_WINDOW_S 1800 No automatic retry of a run that has been going for longer than this MAPI_FINALIZE_MAX_ATTEMPTS 5 Attempts of the finalizer job before a run fails

Catalog and signing

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_CATALOG_PATH unset A catalog JSON exported at image build; unset: the worker queues a sandboxed describe run MAPI_IMAGE_DIGEST sha256 of uv.lock The runner image digest the catalog is cached under MAPI_UV_LOCK_PATH found above the working directory The uv.lock whose hash is the local image digest MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_PATH $MAPI_DATA_DIR/keys/bundle-signing-p256.pem The EC P-256 key that signs bundle manifests (standing in for Cloud KMS). The worker signs and the API verifies, so both must load the same file. mapi-server migrate creates it MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_CREATE true Create the key on first use when it is missing. Compose turns it off for api and worker, so a missing key fails start-up instead of a new key being minted

docs.title: The runner (per run)
docs.text:
Executors start mapi-runner with exactly these variables, and nothing secret in its arguments. Never set them by hand.

Variable Meaning MAPI_RUN_ID, MAPI_NONCE The run, and the 256-bit nonce of its one-time bootstrap object MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL A template with {nonce}: where the supervisor reads (and deletes) the bootstrap object MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN Local executors only: the shim's exec principal, which may only get and delete bootstrap objects MAPI_WORKER_PYTHON The worker's interpreter (default: the supervisor's) MAPI_BASE_IMAGE The base image recorded in the run's lineage MAPI_REQUIRE_ISOLATION Set to 1 by the docker executor: the supervisor fails the run with SANDBOX_VIOLATION instead of running the worker in dev mode

The supervisor passes the untrusted worker only an allow-list of variables (mapi_spec.run.WORKER_ENV_ALLOWLIST: PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, locale and thread-count variables, NUMBA_CACHE_DIR, PYTENSOR_FLAGS, XLA_FLAGS, …). Every MAPI_* is scrubbed.

Inside the runner images, MAPI_CACHE_SEED (/opt/mapi/cache) is the baked, read-only PyTensor and Numba cache and MAPI_CACHE_DIR (/tmp/mapi-cache) the writable symlink farm the entry point builds over it (Container images).

docs.title: The GCS shim
docs.text: mapi-gcs-shim serve takes its defaults from the topology: MAPI_DATA_DIR (state in $MAPI_DATA_DIR/gcs), MAPI_ENV (bucket names), MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT (host and port) and MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN (the CORS origin). Each has a command-line flag; see the GCS shim reference.

docs.title: The CLI and the Python client
docs.text:
Variable Meaning MAPI_URL The API (falls back to MAPI_API_URL, then the profile, then http://127.0.0.1:8000) MAPI_TOKEN A bearer token. Never sent over plain HTTP to a non-loopback host MAPI_PROFILE The profile of the config file to use (see the warning above) MAPI_CONFIG The config file (default $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mapi/config.toml, else ~/.config/mapi/config.toml)

Arguments (--url, --token, --profile, or Client(base_url=…, token=…)) win over the environment, which wins over the file. mapi config show prints the result and where each value came from.

docs.title: make dev
docs.text:
scripts/dev.py reads the topology variables and:

Variable Meaning MAPI_DEV_<NAME>_CMD Replace one service's command (shell-quoted). <NAME> is GCS_SHIM, MIGRATE, API, WORKER, WEB or PLOTS, e.g. MAPI_DEV_API_CMD="uvicorn mapi_server.app:app --reload --port 8000" NO_COLOR, FORCE_COLOR Disable or force coloured service prefixes

make dev ONLY=api and make dev WITHOUT=web,plots choose services; make seed SIZE=full loads the large demo. These are make arguments, not environment variables.

docs.title: The web app and the plot sandbox
docs.text:
Vite build-time variables. make dev sets them from the topology; set them yourself for a production build.

Variable Default Meaning VITE_API_BASE http://127.0.0.1:8000 The API the app calls (it must allow the app's origin) VITE_PLOTS_ORIGIN http://127.0.0.1:5174 The plot sandbox; must differ from the app origin VITE_STORAGE_ORIGINS http://127.0.0.1:4443 Origins of signed storage URLs, allowed by the app's CSP connect-src VITE_APP_ORIGINS (sandbox) http://127.0.0.1:5173,http://localhost:5173 Origins allowed to frame the sandbox and talk to it

The sandbox's index.html carries a %MAPI_CSP% placeholder that its Vite build replaces with the Content-Security-Policy; it is not a variable you set.

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
Compose reads .env in the repository root (copy .env.example).

Variable Default Meaning POSTGRES_PASSWORD required The database password; compose refuses to start without it MAPI_VERSION the workspace version The mapi/* image tag (make compose-up sets it) MAPI_ENV local As above MAPI_EXECUTOR local-process The worker's executor MAPI_WORKER_TMPFS, MAPI_WORKER_MEMORY, MAPI_WORKER_CPUS 4g, 12g, 4 The worker's /tmp (the scratch of every local-process run), memory limit and CPUs DOCKER_GID 0 With the docker executor override: the group that owns the Docker socket

docs.title: The mapi/web image (nginx)
docs.text:
Rendered into the nginx configuration when the container starts (only MAPI_* variables are substituted).

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN, MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN, MAPI_API_URL, MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT the local defaults Origins written into the CSP and frame-ancestors headers MAPI_API_UPSTREAM http://api:8000 Where /v1/ is proxied (a URL without a path) MAPI_WEB_SERVER_NAMES 127.0.0.1 localhost Host names the app server answers (space-separated); any other Host gets no response. Keep in step with MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS MAPI_WEB_SCRIPT_SRC_EXTRA empty Extra script-src sources for the app. Widening the CSP needs a review NGINX_ENVSUBST_TEMPLATE_DIR /etc/nginx/templates/all …/web or …/plots serves only one of the two apps

docs.title: Image build arguments
docs.text:
docker build --build-arg NAME=value (the Makefile passes VERSION, VCS_REF and BUILD_DATE). The defaults define what each image is; change them only to build a variant.

Argument Meaning MAPI_PACKAGES The workspace packages installed into the image (mapi-runner mapi-steps mapi-pymc …) MAPI_WORKER_PACKAGES What the worker target adds to base-bayes (mapi-plugin-ts mapi-server[docker]) MAPI_NO_INSTALL Distributions never installed (the 300 MB nvidia-nccl-cu13) MAPI_APT_PACKAGES System packages of the runtime stage (tini, and g++ for PyTensor) MAPI_ASSERT_PRESENT, MAPI_ASSERT_ABSENT Distributions that must, and must not, be installed; the build fails otherwise MAPI_IMAGE_NAME, MAPI_DESCRIPTION OCI labels, and the name the catalog export records PYTHON_IMAGE (and the other base images) Base images, pinned by tag and digest (make docker-pin)
