docs.title: Docker Compose v0.2
docs.text:
docker-compose.yml runs the platform's container images as a single-tenant stack on one machine: the same services as make dev, on the same ports, but from the exact images that production uses. You do not need Docker for development (see Local, without Docker); use compose to check the images end to end or to run a self-contained demo. What is inside each image, how it is built and the build-time guards are on Container images.

cp .env.example .env               # set POSTGRES_PASSWORD
make docker-build                  # every image, tagged mapi/<name>:<version>
make compose-up                    # docker compose up -d --wait
make seed                          # load the E33 demo through the API
open http://127.0.0.1:5173
make compose-logs SERVICE=api      # follow one service
make compose-down                  # VOLUMES=1 also deletes the database and objects

docs.title: The stack
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph ns["shared network namespace (gcs-shim)"]
        shim["gcs-shim :4443"]
        api["api :8000"]
        worker["worker<br/>(local-process runs)"]
    end
    pg[("postgres :5432")]
    web["web :8080"]
    plots["plot-sandbox :8081"]
    browser(("browser")) -->|127.0.0.1:5173| web
    browser -->|127.0.0.1:5174| plots
    browser -->|"127.0.0.1:4443 (signed URLs)"| shim
    web -->|/v1/ proxy| api
    api --> pg
    worker --> pg
    migrate["migrate (one-shot)"] --> pg
Service Image Published on the host postgres postgres:16 (pinned by digest) not published; see the override example gcs-shim mapi/gcs-shim 127.0.0.1:4443 and 127.0.0.1:8000 (the API, which shares this namespace) migrate mapi/server, migrate; compose waits for it to exit with status 0 — api mapi/server, api via gcs-shim worker mapi/worker, mapi-server worker, MAPI_EXECUTOR=local-process — web mapi/web with only the app server block 127.0.0.1:5173 plot-sandbox mapi/web with only the sandbox server block 127.0.0.1:5174

Why api, worker and gcs-shim share one network namespace. Signed URLs embed the object store's address, and the bootstrap URL template embeds it for runner processes. If the API reached the shim as gcs-shim:4443 while the browser needed 127.0.0.1:4443, every URL would need a public form and an internal form. With a shared namespace, 127.0.0.1:4443 and 127.0.0.1:8000 mean the same thing to the browser, the API, the orchestrator and every runner subprocess. That is exactly the make dev topology, and it matches the LocalDev defaults. The web container reaches the API as api:8000, which is a network alias of the shim's container.

Durable state. Three named volumes outlive the containers: pgdata (the database), gcsdata (the shim's objects and principal key files) and keys (the bundle-signing key). The worker's finalizer signs every bundle manifest, and the API verifies that signature before it hands out an artifact link, a ui/ view or a plot, and before it accepts a score request. Both must therefore load the same key, and the key must survive restarts. migrate creates it once at /var/lib/mapi/keys/bundle-signing-p256.pem (MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_PATH). api and worker mount the volume read-only, with MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_CREATE=false, so a missing key fails start-up loudly instead of a new key being minted silently. MAPI_DATA_DIR (/tmp/mapi-data) is per-container scratch. make compose-down VOLUMES=1 deletes the key along with the data. A new key cannot verify old bundles, so delete it only together with the database and the objects.

Hardening. Every mapi/* service runs as a non-root user, with a read-only root filesystem, a tmpfs on /tmp, all Linux capabilities dropped and no-new-privileges. Ports are published on 127.0.0.1 only. The PostgreSQL password comes from .env, and compose refuses to start without it. The official postgres image is the one exception: it starts as root to fix data directory ownership, then drops to the postgres user.

Host names. The M1 API has no authentication, and a web page whose host name is re-pointed at 127.0.0.1 (DNS rebinding) is same-origin to itself, so CORS does not stop it. The API therefore answers only the Host names in MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS (default 127.0.0.1, localhost, api, plus the host of MAPI_API_URL) and returns 400 for anything else. The app's nginx server answers only MAPI_WEB_SERVER_NAMES (default 127.0.0.1 localhost) and closes the connection for any other host. The GCS shim does the same, for loopback names and the hosts of its endpoints (--allowed-host adds more). If you reach the stack under another name, such as a LAN host name, add it to both variables.

docs.title: Executor choice: local-process vs docker
docs.text:
The compose worker runs the local-process executor inside a runner-capable image: each run is a mapi-runner subprocess of the worker container. That is the default because it needs no Docker socket and is daemon-agnostic. Its trade-offs:

local-process in mapi/worker (default) docker executor (compose.override.example.yml) Isolation Process only: runs share the worker's uid, filesystem (including its keys, see below), /tmp and memory limit One container per run, from the exact runner image, with its own limits and a network that reaches only the shim Images One large image holding every plugin plus the control plane mapi/worker for the orchestrator, and per run the mapi/base-* image that ships the run's plugin (MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGES) Privileges None beyond the worker's own The worker mounts /var/run/docker.sock, which is root-equivalent on the host Networking Runs reach 127.0.0.1:4443 directly Run containers join the gcs-shim network namespace (MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK=container:mapi-gcs-shim) Use it for Day-to-day development, demos, CI Checking production images end to end, and self-hosted setups (gVisor runsc in v0.3)

Docker executor settings. MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGES maps a plugin namespace to its runner image: mmm.* and tabular.* run in mapi/base-bayes, sklearn.* in mapi/base-ml and ts.* in mapi/base-forecast. Runs without a model plugin (ingest, describe) use MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGE. The defaults are the tags make docker-build produces for the current version. MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK must give the run a way to reach the object store, because the bootstrap object and every signed URL point at it. In compose that means joining the shim's network namespace (container:mapi-gcs-shim). An internal Docker network that holds only the shim also works, provided MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT names the shim on that network. none would leave the runner with nothing to fetch its bootstrap object from, so the worker refuses to start with it.

Worker isolation in run containers. A run container starts its supervisor as root, with every Linux capability dropped except the few the uid split needs, and with no-new-privileges. The supervisor then starts the untrusted worker as uid 10001, which has no capabilities at all. So the worker cannot signal the supervisor, read its or the init process's environment, or write to its event pipe. The executor also sets MAPI_REQUIRE_ISOLATION=1, which makes the supervisor fail the run with SANDBOX_VIOLATION rather than run the worker under its own uid.

Neither mode is a multi-tenant boundary. Both are single-tenant local stacks, and the local-process executor refuses any multi-tenant profile.

What a local-process run can reach. Every run is a subprocess of mapi-server worker and runs as the same uid, 10001. There is no uid split before v0.3. Run code, meaning plugins and the steps they load, can therefore read everything the orchestrator can read:

  • the shim's control key (/shim/gcs/_shim/keys/control.json): storage.admin on every bucket, enough to read or rewrite bundles, datasets and run outputs and to mint signed URLs;
  • the bundle-signing key (/var/lib/mapi/keys/), enough to forge a manifest the API accepts;
  • the executions directory under /tmp/mapi-data, including the pid files that name the nonces of runs in flight.

In this mode, then, bundle signatures and the finalizer's output checks protect against accidents, not against hostile plugin code. The orchestrator marks itself non-dumpable, so run code cannot ptrace it or read its /proc/<pid>/environ (DATABASE_URL with the password) or its memory. The worker also logs this warning at start-up. Run only trusted plugin code under local-process. The docker executor does not have this exposure: each attempt runs in its own container with none of these files mounted. The worker's /tmp is the scratch space for local-process runs. Size it with MAPI_WORKER_TMPFS, MAPI_WORKER_MEMORY and MAPI_WORKER_CPUS in .env.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Compose reads .env in the repository root (copy .env.example). POSTGRES_PASSWORD is required; the MAPI_WORKER_* sizes, the image version (MAPI_VERSION, set by the Makefile) and the web image's MAPI_API_UPSTREAM and MAPI_WEB_SCRIPT_SRC_EXTRA are optional. Every variable is in the configuration reference.

compose.override.example.yml shows the two common changes: publishing PostgreSQL on the host, and switching the worker to the docker executor. Copy it to compose.override.yml (ignored by version control) to use it.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: A missing Docker daemon, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, an unhealthy api container, a read-only /tmp and ports that are already allocated are covered in Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Container images v0.2
docs.text:
The platform ships as six images (plus a worker target), built from images/<name>/Dockerfile with the repository root as the build context. They exist to run the exact production artifacts locally (Docker Compose), to back the docker executor, and to become the Cloud Run Jobs in v0.3.

make docker-build                      # every image, tagged mapi/<name>:<version>
make docker-build IMAGES="server web"  # a subset
make docker-pin-check                  # every base image pinned by digest?

docs.title: The images
docs.text:
Image Contents Runs as Entry point mapi/base-bayes mapi-runner, SDK, steps, plot recipes, mapi-pymc, the mmm.* and tabular.* plugins, a C++ compiler for PyTensor 10001 mapi-runner mapi/base-ml mapi-runner, SDK, steps, plot recipes, mapi-sklearn (sklearn.* plugins). No PyMC. 10001 mapi-runner mapi/base-forecast mapi-runner, SDK, steps, plot recipes, mapi-pymc, the ts.* plugins 10001 mapi-runner mapi/worker base-bayes plus the ts.* plugins and mapi-server (target worker of the base-bayes Dockerfile); for compose only 10001 mapi-server worker mapi/server The control plane: mapi-server, mapi-spec, the JSON-only mapi-plots core, docker-py. No science dependencies. 10001 mapi-server api (or worker, migrate) mapi/gcs-shim The local Cloud Storage emulator 10001 mapi-gcs-shim mapi/web nginx serving apps/web (port 8080) and apps/plot-sandbox (port 8081) 101 nginx

make docker-build IMAGES="server web" builds a subset. make docker-build builds them all, plus mapi/worker whenever base-bayes is in the set. Every image is labelled with the OCI title, version, revision (git commit) and created keys.

docs.title: How the Python images are built
docs.text:
Every Python image uses the same multi-stage pattern:

  1. manifests copies the build context and deletes everything except pyproject.toml and uv.lock files. Its output changes only when dependencies change.
  2. builder installs the third-party dependencies of the image's package set from those manifests alone (uv sync --frozen --no-install-workspace, once per package, into /opt/mapi/venv). BuildKit caches this layer, so editing source code does not reinstall PyMC. The builder then copies the sources and installs the workspace packages themselves, non-editable. Every version comes from uv.lock.
  3. runtime starts again from the same python:3.12-slim base, adds tini (and g++ for the PyMC images), creates user 10001, and copies in only the virtual environment. The images that run mapi-server (mapi/server and mapi/worker) also copy uv.lock to /opt/mapi/uv.lock and set MAPI_UV_LOCK_PATH to it. Its SHA-256 is the image digest that the API and the orchestrator cache the step and model catalog under, the same value make dev computes. Both images are built from one lock, so api and worker agree.

The package set is the MAPI_PACKAGES build argument. images/common/install_packages.py turns it into uv sync calls. The xgboost dependency nvidia-nccl-cu13, a 300 MB wheel used only for multi-GPU training, is never installed (MAPI_NO_INSTALL).

docs.title: Build-time guards
docs.text:
An image that is not what it claims to be fails to build:

  • Package assertions. images/common/assert_dists.py checks MAPI_ASSERT_PRESENT and MAPI_ASSERT_ABSENT against the real environment. For example, base-ml must not contain pymc, pytensor or numba, and server must not contain numpy, xarray, pandas, scipy, pyarrow, PyMC, mapi_sdk, mapi_runner or any plugin.
  • Import contracts in the control-plane image. The contracts stage of images/server/Dockerfile installs import-linter (hash-pinned from uv.lock) into a throwaway copy of the environment, and runs the repository's contracts against the packages exactly as installed. The runtime stage depends on that stage, so BuildKit cannot skip it.
  • Catalog export. The runner images load every installed step, model and plot plugin and write /opt/mapi/catalog.json with its digest (/opt/mapi/catalog.digest). If no steps or models are registered, the build fails.

The same claims are also proven without Docker: tests/devops/test_container_invariants.py computes each image's dependency closure from uv.lock (scripts/lock_closure.py) and checks it against the assertions.

docs.title: Compile caches and the read-only root filesystem
docs.text:
PyTensor compiles C at run time, and Numba caches machine code. Both caches are warmed during the build by compiling a small hierarchical model, then baked read-only into /opt/mapi/cache. PyTensor needs a writable compile directory, because it takes a lock and adds new modules. So at start-up the entry point (images/common/runner-entrypoint.sh) builds a symlink farm of the baked cache under /tmp/mapi-cache: real directories, with files that are symlinks to the baked objects. This costs a few KiB of RAM, which matters on Cloud Run's in-memory filesystem, and PyTensor accepts the relocated entries without recompiling.

HOME, PYTENSOR_FLAGS, NUMBA_CACHE_DIR and MPLCONFIGDIR all point under /tmp. The first three are on the runner's worker-environment allow-list (mapi_spec.run.WORKER_ENV_ALLOWLIST), so plugin code sees them after the supervisor scrubs the environment. The result is that every image runs with --read-only and a tmpfs on /tmp.

docker run mapi/base-bayes runs the runner. Arguments starting with - are passed to the runner, and any other command replaces it (docker run mapi/base-bayes python -c ...).

docs.title: The web image and the plot sandbox
docs.text:
mapi/web builds both Vite apps with pnpm, using --frozen-lockfile and --ignore-scripts, so no package lifecycle scripts run. It serves them from one unprivileged nginx with two server blocks. NGINX_ENVSUBST_TEMPLATE_DIR selects which blocks are rendered: /etc/nginx/templates/all (the default), web or plots. Origins are runtime settings rendered into the headers at start-up.

App (:8080, MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN) Plot sandbox (:8081, MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN) CSP default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' (no unsafe-eval, no inline scripts); frame-src = the plots origin; connect-src = self, MAPI_API_URL, MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT; frame-ancestors 'none' default-src 'none'; scripts, styles and images from its own origin only; connect-src = its own /topojson/ only; frame-ancestors = the app origin Other headers X-Frame-Options: DENY, nosniff, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, COOP and CORP same-origin, Trusted Types in report-only mode nosniff, no-referrer, Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * API access /v1/ is proxied to MAPI_API_UPSTREAM, unbuffered with a one-hour read timeout for SSE None: no proxy, and the CSP blocks it

The sandbox documents are framed with sandbox="allow-scripts" and no same-origin access, so they have an opaque origin. Their module scripts, styles and topojson are therefore fetched in CORS mode. That is why the sandbox answers with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *; the assets are static and public, and no cookies are involved. It is also why its CSP lists the plots origin explicitly next to 'self'.

MAPI_WEB_SCRIPT_SRC_EXTRA (empty by default) adds sources to the app's script-src. Use it only after a review, for example if a library needs 'wasm-unsafe-eval'. Trusted Types are in report-only mode until the SPA ships its policy.

docs.title: Base images and pinning
docs.text:
Every base image is a build argument with a readable tag and a digest:

ARG PYTHON_IMAGE=python:3.12-slim-trixie@sha256:a6e3…11b1

The Dockerfile frontend (# syntax=) and the compose postgres image are pinned the same way. make docker-pin re-resolves every tag through the registry API. It needs no Docker daemon, and you should review the resulting diff like any dependency bump. make docker-pin-check (also run in CI and by make release-check) fails if anything is unpinned.

docs.title: CI
docs.text:
.github/workflows/ci.yml builds every image, plus the worker target, on each push and pull request, using the GitHub Actions layer cache. Images are never pushed. A separate job checks the digest pins and validates both compose files with docker compose config.

With the images built and a Docker daemon running, uv run pytest tests/devops/test_compose_smoke.py -m docker boots postgres, gcs-shim, migrate, api and worker under a throw-away project name. It publishes no host ports. It then checks that api and worker started and that they agree on the values bundle verification depends on: the image digest and the bundle-signing key.

docs.title: Local, without Docker v0.2
docs.text:
make dev runs the whole platform on your machine without Docker. PostgreSQL comes from the pgserver wheel and object storage from the GCS shim, so the only requirements are the uv workspace and, for the web app, Node.js with pnpm.

make install          # uv sync --all-packages (+ pnpm install once apps/ exist)
make dev              # start everything; Ctrl-C stops everything
make seed             # in another shell: load the E33 demo data and spec
open http://127.0.0.1:5173

The quickstart walks through fitting, inspecting and scoring the demo model from the browser. This page explains what make dev runs, how to work on one component, and where local state lives.

docs.title: What make dev starts
docs.text:
scripts/dev.py is a small process supervisor. It starts each service in dependency order and waits until the service is ready before starting the ones that need it. All output goes to one terminal, with each line prefixed by its service name (coloured when the output is a terminal).

flowchart LR
    pg[(postgres<br/>.local/pg)] --> migrate
    shim[gcs-shim<br/>:4443] --> api
    migrate --> api[api<br/>:8000]
    migrate --> worker
    shim --> worker
    api --> web[web<br/>:5173]
    plots[plots<br/>:5174]
Service Command Ready when postgres Embedded PostgreSQL 16 (pgserver), data in .local/pg, unix socket only. Skipped when DATABASE_URL is set. pg_ctl reports it running and the mapi database exists gcs-shim mapi-gcs-shim serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4443 --cors-origin <web origin> --root .local/gcs The port accepts connections migrate mapi-server migrate (runs once) It exits with status 0 api mapi-server api --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 GET /healthz returns 2xx worker mapi-server worker with MAPI_EXECUTOR=local-process: dispatcher, reconciler, event ingestion and the finalizer queue. Every run is a mapi-runner supervisor process that starts its own worker process. Started web pnpm --filter @mapi/web dev --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5173 --strictPort The port accepts connections plots pnpm --filter @mapi/plot-sandbox dev --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5174 --strictPort The port accepts connections

Every service receives the same resolved environment: MAPI_ENV, DATABASE_URL, MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT, MAPI_API_URL, MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN, MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN and MAPI_DATA_DIR. The values come from mapi_spec.localdev.LocalDev, the same contract the services themselves read, so they cannot disagree about ports. The configuration reference lists every variable.

The plot sandbox is a separate origin

Plots render in an <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts"> served from MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN (port 5174), never from the app origin (port 5173). LocalDev refuses a configuration that puts both on the same origin.

docs.title: Shutting down
docs.text:
Ctrl+C (or make stop from another shell) stops the services in reverse start order. Each service runs in its own process group. The supervisor sends that group SIGTERM, and sends SIGKILL if it is still running after the grace period (10 s, --grace to change). Child processes such as Vite's esbuild are stopped with their parent. A second Ctrl+C kills everything at once. The embedded PostgreSQL is stopped last, unless you ran scripts/dev.py up --keep-db.

If any long-running service exits on its own, the supervisor stops the whole stack and exits with a non-zero status. It never restarts anything silently: the log above the shutdown shows the reason.

docs.title: The first start
docs.text:
On its first start against a new environment the worker logs no catalog for sha256:…: queued describe run. The catalog (the steps, models and plot recipes installed in the runner, with their settings schemas and schema effects) is produced by a sandboxed describe run of the real runner and cached per uv.lock digest, so it is rebuilt only when the locked dependencies change. Until it is ready, spec validation reports the catalog as unavailable; it takes a few seconds.

Runs use the same isolation as in production, minus what a laptop cannot do: the run event DEV_MODE_ISOLATION notes that the worker process runs as your user, without a uid split or no_new_privs.

Plugin code runs as you, next to the platform's keys

Without a uid split, run code (plugins and the steps they load) can read every file your user can. That includes the shim's control key (.local/gcs/_shim/keys/control.json, full access to every bucket), the bundle-signing key (.local/keys/) and the executions directory. So a hostile plugin could forge a signed bundle or rewrite outputs after the finalizer checked them. The orchestrator makes itself non-dumpable on Linux, so run code cannot read its environment (DATABASE_URL) or its memory. The worker logs the same warning when it starts. Only run plugin code you trust in make dev.

docs.title: Everyday commands
docs.text:
Command What it does make dev (or make run) Start the stack in the foreground make dev ONLY=api Start api and what it depends on (gcs-shim, migrate) make dev WITHOUT=web,plots Everything except the two Vite servers (for example while the web app is not built yet) make stop Stop a stack running in another shell, then its embedded PostgreSQL make status Which services are up, and whether PostgreSQL is running make migrate Apply database migrations once. It starts the embedded PostgreSQL if needed and stops it again afterwards. make db-shell psql on the dev database (the embedded server or DATABASE_URL) make seed Load the E33 demo datasets and the eu-geo-mmm spec through the HTTP API (make seed SIZE=full for the large variant) make e2e The end-to-end suites against the running stack: pytest -m e2e (tests/e2e, through the Python client), then the Playwright @e2e suite (apps/web/e2e, through the browser) make clean-local Delete MAPI_DATA_DIR (database, objects, supervisor state). It refuses while anything is running; YES=1 skips the prompt. uv run python scripts/dev.py env Print the resolved environment as export lines, for running a component by hand

make seed uses only the public API. It creates the datasets eu_media_daily, fx_daily and holidays_eu, uploads each table to the signed URL the API returns, waits for the sandboxed ingest runs, then creates the spec pointing at the new dataset versions. Running it again adds new dataset versions and a new spec revision. The datasets themselves are reused. SIZE is only read from the make command line: some toolchains (conda's compilers) export a SIZE variable of their own.

uv run python scripts/seed.py --export demo/ writes the same tables, the E33 score payloads and the spec as files instead, for uploading through the web app.

docs.title: End-to-end tests
docs.text:
make e2e drives the M1 flow through the running stack: upload the E33 data, validate and fit the spec, follow the run over SSE, check the signed manifest and the bundle, score an 8-week forecast, a new market, a weekly EUR plan and counterfactuals, and probe the security boundaries that are visible from outside (the bootstrap object is gone, forged events are refused, the plot iframe is an opaque origin). Start make dev first; both suites read the same MAPI_* variables, so export them in the shell that runs make e2e when you moved a port. The browser suite writes screenshots to apps/web/e2e/screenshots/ (git-ignored).

export MAPI_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8010   # only if you moved the API
make dev                                     # shell 1
make e2e                                     # shell 2: about 5 minutes

The mocked Playwright smoke suite (pnpm --filter @mapi/web test) serves its own build on port 5173, so run it while make dev is stopped.

docs.title: Working on one component
docs.text:
To run a component yourself, for example with a debugger or auto-reload, either exclude it and start it by hand with the same environment:

make dev WITHOUT=api,web           # web depends on api, so exclude it too
eval "$(uv run python scripts/dev.py env)"
mapi-server api --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000

or replace its command with MAPI_DEV_<NAME>_CMD. The command is shell-quoted; <NAME> is GCS_SHIM, MIGRATE, API, WORKER, WEB or PLOTS:

MAPI_DEV_API_CMD="uvicorn mapi_server.app:app --reload --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000" make dev

The readiness probe still applies, so a replacement api must answer GET /healthz.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
make dev reads your shell environment. It does not read .env, which is only for docker compose. With nothing set, everything uses the defaults above. To change something, export the variable first:

export MAPI_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9000          # move the API (and its probe) to port 9000
export DATABASE_URL=postgresql://me@localhost/mapi  # use your own PostgreSQL instead of pgserver
make dev

Export the same MAPI_* URLs in every shell that talks to the stack (make seed, make e2e, the CLI, the Python client). The configuration reference lists every variable, including those that only compose or the images use.

docs.title: Where state lives
docs.text:
All local state lives under MAPI_DATA_DIR, which defaults to .local/ in the repository root and is ignored by git.

.local/
├─ pg/                    PostgreSQL data directory (pgserver); log in pg/log
├─ gcs/                   GCS shim objects (buckets mapi-local-*)
│  └─ _shim/keys/         the shim's principals: control.json (control plane), exec.json (runs)
├─ keys/                  bundle-signing-p256.pem: signs bundle manifests (stands in for KMS)
├─ executions/            per-run scratch of the local executor (removed when a run ends)
└─ dev/supervisor.json    pid of the running supervisor and its services (make stop/status)

Deleting keys/ makes every registered model version unusable: their manifests no longer verify, so the API refuses to mint download links for them (INTEGRITY_FAILURE).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Port conflicts, a stale supervisor, PostgreSQL that will not start, failed migrations, an API that never becomes ready and blank plots are covered in Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Troubleshooting v0.2
docs.text: Start with make status: it shows which services of a make dev stack are up and whether the embedded PostgreSQL is running. The web app's Settings page shows the API's readiness checks, and curl -s $MAPI_API_URL/readyz shows the same from a shell.

docs.title: Port conflicts
docs.text:
make dev refuses to start when a port it needs is taken:

cannot start - fix these first
  - 127.0.0.1:8000 is already in use

Another make dev (in another terminal or worktree), a compose stack, or an unrelated program owns the port. Find it, and either stop it or move the platform:

lsof -iTCP:8000 -sTCP:LISTEN          # who has it?
make stop                              # if it is another make dev of this checkout

To move the platform, export the addresses in every shell that talks to it, then start again. Every component (make dev, make seed, make e2e, the CLI, the Python client, the web app's build) reads the same variables:

export MAPI_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18000
export MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:14443
export MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:15173
export MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:15174
make dev
Port Variable Service 8000 MAPI_API_URL API 4443 MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT GCS shim (signed URLs point here) 5173 MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN Web app 5174 MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN Plot sandbox

A state directory belongs to one stack at a time; to run two stacks side by side, also give each its own MAPI_DATA_DIR. The Playwright smoke suite (pnpm --filter @mapi/web test) serves its own build on 5173 and 5174, so run it while make dev is stopped. Docker Compose publishes the same four ports as make dev, on purpose: run one or the other.

docs.title: The local stack
docs.text:
cannot start - fix these first

The supervisor checks every requirement before starting anything. Besides ports:

  • module 'mapi_server.__main__' not found: your environment is stale. Run uv sync --all-packages (or make install).
  • exe 'pnpm' not found or run pnpm install first: install pnpm (corepack enable) and the JavaScript dependencies (pnpm install), or skip the front end with make dev WITHOUT=web,plots.
already running (supervisor pid N) A previous make dev is still alive, perhaps in another terminal. Run make stop. If that process is gone but its state file stayed behind (after kill -9, for example), the next start detects the dead pid and ignores the file. plots exited unexpectedly with status 143; stopping the stack Something outside the stack sent the service SIGTERM (a pkill vite, for example). The supervisor never restarts services silently: it stops everything and exits. Start it again; runs that were in flight are recovered by the reconciler as a new attempt. postgres | failed to start Read .local/pg/log. If the data directory came from a different PostgreSQL major version, or is corrupt, run make clean-local; this deletes the local database. An orphaned server from an earlier crash is stopped by make stop. migrate exited with status 1 The migration's own output is printed just above this line. Fix the migration, or reset the database with make stop && make clean-local, then run make dev again. api not ready after 60s The API process is running but GET /healthz never succeeded. Look at the api | lines. A wrong DATABASE_URL, or a GCS shim that is not reachable, are the usual causes. Validation says the catalog is unavailable On the first start against a new environment (and after every change to uv.lock) the worker queues a sandboxed describe run to export the catalog: no catalog for sha256:…: queued describe run. It takes a few seconds. If it fails, its run page under Runs shows why. The server refuses MAPI_PROFILE MAPI_PROFILE is also the CLI's config-profile variable. If you exported a client profile name, unset it in the shell that runs make dev (the server accepts only single-tenant or multi-tenant). Leftover processes after a crash Each service runs in its own process group, which you can find with ps -o pid,pgid,command. make stop also kills the process groups recorded in .local/dev/supervisor.json when the supervisor itself does not respond within 30 s.

docs.title: The web app and plots
docs.text: API unreachable in the header, or the app cannot load anything The app calls the API at the VITE_API_BASE it was started with. make dev sets it from MAPI_API_URL; if you start Vite yourself, set it too. The API must also allow the app's origin: it allows MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN, so both must agree. Plots stay blank MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN and MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN must be different origins, the plot sandbox must be running (make status), and the sandbox must allow the app's origin (VITE_APP_ORIGINS, set by make dev). The browser console names the blocked origin. Uploads fail in the browser The browser PUTs files straight to MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT. The shim must allow the app's origin (--cors-origin, set by make dev from MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN), and the app's CSP must allow the storage origin (VITE_STORAGE_ORIGINS).

docs.title: Runs and scoring
docs.text: A run is stalled No progress arrived for a while. It is a warning, not a failure: the executor's own status decides whether the run is alive. A long PyTensor compile on the first fit of a new machine can cause it. DEV_MODE_ISOLATION on every run Expected on a laptop: the local executor runs the model code as your own user, without a separate uid or no_new_privs. See the security model. SIDE_TABLE_COVERAGE when scoring A side table with score_policy: supplied (in the demo, fx) must be given in the score request (side_tables: {fx: dataset://default/fx_daily@latest}) and cover the scored dates. Enter the pipeline after the step that uses it (inputs_stage: weekly) to skip it. MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED, UNSEEN_LEVELS, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT, … Typed errors from the static checks: the request asks for something the model cannot answer honestly. The problem's detail and JSON pointer say what; the codes are listed in Error codes. RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED The run ran out of memory or scratch space. Retry on the run page suggests the next resource class. Under compose, raise MAPI_WORKER_MEMORY and MAPI_WORKER_TMPFS. INTEGRITY_FAILURE when downloading The bundle's signed manifest no longer verifies, so the API refuses to mint download links. Locally this happens when .local/keys/ was deleted: the old model versions cannot be trusted any more. Fit again.

docs.title: Docker and compose
docs.text: error: the Docker daemon is not reachable make docker-build and make compose-up check docker info first. Start Docker Desktop, Colima or dockerd, or use make dev, which needs no Docker. required variable POSTGRES_PASSWORD is missing a value Copy .env.example to .env and set POSTGRES_PASSWORD. Compose reads .env from the repository root. image check failed: forbidden distribution 'numpy' is installed (server build) A control-plane dependency started pulling in a science package. Run uv run python scripts/lock_closure.py "mapi-server[docker]" --lacks numpy to see the closure, then find which dependency brings numpy in. Contracts: 1 broken in the contracts stage Server code imports a forbidden module. make lint (lint-imports) shows the same failure locally, with the import chain. PyTensor found no C++ compiler (base-bayes / base-forecast build) g++ is missing from MAPI_APT_PACKAGES. The PyMC images need it at run time too. The api container is unhealthy make compose-logs SERVICE=api. Typical causes are that migrate failed (look at its logs), or that the DATABASE_URL password does not match the database volume, which happens after you change POSTGRES_PASSWORD. In that case reset with make compose-down VOLUMES=1; this deletes the data. no bundle-signing key at /var/lib/mapi/keys/... and MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_CREATE is off api or worker started before migrate created the key, or without the keys volume. Check make compose-logs SERVICE=migrate. Never point the two at different keys: the API would reject every bundle the worker signs with INTEGRITY_FAILURE. 400 Invalid host header from the API, or nginx closes the connection The stack answers only known host names (a DNS-rebinding guard). If you reach it under a name other than 127.0.0.1, localhost or api, add that name to MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS (the API) and MAPI_WEB_SERVER_NAMES (the web image's nginx). mapi-entrypoint: /tmp/mapi-cache is not writable The container runs with a read-only root filesystem but without a writable /tmp. Add --tmpfs /tmp (compose already does). Port already allocated on docker compose up A make dev stack, or another process, holds 4443, 8000, 5173 or 5174. Stop it with make stop. Both stacks use the same ports on purpose, so the same URLs work with either. nginx exits with host not found or invalid number of arguments in "set" MAPI_API_UPSTREAM is empty or malformed. It must be a URL without a path, for example http://api:8000.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes are documented here. The project follows Semantic Versioning; milestone releases are tagged on main.

docs.title: [0.2.0] — M1: local vertical slice — 2026-10-15
docs.text:
The platform now runs end to end on one machine. From the Expert web app (or the CLI, the Python client or plain HTTP) you can upload data, write and validate a spec, fit an E33-style hierarchical geo MMM, inspect it, and score it: an 8-week forecast, a new market, a weekly EUR plan and counterfactuals. Real Cloud Run and multi-tenancy come in M2 (v0.3.0). In summary:

  • server (mapi-server): a single-tenant FastAPI control plane on PostgreSQL with procrastinate. It includes a dispatcher, a level-triggered reconciler, a metadata-only finalizer with signed bundle manifests, HMAC-verified run events, SSE with resume, and local-process and docker executors. It never imports plugin code or array libraries.
  • runner (mapi-runner): a trusted supervisor and an untrusted worker harness for ingest, describe, validate, fit, score, evaluate, derive and render runs. It produces signed events, checkpoints, partial manifests and the ui/ views the web app reads.
  • gcs-shim (mapi-gcs-shim): a local Cloud Storage emulator. It provides generations, server-side CRC32C/MD5, V4 signed URLs and POST policies, per-principal permissions and a write-once bundles bucket.
  • web and plot-sandbox: the Expert web app (YAML editor with live validation, runs with live progress and logs, model inspection, scoring) and a separate-origin, CSP-locked plot renderer.
  • client and cli: a typed sync/async Python client for every v1 endpoint, and mapi for local and remote work.
  • devops: make dev (the whole stack without Docker), digest-pinned images, docker compose, make seed, make e2e and make release-check.
  • conformance: the corpus also runs through the live stack (run --stack URL), and a sklearn conformal fixture is added (7 fixtures in all).
  • docs: a 10-minute quickstart, guides to the web app, CLI, client and HTTP API, a deployment section, an architecture overview and a security model.

Every workspace package and both web apps are versioned 0.2.0. Contract v0.1 gains only additive changes.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• spec: the M1 shared contracts, so the API, runner, executors, GCS shim, web app and plot sandbox can be built in parallel against one source of truth:
  • mapi_spec.run: the run state machine (RunState, RunTrigger, a pure transition() with owners, failure classes and attempt bumps), the RunSpec bootstrap object, typed event payloads, canonical HMAC-SHA256 event signing, the {"mapi_event": …} stdout format, OutputManifest with metadata-only verification, the signed BundleManifest, RunnerEnv and exit codes.
  • mapi_spec.storage: ObjectMeta, the async ObjectStore protocol, signed GET/PUT and POST policy shapes, GCS-style CRC32C/MD5 helpers, storage errors and the bucket/key naming scheme.
  • mapi_spec.api: REST DTOs for the v1 surface (each with examples), SSE/Prefer/idempotency helpers and M1_ENDPOINTS, the machine-readable endpoint table.
  • mapi_spec.localdev: local ports, origins and environment variable names.
  • spec (additive, contract v0.1): RunKind gains the fan-out parents (sweep, backtest, sbc, campaign); RunEventType gains checkpoint and metric; RunEvent.ts must be timezone-aware and is normalised to UTC; PlotSpec carries a schema example. The new schemas join export_schemas() and the contract snapshot.
  • docs: the "HTTP API (v1)" and "Run protocol" reference pages (docs/reference/http-api.md, docs/reference/run-protocol.md).
  • gcs-shim: mapi-gcs-shim, a local Cloud Storage emulator. It serves the GCS JSON-API subset the platform uses, with generation and metageneration preconditions, plus V4 signed GET (with Range) and PUT URLs and V4 POST policies (key prefix and size range). It adds IAM-lite principals (control, and exec with bootstrap get and delete only), a write-once bundles bucket, lifecycle sweeps, and server-computed CRC32C and MD5 on a crash-safe filesystem backend. ShimObjectStore and the import-guarded GcsObjectStore implement mapi_spec.storage.ObjectStore, and a pytest11 plugin provides the gcs_shim fixture. See docs/reference/gcs-shim.md.
  • runner: mapi-runner, the sandboxed run harness. A trusted supervisor reads and deletes the bootstrap object, starts the untrusted worker with a scrubbed environment (uid 10001 and no-new-privs as root, dev mode otherwise), signs every stdout event, caps logs, events, scratch and outputs, handles SIGTERM/deadline with partial manifests from checkpoints, and uploads outputs plus a signed OutputManifest. The worker runs ingest (CSV/Parquet with a column mapping or the MFF preset, zarr zip, netCDF), describe, validate (dry run), fit (bundle, sidecars, plots, ui/ views, checkpoints), score, evaluate, derive and render through the SDK harness. See docs/reference/runner.md.
  • server: the M1 control plane (mapi-server api|worker|migrate|dev): FastAPI /v1 API covering every M1_ENDPOINTS row plus /v1/me, spec diff, ui/ redirects and :evaluate; SQLAlchemy 2 + Alembic schema (every row carries tenant_id/project_id) with procrastinate on the same Postgres; dispatcher (token bucket, intent row before submit), level-triggered reconciler (executor status is the liveness source of truth, STALLED is a warning, orphan adoption by nonce), metadata-only finalizer with server-side copy and EC P-256 signed bundle manifests verified at URL minting; HMAC-verified event ingestion from the executor pipe and POST /internal/events; SSE with Last-Event-ID resume over one LISTEN connection per process; local-process and docker/docker-gvisor executors; OpenAPI 3.1 export (python -m mapi_server.openapi).
  • web: apps/web, the Expert-mode web app (React 19, TanStack Router/Query/Table, Tailwind + shadcn/ui, Monaco + monaco-yaml with live :validate diagnostics, SSE run progress per chain, dataset upload via signed URLs, model inspection, scoring) and the Guided-mode shell; a pnpm workspace at the repo root.
  • plot-sandbox: apps/plot-sandbox, the separate-origin Vega-Lite/Plotly renderer with a strict CSP and a validated postMessage protocol.
  • devops: containers, local orchestration and developer tooling for M1:
  • images/: base-bayes (with a worker target), base-ml (no PyMC), base-forecast, server (control plane only, checked with import-linter and package assertions at build time), gcs-shim and web (nginx serving the app and the plot sandbox on separate origins with strict CSPs). All are digest-pinned, run as non-root with a read-only root filesystem, and have health checks. The runner images bake the catalog JSON and a warmed PyTensor/Numba cache.
  • docker-compose.yml (postgres 16, gcs-shim, migrate, api, worker with the local-process executor, web, plot-sandbox), compose.override.example.yml and .env.example, which documents every MAPI_* variable.
  • scripts/dev.py (make dev): runs the whole stack without Docker (pgserver PostgreSQL, GCS shim, migrations, api, worker and both Vite servers) with readiness probes, prefixed logs and clean process-group shutdown. Also stop, status, migrate, db-shell and clean.
  • New make targets: dev/run, stop, status, migrate, db-shell, seed (the E33 demo through the API), clean-local, docker-build, docker-pin, compose-up/down/logs, web-build, web-test, test-all, e2e and release-check.
  • CI: a web job, a build-only docker job for every image, and digest-pin and compose checks.
  • Docs: "Local development" and "Containers and docker compose" (Operations), and deploy/README.md.
  • client: mapi-client, the typed Python client (Client, AsyncClient) for every M1_ENDPOINTS row: DTO-typed resources, RFC 7807 errors as MapiError subclasses, idempotency keys and safe retries, lazy pagination, SSE with Last-Event-ID resume, dataset upload through signed URLs, Prefer: wait scoring, CRC32C-checked transfers without the API token. See docs/reference/cli.md.
  • cli: mapi (new, check, fit, score locally or --remote, runs, datasets, catalog, plugin init|test, spec upgrade, serve, config), with --json output and ANSI-stripped untrusted text.
  • spec: mapi_spec.jobs, the run job contract shared by the dispatcher and the runner (IngestJob, DescribeJob, ScoreJob, EvaluateJob, DeriveJob, RenderJob, input and output object names, MetricsSidecar, DATASET_SCHEMA_ATTR), and mapi_spec.views, the UI views the web app reads (mapi.preview/v1, mapi.profile/v1, mapi.tree-index/v1).
  • gcs-shim: CORS for the web origin (--cors-origin, default $MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN) so browsers can use signed URLs, and a wrap hook on ShimServer.
  • server: mapi-server dev (and so mapi serve) starts an embedded GCS shim when nothing listens at MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT; the OpenAPI document publishes the run-event payload schemas.
  • docs: "CLI and Python client" and "Web app and plot sandbox" reference pages; the run protocol documents job payloads, object names and UI views.
  • server: GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/plots (list_run_plots) returns the plots a succeeded run rendered, sanitized on every read; the client has runs.plots().
  • web: the score form takes the input dataset and the spec's side tables (defaulting to the versions the fit used), shows the score run's own plots and pivots the summary by statistic.
  • devops: scripts/seed.py --export DIR writes the E33 demo tables, score payloads and spec as files for the web app.
  • tests: the M1 exit criterion end to end against the running stack: tests/e2e (Python client: fit, SSE, signed manifest and bundle generations, the bundle read back with the corpus' checks, five E33 score requests, bootstrap deletion, forged events) and apps/web/e2e/m1-flow.e2e.spec.ts (the same flow in the browser, plots in the sandbox iframe); a server test proves the finalizer refuses tampered output of the real runner.
  • docs: "Your first model in the web app" guide; the local-development page covers the first start, make e2e and the state under .local/.
  • docs: the M1 documentation set. A landing page with screenshots of the running platform (docs/assets/screenshots/, captured by scripts/docs_screenshots.mjs and shrunk by scripts/optimise_screenshots.py, make docs-screenshots); a validated "zero to first model in 10 minutes" quickstart; guides to every page of the Expert web app, the CLI, the Python client and the HTTP API; an OpenAPI explorer page (a vendored, hash-pinned Redoc bundle over the committed openapi.json, scripts/vendor_redoc.py); a Deployment section (local, Docker Compose, container images, a configuration reference naming every MAPI_* variable, troubleshooting); an architecture overview and a security model; an updated roadmap (M2 cloud and multi-tenant, M3 Guided mode). scripts/gen_docs_reference.py (run by make docs-build and the MkDocs hook) generates the CLI reference from the Typer app, the server settings table from Settings, and copies the OpenAPI document. conformance/tests/test_docs_platform.py runs the CLI walkthrough, checks the generated pages, the configuration reference, the Redoc pin and the screenshots, and (under make e2e) runs the client, HTTP and remote-CLI walkthroughs against the live stack.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• docs: anchors are validated in strict builds; mermaid is pinned to 11.17.2 instead of Material's moving mermaid@11.
  • server: the object store is ShimObjectStore built from the shim's control key file (MAPI_GCS_ROOT, default $MAPI_DATA_DIR/gcs, or MAPI_GCS_KEY_FILE); local executions get the exec token from the same directory unless MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN is set. RunSpec payloads and input names follow mapi_spec.jobs (score data under dataset, side tables under side.<name>, bundle.manifest passed to score runs); evaluate/derive default to the fit dataset and render gets the bundle's plots.json. metrics.json is read as MetricsSidecar.
  • runner: fit writes coords.json and ingest writes summary.json (the control plane's CoordPlan metadata); preview.json, profile.json and ui/tree_index.json follow mapi_spec.views. The runner tests run against the real GCS shim.
  • web: openapi.json and schema.d.ts are generated from the real server (apps/web/scripts/gen_openapi.py, checked in CI); the @e2e specs can reuse a running stack on any ports.
  • devops: make dev starts mapi-gcs-shim serve --root … with CORS and passes the resolved URLs to the Vite servers; compose mounts the shim volume read-only into api and worker (MAPI_GCS_ROOT) so they can load the principal keys.
  • sdk: zarr zips record their data-variable order (group attribute _mapi_var_order, removed again on read).
  • devops: make e2e runs the browser @e2e suite (it ran the mocked smoke suite).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• spec: static score validation binds dataset names to canonical names at every inputs_stage, as the runtime does (a weekly EUR plan entering at weekly was refused).
  • server: the dry-run and evaluate endpoints declare their Run response in OpenAPI.
  • seed: make seed ships E33's raw schema with the data, so the fit keeps market: new_levels and new-market scoring works.
  • client: the run event stream decodes the live progress and log frames (sent without an id) as RunLiveFrame; it aborted on the first progress frame of a real fit.
  • server: model lineage records the side-table versions a fit read (it was always empty).
  • sdk: variables come back from a zarr zip in their written order; plot recipes that default to the first variable chose a random one on a bundle read back from storage (mmm.response_curves failed). The response-curve recipe also prefers variables with a channel dim.
  • plot-sandbox: composite Vega-Lite specs (concat, facet) rendered at zero width; they now keep their own size and scroll when wider than the frame.
  • plots: the convergence table's columns no longer overlap; the fan chart draws and captions only the intervals a summary holds.
  • web: a spec opened right after "Save spec" no longer shows unsaved changes (the editor used CRLF for models created empty on Windows user agents), so Fit is enabled; the run page's result column no longer overflows; result tables show dates as dates.
  • devops: make seed ignores a SIZE exported by other toolchains (conda).
  • devops: the compose api and worker containers start. The mapi/server and mapi/worker images bake uv.lock and set MAPI_UV_LOCK_PATH, so both resolve the same image digest. Before, neither could resolve one and both failed at start-up.
  • devops: compose keeps the bundle-signing key on a keys volume that migrate writes and api/worker mount read-only (MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_PATH, MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_CREATE=false). Each container used to mint its own key on its tmpfs, so the API rejected every bundle the worker signed, and a restart orphaned every model. mapi-server migrate now creates the key, and concurrent first starts converge on one key.
  • server: mapi-server api|worker|dev make themselves non-dumpable on Linux, so local-process runs (same uid) cannot read their environment or memory. The worker's start-up warning and the operations docs state what such runs can still read.
  • server: a Prefer: wait long-poll stops waiting when its client disconnects.
  • client: models.score() extends the read timeout of each long-poll by its wait and treats a read timeout as "still running", so scores slower than about 90 s no longer raise TransportError. stream_events() counts only connections that deliver nothing towards max_reconnects, so it follows long fits behind proxies that cut connections.
  • cli: run progress and state messages are never parsed as rich markup (no terminal hyperlink injection, no MarkupError aborting mapi fit).
  • devops: .env.example documents every mapi-server setting, and the devops test now derives the list from Settings.

docs.title: Fixed (M1 review: spec, runner, shim and plots)
docs.text:
• runner: fit runs write ui/preprocess.json (mapi_spec.views.PreprocessView, mapi.preprocess/v1): each step's resolved plugin, learned JSON and small numeric state arrays, so the web app's Preprocessing tab is no longer empty.
  • runner: an INFRA_ERROR reported by the worker fails the run as a user error. Only failures the supervisor sees itself are retried automatically as infrastructure failures.
  • runner: every string the worker sends has ANSI, control and bidi characters stripped. The CLI's strip_control also removes the bidi ranges.
  • server, gcs-shim: the artifacts upload policy is create-only (post_policy(create_only=True) signs x-goog-if-generation-match: 0, and the shim answers 412 for an existing key).
  • plots: recipes draw from mapi_plots.palette, whose dark variants keep at least 3:1 contrast, and the plot sandbox swaps them in dark mode. The decomposition legend is titled "component" when baseline or controls join the channels. Faceted fans and MMM curves give each panel its own axes, in coordinate order.
  • conformance: new sklearn_store_demand fixture. Fixtures not yet ported are listed in DEFERRED with reasons (list --deferred). run --stack URL drives fixtures through the API.

docs.title: Fixed (M1 review: server)
docs.text:
• GET /v1/runs/{id}/plots and score results are scoped to the caller's tenant and project.
  • Runner JSON is parsed with a nesting limit, and deep nesting is reported as INTEGRITY_FAILURE.
  • Bundle inputs are verified again at dispatch and on :retry.
  • The API refuses unexpected Host headers (MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS), nginx answers only MAPI_WEB_SERVER_NAMES and the GCS shim checks hosts too, which guards against DNS rebinding.
  • Ingest and spec validation enforce the per-resource-class data caps (PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE).
  • An omitted fit seed is pinned to 0 at submission, so lineage records the seed actually used.
  • Run lifecycle:
  • A cancelled checkpointed fit ends PARTIAL and can be resumed (new CANCELLING --complete--> FINALIZING edge).
  • :cancel on a finalizing run is a no-op.
  • A run stopped at its deadline fails as TIMEOUT or finalizes as PARTIAL.
  • An exit counts only after its event backlog is ingested.
  • A restarted reconciler re-adopts live executions.
  • Stalled finalize jobs are re-queued.
  • Executor cancels no longer block the reconcile pass.
  • SSE reads the run state before its events, and a run never shows another attempt's progress.
  • Docker executor:
  • Each plugin namespace gets its own versioned mapi/base-* image (MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGES).
  • Run containers join the shim's network namespace; none is refused.
  • The supervisor and the worker run under separate uids (10001 for the worker), and MAPI_REQUIRE_ISOLATION=1 fails a run closed rather than falling back to dev mode.
  • The import-linter contract also forbids plugin packages, plot recipes and columnar libraries in mapi_server.
  • Docs: invalid submissions are refused without a run, and REJECTED is reserved.

docs.title: Fixed (M1 review: web)
docs.text:
• Plots:
  • The plot host accepts a sandbox exported reply only for an export the app requested.
  • Downloading a score output saves a checksum-verified file instead of leaving the app.
  • Run pages:
  • Live progress and log SSE frames, which the server sends without an id, are delivered.
  • The live log view follows the tail.
  • Performance: Monaco and Arrow are no longer in first paint, and routes are lazy-loaded. A build-time budget keeps first-paint JavaScript under 640 KiB (it was 4.26 MB; now about 515 KB).
  • Spec editor:
  • It never replaces unsaved edits when a newer revision appears.
  • Save sends the revision the text came from as parent_revision.
  • Accessibility:
  • No sideways scroll at phone width, and the compact nav shows every page.
  • Status colours and form borders meet WCAG AA.
  • Score form errors are marked on their fields and announced.
  • The Score page resets its form and results when the version changes, and shows a loading state while the version loads.

docs.title: Fixed (integration)
docs.text:
• tests: a devops docstring no longer names a fake MAPI_ variable that the configuration reference test picked up.
  • web: openapi.json and schema.d.ts are regenerated (the cancel endpoint documents the finalizing no-op).
  • docs: pages written before the review fixes landed now describe the shared compose signing key, ui/preprocess.json, the docker executor's network and images, and the new MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS, MAPI_WEB_SERVER_NAMES, MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGES, MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_CREATE and MAPI_REQUIRE_ISOLATION settings.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• The docker executor, the compose stack and the new compose smoke test have not run against a real Docker daemon yet.
  • Under the local-process executor, run code shares the orchestrator's uid and can read its key files. The uid split is M2.
  • MAPI_PROFILE means a config profile to the CLI and client, but the deployment profile to the server.
  • The API's built-in /docs and /redoc pages load assets from a public CDN.
  • Conformance fixtures E13, E84-lite, E82-slim and E45 are deferred: they need new plugins or run kinds.

docs.title: [0.1.0] — M0: contract layer — 2026-10-15
docs.text:
First milestone release: the typed contract layer and the in-process xarray runtime, with no platform services yet. In summary:

  • spec (mapi-spec): pure-Pydantic contracts (DataSchema, SchemaEffect, ModelSpec, ScoreRequest, capabilities, representations, PlotSpec envelope, error codes) with static validation and JSON Schema export, frozen as contract v0.1.
  • sdk (mapi-sdk): wire formats, the stage/split/context/replay/inverse pipeline engine, CoordPlan, bundles without pickle, the fit_spec/score_bundle harness, the in-process executor and the mapi_sdk.testing contract kit.
  • steps (mapi-steps): 28 built-in core.* preprocessing steps and five split kinds, each with exported static effects.
  • pymc (mapi-pymc) and sklearn (mapi-sklearn): model adapters where an author writes only build() or estimator().
  • plots (mapi-plots): JSON-only Vega-Lite/Plotly sanitizer and the core, mmm and ml recipe catalogs.
  • plugins: mmm.hierarchical_geo, mmm.pymc_marketing, ts.hsgp_trend, ts.gaussian_hmm, tabular.hierarchical_glm and tabular.regressor.
  • conformance (mapi-conformance): the corpus runner and six fixtures (E02, C08, E24, store demand, E33, pymc-marketing), all passing at --size tiny.
  • docs: the MkDocs Material site with tested snippets and generated catalogs.

Every workspace package is versioned 0.1.0. The server, runner, CLI, client and GCS shim packages are still skeletons.

  • Repository scaffold: uv workspace, package skeletons, split Apache-2.0 / AGPLv3+commercial licensing.

docs.title: Contract v0.1 (frozen)
docs.text:
• mapi_spec.CONTRACT_VERSION = "0.1" names the contract the exported JSON Schemas describe; every exported schema carries it as x-mapi-contract-version.
  • The contract is frozen for the v0.1.x line: packages/spec/tests/snapshots/contract.json pins a digest of every exported schema and the drift test fails on any change. Additive changes (new optional fields, new error codes) regenerate the snapshot (MAPI_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1); breaking changes bump CONTRACT_VERSION first.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• mapi-spec: the pure-Pydantic contract layer.
  • DataSchema, DimSpec and VarSpec, with schema templates.
  • SchemaEffect propagation; ModelSpec, ScoreRequest and the Sweep, Backtest, SBC and Campaign wrappers.
  • A strict YAML 1.2 loader, canonical JSON and spec hashes.
  • Static validation: split stage, LEAKAGE_RISK, dim policies, recursion and the CoordPlan checks.
  • Capabilities, representation rules, the PlotSpec envelope, stable RFC 7807 error codes, the Executor protocol shapes, JSON Schema export and the mapi-spec CLI.
  • mapi-sdk: the xarray runtime.
  • Wire formats: XrJSON, single-object zarr v3 zips, DataTree zips and Arrow IPC.
  • Array-level schema validation; the step contract, pipeline engine and stages.
  • Split and per-group context replay; inverse chains with output-space labels.
  • CoordPlan and coordinate canonicalisation, the representation-aware summariser and metrics.
  • Bundle IO with integrity sidecars and no pickle; the fit_spec/score_bundle harness with evaluate_then_refit.
  • The entry-point registry, the in-process executor, and the mapi_sdk.testing contract kit (check_step, check_model, pytest plugin).
  • mapi-steps: 28 built-in core.* steps (reshape, value, feature, formula, adstock and saturation).
  • Each exports a templated SchemaEffect and a shipped catalog JSON.
  • Catalog entries for the five split kinds.
  • mapi-pymc: PyMCModel, where an author writes only build().
  • BuildContext with hier_effect new levels.
  • Engines: nutpie, pymc, MAP and ADVI, plus guarded numpyro, blackjax and pathfinder.
  • Segmented, resumable sampling with checkpoints; CRN counterfactuals.
  • Convergence diagnostics, FrozenPredictor fast scoring and check_fast_score.
  • mapi-sklearn: SklearnModel with an allow-listed estimator registry (sklearn and xgboost).
  • skops and xgboost-JSON persistence.
  • Point, quantile, bootstrap, conformal and classifier plugins (sklearn.tabular_*).
  • Pooled new levels; exact or zeroing contributions.
  • mapi-plots: a JSON-only PlotSpec sanitizer (pinned Vega-Lite 6.4.1 and plotly.js 4.1.1 schemas, an expression allow-list, HTML stripping) and role-bound templates.
  • The standard core.* recipe catalog, plus the mmm.* and ml.* domain packs.
  • Altair and Plotly converters with named Arrow datasets, and the render_plots batch entry point.
  • mapi-plugin-mmm: marketing-mix model plugins (entry point mapi.models: mmm).
  • mmm.hierarchical_geo 1.3.0, the E33 hierarchical geo MMM: adstock over core.lag_tensor features, logistic/Hill saturation, channel effects partially pooled across geos, new geos from the hyperprior, additive contributions.
  • Fit-cached derived quantities in original units: contributions, per-draw response-curve grids for Guided sliders, marginal cost/ROI; a decision objective for budgets; fast scoring.
  • mmm.pymc_marketing 1.0.0, an adapter around pymc-marketing 1.2's MMM (verified on PyMC 6.3) that owns scaling, carry-over and units and never pickles.
  • Declarative priors in pymc-marketing's dict form, typed per parameter so wrong priors fail static validation; a synthetic E33 simulator with known parameters and a parameter-recovery test.
  • mapi-sdk: outputs.derived with cache: fit is computed on the production fit through the plugin's derive hook; ScoreContext.to_original maps model-stage arrays to the output space.
  • Cross-package conformance suites:
  • the plan's xgboost spec through real steps, models and plots;
  • an E33-shaped core.* pipeline in front of a PyMC model.
  • mapi-plugin-ts: ts.hsgp_trend (C08: HSGP trend + seasonality whose domain comes from the anticipated coords; HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT past max_extension; sentinel months left out of the likelihood) and ts.gaussian_hmm (E24: forward-algorithm HMM over padded tracks with a terminal_state group, forecast and filter modes, relabelling postprocess, LOO declared invalid).
  • mapi-plugin-tabular: tabular.hierarchical_glm (E02: partially pooled GLM in long layout, hyperprior new groups, group-level covariates, four families) and tabular.regressor (plan §6.2 store demand: quantile regression restricted to the registry's quantile-capable estimators).
  • mapi-conformance: the corpus runner python -m mapi_conformance run [--size tiny|full] [--fixture id] (validate, fit, score requests, evaluate, contract kit, plots, expectations; summary table and JSON) with the e02, c08, e24, xgb_store_demand, e33 and pymc_marketing fixtures; pytest -m conformance, make conformance (tiny) and make conformance-full.
  • Score cases can opt out of side tables (side_tables: false, e.g. a weekly EUR plan entering after the FX step).
  • Expectation hooks that declare ctx receive a FixtureContext (seed, size, registry, side tables and earlier score results).
  • Docs: spec format, SDK, built-in steps and plots references; guides for plugins, PyMC, tabular models and plots.
  • Docs: built-in models reference, marketing-mix models guide, forecasting and sequential models guide, conformance corpus guide.
  • Docs: the MkDocs Material site.
  • A landing page, getting started (install, first model, runs and executors), concepts (labelled data, pipelines and stages, representations, bundles, coord plans, capabilities), the "port a model in 15 minutes" guide, licensing, contributing and roadmap pages for v0.2–v0.4.
  • Generated reference pages: steps, models and plot-recipe catalogs, the ModelSpec/ScoreRequest schema and error codes (scripts/gen_docs_catalog.py, run by an MkDocs hook and make docs-catalog); API reference via mkdocstrings.
  • Every Python example lives in docs/snippets/ and is executed by conformance/tests/test_docs_snippets.py (make docs-test).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The workspace runs numpy 2.4 (pymc-marketing 1.2 requires numpy < 2.5).
  • make typecheck also covers plugins/mmm, plugins/ts, plugins/tabular and conformance.
  • Score requests that name a pinned side table now fail validation. Score outputs along time and extend dims come back sorted. validate_spec emits an INFO issue when the model's target role overrides a declared role.
  • Plugin-raised error text now appears in untrusted_text, not in detail.

docs.title: Fixed (integration)
docs.text:
• The plan's xgboost example names the real quantile plugin (sklearn.tabular_quantiles). A new ml.feature_importance recipe covers its plot list.
  • core.fit_vs_actual and core.residuals_over_time compare quantile and interval summaries cell by cell instead of refusing them.
  • The contract kit flags step settings whose defaults are missing from the exported JSON Schema (default_factory), and finds reverse-bound outputs when checking units.
  • Holdout metrics no longer invert the predictions of models that own inverse_units a second time.
  • Score outputs that declare their own units (e.g. state probabilities) no longer go through the target's inverse transforms.
  • The contract kit runs its shuffled, subset and new-level checks on long layouts (index variables are remapped) and shifts calendar-frequency time coords by whole periods.
  • The in-process executor no longer resolves a score request's side-table refs when the run payload already supplies those tables.
  • The contract kit's score requests name the spec's score_policy: supplied side tables, so models with supplied tables (E33's FX) pass the scoring checks.
  • The E33 and pymc-marketing fixtures use the corpus runner's fixture layout and run in python -m mapi_conformance run.

docs.title: Fixed (M0 review: spec and SDK)
docs.text:
• Counterfactuals: score_bundle takes a baseline data payload and a separate scenario payload, and scores the scenario's interventions against the baseline. A scenario without baseline data, or a named scenario that was not supplied, is SCHEMA_INVALID.
  • owns is enforced: catalog steps declare provides (scaling, carryover), and validate_spec rejects such a step on the target, media or spend variables of a model that owns that preprocessing (CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED).
  • Target dependence follows the model template's target roles, even with an inferred raw schema, so RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED fires reliably. The recursion and future-covariate checks measure how far the payload extends past the fit, not only horizon.
  • No target leakage into evaluation lags for dynamic or cell-level splits. as_of gap periods stay in the holdout with masked targets and are excluded from metrics.
  • Pinned side tables always replay the fit-time version; a request that names one fails with SIDE_TABLE_COVERAGE.
  • Score payloads are sorted along ordered/extend dims before the pipeline; duplicate labels are COORD_NOT_ALLOWED.
  • Chained look-back steps (adstock then lag) replay with fit-time history. A score window that starts inside the fitted range and loses look-back history gets a WARNING.
  • Long-layout per-group context works end to end.
  • Inverses: steps declare additive inverses, and decompositions along component only go through additive steps (otherwise they stay at the blocking stage, with a WARNING). Smearing residuals come only from target-shaped outputs. The moments sd uses the delta method.
  • Model-owned outputs are labelled per variable with their units and output_space.
  • Derived quantities named in output.vars come back from the fit cache. An uncached one is refused.
  • PyMC CRN counterfactuals give identical draws in untouched cells for Poisson, negative binomial and binomial likelihoods (crn_ppf).
  • Wire and bundle hardening: XrJSON budgets decoded bytes (max_decoded_bytes), caps declared dim sizes and accepts only ISO-8601 dates. Zarr-zip decoding is bounded by declared shapes, string lengths and an expansion ratio. Pickle is detected by opcode stream, in object .npy and inside archives. The evaluation sub-bundle is verified and never kept stale. Entry points can no longer replace registered or built-in plugin ids.
  • Spec parsing rejects non-finite floats and reports oversized JSON integers as SpecParseError.

docs.title: Fixed (M0 review: models and steps)
docs.text:
• core.formula: scalar ~ is logical not; overflow and division by zero give inf/nan, and other arithmetic errors are reported as SCHEMA_INVALID rather than escaping.
  • PyMC checkpoints: the codec rebuilds only classes defined in PyMC step-method modules (plus pymc.util and mapi_pymc), at exactly the encoded module:qualname.

docs.title: Fixed (M0 review: plots, conformance and tooling)
docs.text:
• Plot sanitizer (Plotly): updatemenus/sliders method args are checked in the positional [attr, value] form and inside nested frame/trace objects, so external image sources, href/url paths, tile-map subplots and tile-map trace types can no longer hide there.
  • Plot sanitizer (Vega-Lite): select.toggle strings and bind.legend event filters are checked as expressions, event['view'] is rejected like event.view, and usermeta.embedOptions is rejected.
  • from_plotly strips HTML from (and scans) the strings it moves into Arrow datasets, which the JSON sanitizer never decodes.
  • Plugin-originated error text stays out of trusted fields: render_plots and the step/model wrappers (Pipeline, harness fit/score/derive) move a plugin MapiError's detail into untrusted_text and keep its code only when plugin code may raise it (mapi_spec.errors.from_plugin_error, PLUGIN_ERROR_CODES).
  • Contract kit, check_step: effect_matches_output also compares each dim's kind and frequency and each variable's units; the toy FX and scale steps now set the units they declare.
  • Contract kit, check_model: new horizon_exceeds_fit, missing_future_covariate, recursive_unsupported, fast_score_matches_exact (plugin check_fast_score hook, provided by PyMCModel), plots_sanitize and outputs_match_manifest checks; extend_typed_errors covers integer extend dims; output_space_and_units covers outputs that inherit the target implicitly.
  • OutputDecl.dims_of (additive) lets a manifest declare settings-dependent data dims; the sklearn models (and so tabular.regressor) and mmm.pymc_marketing use it, so their static output dims match what score returns.
