docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
make install          # uv sync --all-packages (+ pnpm install once apps/ exist)
make help             # every developer entry point
Command What it does make test The default test suite (everything except Docker, cloud and end-to-end tests) make test-fast Unit tests only, skipping slow MCMC tests make lint ruff, ruff format check and the import-linter contracts make typecheck mypy over every type-checked package make conformance The conformance corpus at size tiny (FIXTURE=e33 for one) make docs-serve This site with live reload make docs-build Regenerate the generated reference pages and build the site strictly make docs-test Run every documentation snippet and the docs checks make dev The whole stack locally without Docker (Local, without Docker) make docker-build / make compose-up Build the images / run the compose stack (Docker Compose) make release-check Version consistency, changelog entry, no plan files, pinned images

docs.title: Branching model
docs.text:
We use git flow with two long-lived branches, main and develop.

gitGraph
    commit id: "v0.1.0" tag: "v0.1.0"
    branch develop
    checkout develop
    commit id: "integration"
    branch feat/m1-runner
    checkout feat/m1-runner
    commit id: "feat(runner): …"
    commit id: "test(runner): …"
    checkout develop
    merge feat/m1-runner
    branch feat/m1-docs
    checkout feat/m1-docs
    commit id: "docs: …"
    checkout develop
    merge feat/m1-docs
    checkout main
    merge develop tag: "v0.2.0"
Branch Purpose main Releases only. Each milestone is merged from develop and tagged vX.Y.Z. Nobody commits to main directly. develop Integration. Feature branches are merged here with --no-ff. feat/<milestone>-<topic> One unit of work, branched from the latest develop. 
git checkout -B feat/m1-my-change develop
# ... small, logical commits ...
make fmt lint typecheck test

Never rebase or rewrite develop or main. Keep changes to shared files (the root pyproject.toml, the Makefile, uv.lock, CI) minimal and additive, and mention them in your pull request.

docs.title: Commit messages
docs.text:
Conventional commits, scoped by package:

feat(sdk): replay context tails at each step's input stage
fix(server): reject score requests whose horizon exceeds the fit
docs: add the porting guide
test(conformance): add the e24 filter fixture
chore: bump ruff

docs.title: Code style
docs.text:
• Python 3.12, ruff (line length 100), type hints everywhere; mypy strict for the core packages.
  • Tests live next to each package in tests/. PyMC fits in tests use tiny settings (tune: 50–150, draws: 50–150, chains: 2) and are marked slow when they take more than about ten seconds.
  • Docstrings are concise (Google style). The contract tests are the executable documentation.
  • mapi_spec must not import numpy, xarray or pandas; the server must not import plugin or array code. make lint enforces both.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The site is MkDocs Material (mkdocs.yml at the repository root, pages in docs/).

  • Every Python example is executed. Examples live in docs/snippets/*.py, are included in pages with --8<-- "file.py:section", and conformance/tests/test_docs_snippets.py runs each
  • Platform examples run against a live stack. The client, HTTP and remote-CLI walkthroughs (docs/snippets/client_tour.py, http_tour.sh, cli_remote.sh) run under make e2e; the local CLI walkthrough (cli_local.sh) runs in the default suite (conformance/tests/test_docs_platform.py). Shell snippets use the same section markers.
  • Reference pages are generated. scripts/gen_docs_catalog.py writes the steps, models, plot recipes, spec schema and error-code pages, and scripts/gen_docs_reference.py the CLI reference, the server settings and a copy of apps/web/openapi.json, into docs/reference/generated/ (git-ignored); an MkDocs hook runs both before every build.
  • New MAPI_* variables go into the configuration reference (docs/operations/configuration.md); a test scans the source tree for them.
  • Screenshots live in docs/assets/screenshots/ (at most 300 KB each, each used by a page). make docs-screenshots recaptures them from a running, seeded stack.
  • make docs-build must pass (mkdocs build --strict, with anchor validation).
  • Write for two readers: an analyst who wants to know what a feature does for them, and a data scientist who wants to know exactly how it works.

docs.title: Licensing
docs.text:
modeling-api uses a split licence. People who write models and integrations are never pulled into copyleft; the hosted platform itself is protected.

Component Where Licence SDK and contracts: mapi-spec, mapi-sdk, mapi-pymc, mapi-sklearn packages/spec, packages/sdk, packages/sdk-pymc, packages/sdk-sklearn Apache-2.0 Built-ins: steps, plots, model plugins, conformance corpus packages/steps-core, packages/plots-core, plugins/*, conformance/ Apache-2.0 Tools: CLI, Python client, GCS emulator packages/cli, packages/client, packages/gcs-shim Apache-2.0 Platform: API server, run harness, web apps, images, infrastructure packages/server, packages/runner, apps/*, images/, infra/, ops/, security/ AGPLv3 or a commercial licence Documentation docs/ CC BY 4.0

Each package declares its SPDX expression in its pyproject.toml (Apache-2.0, or AGPL-3.0-only OR LicenseRef-mapi-commercial) and carries its own LICENSE file. The full texts are in the repository root: LICENSE.md, LICENSE-APACHE.txt, LICENSE-AGPL.txt and COMMERCIAL-LICENSE.md.

docs.title: What this means in practice
docs.text:
Plugins you write are yours

A step, model or plot recipe written against mapi-sdk, mapi-pymc or mapi-sklearn uses Apache-2.0 libraries. License it however you like, including proprietary.

Applications that call the platform are not derivative works

Calling the platform over HTTP, with the Python or TypeScript client, through webhooks or MCP, does not make your application subject to the AGPL.

Modifying and hosting the platform

If you modify the platform components (server, runner, apps) and offer them as a network service, the AGPLv3 requires you to publish your modifications, unless you hold a commercial licence. Contact mattreda@mattreda.pro for commercial terms.

docs.title: Third-party libraries
docs.text: The SDK builds on xarray, numpy, pandas, zarr and Pydantic; the model packages on PyMC, ArviZ, scikit-learn, xgboost and skops; the marketing-mix adapter on pymc-marketing; the plot recipes on Altair and Plotly. Each keeps its own licence.

docs.title: Contributions
docs.text: Contributions are accepted under the Contributor Licence Agreement (CONTRIBUTOR-LICENSE.md), which lets the project keep offering the platform under both licences. See Contributing.

docs.title: CLI and Python client v0.2
docs.text:
Two Apache-2.0 packages talk to the /v1 HTTP API:

  • mapi-client (mapi_client): a typed Python client, sync and async, built on httpx;
  • mapi-cli (mapi): the command line, built on the client and on the SDK for local runs.

Both use the Pydantic DTOs from mapi_spec.api for every request and response, and raise mapi_spec.errors.MapiError subclasses rebuilt from RFC 7807 problem documents.

This page is a compact summary. The guides walk through each with tested examples (command line, Python client), and the CLI reference lists every command's --help, generated from the installed CLI.

docs.title: Python client
docs.text:
from mapi_client import Client

with Client() as api:  # MAPI_URL / MAPI_TOKEN / ~/.config/mapi/config.toml / 127.0.0.1:8000
    version = api.datasets.upload("eu_media.zarr.zip", dataset="eu_media_daily")
    rev = api.specs.upsert(open("spec.yaml").read())
    run = api.runs.fit(rev.spec_id, rev.revision)
    for item in api.runs.stream_events(run.id):  # SSE, resumes with Last-Event-ID
        print(item)
    run = api.runs.wait(run.id, raise_on_failure=True)
    result = api.models.score(
        model_id,
        1,
        {
            "model": "model://default/eu-geo-mmm@v1",
            "mode": "forecast",
            "horizon": {"dim": "time", "periods": 8},
        },
    )
    result.tree  # xr.DataTree with the `xarray` extra
Resource Calls projects list, get catalog get, models, model, steps, plots, schema datasets create, list, get, find, ensure, create_upload, create_version, versions, version, wait_version, upload, artifact, download specs validate, create, list, get, find, revise, upsert, revisions, revision, dry_run runs create, fit, get, list, wait, stream_events, events, logs, plots, cancel, resume, retry models list, get, versions, version, artifact, download, score plots list, get, validate
  • AsyncClient has the same resources with await and async for.
  • List calls return lazy paginators that follow next_cursor.
  • Calls that accept an Idempotency-Key get a fresh UUID unless you pass one. Idempotent calls are retried on 429, 502, 503, 504 and connection errors, honouring Retry-After.
  • datasets.upload accepts a path, bytes or an xr.Dataset (with the xarray extra). It creates the dataset if needed, PUTs the file to the signed URL, starts the ingest run and waits for the version to be ready. A dataset that carries its raw schema in the mapi_schema attribute keeps its dim policies and roles.
  • runs.stream_events yields RunSnapshot, RunEventFrame (persisted events, with an id), RunLiveFrame (live progress and log frames, without an id) and finally RunEnd.
  • models.score sends Prefer: wait=N. While the run is still going it repeats the same request with the same Idempotency-Key; the server's idempotent replay returns the finished ScoreCallResult with fresh output links.
  • Signed storage URLs are fetched without the API's Authorization header, and every transfer is checked against the storage-computed CRC32C and size.

Configuration. Arguments beat MAPI_URL (fallback MAPI_API_URL), MAPI_TOKEN and MAPI_PROFILE, which beat a profile in ~/.config/mapi/config.toml ($MAPI_CONFIG, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME), which beats http://127.0.0.1:8000. A token is never sent over plain HTTP to a non-loopback host. M1 has no authentication; OIDC arrives in M2.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
mapi new geo-mmm -o spec.yaml --with-data   # template + tiny sample data (needs mapi-conformance)
mapi check spec.yaml --data data.zarr.zip   # full static validation against installed plugins
mapi fit spec.yaml --data data.zarr.zip \
    --side-table fx=fx.zarr.zip --side-table holidays=holidays.zarr.zip   # in-process fit
mapi score request.yaml --bundle bundles/geo-mmm --data future.zarr.zip -o result.zarr.zip

mapi serve                                  # the local stack in one process (see below)
mapi fit spec.yaml --data data.zarr.zip --remote @   # upload, create/revise spec, fit, follow
mapi runs ls --state running | get RUN | logs RUN | watch RUN | cancel RUN | retry RUN
mapi datasets ls | upload file.csv --name sales --mapping mapping.yaml
mapi score request.yaml --remote @ --model MODEL_ID --version 1 -o result.zarr.zip
mapi catalog [models|steps|plots] [--remote @]

mapi plugin init acme-demand && mapi plugin test acme-demand   # scaffold + contract kit
mapi spec upgrade spec.yaml --check
mapi config show
Template (mapi new) What it is Conformance fixture geo-mmm Hierarchical geo MMM (weekly EUR, adstock, saturation) E33 forecast HSGP trend + seasonality forecast C08 tabular XGBoost demand with quantile uncertainty xgb_store_demand glm Hierarchical GLM, long layout E02
  • --remote @ means "the configured API"; --remote URL overrides it for one command.
  • --json prints one JSON document on stdout (runs watch --json prints one JSON event per line). Errors become {"error": {...}} with exit status 1; usage errors exit 2.
  • Local fit and score run plugins in-process (isolation NONE): use them only with code and data you trust. Server, plugin and log text is printed with ANSI and control sequences and bidi overrides removed.

docs.title: mapi serve
docs.text: mapi serve runs mapi-server dev: database migrations, then the API and the orchestrator (dispatcher, reconciler, finalizer and event pump) in one process. Postgres is the embedded pgserver unless DATABASE_URL is set, and the GCS shim is started in-process when nothing listens at MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT. Runs execute through the local-process executor with the real mapi-runner. For the web app as well, use make dev (Local development).

docs.title: GCS shim (local Cloud Storage)
docs.text:
mapi-gcs-shim is a local emulator of the parts of Google Cloud Storage the platform relies on. The local stack, the test suites and the runner use it in place of real GCS. It implements:

  • object generations and metagenerations, with generation preconditions;
  • server-computed CRC32C and MD5, in the GCS wire forms (base64);
  • V4 signed URLs: GET with HTTP Range, and PUT;
  • V4 POST policies that limit uploads to a key prefix and a content-length-range;
  • IAM-lite: per-principal tokens and keys, with per-bucket role bindings;
  • a retention lock (write-once buckets) and lifecycle (age-based delete).

The control plane talks to it through ShimObjectStore, which implements the ObjectStore protocol from mapi_spec.storage. GcsObjectStore implements the same protocol on real GCS.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
mapi-gcs-shim                                   # serve .local/gcs on 127.0.0.1:4443
python -m mapi_gcs_shim --root .local/gcs --port 4443
mapi-gcs-shim init --root .local/gcs            # write config + key files, then exit
mapi-gcs-shim key exec --field token            # print the exec principal's bearer token

The defaults come from the local-dev variables:

  • MAPI_DATA_DIR: the root is $MAPI_DATA_DIR/gcs;
  • MAPI_ENV: bucket names are mapi-{env}-*;
  • MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT: the host and port.

--port 0 picks a free port. The server stops gracefully on SIGINT or SIGTERM. Only one server may serve a root at a time, which is enforced by a lock file.

docs.title: State on disk
docs.text:
Path Content _shim/config.json Buckets and principals, including secrets. Mode 0600. _shim/keys/{principal}.json One key file per principal: email, bearer token, HMAC secret and endpoint. Mode 0600. buckets/{bucket}/bucket.json The bucket's retention and lifecycle policies. buckets/{bucket}/objects/{h[:2]}/{h}.json The live generation's metadata, where h = sha256(object name). buckets/{bucket}/objects/{h[:2]}/{h}.{generation}.bin The object's bytes. tmp/ The staging area for uploads.

No object name ever becomes a filesystem path. Names are hashed, and bucket names must match the GCS bucket grammar. Names with empty, . or .. segments, a leading / or control characters are rejected with 400, whether they arrive in the JSON API, the XML API or a POST-policy key.

Writes are crash-safe:

  1. bytes are streamed into tmp/ while the CRC32C and MD5 are computed;
  2. the data file is renamed into place;
  3. the metadata sidecar is atomically replaced, which is the commit point.

On startup, the shim deletes leftover staging files and any data files that never committed. Only the live generation is kept, as in a bucket without object versioning. Reading a superseded generation therefore returns 404.

docs.title: Buckets and principals
docs.text:
By default init creates the five buckets from the plan's storage layout:

Bucket Policy mapi-{env}-quarantine Lifecycle: objects are deleted after 7 days. mapi-{env}-bootstrap Lifecycle: objects are deleted after 1 day. mapi-{env}-runs No policy. mapi-{env}-bundles Locked retention of about 100 years. Objects cannot be overwritten or deleted, even by an admin. mapi-{env}-data No policy.

It also creates two principals:

Principal Bindings control (control@mapi-{env}.iam.gserviceaccount.com) roles/storage.admin on every bucket. Used by the control plane and the finalizer. exec (exec@…) storage.objects.get and storage.objects.delete on the bootstrap bucket only. It cannot list that bucket and has no access to the bundles bucket. Its token is the local executor's MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN.

You can add principals and bindings to config.json. The predefined roles are:

  • roles/storage.admin
  • roles/storage.objectAdmin
  • roles/storage.objectUser
  • roles/storage.objectViewer
  • roles/storage.objectCreator
  • roles/storage.legacyBucketReader

A binding targets one bucket, or "*" for every bucket.

Permissions are checked as follows:

  • JSON-API calls are checked against the caller's bearer token. A missing or unknown token returns 401, and a missing permission returns 403.
  • Signed URLs and POST policies carry the signer's authority, which is checked when the URL is used. A URL signed by exec for the runs bucket is refused.
  • Overwriting an existing object also requires storage.objects.delete, as in GCS.

docs.title: JSON API
docs.text:
Every JSON-API request needs Authorization: Bearer <token>.

Method and path Operation GET /storage/v1/b List buckets. Needs storage.buckets.list. POST /storage/v1/b Create a bucket. The body may set retentionPolicy and lifecycle (Delete with an age condition). GET or DELETE /storage/v1/b/{bucket} Get a bucket, or delete it if it is empty. GET /storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o List objects. Accepts prefix, delimiter, pageToken, maxResults, startOffset and endOffset. GET /storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o/{object} Get metadata. With alt=media it returns the content, and Range gives 206. PATCH /storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o/{object} Update contentType or metadata, which increments metageneration. DELETE /storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o/{object} Delete an object. Accepts generation. POST /storage/v1/b/{b}/o/{o}/rewriteTo/b/{b2}/o/{o2} Server-side copy. Also available as copyTo. Accepts sourceGeneration. POST /upload/storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o Upload with uploadType=media or multipart. Resumable uploads return 501. GET /download/storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o/{object} Download the content.

Every object operation accepts the ifGenerationMatch, ifGenerationNotMatch, ifMetagenerationMatch and ifMetagenerationNotMatch preconditions. A rewrite also accepts the ifSource… forms.

  • On writes, a failed precondition returns 412.
  • On reads, a failed …NotMatch returns 304.
  • ifGenerationMatch=0 means "the object must not exist yet".

Errors use the GCS JSON shape: {"error": {"code", "message", "errors": [{"reason"}]}}.

docs.title: Signed URLs (XML style)
docs.text:
Method and path Operation GET /{bucket}/{object}?X-Goog-… Download. With Range it returns 206, with Content-Range. An unsatisfiable range returns 416. PUT /{bucket}/{object}?X-Goog-… Upload. POST /{bucket} (multipart/form-data) Upload through a V4 POST policy. The file field must be last.

Signing follows GOOG4-HMAC-SHA256 with per-principal HMAC keys:

  • Canonical request: method, path, every query parameter except X-Goog-Signature, the signed headers (always including host) and UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD.
  • Signed values: X-Goog-Expires (at most 7 days) and X-Goog-Date are signed. Expiry is strict, but X-Goog-Date may be up to 5 minutes in the future to allow for clock skew.
  • Bound to the signature: the method, path, host, query (for example generation) and signed header values. Changing any of them returns 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch.
  • Unsigned headers: any x-goog-* header that was not signed returns 400, except x-goog-hash.
  • Expiry: an expired URL returns 400 ExpiredToken.

Signed GET URLs from sign_get are pinned to a generation. If the object is overwritten, the URL returns 404; it never silently serves the new bytes.

Signed PUT URLs from sign_put sign these headers, which the uploader must send verbatim:

  • content-type;
  • x-goog-if-generation-match: 0, so the object is write-once by default;
  • x-goog-content-length-range: 0,<max>.

The uploader may also send Content-MD5 or x-goog-hash: crc32c=…,md5=…. A mismatch returns 400 BadDigest, and nothing is stored.

POST policies from post_policy are a base64 JSON document of conditions, with an HMAC signature over the document. The conditions are:

  • {"bucket": …};
  • ["starts-with", "$key", prefix];
  • ["starts-with", "$content-type", ""];
  • ["content-length-range", min, max];
  • the x-goog-* credential fields;
  • with create_only=True, {"x-goog-if-generation-match": "0"} (also sent as a form field).

When the policy is used, the shim enforces:

  • the signature and the expiration;
  • every condition;
  • that every form field is covered by a condition, except x-goog-signature, policy, file and x-ignore-*;
  • the size range. A body that is too large is rejected while it streams;
  • an x-goog-if-generation-match form field as a precondition, so a create-only policy returns 412 for a key that already exists, whatever the signer may delete.

Real GCS takes no generation precondition in a POST form. GcsObjectStore signs create-only policies with uploader_credentials instead: a principal without storage.objects.delete, which GCS requires to overwrite.

success_action_status (200, 201 with an XML PostResponse, or 204 by default) and ${filename} in key behave as in GCS.

docs.title: Shim-only endpoints
docs.text:
• GET /_shim/healthz: no authentication.
  • POST /_shim/v1/lifecycle:sweep?now=<iso>: needs shim.admin. It runs the lifecycle rules now; objects under retention are never swept.

The server also sweeps every --sweep-interval seconds. The default is 300.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
from datetime import timedelta
from mapi_gcs_shim import ShimObjectStore

async with ShimObjectStore.from_root(".local/gcs", "control") as store:
    meta = await store.put("mapi-local-runs", "t/default/runs/r1/a1/x.json", b"{}",
                           content_type="application/json", if_generation_match=0)
    url = await store.sign_get("mapi-local-runs", meta.name, expires_in=timedelta(minutes=15))

ShimObjectStore has three constructors:

  • ShimObjectStore(endpoint, credentials, public_endpoint=None). public_endpoint is the host written into signed URLs, so a sandbox can reach the shim under another name. The host is signed.
  • .from_root(root, principal).
  • .from_local_dev(LocalDev).

Besides the protocol methods, it offers create_bucket, get_bucket and sweep_lifecycle. Errors map to NotFound, PreconditionFailed, AccessDenied, InvalidRange and StorageError:

  • get(max_bytes=…) raises PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE before it reads the body;
  • a full read whose CRC32C does not match raises INTEGRITY_FAILURE.

mapi_gcs_shim.transfer has helpers for whoever holds a URL:

  • download_signed;
  • upload_signed_put;
  • upload_post_policy.

They speak plain GCS XML semantics, so they also work against real GCS.

GcsObjectStore (install mapi-gcs-shim[gcp]) implements the same protocol with google-cloud-storage. It has been tested only with a fake client, never against live GCP.

docs.title: pytest fixtures
docs.text:
The package registers a pytest11 plugin, so every workspace test can use these fixtures:

async def test_something(gcs_shim):            # a fresh shim per test, on a free port
    async with gcs_shim.store() as store:       # the control principal; store("exec") also works
        await store.put(gcs_shim.buckets.runs, "t/default/x", b"...")
    headers = gcs_shim.auth_headers("exec")     # for raw httpx calls

gcs_shim_session gives one shim for the whole session. For use outside pytest, ShimServer(root) is a context manager that runs the shim on a background thread.

docs.title: Differences from real GCS
docs.text:
• There is no object versioning: only the live generation is kept.
  • Resumable uploads (uploadType=resumable) are not implemented. Use media or multipart uploads, or a signed PUT.
  • Signing uses HMAC keys (GOOG4-HMAC-SHA256) instead of service-account RSA keys (GOOG4-RSA-SHA256). GcsObjectStore uses the library's RSA or IAM signing.
  • There are no ACLs, CMEK, storage classes, notifications or bucket PATCH. Bucket policies are set when the bucket is created or in config.json.
  • A signed URL is valid only for the method it was signed for. A HEAD request needs its own signature, as in GCS.

docs.title: HTTP API (v1) v0.2
docs.text:
The platform API that ships with v0.2 (milestone M1, the local vertical slice). Every request and response body is a Pydantic model in mapi_spec.api. The server serves an OpenAPI 3.1 document generated from those models, and each model carries examples. The endpoint table on this page matches mapi_spec.api.M1_ENDPOINTS, and a test fails if the two drift apart.

See also OpenAPI explorer The OpenAPI 3.1 document, browsable, with every schema and example (full screen) HTTP API guide The main flow with curl and jq: upload, validate, fit, follow, score Python client The same flow with mapi_client

M1 is single-tenant

A local install has one tenant and one project, both called default. Every resource still carries tenant_id and project_id, and every storage key starts with t/{tenant}/, so multi-tenancy in v0.3 adds row-level security without changing the schema. There is no authentication in M1. The API listens on 127.0.0.1 only.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text: Topic Rule Base URL http://127.0.0.1:8000 locally. Resource paths start with /v1. Bodies application/json (UTF-8). Spec text travels as a string field (yaml) inside JSON. Unknown fields Request bodies reject unknown fields (SCHEMA_INVALID). Clients ignore unknown response fields, so the server can add fields without a new version. Timestamps RFC 3339, timezone-aware, UTC (2026-10-15T09:30:00Z). Ids <prefix>_<26 lowercase Crockford base32>, ULID layout, sortable by creation time (run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0). Prefixes: ds, upl, spc, run, mdl, mv. Projects and tenants use slugs (default). Durations "45m", "1h30m", "90s". Actions Non-CRUD actions use a colon suffix: POST /v1/runs/{run_id}:cancel. Untrusted text Log lines, tracebacks and plugin messages only ever appear in untrusted_text or LogLine.line. Render them as text, never as HTML or markdown.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Every error is an RFC 7807 problem document (application/problem+json, model mapi_spec.Problem) with a stable code:

{
  "type": "urn:mapi:error:LEAKAGE_RISK",
  "title": "A stateful step runs before the split",
  "status": 422,
  "code": "LEAKAGE_RISK",
  "detail": "validation failed with 1 error; first at /pipeline/2: …",
  "errors": [
    {"code": "LEAKAGE_RISK", "severity": "error", "pointer": "/pipeline/2",
     "message": "stateful step 'scale_y' runs before the split"}
  ]
}
  • Malformed request bodies, path parameters and query parameters return 422 SCHEMA_INVALID. Each problem goes in errors[] with an RFC 6901 pointer into the request (/body/kind, /query/limit).
  • Every endpoint can also return RATE_LIMITED (429), INTERNAL_ERROR (500) and INFRA_ERROR (503). These are not repeated in the table.
  • The full list of codes and their HTTP statuses is in Error codes.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
List endpoints return Page[T]:

{"items": [ … ], "next_cursor": "eyJpZCI6InJ1bl8wMWphZiJ9"}
  • Pass ?limit= (default 50, maximum 200) and ?cursor=<next_cursor> to fetch the next page. A null cursor means the current page is the last one.
  • Cursors are opaque and only valid for the same list and filters.
  • Items are ordered newest first by id.

docs.title: Idempotency
docs.text:
POST /v1/runs, …:score, …:retry, …:dry-run and POST …/versions (ingest) accept an Idempotency-Key header (1–255 printable ASCII characters, scoped to the project and kept for 24 hours):

Situation Response First request with the key The normal response, for example 201 Created with the Run Same key, same body (byte-equal after canonical JSON) 200 OK with the originally created resource. No second run is created. Same key, different body 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT Same key while the first request is still in flight 409 CONFLICT. Retry later.

Clients should generate one key per user intent, for example a UUIDv4 when the user clicks Fit, and reuse it on every network retry.

docs.title: Long-running work and Prefer: wait
docs.text:
Runs are asynchronous. Creating one returns the Run at once in state created or queued. POST /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}:score also honours RFC 7240 Prefer: wait=N, with N capped at 60 seconds:

  • If the score run reaches a terminal state within N seconds, the response is 200 with ScoreCallResult{done: true, run, outputs: [ArtifactLink…]}.
  • Otherwise the response is 202 with done: false and the run. Follow the run with GET /v1/runs/{run_id} or its event stream.
  • The Preference-Applied: wait=N response header echoes the wait the server actually used.

docs.title: Run events (server-sent events)
docs.text:
GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/events has two representations:

  • Accept: text/event-stream: a live SSE stream.
  • Any other Accept: a JSON Page[RunEventView] of persisted events. Pass ?after=<id> to read events after a given id.

The stream sends these frames, in this order:

  1. event: snapshot with the full Run JSON. It is the first frame on every connection and has no id:.
  2. A replay of the persisted events whose id is greater than the Last-Event-ID request header. Without the header the replay starts from the beginning. Every replayed frame carries id: <RunEventView.id>. The ids increase per run, so a reconnecting client resumes exactly where it stopped, including across the 60-minute request cut on Cloud Run.
  3. Live frames as events arrive: state, progress, log, diagnostic, warning, checkpoint, metric, complete and error. The data: of each frame is one line of compact JSON (RunEventView).
  4. event: end once the run is terminal (data: the final Run). The server then closes the stream. A client that sees end must not reconnect.

The server also sends a fresh event: snapshot (no id:) whenever the run's state changes, so a client can re-render from the latest Run without reassembling it from events. progress and log frames are not persisted: they are sent live without an id: (data: {run_id, attempt, seq, ts, type, payload}) and are never replayed; Last-Event-ID only covers persisted events.

Between events the server writes a heartbeat comment (: keepalive) every 15 seconds. The first frame also carries retry: 3000.

Progress frames are coalesced to at most one every 2–5 seconds. Only state changes, warnings, diagnostics, checkpoints, metrics and terminal events are persisted and replayable. A reconnecting client gets the latest progress from the snapshot frame. Log lines are paged from GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/logs.

retry: 3000
event: snapshot
data: {"id":"run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0","state":"running", …}

id: 17
event: state
data: {"id":17,"run_id":"run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0","attempt":1,"seq":3,"type":"state", …}

: keepalive

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
Data reaches the platform in three steps:

  1. Create the dataset.
  2. PUT the file to the signed URL from an upload session. The URL points into the quarantine bucket and the API never sees the bytes.
  3. Create a version. A sandboxed ingest run parses the upload, validates it, and writes the content-addressed data.zarr.zip with its schema, profile and preview.

Accepts Idempotency-Key. docs.title: Specs
docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors POST /v1/specs:validate Synchronous static validation. Returns every issue at once with JSON pointers, plus the schema at each pipeline stage. ValidateRequest ValidateResponse 200 SPEC_PARSE_ERROR, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, SCHEMA_INVALID POST /v1/specs Create a spec and its revision 1 SpecCreate SpecDoc 201 SPEC_PARSE_ERROR, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, SCHEMA_INVALID, CONFLICT GET /v1/specs List specs — Page[SpecDoc] 200 — GET /v1/specs/{spec_id} Get a spec with its latest revision — SpecDoc 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/specs/{spec_id}/revisions Add an immutable revision SpecRevisionCreate SpecRevision 201 NOT_FOUND, SPEC_PARSE_ERROR, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, SCHEMA_INVALID, CONFLICT (stale parent_revision) GET /v1/specs/{spec_id}/revisions List revisions — Page[SpecRevision] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/specs/{spec_id}/revisions/{revision} Get one revision — SpecRevision 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/specs/{spec_id}/revisions/{revision}:dry-run Explicit sandboxed dry-run, the same as POST /v1/runs with kind: validate. Accepts Idempotency-Key. — Run 202 NOT_FOUND, QUOTA_EXCEEDED

How validation reports results:

  • POST /v1/specs:validate returns 200 even when the document is invalid. The verdict is in ValidateResponse.valid and issues.
  • The non-2xx statuses are kept for requests that cannot be validated at all: unparseable YAML, an oversized document, or a malformed request body.
  • Creating a spec or a revision stores invalid revisions too, with valid: false and their issues, so the editor can save work in progress.
  • POST /v1/runs refuses invalid revisions with the first error's code. Examples: LEAKAGE_RISK, UNSEEN_LEVELS.

docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors POST /v1/runs Submit a run (200 on an idempotent replay). Accepts Idempotency-Key. RunCreate Run 201 NOT_FOUND, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, QUOTA_EXCEEDED, MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED, LEAKAGE_RISK, UNSEEN_LEVELS, COORD_NOT_ALLOWED, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT, MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE, RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED GET /v1/runs List runs (filters: kind, state, spec_id) — Page[Run] 200 — GET /v1/runs/{run_id} Get a run (state, failure class and problem, attempt, progress snapshot, cost placeholders) — Run 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/events SSE stream or JSON page of persisted events (see Run events). Accepts Last-Event-ID. — Page[RunEventView] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/logs Captured log lines; filters attempt, stream — Page[LogLine] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/plots Plots a succeeded run rendered (plots.json: forecast fans, counterfactual bands), passed through the plot sanitizer on every read; rejected plots are left out. A finalizing run is left alone and returned as it is: its execution is already over. — Run 202 NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT POST /v1/runs/{run_id}:resume Resume a partial run from its checkpoints (new attempt) — Run 202 NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT (not partial) POST /v1/runs/{run_id}:retry Start a new run from a failed one, for example one resource class up after RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. What RunCreate needs depends on kind:

kind Required Not allowed fit, validate (sandboxed dry-run) spec_id, revision model_version_id, request score model_version_id, request (a ScoreRequest document) spec_id, revision evaluate, derive, render model_version_id (optional params) spec_id, revision, request

Artifact links are minted only after two checks pass:

  2. Verification of the model version's signed bundle manifest: tenant, model version, digests and object generations must all match.

If the second check fails, the response is INTEGRITY_FAILURE and no URL is issued. Each link is pinned to an object generation, expires after 15 minutes, and supports HTTP Range requests.

docs.title: Built-in models
docs.text:
These model plugins ship with the platform (tier T0). They register through the mapi.models entry point, so default_registry() and the control-plane catalog list them without any configuration. Every one passes the contract kit (mapi_sdk.testing.check_model) and has a conformance fixture (see Conformance corpus).

Plugin Package Representation Score modes Corpus fixture mmm.hierarchical_geo@1 mapi-plugin-mmm draws predict, forecast, counterfactual, simulate, evaluate e33 mmm.pymc_marketing@1 mapi-plugin-mmm draws predict, forecast, counterfactual, evaluate pymc_marketing ts.hsgp_trend@1 mapi-plugin-ts draws predict, forecast, evaluate c08 ts.gaussian_hmm@1 mapi-plugin-ts draws predict, forecast, filter, evaluate e24 tabular.hierarchical_glm@1 mapi-plugin-tabular draws predict, counterfactual, evaluate e02 tabular.regressor@1 mapi-plugin-tabular quantiles predict, forecast, counterfactual, evaluate xgb_store_demand

Plugins use canonical names for their inputs; bind your dataset's names onto them in the spec's data.bind block. Outputs come back under your names (reverse binding) unless they are new variables such as y_hat.

The mapi-sklearn package also registers five general-purpose tabular plugins, sklearn.tabular_regressor, sklearn.tabular_quantiles, sklearn.tabular_bootstrap, sklearn.tabular_conformal and sklearn.tabular_classifier; see Tabular models.

Every setting, generated

The models catalog is generated from the installed manifests: capabilities, outputs, derived quantities, every setting with its default and Guided-mode level, and the input data contract.

docs.title: mmm.hierarchical_geo: geo marketing mix
docs.text:
A hierarchical marketing-mix model: adstock over a core.lag_tensor spend tensor, logistic or Hill saturation, channel effects partially pooled across geos, a hierarchical intercept and controls. New geos are drawn from the fitted hyperprior. Contributions are additive and, with outputs.derived, the fit caches contributions, per-draw response curves and marginal costs in original units. It declares a decision objective for budget optimisation.

Inputs. y(geo, time), spend(geo, channel, time, lag) from core.lag_tensor (the adstock.l_max setting must equal the step's l_max), and any other numeric variable along time as a control. geo is new_levels (hyperprior), channel is fixed, time extends.

Outputs. y_hat(geo, time) and contributions(component, geo, time) (one component per channel, baseline and one per control; they sum to y_hat).

Read the marketing-mix guide for the model, its priors and a complete spec.

docs.title: mmm.pymc_marketing: the pymc-marketing adapter
docs.text: Runs pymc_marketing.mmm.MMM behind the platform. The model scales data, carries spend over and reports original units itself, so the plugin declares owns: [scaling, carryover, inverse_units] and the platform skips its own versions of those. Bundles store the posterior, pymc-marketing's fit_data and its JSON model description, never a pickle. Markets are a fixed dim: pymc-marketing cannot score a market it has not seen. See the adapter section.

docs.title: ts.hsgp_trend — smooth trend with seasonality
docs.text:
A Hilbert-space Gaussian process (HSGP) trend plus an optional linear drift and Fourier seasonality, for one regularly spaced series (Mauna-Loa style CO2, sales, traffic).

Inputs. t (time, policy extend) and the target y(t). Missing months are allowed: replace sentinel codes with core.replace_sentinel and they are left out of the likelihood while the model still interpolates them. Put core.standardize on y; the priors are on the standardised scale and outputs are mapped back to your units.

Forecast horizon. max_extension (default 24 periods) is part of the model's input schema. The HSGP domain is sized at fit time from the anticipated coordinates (the fitted range plus max_extension periods), so every forecast up to that horizon evaluates exactly the fitted functions. A longer horizon is rejected before any compute with HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT (HTTP 409): refit with a larger max_extension.

Setting Default Meaning max_extension 24 Periods a forecast may reach past the fit without a refit kernel expquad expquad, matern52 or matern32 m, c 30, 1.5 Basis functions and boundary factor of the approximation lengthscale_mu, lengthscale_sigma 0.4, 0.5 Log-normal lengthscale prior on the scaled axis [-1, 1] eta_sigma 1.0 Half-normal scale of the GP amplitude linear_trend true Add intercept + slope * t season_period, season_order 12, 3 Fourier seasonality (periods of t, order) noise_sigma 0.5 Half-normal scale of the observation noise

Outputs. y_hat(t) (expected value or a predictive draw) and trend(t), the long-term component without seasonality, both in the target's units.

data:
  bind: {dims: {t: date}, vars: {y: co2}}
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: t, last: 12}
pipeline:
  - {id: clean, use: core.replace_sentinel@^1, with: {vars: [y], below: 0}}
  - {id: scale, use: core.standardize@^1, with: {vars: [y], over: [t]}}
model:
  use: ts.hsgp_trend@^1
  settings: {max_extension: 24, season_order: 2}
  fit: {mode: evaluate_then_refit, engine: pymc, seed: 11}

docs.title: ts.gaussian_hmm — hidden states with a terminal state
docs.text:
A K-state Gaussian hidden Markov model over many sequences at once (animal tracks, machine regimes, customer phases). Hidden states are summed out with the forward algorithm, so sampling is fast and exact.

Inputs. Padded layout: animal (the sequence dim, new_levels with strategy pooled), step (extend), y(animal, step) with NaN padding and a boolean mask(animal, step).

Terminal state. After the fit the filtered state distribution at the last fitted step is stored as the bundle's terminal_state group, alpha_T(chain, draw, animal, state).

  • predict / evaluate use the one-step-ahead state distribution of the fit inside the fitted range and alpha_T propagated by the transition matrix after it; they never look at targets in the payload.
  • forecast propagates alpha_T over the horizon.
  • filter runs the forward filter over new observations that continue the fitted steps and returns an updated terminal_state group with the filtered state_prob.
  • New animals start from the initial distribution pi at the first fitted step.

Draws are relabelled after sampling so that the state means increase (label switching); identification: ordered uses an ordered prior instead. Pointwise LOO is declared invalid (elpd_loo is rejected at validation): steps within a track are dependent.

Setting Default Meaning n_states 2 Number of hidden states mu_center, mu_sigma 0.0, 2.0 Normal prior of the state means sigma_scale 1.0 Half-normal scale of the per-state sds stickiness 2.0 Extra Dirichlet weight on staying in a state pi_concentration 1.0 Dirichlet weight of the initial distribution identification relabel relabel (sort draws by mean) or ordered

Outputs. y_hat(animal, step) in your units and state_prob(animal, step, state) (units probability, never inverse-transformed).

docs.title: tabular.hierarchical_glm — partial pooling in long layout
docs.text:
Varying intercepts (and optionally slopes) by group with group-level predictors: the radon model and its many relatives (schools, stores, clinics).

Inputs. Long layout: rows along obs (extend), a group dim (group_dim, default county, new_levels with strategy hyperprior), the index <group_dim>_idx(obs), the target y(obs), observation-level covariates and group-level group_covariates. Covariates are part of the input schema, so a spec naming a missing one fails validation.

New groups. A county the model never saw is drawn from the fitted hyperprior for every posterior draw; its group-level covariates shift its prior mean exactly as for fitted counties. Score payloads may list counties in any order: the platform remaps county_idx.

Setting Default Meaning group_dim county The grouping dim family normal normal, student_t, poisson (log link) or bernoulli (logit) covariates [] Predictors over obs varying_slopes [] Covariates whose slope varies by group group_covariates [] Predictors over the group dim centered false Centred group effects

docs.title: tabular.regressor — quantile regression for panels
docs.text:
The plan's store-demand model: rows are stacked from labelled dims (store × sku × week), the coordinates become categorical features, and an allow-listed estimator predicts conditional quantiles. Its estimator setting accepts exactly the quantile-capable estimators of the registry (xgboost, scikit-learn's gradient boosting and histogram boosting, and quantile regression), so other estimators are rejected at validation.

  • Defaults: xgboost (300 trees, depth 5, learning rate 0.05) and quantiles [0.1, 0.5, 0.9].
  • New stores are pooled (new_levels: pooled); forecasting is direct, so future covariates marked future_required must be supplied (MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE otherwise).
  • Quantiles are per cell: aggregating them across stores is refused (CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED).
  • The manifest lists core.fit_vs_actual, core.residuals_over_time and ml.feature_importance.

All other settings are those of mapi_sklearn (see Tabular models).

docs.title: OpenAPI explorer v0.2
docs.text:
The /v1 API's OpenAPI 3.1 document, rendered with Redoc. It is the committed apps/web/openapi.json, generated from the server's own FastAPI app and the mapi_spec.api models (uv run python apps/web/scripts/gen_openapi.py); CI fails when it drifts from the server. A running API serves the same document at /openapi.json.

Open full screen Download openapi.json

The explorer loads nothing from outside this site: the Redoc bundle (version 2.5.4) is vendored by scripts/vendor_redoc.py, which checks the npm tarball's integrity and pins the bundle's SHA-256, and a Content-Security-Policy on the page allows scripts, styles, images and requests from this site only.

For prose (conventions, idempotency, server-sent events, which errors each endpoint returns) read the HTTP API reference; for a worked example, the HTTP API guide.

docs.title: Plots reference (mapi-plots)
docs.text:
mapi-plots has two halves with different dependency footprints:

Install Modules Imports Runs in mapi-plots mapi_plots.sanitize, mapi_plots.templates mapi-spec, jsonschema (JSON only) API server, runner, notebooks mapi-plots[recipes] mapi_plots.convert, mapi_plots.recipes, mapi_plots.packs, mapi_plots.examples + altair, plotly, numpy, pandas, pyarrow, xarray runner images, notebooks

An import-linter contract keeps the sanitizer and templates free of numpy, pandas, xarray, pyarrow, altair, plotly and mapi_sdk, and import mapi_plots loads nothing heavy (exports are lazy).

docs.title: The PlotSpec envelope
docs.text:
Defined in mapi_spec.plots (the contract package):

id: core.ppc_fan                    # [A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}
title: Fit and forecast
kind: vega-lite                     # or plotly
spec: {...}                         # Vega-Lite JSON, or Plotly {data, layout, frames, config}
datasets:                           # referenced BY NAME only
  fan: {kind: inline_arrow, data: <base64 Arrow IPC stream>, rows: 84}
  big: {kind: data_ref, path: ui/plotdata/fan.arrow, format: arrow}
bindings: {x: "dim:time", y: "role:target", facet: "dim:geo"}   # templates only
schema_version: v6.4.1
persona: both                       # guided | expert | both
caption_plain: "The line is the model's median estimate ..."
provenance: {recipe: core.ppc_fan@1.0.0, bundle_id: ..., generated_at: ...}
  • Vega-Lite references data with {"data": {"name": "fan"}}.
  • Plotly references a column with {"$ref": "<dataset>.<column>"} in any data-array attribute (and in arrayOk attributes such as marker.color). The part before the first . is the dataset; the rest is the column (trace0.marker.color → dataset trace0, column marker.color). Its JSON Schema ships as mapi_plots.sanitize.PLOTLY_REF_SCHEMA and as the file mapi_plots/sanitize/schemas/plotly-ref.schema.json:
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "urn:mapi:schema:plotly-dataset-ref:v1",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {"$ref": {"type": "string",
    "pattern": "^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_\\-]{0,63}\\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.\\-]{0,127}$"}},
  "required": ["$ref"],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
  • Inline Arrow datasets are at most 2 MiB of base64 each. Recipe datasets are written compactly (float32, int32, dictionary-encoded strings); timestamps are UTC milliseconds.

docs.title: Sanitizer
docs.text:
from mapi_plots.sanitize import sanitize_plot, check_plot, sanitize_spec, SanitizeLimits

result = sanitize_plot(doc)            # PlotSpec | dict | JSON str | bytes
result.plot                            # validated, sanitized PlotSpec
result.changes                         # list[Issue] (severity info): HTML stripped, $schema pinned ...

issues = check_plot(doc)               # errors + changes, never raises
spec, changes = sanitize_spec("plotly", figure_dict)   # bare spec, no envelope

SanitizeError is a MapiError; err.issues lists every violation (capped at max_issues), each with an RFC 6901 pointer, a platform-written message, the rule in context["rule"] and any user-supplied text only in untrusted_text. err.rules is the set of rules that fired. The error code is the most severe present:

Code HTTP Rules PLOT_UNSAFE 422 url_data, href, external_image, tile_map, proto_key, script_url, css_url, expression, format_type, config PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE 413 too_large, too_deep, too_many_nodes, string_too_long, array_too_long SPEC_PARSE_ERROR 400 parse (invalid JSON, duplicate keys, NaN/Infinity) SCHEMA_INVALID 422 schema, envelope, dataset_ref, typed_array

Changes (never errors) use the rules html_stripped, schema_url and template_pruned.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: SanitizeLimits field Default max_document_bytes 16 MiB (whole PlotSpec, inline Arrow included) max_spec_bytes 2 MiB (the spec member) max_depth 48 max_nodes 200 000 max_string_bytes 64 KiB (inline Arrow payloads are capped by the envelope instead) max_array_items 100 000 max_expr_chars 2 000 max_typed_array_bytes 8 MiB max_issues 50

docs.title: Vega-Lite rules
docs.text:
1. $schema must be an official Vega-Lite v5 or v6 URL (or absent); it is pinned to v6.4.1.
  2. The spec must validate against the vendored Vega-Lite v6.4.1 JSON Schema (draft-07, local $refs only).
  3. No url key anywhere; no href; no image mark; formatType only number, time or utc; config.customFormatTypes must not be enabled.
  4. Expressions — expr, calculate, filter/test strings (and their and/or/not compositions), any …Expr key such as labelExpr, and bracketed filters inside selection event streams — must use only allow-listed Vega functions. Method calls, this/new, assignment, statements, template and regex literals, \u/\x escapes, non-ASCII outside strings, computed member access with a non-literal key, browser globals (window, document, fetch, globalThis …) and event.view are rejected.

docs.title: Plotly rules
docs.text:
1. Top level has only data, layout, frames and config.
  2. Trace types, attribute names and value types are checked against a table derived from the official plotly.js 4.1.1 plot-schema.json (enumerations, flag lists, subplot ids, colour scales, info arrays; xaxis2-style subplot keys; annotationdefaults-style keys in templates). Unknown attributes are errors — except inside layout.template, where they (and tile-map sections) are pruned and reported.
  3. Data arrays are inline lists, dataset references or plotly.py typed arrays ({dtype: i1|u1|u1c|i2|u2|i4|u4|f4|f8, bdata, shape?}, validated for base64, length and shape).
  4. Tile-map traces/subplots, non-data:image/(png|jpeg|gif|webp);base64 image sources (also inside updatemenus/sliders relayout arguments), url/href/topojsonURL keys and network config options are rejected.
  5. Strings are stripped to <b> <i> <br> <sub> <sup> (attributes dropped, stray < escaped); <extra> survives in hover templates.

docs.text:
get_recipe(id) -> Recipe                 # bundled recipes (core + packs)
standard_recipes() -> list[Recipe]       # entry point  mapi.plots: core
mapi_plots.packs.mmm.mmm_recipes()       # entry point  mapi.plots: mmm
mapi_plots.packs.ml.ml_recipes()         # entry point  mapi.plots: ml
Recipe.render(data, **settings) -> PlotSpec       # also Recipe(data, **settings)
Recipe.catalog_entry() -> PlotCatalogEntry        # id, version, persona, required groups/representation

# what the runner calls for outputs.plots: never raises for a single bad plot
report = render_plots(tree, ["core.ppc_fan", "mmm.response_curves@^1"],
                      registry=None, options={"core.ppc_fan": {"facet": "market"}})
report.plots          # sanitized PlotSpecs
report.issues         # skipped plots: REF_UNRESOLVED / SCHEMA_INVALID / USER_CODE_ERROR
                      # (warnings) and PLOT_UNSAFE (error)
report.to_json()      # plots.json sidecar body

Write your own with the decorator — the result works with Registry.register and the mapi.plots entry-point group:

import altair as alt
from mapi_plots.recipes import Figure, RecipeSettings, named, recipe


class Settings(RecipeSettings):
    var: str = "y_hat"


@recipe("acme.weekly_total", title="Weekly total", settings=Settings, persona="guided")
def weekly_total(inp, s: Settings) -> Figure:
    ds = inp.require("summary")
    frame = ds[s.var].sel(stat="mean").sum("market").to_dataframe().reset_index()
    chart = alt.Chart(named("weekly")).mark_line().encode(x="date:T", y=f"{s.var}:Q")
    return Figure(chart, {"weekly": frame}, caption=f"Total {s.var} per week.")
