docs.title: Run protocol v0.2
docs.text:
This page specifies how a run moves from the API to a sandbox and back. It covers:

  • the run state machine;
  • the bootstrap object and the environment an execution receives;
  • the event stream the runner writes;
  • the output manifest, its verification at finalisation, and the signed bundle manifest;
  • the storage layout;
  • the ports and environment variables of a local install.

Every shape on this page is a Pydantic model or a constant in mapi_spec.run, mapi_spec.storage or mapi_spec.localdev. The API server, the executors, the runner and the tests all import them from there.

sequenceDiagram
    participant API
    participant D as Dispatcher
    participant S as Object store
    participant X as Executor
    participant R as Supervisor (runner)
    participant W as Worker (plugin code)
    API->>API: CREATED → QUEUED (static validation, quota)
    D->>D: lease → DISPATCHING, intent row (run, attempt, nonce)
    D->>S: PUT bootstrap/{nonce} (RunSpec: signed URLs, HMAC key)
    D->>X: submit(env: MAPI_RUN_ID, MAPI_NONCE)
    X->>R: start execution → PROVISIONING
    R->>S: GET + DELETE bootstrap/{nonce}
    R->>W: spawn with scrubbed env (socketpair)
    R-->>API: stdout {"mapi_event": …} (HMAC per line) → RUNNING
    W->>R: progress / results
    R->>S: signed POST/PUT outputs + manifest.json
    R-->>API: "complete" event, exit 0
    API->>S: stat + list (metadata only), server-side copy → bundles
    API->>API: FINALIZING → SUCCEEDED, signed BundleManifest

docs.title: Run states
docs.text:
RunState values are lower-case on the wire. This page writes them in upper case.

State Meaning CREATED Accepted by the API; static validation and quota not yet decided REJECTED Reserved for submissions refused by static validation or quota (terminal). The current server does not create such runs: see the note below the transition table. QUEUED Waiting for the dispatcher DISPATCHING Leased; intent row written; executor call in progress PROVISIONING The executor accepted the execution; no event seen yet RUNNING At least one verified event arrived STALLED No event for K × the progress interval. This is a warning, not a failure: the executor's status API is the liveness source of truth. FINALIZING Execution finished. Outputs are being verified and copied. SUCCEEDED A verified bundle exists (terminal) PARTIAL A verified partial bundle exists, written from checkpoints after a SIGTERM or deadline. Terminal, but can be resumed. FAILED Terminal, with a failure class: user, resource_exhausted, infra, integrity, timeout or sandbox CANCELLING The user asked to cancel; waiting for the executor to confirm CANCELLED Terminal

docs.title: Transitions
docs.text:
mapi_spec.run.transition(state, trigger, actor=...) is a pure function. It returns the matching rule, or raises IllegalTransition, which maps to 409 CONFLICT. Callers persist rule.target with a compare-and-set on the old state. When rule.new_attempt is set they also increment attempt and generate a fresh nonce. A test checks the table below against the code exhaustively, all 13 × 19 state and trigger pairs.

From Trigger To Owner Failure class New attempt CREATED accept QUEUED api CREATED reject REJECTED api QUEUED lease DISPATCHING dispatcher DISPATCHING submitted PROVISIONING dispatcher, reconciler (orphan adoption) DISPATCHING infra_retry QUEUED dispatcher, reconciler yes DISPATCHING fail_infra FAILED dispatcher, reconciler infra PROVISIONING, RUNNING, STALLED event RUNNING events PROVISIONING, RUNNING, STALLED complete FINALIZING reconciler PROVISIONING, RUNNING, STALLED infra_retry QUEUED reconciler yes PROVISIONING, RUNNING, STALLED fail_user / fail_resource_exhausted / fail_infra / fail_timeout / fail_sandbox FAILED reconciler user / resource_exhausted / infra / timeout / sandbox RUNNING silence STALLED reconciler STALLED silence STALLED (no-op) reconciler FINALIZING event FINALIZING (no-op) events FINALIZING verified SUCCEEDED finalizer FINALIZING verified_partial PARTIAL finalizer FINALIZING fail_integrity FAILED finalizer integrity FINALIZING fail_infra FAILED finalizer infra every non-terminal state except CANCELLING cancel CANCELLING api CANCELLING cancel / event CANCELLING (no-op) api / events CANCELLING cancel_confirmed CANCELLED reconciler CANCELLING complete FINALIZING reconciler PARTIAL resume QUEUED api yes

Invalid submissions create no run. POST /v1/runs and the model :score action run static validation before a run row exists. When it finds an error, the request is refused with a 4xx problem whose code is the first error's and whose errors list every issue with its JSON pointer, and nothing is stored, so there is no REJECTED run and no run history for it. CREATED → reject → REJECTED stays in the table for a later server that records refused submissions.

Rules that every component follows:

  • Events only move a run to RUNNING. All other execution-time transitions come from the reconciler. The reconciler is level-triggered and reads the executor's status.
  • complete fires when the executor reports exit code 0 or 16 and the complete event has been received. The finalizer then reads OutputManifest.status and fires verified or verified_partial.
  • infra_retry is applied only after the old execution is confirmed gone. Automatic retries are capped by cost, and there is no automatic retry once a run has spent more than 30 minutes without user consent.
  • Late events. The events service drops verified events for runs that are already terminal. Every terminal state rejects event.
  • Cancelling a FINALIZING run is a no-op at the API. The table allows the edge, but POST /v1/runs/{id}:cancel returns the run unchanged: the execution has already finished, and the finalizer may already have reserved a version number and copied write-once bundle objects.

docs.title: Bootstrap
docs.text:
The executor passes no credentials, URLs or keys through argv or the environment. The only per-execution values are MAPI_RUN_ID and MAPI_NONCE.

  1. The dispatcher writes an intent row (run, attempt, nonce). The nonce is 256 random bits written as 64 lowercase hex characters (new_nonce()).
  2. The dispatcher writes a RunSpec to gs://mapi-{env}-bootstrap/{nonce} (mapi_spec.run.RunSpec, schema runspec.json).
  3. The dispatcher calls Executor.submit(RunSubmit, nonce). For every out-of-process executor, RunSubmit.payload stays empty: the executor sees only the run id, attempt, kind, resource class, timeout and labels. Everything secret travels in the RunSpec.
  4. The supervisor resolves MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL, GETs the object, and deletes it immediately. It then validates the object as a RunSpec and starts the worker with worker_environ(), an allow-listed environment in which every MAPI_* variable is removed. If the object is missing or invalid, the supervisor exits with code 2 CONFIG_ERROR.
RunSpec field Meaning schema_version mapi.runspec/v1 run_id, attempt, nonce, kind Run identity. Parent kinds (sweep, backtest, sbc, campaign) never execute. tenant_id, project_id Always present (default in M1) spec, spec_hash, catalog_digest The resolved spec JSON (use: ranges pinned), its canonical hash, and the catalog snapshot it was resolved against inputs name → SignedGet{url, expires_at, generation, size, crc32c, md5_hash?}. Well-known names are dataset and bundle. URLs are pinned to a generation and support HTTP Range. The runner checks size and CRC32C after download and exits 13 INTEGRITY_ERROR on a mismatch. outputs name → SignedPut \| PostPolicy. manifest is a required write-once signed PUT for {prefix}manifest.json. artifacts is a create-only V4 POST policy on the attempt prefix with a content_length_range: it cannot replace an existing object, so it can't overwrite the manifest or swap an output after it was written. checkpoints is a POST policy on checkpoint_prefix, present only for checkpointable runs. resume Checkpoint objects from the previous attempt, as SignedGets checkpoint_prefix {attempt prefix}checkpoints/, or null hmac_key Base64 encoding of at least 32 random bytes; the per-run event HMAC key (new_hmac_key()). Never logged: RunSpec.redacted() blanks it, together with every URL. limits RunLimits: log_line_bytes (4096), log_total_bytes (20 MiB), max_event_bytes (64 KiB), progress_interval_s (2 s), max_output_bytes and scratch_bytes (from the resource class), max_output_objects (10 000) resource_class, deadline, created_at, labels The class (S/M/L/XL), a hard UTC deadline, and metadata

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
Variable Set by Value MAPI_RUN_ID executor, per execution The run id MAPI_NONCE executor, per execution 64 hex characters MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL executor, static per Job or backend A template with exactly one {nonce}. Cloud: gs://mapi-prod-bootstrap/{nonce}, read with the execution service account, which may get and delete but not list. Local: http://127.0.0.1:4443/storage/v1/b/mapi-local-bootstrap/o/{nonce}. MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN local executor only Bearer token of the GCS shim's exec principal, which may get and delete in the bootstrap bucket. Never set in the cloud.

RunnerEnv.from_environ() parses these and names any missing variable. RunnerEnv.resolved_bootstrap_url() substitutes the nonce into the template.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The worker cannot write the real stdout. It reports to the supervisor over a socketpair. The supervisor captures the worker's stdout and stderr, strips ANSI and control sequences, and writes one JSON object per line to its own stdout:

{"mapi_event":{"attempt":1,"hmac":"5f0c…","payload":{"chains":[],"fraction":0.4,"phase":"sample"},"run_id":"run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0","seq":12,"ts":"2026-10-15T09:31:00.123456Z","type":"progress"}}

Cloud Logging stores each line as the jsonPayload of a log entry. The sink filter is jsonPayload.mapi_event:*, and the run identity is cross-checked against the execution label. The local executor reads the same lines from the supervisor's stdout pipe. encode_event_line() and decode_event_line() implement the wire format:

  • lines that are not JSON, or JSON without mapi_event, are not events and are ignored;
  • an invalid mapi_event object, or a line over 64 KiB, raises InvalidEvent, which is a SANDBOX_VIOLATION.

Each event has these fields:

Field Rule run_id, attempt Must match the run and its current attempt seq Starts at 0 per attempt and increases by 1 per line. The receiver deduplicates on (run_id, attempt, seq). Gaps are tolerated, because logging can drop entries. ts Timezone-aware and normalised to UTC type state, progress, log, diagnostic, warning, checkpoint, metric, complete or error payload Validated against the payload model for type; see below hmac Lower-case hex HMAC-SHA256 under the run's hmac_key

What the HMAC covers:

"mapi.run-event.v1" 0x00 ‖ canonical JSON of the event without "hmac"

Canonical JSON (canonical_bytes()) is defined as follows:

  • the model is dumped in JSON mode with defaults included;
  • keys are sorted;
  • there is no whitespace;
  • the text is UTF-8 with no ASCII escaping;
  • integral floats are written as integers;
  • NaN and Infinity are rejected.

Verification uses a constant-time comparison (verify_event()). An event that fails verification is dropped and counted as a sandbox violation for that run. It never changes the run's state. Output manifests use the context tag mapi.output-manifest.v1 and bundle manifests use mapi.bundle-manifest.v1, so a signature from one domain is never valid in another.

type Payload model Notes state StatePayload{phase, message?} Runner phases: bootstrap, load_inputs, validate, preprocess, fit, sample, score, evaluate, derive, plots, upload, done progress ProgressPayload{phase, fraction?, message?, eta_seconds?, chains[]} Coalesced to at most one every limits.progress_interval_s; upserted into one run_progress row log LogPayload{stream, line, truncated} One line, at most log_line_bytes. Beyond log_total_bytes the run fails with SANDBOX_VIOLATION (log flood). diagnostic Diagnostic (mapi_spec) Rolls up into the scorecard warning WarningPayload{code, message, untrusted_text?} checkpoint CheckpointPayload{name, size, crc32c, segment, draws_done?} name is relative to checkpoint_prefix metric MetricPayload{name, value, step?, labels} complete CompletePayload{status, manifest_name, manifest_crc32c, objects, total_bytes} The last event of a successful (complete) or checkpointed (partial) attempt error ErrorPayload{code, failure_class, message, untrusted_text?} code must equal failure_class.error_code

make_event(run_id, attempt, seq, payload, key=...) infers type from the payload model and signs the event.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
The supervisor exits with 0 only after it has uploaded the manifest and emitted the complete event. failure_class_for_exit() classifies the code. Any other non-zero code, for example 1 from a crashed supervisor, is infra.

Code Name Failure class 0 OK — (success) 2 CONFIG_ERROR infra: bad environment, bootstrap missing or invalid 10 USER_ERROR user: plugin or user code raised, or produced invalid output 11 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED resource_exhausted: MemoryError or scratch budget exceeded 12 INFRA_ERROR infra: the supervisor's uploads or downloads failed after retries (a worker-reported INFRA_ERROR exits 10) 13 INTEGRITY_ERROR integrity: an input did not match its size or CRC32C 14 TIMEOUT timeout: deadline reached with no checkpoint to flush 15 SANDBOX_VIOLATION sandbox: log flood, output caps exceeded, forged or oversized events 16 PARTIAL — (SIGTERM or deadline; checkpoint flushed and a partial manifest uploaded) 137 KILLED resource_exhausted: SIGKILL, usually the OOM killer. The user is offered "retry at class + 1". 143 TERMINATED timeout: SIGTERM not handled in time

When the user cancels a run, the run is already in CANCELLING, so the exit code does not decide the outcome, with one exception. A checkpointing fit that receives the SIGTERM flushes its last checkpoint, uploads a partial manifest, sends a partial complete event and exits with 16. The reconciler then fires complete from CANCELLING, and the finalizer verifies the partial bundle, so the run ends PARTIAL and can be resumed. Any other exit ends CANCELLED.

docs.title: Outputs and finalisation
docs.text:
The runner uploads every output under its attempt prefix t/{tenant}/runs/{run}/a{attempt}/ in the runs bucket, using the artifacts POST policy. It streams each object and computes CRC32C and MD5 as it goes. Last, it PUTs manifest.json, an OutputManifest signed with the run HMAC key:

{
  "schema_version": "mapi.output-manifest/v1",
  "tenant_id": "default", "project_id": "default",
  "run_id": "run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0", "attempt": 1, "kind": "fit",
  "status": "complete",
  "prefix": "t/default/runs/run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0/a1/",
  "spec_hash": "sha256:…", "catalog_digest": "sha256:…",
  "inputs": {"dataset": {"generation": 3, "size": 1048576, "crc32c": "4waSgw=="}},
  "objects": {
    "bundle.zarr.zip": {"key": "t/default/runs/run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0/a1/bundle.zarr.zip",
                        "size": 2097152, "crc32c": "AAAAAA==", "md5": "1B2M2Y8AsgTpgAmY7PhCfg=="}
  },
  "runner_version": "0.2.0", "created_at": "2026-10-15T10:20:00Z", "hmac": "…"
}

Each object's key must equal prefix + name. Names must not contain empty, . or .. segments, and the manifest must not list itself.

Hashes follow GCS conventions:

  • CRC32C is the base64 encoding of the 4-byte big-endian value (crc32c_to_base64());
  • MD5 is the base64 encoding of the 16-byte digest.

The manifest is a claim. The control plane verifies it in the FINALIZING state without reading any object content:

  1. Metadata only. List the attempt prefix and stat objects. This yields the server-computed size, crc32c, md5Hash and generation.

  2. Compare. verify_output_objects(manifest, listing, expected_prefix=…) requires the following:

    • every claimed object exists with identical size, CRC32C and MD5;
    • no unexpected object exists under the prefix, except manifest.json and checkpoints/….

    Any discrepancy is an INTEGRITY_FAILURE issue. The run moves to FAILED(integrity) and a security alert is raised. 3. Validate sidecars. JSON sidecars (diagnostics.json, plots.json, metrics.json, coords.json; schema.json and summary.json for ingest; catalog.json for describe) are read with size caps, validated with Pydantic, and plots are sanitized. 4. Server-side copy. Each verified object is copied into the bundles bucket under t/{tenant}/models/{model}/{version}/. The copy pins source_generation to the verified generation and uses if_generation_match=0, so bundle objects are write-once. The execution service account has no access to this bucket. 5. Sign. The platform writes a BundleManifest that binds the tenant, run, base image, overlay hash, spec hash, data hash, catalog digest and every destination generation, and signs it: - M1 (local): KMS-EC-P256-SHA256 with a local P-256 key the server keeps under MAPI_DATA_DIR/keys/ (an emulation of the KMS signer, so a real KMS key can be swapped in without changing the signing bytes). Bundles signed HS256 are refused when URLs are minted; - v0.3 (M2): a Cloud KMS asymmetric signature over the same bytes.

    URLs to the bundle are minted only after verify_bundle_manifest() succeeds.

docs.title: Job payloads and object names
docs.text:
mapi_spec.jobs is the contract between the dispatcher, which writes RunSpec.spec and names the inputs, and the runner, which reads them and names the outputs. Both sides import it, so a renamed input or a changed payload fails type checks and tests on both sides.

Kind RunSpec.spec Inputs Outputs the control plane reads ingest IngestJob (a mapping or the MFF preset; dataset and source are informational) upload data.zarr.zip, schema.json (DataSchema), summary.json (DataSummary), profile.json, preview.json describe DescribeJob (image_digest) none catalog.json (Catalog) validate the resolved ModelSpec dataset, side.<name> validation.json fit the resolved ModelSpec (use: and dataset refs pinned) dataset, side.<name> bundle.zarr.zip, diagnostics.json, metrics.json (MetricsSidecar), plots.json, coords.json (ScoreMetadata.fit_coords), ui/… score the ScoreRequest bundle, bundle.manifest, dataset (the request's data), scenario, side.<name> score.zarr.zip, result.json, plots.json, ui/summary.arrow evaluate / derive / render EvaluateJob / DeriveJob / RenderJob from the run's params bundle, dataset (default: the fit dataset), side.<name>; plots for render as listed in the runner reference

side_table_input(name) builds side.<name>; SCORE_INPUTS maps a ScoreRequest's data and scenario fields to their input names. A *.zarr.zip dataset may carry its raw DataSchema as JSON in the root attribute DATASET_SCHEMA_ATTR (mapi_schema); ingest writes it, and an upload that carries it keeps its dim policies, roles and units instead of an inferred schema.

docs.title: UI views
docs.text:
Small JSON views go next to datasets and bundles for the browser (the control plane never decodes them; the web app fetches them through signed URLs). mapi_spec.views defines them and each carries a format tag:

Object format Model preview.json mapi.preview/v1 PreviewView: dim columns then variable columns, the first rows, total_rows profile.json mapi.profile/v1 ProfileView: per-variable statistics and a missingness grid along the time-like dim (at most 1,000 binned columns) ui/tree_index.json mapi.tree-index/v1 TreeIndexView: every DataTree node's dims, coordinates (values for small ones), variables and scalar attributes; no arrays ui/preprocess.json mapi.preprocess/v1 PreprocessView: every pipeline step in order (id, resolved use, kind, stateful), its learned JSON (capped at 16 KB, learned_truncated) and its numeric state arrays of at most two dims and 10,000 cells with their labels; larger arrays are named in omitted

docs.title: Storage layout
docs.text:
mapi_spec.storage builds every key on the server from validated ids (check_segment). User input never becomes a path.

Bucket (Buckets(env)) Keys Access mapi-{env}-quarantine t/{tenant}/uploads/{upload_id} Signed PUT from the browser; 7-day lifecycle mapi-{env}-bootstrap {nonce} The execution identity may get and delete, but not list; 1-day lifecycle mapi-{env}-runs t/{tenant}/runs/{run}/a{n}/[tasks/{i}/], with checkpoints/ inside Written only through signed URLs mapi-{env}-bundles t/{tenant}/models/{model}/{version}/: bundle.zarr.zip, manifest.json, manifest.sig, diagnostics.json, plots.json, metrics.json, ui/… Control plane only; write-once mapi-{env}-data t/{tenant}/datasets/{sha256}/: data.zarr.zip, schema.json, summary.json, profile.json, preview.json Content-addressed

The control plane accesses storage only through the async ObjectStore protocol:

  • reads and writes: put, get (with byte ranges and a max_bytes cap), stat (metadata only), list, delete and copy;
  • signing: sign_get (pinned to a generation), sign_put (write-once by default) and post_policy.

if_generation_match=0 means "only if the object does not exist yet". Failures raise NotFound, PreconditionFailed or AccessDenied.

docs.title: Local development
docs.text:
Component Address Override API (FastAPI) http://127.0.0.1:8000 MAPI_API_URL GCS shim (local Cloud Storage emulator) http://127.0.0.1:4443 MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT Web app (Vite dev server) http://127.0.0.1:5173 MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN Plot sandbox http://127.0.0.1:5174 MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN Postgres 16 Embedded pgserver, with its data under MAPI_DATA_DIR (default .local/) DATABASE_URL (any postgresql:// URL)

The plot sandbox must be a different origin from the web app, because plots render in a sandbox="allow-scripts" iframe with no same-origin access. LocalDev refuses a configuration that puts both on the same origin.

Other environment variables:

  • MAPI_ENV (default local) selects the bucket names, for example mapi-local-runs.
  • LocalDev.from_environ(os.environ) resolves the full configuration.
  • LocalDev.bootstrap_url_template() gives the MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL value for the local executor.

No Docker daemon is needed. Postgres comes from pgserver and storage from the GCS shim.

docs.title: Runner v0.2
docs.text:
mapi-runner executes one run inside a sandbox. It implements the run protocol from the execution's side. Two processes take part:

  • the supervisor is trusted. It holds the run's HMAC key and the signed URLs, and it is the only process that writes to the execution's stdout;
  • the worker is untrusted. It runs the platform harness (mapi_sdk) together with plugin code, and receives neither the key nor any write URL.
sequenceDiagram
    participant X as Executor
    participant S as Supervisor
    participant G as Object store
    participant W as Worker
    X->>S: start (env: MAPI_RUN_ID, MAPI_NONCE, MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL)
    S->>G: GET bootstrap/{nonce}, then DELETE that generation
    S->>W: spawn (scrubbed env, uid 10001), start message over a socketpair
    W->>G: range-read inputs (signed GET)
    W-->>S: state / progress / diagnostic / metric / checkpoint messages
    W-->>S: stdout + stderr (pipes, captured as log lines)
    S-->>X: stdout: {"mapi_event": …} (HMAC + seq per line)
    S->>G: POST outputs (policy), PUT manifest.json
    S-->>X: "complete" event, exit 0

docs.title: Starting a run
docs.text:
MAPI_RUN_ID=run_01… MAPI_NONCE=<64 hex> \
MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL='http://127.0.0.1:4443/storage/v1/b/mapi-local-bootstrap/o/{nonce}' \
MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN=<local shim exec token> \
mapi-runner

All run configuration comes from the environment. The command-line options describe the image only and never carry secrets:

Option Default Meaning --worker-python PATH this interpreter, or MAPI_WORKER_PYTHON Interpreter of the worker environment (the base image's site-packages plus any overlay) --worker-registry MODULE:CALLABLE entry points Plugin registry factory for the worker --scratch-dir DIR $TMPDIR Parent directory of the run's scratch space --keep-scratch off Keep the scratch directory after the run, for debugging --term-grace SECONDS 5 How long the worker gets to stop after SIGTERM before it is killed --deadline-reserve SECONDS 15 Time kept before the deadline for the checkpoint flush and a partial manifest --base-image NAME MAPI_BASE_IMAGE Recorded in the output manifest

docs.title: What the supervisor guarantees
docs.text:
• The bootstrap object is deleted before any untrusted code runs. The supervisor reads the object, then deletes exactly the generation it read. If the delete fails, the run stops with exit code 2.
  • Only signed events reach stdout. The supervisor keeps a private copy of the stdout descriptor for its event writer and points fd 1 at stderr. Anything the worker prints, including text that looks like an event, ends up in the line of a log event. Every line carries seq and an HMAC under the run key.
  • The worker gets a scrubbed environment. Only WORKER_ENV_ALLOWLIST passes through, so no MAPI_* variable reaches it. It starts with python -I -u in a new session, with TMPDIR set to its scratch directory. When the supervisor runs as root (Cloud Run, docker) the worker also runs as uid/gid 10001 with no supplementary groups, no_new_privs and no core dumps, and the supervisor marks itself non-dumpable. Anywhere else (macOS, a non-root shell) the run continues in dev mode: the supervisor reports a DEV_MODE_ISOLATION warning event. Dev mode is not a security boundary. An executor that promises the split sets MAPI_REQUIRE_ISOLATION=1 (the docker executor does); the supervisor then fails the run with SANDBOX_VIOLATION instead of entering dev mode.
  • Worker messages are validated. Each message is a length-prefixed JSON frame of at most 256 KiB and must match its Pydantic model. A malformed frame, an unknown type or anything sent after the final result is a SANDBOX_VIOLATION.
  • Logs are capped. ANSI escapes, control characters and bidi overrides are stripped. Lines are cut at limits.log_line_bytes (4 KB) and flagged truncated. More than limits.log_total_bytes (20 MB) of worker output is SANDBOX_VIOLATION (log_flood).
  • Worker text is cleaned. The same stripping applies to every other string the worker sends: state and progress messages, warnings, diagnostics, metric labels, and error and issue messages. Line breaks become spaces, except in untrusted_text.
  • Progress is coalesced. At most one progress event is sent per limits.progress_interval_s (2 s), and the newest value wins.
  • Outputs are uploaded only from regular files. The supervisor opens each file with O_NOFOLLOW, relative to directories it has already opened. A symlink, FIFO or device in the outputs tree is a violation, and so are the reserved names manifest.json and checkpoints/. The object and byte caps from limits apply, and the supervisor picks each object's content type from its extension.
  • The manifest describes exactly the bytes that were sent. CRC32C and MD5 are computed while each file streams through the POST policy. The OutputManifest is signed with the run key and PUT last, and the complete event follows it.
  • The scratch budget is enforced. The supervisor measures the scratch directory every 2 s, and the worker refuses any input larger than the space left. Exceeding limits.scratch_bytes is RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED.

docs.title: SIGTERM, the deadline and checkpoints
docs.text:
On SIGTERM, or when the deadline minus the reserve is reached, the supervisor:

  1. sends a RUN_TERMINATING warning event and forwards SIGTERM to the worker's session;
  2. waits for the worker to stop. The worker cancels cooperatively: samplers check for cancellation every few draws, and PyMC's segmented sampler writes a final checkpoint before it stops. After --term-grace the worker is killed;
  3. waits for checkpoint uploads that are still running;
  4. if checkpoints exist, uploads a manifest with status: partial that lists the checkpoint objects, and exits with 16 PARTIAL. Otherwise it exits with 143 (SIGTERM) or 14 (deadline).

Checkpoints are written to {scratch}/checkpoints/ as two flat files per fit key: ckpt-<key>.draws.zarr.zip and ckpt-<key>.meta.json. The supervisor uploads both with the checkpoints POST policy and emits a checkpoint event for each. A resumed attempt receives the same names in RunSpec.resume: resume names equal object names relative to the checkpoint prefix. They are downloaded before the fit starts, and the engine continues from them.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Exit When 0 Outputs and the manifest were uploaded and the complete event was emitted 2 Bad environment, missing or invalid bootstrap, or unusable outputs (no events when the RunSpec could not be read) 10 The worker reported a user, spec or data error, crashed, or exited without a result 11 Out of memory (MemoryError, or the worker was killed by SIGKILL) or the scratch budget was exceeded 12 The supervisor's own uploads or downloads failed after retries 13 An input did not match its size, CRC32C or MD5, or a bundle did not match its manifest 14 The deadline was reached without a checkpoint 15 Sandbox violation: log flood, malformed messages, unsafe outputs, oversized events or output caps 16 Partial: a checkpoint was flushed after SIGTERM or at the deadline 143 SIGTERM with no checkpoint to flush

A failure is always reported in an error event whose message is written by the supervisor. Text that comes from the worker or a plugin goes in untrusted_text. Typed issues reported by the worker, such as MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE, are also emitted as diagnostic events. The supervisor accepts only three failure classes from the worker: resource_exhausted, integrity and sandbox. A worker that reports INFRA_ERROR (for example a failed input download) fails the run as user: the infra exit makes the platform retry the whole run automatically, so only failures the supervisor observes itself may use it. Any other failure the worker reports becomes user.

docs.title: What RunSpec.spec holds, per kind
docs.text:
The dispatcher writes these documents and the runner reads them; both import the models and the input/output names from mapi_spec.jobs (see the run protocol). Inputs are read with HTTP range requests. Every dataset is a single-object *.zarr.zip. A dataset's raw schema comes from the schema input if there is one, otherwise from the zarr root attribute mapi_schema (mapi_spec.jobs.DATASET_SCHEMA_ATTR, which ingest writes and uploads may carry), and otherwise it is inferred.

Kind spec Inputs Outputs (relative to the attempt prefix) ingest IngestMapping, or IngestJob ({"mapping": …} or {"preset": "mff", "mff": {…}}, plus the informational dataset and source) upload data.zarr.zip, schema.json, summary.json (DataSummary), profile.json (mapi.profile/v1, plus sha256 and size_bytes of the data), preview.json (mapi.preview/v1) describe DescribeJob ({"image_digest": …?}) none catalog.json (Catalog), describe.json (catalog_digest, versions) validate a ModelSpec dataset, optional schema, side.<name> validation.json (ValidateResponse with the stages resolved by a dry run) fit a ModelSpec dataset, optional schema, side.<name> bundle.zarr.zip, bundle.manifest.json, diagnostics.json, plots.json, metrics.json, coords.json ({stage: {dim: CoordSummary}}), evaluation/…, ui/thin.zarr.zip, ui/summaries.json, ui/tree_index.json (mapi.tree-index/v1), ui/preprocess.json (mapi.preprocess/v1), ui/grids/*.arrow, ui/plotdata/*.arrow score a ScoreRequest, or {"request": …, "plots": […], "max_draws": n} bundle, optional bundle.manifest, dataset (payload), scenario, side.<name> score.zarr.zip, result.json, ui/summary.arrow, plots.json evaluate {"request": …?, "metrics": […]?} bundle, dataset, side.<name> the score outputs plus metrics.json derive {"names": […], "draws": n?, "data": "dataset://…"?} bundle, dataset, side.<name> derived.zarr.zip, ui/grids/<name>.arrow, result.json render {"plots": […]?, "format": "png" \| "svg", "scale": 2} plots (a plots.json) renders/<plot id>.<format>

At the top level of the attempt prefix, manifest.json is the runner's OutputManifest. For that reason the SDK bundle's own manifest is uploaded as bundle.manifest.json. The evaluation sub-bundle keeps the SDK layout (evaluation/manifest.json).

In plots.json, inline Arrow datasets larger than 64 KiB are moved to ui/plotdata/<plot>.<dataset>.arrow and referenced as data_ref, with their size and CRC32C.

docs.title: MFF preset
docs.text: The preset reads a long table with Period, VariableName and VariableValue columns. Period becomes the time dim (date, policy extend, frequency inferred). Each key column (Geography, Product, Campaign, Outlet, Creative) becomes a categorical dim only if it holds more than one distinct value. Each VariableName becomes a variable. Roles, units and column names can be overridden in mff.

docs.title: Not implemented yet
docs.text:
• optimize runs. They fail with CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED, which is reported as exit 10.
  • render needs vl-convert-python (Vega-Lite) or kaleido (Plotly) in the image. Without them the run fails with a clear message. Plots whose datasets are data_ref are not rendered.
  • netCDF-4 (HDF5) uploads need h5netcdf in the image. netCDF-3 files are read with SciPy.

docs.title: Python SDK (mapi-sdk)
docs.text:
mapi-sdk is the runtime that actually touches your arrays. It runs inside runner images and in your notebook — never in the API server — and does everything between a spec and a fitted, scoreable model: binding, preprocessing with fitted state, the train/holdout split, the model plugin, coordinate handling at score time, inverse transforms, summaries and bundles.

uv add mapi-sdk          # or: pip install mapi-sdk

docs.title: Fit and score in a notebook
docs.text:
The first-model walkthrough builds this step by step. In short, with spec, data and schema from there:

from mapi_sdk import fit_spec

bundle = fit_spec(spec, data, registry=registry, raw_schema=schema)
print(bundle.metrics.values)  # holdout metrics, in units sold: {'rmse': ..., 'mape': ..., ...}
print(bundle.metrics.n_holdout)  # 48 cells: 3 stores x 2 skus x 8 weeks

from mapi_sdk import score_bundle

future_weeks = pd.date_range(weeks[-1] + pd.Timedelta(weeks=1), periods=4, freq="W-SUN")
plan = xr.Dataset(
    {
        "price": (dims, np.full((4, 2, 4), 2.9)),
        "promo": (dims, np.zeros((4, 2, 4))),
    },
    # "west" opens next month: the model has never seen it
    coords={"store": [*stores, "west"], "sku": skus, "week": future_weeks},
)

forecast = score_bundle(
    bundle,
    """
    apiVersion: mapi/v1
    kind: ScoreRequest
    model: endpoint://quickstart/fruit-demand
    mode: forecast
    horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}
    output: {summary: [median, q10, q90]}
    """,
    plan,
    registry=registry,
)
summary = forecast["summary"].to_dataset()
print(summary["y_hat"].dims)  # ('stat', 'store', 'sku', 'week'), in your names
print(summary["y_hat"].sel(stat="median", store="west").values.round(1))
print(forecast.attrs["representation"])  # quantiles: what this model's uncertainty is
print(forecast.attrs["output_space"])  # {"y_hat": "raw"}: log1p undone, back in units sold
print(forecast.attrs["issues"])  # an info notice: 1 new level of 'store' uses 'pooled'

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from mapi_sdk import Bundle

out = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "fruit-demand-v1"
manifest = bundle.write(out)
print(sorted(p.name for p in out.iterdir()))
# ['bundle.zarr.zip', 'diagnostics.json', 'evaluation', 'manifest.json', 'metrics.json',
#  'plots.json']  - `evaluation/` is the train-only fit that produced the holdout metrics

again = Bundle.read(out, registry)  # every file's size and hashes are verified here
assert again.bundle_id == bundle.bundle_id

For a model whose representation is draws, add draws: 50 to output and the tree also has a draws group: 50 joint draws taken from the bundle-wide thinning index.

score_bundle returns an xr.DataTree. Its root attributes record the representation, the output kind (expected or predictive), the output space of every variable (for example weekly — inverse transforms stop at the last reshape step), retransformation labels for point models, and any warnings. Counterfactual requests add baseline/ and delta/ groups.

docs.title: How fitting works
docs.text:
fit.mode: evaluate_then_refit (the default) does this:

  1. Bind dataset names to canonical names and check the data against its schema.
  2. Run the stateless prefix of the pipeline on all data, up to the split stage.
  3. Split, fit the remaining steps and the model on train.
  4. Score the holdout through the normal score path (with context rows from train) and compute evaluate.metrics.
  5. Refit every step and the model on all data, so the context tails and terminal state that forecasts start from are the latest ones. The production bundle links the evaluation bundle in its lineage.

train_only stops after step 4 and keeps the train fit.

docs.title: How scoring works
docs.text: Phase What happens CoordPlan Typed early errors from metadata: UNSEEN_LEVELS, COORD_NOT_ALLOWED, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT (409), MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE, NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION, MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED, ... Entry Data enters at inputs_stage (default raw). Steps before it — and their side tables — are skipped. Replay Each step's stored state is applied; steps with a look-back (lags) get their stored per-group context rows prepended first, after a contiguity check. Canonical coords Model-stage data is reordered to the fit order, padded to the full fit set, and new levels are appended with a <dim>__is_new flag. Model plugin.score(...) returns the predictions group in the plugin's representation. Back to you Context rows are dropped, requested coords selected, outputs inverted to the output space, aggregated (only if statistically valid), summarised and reverse-bound to your dataset names.

docs.title: Representations and summaries
docs.text:
Representation Shape Summaries Aggregation draws (chain, draw, …) mean, sd, median, hdi_<p>, eti_<p>, q<p> any (per draw) quantiles (quantile, …) median, q<p>, eti_<p> (interpolated, never extrapolated) none interval (bound, …) interval, point none point (…) mean, point sum/mean, flagged moments (moment, …) mean, sd, eti_<p> none

Asking for something invalid — summing quantiles, draws from a point model — fails with CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED instead of returning a misleading number.

docs.title: Data on the wire
docs.text:
mapi_sdk.wire reads and writes the platform's formats. Readers treat every payload as hostile.

  • XrJSON (to_xrjson / from_xrjson): the xr.Dataset.to_dict() shape with explicit dtypes, null for missing values and caps on elements, dims and string length. Good for small payloads and curl.
  • zarr zip (write_zarr_zip / read_zarr_zip, write_datatree_zip / read_datatree_zip): single-object zarr v3 archives. Strings are vlen-utf8, datetimes are int64 nanoseconds with explicit units, only zstd/blosc compression is accepted, MultiIndexes are reset and restored. The bytes are deterministic.
  • Rows (stack_rows / unstack_rows): stack dims into rows, drop empty rows, and restore them later from the recorded row mask.
  • Arrow IPC (to_arrow_table, write_arrow_ipc): tidy tables for UI views.

Pickle is never used, anywhere.

docs.title: Data checks in plain language
docs.text:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import xarray as xr
from mapi_sdk import infer_schema, validate_dataset
from mapi_spec import DimPolicy

days = pd.date_range("2026-03-01", periods=28, freq="D")
markets = ["DE", "FR", "UK"]
channels = ["tv", "search"]
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
media = xr.Dataset(
    {
        "revenue": (("market", "date"), rng.gamma(50.0, 20.0, (3, 28))),
        "spend": (("market", "channel", "date"), rng.gamma(5.0, 100.0, (3, 2, 28))),
    },
    coords={"market": markets, "channel": channels, "date": days},
)

schema = infer_schema(
    media,
    targets=["revenue"],
    policies={"market": "new_levels"},
    units={"revenue": "EUR", "spend": "EUR"},
)
print(schema.dims["date"].policy, schema.dims["date"].freq)  # extend D
print(schema.dims["channel"].policy)  # fixed
print(schema.vars["revenue"].role)  # target

broken = media.copy(deep=True)
broken["revenue"].loc[{"market": ["FR", "UK"], "date": days[10:12]}] = np.nan

for issue in validate_dataset(schema, broken):
    print(issue.severity, issue.code, "-", issue.message)
# error SCHEMA_INVALID - 2 markets are missing 2 days of revenue in March 2026

docs.title: Bundles
docs.text: A bundle directory holds bundle.zarr.zip (spec, schemas, binding, every step's state and context, the model's ArviZ-named groups, native artifacts, fit coordinates per stage, pinned side tables and the thinning index) plus manifest.json, diagnostics.json, plots.json and metrics.json. The manifest records CRC32C and MD5 (in the form GCS reports) and SHA-256 for every file; Bundle.read verifies them.

docs.title: Running work through an executor
docs.text:
InprocExecutor implements the platform's Executor protocol in your own process — handy for notebooks and tests, never for untrusted code:

import asyncio

from mapi_plugin_tabular.datasets import (
    STORE_DEMAND_SCHEMA,
    STORE_DEMAND_SPEC_YAML,
    store_demand_dataset,
)
from mapi_sdk import InprocExecutor
from mapi_spec.executor import ExecState, RunEventType, RunKind, RunSubmit

history = store_demand_dataset(stores=4, skus=2, weeks=60, seed=1)
recent = history.isel(week=slice(-8, None))  # a window of fitted weeks to re-score

executor = InprocExecutor(
    # dataset refs in specs and requests resolve to in-memory datasets
    resolver={
        "dataset://retail/store_sku_weekly@latest": history,
        "dataset://retail/last_8_weeks@v1": recent,
    },
)
print(executor.caps().isolation.name)  # NONE: your own code, in your own process

async def main() -> None:
    fit = await executor.submit(
        RunSubmit(
            run_id="fit-001",
            kind=RunKind.FIT,
            payload={
                "spec": STORE_DEMAND_SPEC_YAML,
                "raw_schema": STORE_DEMAND_SCHEMA.model_dump(mode="json"),
            },
        ),
        nonce="nonce-fit-0001",  # resubmitting the same nonce returns the same run
    )
    status = await executor.wait(fit, timeout=300)
    print(status.state)  # succeeded
    for event in executor.events(fit):  # the same event stream a cloud run will produce
        if event.type is RunEventType.PROGRESS:
            print(event.seq, event.payload.get("message"))  # 2 validated the spec and the data

    executor.put_bundle("store-demand@1", executor.result(fit))
    score = await executor.submit(
        RunSubmit(
            run_id="score-001",
            kind=RunKind.SCORE,
            payload={
                "bundle": "store-demand@1",
                "request": {
                    "apiVersion": "mapi/v1",
                    "kind": "ScoreRequest",
                    "model": "endpoint://retail/store-demand-xgb",
                    "mode": "predict",
                    "data": "dataset://retail/last_8_weeks@v1",
                },
            },
        ),
        nonce="nonce-score-0001",
    )
    assert (await executor.wait(score, timeout=300)).state is ExecState.SUCCEEDED
    tree = executor.result(score)  # an xr.DataTree, exactly what score_bundle returns
    print(dict(tree["summary"].to_dataset()["y_hat"].sizes))
    # {'stat': 3, 'store_id': 4, 'sku': 2, 'week': 8}


asyncio.run(main())  # in Jupyter: `await main()`

See Runs and executors.

docs.title: Error codes you may see
docs.text: Every error is a MapiError with a stable code and, where useful, a JSON pointer. Anything your data or a plugin said is kept in untrusted_text, separate from the message. StepError (USER_CODE_ERROR) wraps failures inside steps, SchemaValidationError (SCHEMA_INVALID) reports data problems, BundleError (INTEGRITY_FAILURE) reports damaged or tampered bundles and RunCancelled (CANCELLED) reports cooperative cancellation.

docs.title: Spec format reference
docs.text:
Every model on modeling-api starts as a ModelSpec: a small YAML (or JSON) file that names your dataset, the preprocessing pipeline, the model plugin and how to fit and evaluate it. The same file drives the Guided wizard, the Expert editor, the CLI and the API.

apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: eu-geo-mmm, project: growth}

data:
  dataset: dataset://growth/eu_media_daily@latest
  side_tables:
    fx: {ref: dataset://growth/fx_daily@latest, score_policy: supplied}
  bind:
    dims: {geo: market, channel: channel, time: date}   # canonical name: dataset name
    vars: {y: revenue_local, spend: spend_local}
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: time, last: 8, after_step: weekly}

pipeline:
  - {id: to_eur, use: core.fx_convert@^1, with: {vars: [y, spend], table: fx, to: EUR}}
  - {id: weekly, use: core.resample@^1,   with: {dim: time, freq: W-SUN, how: sum}}
  - {id: scale,  use: core.mean_scale@^1, with: {vars: [spend], over: [time]}}

model:
  use: mmm.hierarchical_geo@^1.3
  settings:
    dim_policies: {geo: fixed}      # may only tighten the plugin's policy
  fit: {mode: evaluate_then_refit, draws: 1000, chains: 4, seed: 7}

evaluate: {metrics: [elpd_loo, coverage_90, mape]}
execution: {resource_class: M, timeout: 45m}

docs.title: Sections
docs.text: Section Purpose metadata name and project (lowercase slugs), optional labels and description data.dataset dataset://<project>/<name>@latest|vN|sha256:<hex> — pinned to an exact version at submit data.side_tables Small constant datasets (FX, holidays). score_policy: pinned, latest or supplied data.bind Maps canonical names (what plugins and steps use) to dataset names. Outputs are reverse-bound by default data.split time_holdout, last_per_group, as_of, leave_group_out or mask_block, applied at after_step pipeline Ordered steps {id, use: <id>@<semver range>, with: {...}} model Plugin use, its settings and the fit block outputs Derived quantities, plot recipes and the number of draws kept for the UI evaluate Holdout metrics (elpd_loo, coverage_90, mape, rmse, ...) execution Resource class (S, M, L, XL) and timeout (45m, 1h30m). Each class caps the input data a run reads (dataset plus side tables): S 0.5 GB, M 2 GB, L 5 GB, XL 50 GB. Validation reports PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE at /execution/resource_class when the data is bigger, and names the class that fits. Ingest runs pick the smallest class that holds the upload.

docs.title: Versions in use:
docs.text: use: takes an npm-style semver range: ^1 (any 1.x), ~1.2 (1.2.x), >=1.2 <2, 1.x, an exact 1.2.3, or *. The highest matching non-yanked version is chosen at submit time and recorded with the run, so re-running a revision is reproducible.

docs.title: Where the split happens
docs.text: Some dims only exist after preprocessing — daily data resampled to weeks, for instance. The split therefore happens at a named stage (after_step). If you leave it out, the split happens right after the leading steps that learn nothing from the data (such as unit conversion and resampling). If a step that learns from the data (scaling, encoding, seasonality fits) runs before the split, validation reports LEAKAGE_RISK: its state would be learned from the holdout.

docs.title: Validation messages
docs.text:
mapi spec check and POST /v1/specs:validate return every problem at once, each with a stable code and a JSON pointer to the offending field:

{"code": "SPLIT_INVALID", "pointer": "/data/split/dim",
 "message": "split dim 'week' does not exist at stage 'raw'",
 "suggested_action": "Set data.split.after_step to the stage where the dim exists (e.g. after a resample step)."}
Code Meaning SCHEMA_INVALID A field has the wrong shape, or a step/model needs data the pipeline does not produce SPEC_PARSE_ERROR Not valid YAML/JSON, or uses anchors, aliases or tags (not allowed) PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE Over 256 KB, nesting deeper than 32 or more than 10 000 values REF_UNRESOLVED Unknown step, model, plot, side table or derived quantity, or no matching version SETTINGS_INVALID Settings don't match the step's or model's settings schema BINDING_INVALID data.bind names something the dataset does not have SPLIT_INVALID The split dim does not exist at the split stage LEAKAGE_RISK A stateful step runs before the split DIM_POLICY_LOOSENED dim_policies tries to loosen a plugin's dim policy RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED A lag of the target is shorter than the holdout/horizon

docs.title: Score requests
docs.text:
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ScoreRequest
model: endpoint://growth/eu-geo-mmm-prod
mode: forecast                    # predict | forecast | counterfactual | simulate | filter | evaluate
horizon: {dim: time, periods: 26}
inputs_stage: scale_spend         # supply weekly EUR spend directly; earlier steps are skipped
scenario: dataset://growth/plan_2027h1
interventions: [{var: spend, sel: {channel: meta}, multiply: 1.2}]
output: {kind: expected, summary: [mean, hdi_90], draws: 200}

Score requests are checked against the fitted model before anything runs: unseen levels on fixed dims (UNSEEN_LEVELS), horizons beyond what the fit supports (HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT, HTTP 409 — refit required), missing future values of covariates (MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE), gaps after the fitted range (NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION) and summaries the model's uncertainty representation cannot support (CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED — for example summing quantiles).

docs.title: JSON Schemas
docs.text: Editors can validate specs as you type using the published JSON Schemas (GET /v1/schemas/modelspec.json, or python -m mapi_spec export-schemas ./schemas).

docs.title: Built-in steps (core.*)
docs.text:
The mapi-steps package ships the preprocessing steps every spec can use without writing code. Each step is a small, versioned, typed transform with:

  • a settings model (validated twice: by the API against the exported JSON Schema, and by the runner with Pydantic);
  • a fitted state for steps that learn something (scales, levels, a Fourier origin). States are learned on the training data only and replayed — never refitted — at score time;
  • a static schema effect, so the API can check a whole pipeline (names, dims, units, the split stage) in milliseconds without running any step code;
  • a context need for steps that look back in time (lags, carry-over), so scoring a forecast sees exactly the history the model was fitted with.

Reference a step in a spec by id and semver range, e.g. use: core.mean_scale@^1.

Where the data is after each step

The API shows the schema at every stage (POST /specs:validate). Use it to see which variables, dims and units each step produces before you fit anything.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
Step Kind Learns state Invertible Looks back What it does core.resample reshape – – – Aggregate a time dim to a coarser frequency (W-SUN, MS, …); drops partial periods core.count_events reshape – – – Count rows of an event table per period (and per group) on a dense grid core.filter_coords reshape – – – Keep/drop labels of a dim, or an inclusive date range core.to_long reshape – – – Padded ragged data → one row per observation plus *_idx index variables core.to_padded reshape – – – Long ragged rows → padded (group, position) grid with a mask core.stack / core.unstack reshape – – – Combine dims into one, and back core.fx_convert value – ✓ – Currency conversion with per-period rates from a side table core.mean_scale value ✓ ✓ – Divide by the mean absolute value over named dims core.max_abs_scale value ✓ ✓ – Divide by the maximum absolute value over named dims core.standardize value ✓ ✓ – (x - mean) / sd over named dims core.log1p value – ✓ (non-linear) – log(1 + x) core.logit value – ✓ (non-linear) – log(p / (1 - p)) for shares core.impute value ✓ – – Fill gaps: mean, median, constant or forward fill (ffill) core.replace_sentinel value – – – Turn codes such as -99 (or values below/above a bound) into missing core.clip value – – – Cap values to [lower, upper] core.fourier feature ✓ (origin) – – Seasonal sin/cos features core.trend feature ✓ (origin, span) – – Polynomial time trend scaled to the fitted range core.calendar feature – – – Day of week, ISO week, month, quarter, weekend/month-end flags core.holidays feature – – – Holiday days per period from a side table core.lag feature – – ✓ Lagged copies {v}_lagged(…, lag) within groups core.lag_tensor feature – – ✓ Replace v by its lags 0 … l_max-1 (for in-model carry-over) core.one_hot feature ✓ (levels) – – Indicator columns for categories seen at fit core.encode_levels feature ✓ (levels) – – Integer codes for categories or dim labels core.missing_indicator feature – – – {v}_missing flags core.formula feature – – – A new variable from an arithmetic expression core.adstock value – – ✓ Carry-over with fixed parameters (point models) core.saturation value – – – Diminishing returns with fixed parameters (point models)

Reshape steps change structure and are never inverted: predictions come back through value steps as far as the last reshape (an E33 model fitted on weekly EUR returns weekly EUR). Value steps that are invertible are undone on the way out. Non-linear inverses (log1p, logit) label point predictions as median or use retransform: smearing.

docs.title: The E33 pipeline, step by step
docs.text:
pipeline:
  - {id: to_eur,      use: core.fx_convert@^1, with: {vars: [y, spend], table: fx, to: EUR,
                                                     currency_dim: geo, currencies: {UK: GBP},
                                                     default_currency: EUR}}
  - {id: weekly,      use: core.resample@^1,   with: {dim: time, freq: W-SUN, how: sum}}
  - {id: scale_spend, use: core.mean_scale@^1, with: {vars: [spend], over: [time], unseen_levels: pooled}}
  - {id: scale_y,     use: core.mean_scale@^1, with: {vars: [y], over: [time], unseen_levels: pooled}}
  - {id: lags,        use: core.lag_tensor@^1, with: {vars: [spend], along: time, within: [geo], l_max: 6, pad: first}}
  - {id: season,      use: core.fourier@^1,    with: {along: time, period: 52.18, order: 3}}
  - {id: hols,        use: core.holidays@^1,   with: {table: holidays, along: time}}
  1. to_eur multiplies daily local-currency revenue and spend by the day's rate. Markets map to currencies with currencies, and anything unlisted uses default_currency, so a new market can still be scored. Markets already in EUR use a rate of 1. Rates must cover every needed day; otherwise the step raises SIDE_TABLE_COVERAGE.
  2. weekly sums days into Sunday-ending weeks and drops the partial first and last weeks. This is the default split stage, and the holdout is the last weeks.
  3. scale_* learn scale(geo, channel) and scale(geo) on the training weeks. A market that wasn't seen at fit gets the average scale (unseen_levels: pooled).
  4. lags turns spend(geo, channel, time) into spend(geo, channel, time, lag). It stores the last 6 weekly, scaled rows per market at fit time. When you forecast, those rows are prepended, so the first forecast week sees real history. A brand-new market has no stored history, so its earliest lags are padded with its first value (pad: first).
  5. season learns the origin week once. Forecasts continue the same seasonal phase.
  6. hols counts holiday days per week from the daily holidays table.

docs.title: Unseen levels
docs.text:
Steps that learn per-level state (mean_scale, max_abs_scale, standardize, impute, one_hot, encode_levels) take unseen_levels. It decides what happens when a score request contains a level that wasn't in the training data:

Policy Scaling/impute steps one_hot encode_levels error (default) UNSEEN_LEVELS (422) UNSEEN_LEVELS UNSEEN_LEVELS pooled average of the learned values training frequencies of each level one shared "new" code fill fill_value (neutral by default) all zeros fill_code

docs.title: Looking back: lag, lag_tensor, adstock
docs.text:
along is the time dim. within lists the group dims; on long data it lists row variables such as a household id. Each step stores the last n rows per group at its own input stage. When a forecast starts right after the fitted range, the stored rows are prepended and the result is identical to transforming the whole series. If the request skips periods, the step raises NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION.

core.lag of a target is a recursive feature: a forecast horizon longer than the smallest lag is rejected with RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED unless the model handles recursion itself.

docs.title: Forward fill
docs.text: core.impute with method: ffill carries the last observation along along within groups. At fit time it also stores the last observed value per series. Data that starts right after the fitted range (a holdout or a forecast) therefore continues the fitted series exactly, for any gap length. limit caps how many consecutive missing values are filled, counting the missing rows at the end of the training data.

docs.title: Full periods
docs.text: core.resample with full_periods_only: true (the default) keeps a period only if the source data covers every day of it. It checks this against the source frequency (for example D), so a short February still counts as a full month.

docs.title: core.formula
docs.text:
- {id: margin, use: core.formula@^1,
   with: {out: margin, expr: "(price - cost) / price", dims: [store, sku, time], units: "1"}}

The expression language has numbers, variable names and 'strings' (for dim names). It supports these operators:

  • + - * / **
  • comparisons < <= > >= == !=
  • & | ~
  • parentheses
Functions element-wise log log1p exp expm1 sqrt abs sign floor ceil sin cos tanh expit logit two arguments minimum maximum fillna three arguments clip(x, lo, hi), where(cond, a, b) missing values isnull notnull reductions sum mean max min — sum(spend, 'channel') names that are not identifiers var('unit-price')

The result is float64 and must have the declared dims; it is broadcast when it has fewer. There are no attribute lookups, indexing, imports or other calls, and expressions are limited in length and nesting.

Note

The formula language exists to make specs easier to write. It is not a security boundary: like all step code, it only ever runs inside the sandboxed runner.

docs.title: Precompute for point models: adstock and saturation
docs.text:
Bayesian models learn carry-over and saturation inside the model. Point models (sklearn, ridge) get them as preprocessing with fixed parameters. Each parameter is either a number or a mapping per level of by, for example a different decay per channel:

- {id: carry, use: core.adstock@^1,
   with: {vars: [spend], along: time, within: [geo], kind: geometric, l_max: 8,
          alpha: {tv: 0.7, search: 0.2, social: 0.4}, by: channel, normalize: true}}
- {id: sat, use: core.saturation@^1, with: {vars: [spend], kind: hill, slope: 1.2, half: 80}}
adstock kind weights over lags l = 0 … l_max-1 parameters geometric alpha ** l alpha in [0, 1) delayed alpha ** ((l - theta) ** 2) alpha, theta ≥ 0 weibull_pdf Weibull density at l + 1, scaled to [0, 1] lam, k > 0 weibull_cdf cumulative survival, starting at 1 lam, k > 0 saturation kind curve parameters logistic (1 - exp(-lam x)) / (1 + exp(-lam x)) lam hill x^slope / (half^slope + x^slope) slope, half michaelis_menten alpha x / (lam + x) alpha, lam tanh alpha tanh(x / (alpha c)) alpha, c

docs.title: Splits
docs.text:
A spec chooses its train/holdout split in data.split. The split is applied at the split stage, after the stateless prefix. In E33 that is after weekly resampling, because the week dim only exists from there on. The built-in kinds also have catalog identities, so the UI and the docs can describe them:

Split Use it for core.time_holdout the last last periods, a fraction, or everything after a label core.as_of backtests: train up to as_of, skip gap periods, evaluate the rest core.leave_group_out new markets or stores: hold out whole groups core.last_per_group panels and choice data: the last rows of each group with at least min_len rows core.mask_block random blocks of cells over several dims (the model must accept missing targets)

docs.title: The catalog the API uses
docs.text:
python -m mapi_steps.catalog            # Catalog JSON: steps, settings schemas, effects
python -m mapi_steps.catalog --splits   # … plus the split catalog

Runner images generate this JSON when they are built, and the API validates specs against it without importing step code. The same file ships inside the package as mapi_steps/catalog.json.

In a notebook, mapi_steps.registry() returns a registry with every step. The mapi.steps entry point also makes them available to mapi_sdk.default_registry().

docs.title: API client
docs.text:
apps/web/openapi.json is the control plane's own OpenAPI 3.1 document, written by uv run python apps/web/scripts/gen_openapi.py from mapi_server.app.openapi_document() (no database needed). pnpm --filter @mapi/web openapi:types generates src/api/schema.d.ts from it, and openapi-fetch gives typed calls. CI fails when either file drifts from the server (gen_openapi.py --check, openapi:check). Run-event payloads (StatePayload, ProgressPayload, …) are published as components so SSE frames are typed too.

Variable Default Meaning VITE_API_BASE http://127.0.0.1:8000 The API. It must allow this origin (MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN, CORS). VITE_PLOTS_ORIGIN http://127.0.0.1:5174 The plot sandbox; must differ from the app origin. VITE_STORAGE_ORIGINS http://127.0.0.1:4443 Signed-URL origins allowed by the CSP connect-src. The GCS shim answers CORS for MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN. VITE_APP_ORIGINS (sandbox) http://127.0.0.1:5173,http://localhost:5173 Origins allowed to embed the sandbox and talk to it.

scripts/dev.py sets these from the MAPI_* URLs, so make dev on other ports just works.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• App origin. A strict CSP with script-src 'self', connect-src limited to the API and storage origins, frame-src the plot sandbox only, and require-trusted-types-for 'script' with a default policy that admits same-origin script URLs only. Untrusted text (logs, tracebacks, untrusted_text, plugin messages) renders as text with ANSI, control and bidi characters stripped. Artifact downloads are checked against the ArtifactLink size and CRC32C.
  • Plots. Every plot, first-party included, renders in a sandbox="allow-scripts" iframe on the sandbox origin (no allow-same-origin). The sandbox refuses URL data, href encodings, image marks, Plotly layout images and tile maps before any library loads; Vega runs with ast: true and the interpreter, a loader that rejects every URL and a text-only tooltip; Plotly uses the strict bundle. Its CSP is default-src 'none' with frame-ancestors set to the app origins.
  • Messages. The mapi.plot/v1 postMessage protocol is validated strictly in both directions. Because the framed document has an opaque origin, the app accepts a message only when event.source is the iframe's window and event.origin is "null", and stops posting if the frame ever navigates after its first load.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
pnpm -r test            # Vitest (both apps) + the Playwright smoke suite (mock API, production build)
pnpm --filter @mapi/web e2e   # @e2e specs against a running stack (MAPI_E2E=1)

The smoke suite runs the mock-mode production build and fails on any CSP or Trusted Types violation. The @e2e specs reuse a running make dev stack; set VITE_API_BASE, MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN and MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN when it runs on other ports.

docs.title: Sanitizer
docs.text:
The JSON-only PlotSpec sanitizer (plan §10.3, step 1).

This is the control-plane half of plot safety. It depends only on mapi-spec and jsonschema and never imports numpy, pandas, altair or plotly (enforced by import-linter and a subprocess test), so mapi_server can run it on every plot it stores or serves.

from mapi_plots.sanitize import sanitize_plot result = sanitize_plot(plot_json) # PlotSpec | dict | str | bytes result.plot # the sanitized PlotSpec result.changes # what was rewritten (HTML stripped, ...)

Anything unsafe raises :class:SanitizeError (a MapiError) whose issues carry the JSON pointer, the :class:SanitizeRule (in context["rule"]) and any user-supplied text in untrusted_text. :func:check_plot returns the same issues without raising (for editors).

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
Role/dim-bound plot templates (plan §10.1).

A template is an ordinary :class:~mapi_spec.plots.PlotSpec whose bindings say what to plot in schema terms ({x: "dim:time", y: "role:target", facet: "dim:geo"}) instead of naming one bundle's variables. :func:apply_template resolves the bindings against a :class:~mapi_spec.schema.DataSchema and fills the placeholders in the spec, so one user-authored "fan chart of the target over time, faceted by geo" applies to every model of a family. This module is JSON-only (it runs in the control plane).

Placeholders inside spec:

  • {"$bind": "y"} - replaced by a Vega-Lite field definition {"field": ..., "type": ..., "title": ...}; dropped entirely when the channel is optional and unresolved (so encoding.facet simply disappears for a model without geo);
  • "{{y}}" - the bound name; "{{y.field}}" - the name escaped for Vega-Lite field access (dots); "{{y.type}}" - the Vega-Lite type; "{{y.title}}" - name plus units. Placeholders may be embedded in longer strings (titles, captions).

docs.title: Converters
docs.text:
Build :class:~mapi_spec.plots.PlotSpec envelopes from Altair charts and Plotly figures.

Extra recipes only (needs altair, plotly, numpy, pandas and pyarrow).

  • :func:from_altair moves every inline dataset (Altair's consolidated datasets and any data.values) into named Arrow datasets and rewrites the references to {"name": ...}; named data (alt.Data(name=...)) is filled from datasets=.
  • :func:from_plotly decodes plotly.py 6 typed arrays ({dtype, bdata, shape}) and inline data arrays into named Arrow datasets, one per trace (and array length), and binds them with {"$ref": "<dataset>.<column>"}. String columns get the inline-text rules here (HTML stripped to the Plotly allow-list, script/CSS URLs rejected) because the control-plane sanitizer never decodes Arrow; the plot iframe must still re-strip dataset strings.

Both run the result through the sanitizer unless sanitize=False. Datasets are base64 Arrow IPC streams (:class:~mapi_spec.plots.InlineArrow); datetimes are stored as UTC millisecond timestamps, which JavaScript reads as numbers.

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text:
The standard plot recipe catalog (plan §10.2). Extra recipes only.

Every recipe is a function (DataTree-like, settings) -> PlotSpec with its data in named Arrow datasets (never URLs), a persona and a plain-language caption. They are generated in the runner from a fitted bundle or a score output, so every plugin gets them for free:

============================ ========================================================== core.data_overview series per variable, missingness heatmap, group sizes core.prior_predictive prior predictive densities (+ fan over time) core.convergence R-hat / ESS per parameter, worst-parameter table, trace, rank core.posterior_forest point, 50% and 94% HDI per parameter core.ppc predictive density overlay, PIT histogram, coverage core.ppc_fan fit + forecast fan with the split line core.fit_vs_actual predicted against actual core.residuals_over_time actual minus predicted over time core.decomposition stacked contributions and totals core.model_comparison elpd forest (precomputed LOO table, or WAIC) core.counterfactual scenario vs baseline band + total-change distribution core.decision_distribution scalar decision objective per option ============================ ==========================================================

The MMM domain pack lives in :mod:mapi_plots.packs.mmm and the tabular-ML pack (ml.feature_importance) in :mod:mapi_plots.packs.ml. All are exposed through the mapi.plots entry-point group, so mapi_sdk.registry.default_registry() finds them.

docs.title: mapi_pymc
docs.text: PyMC models: write build(), get engines, diagnostics, new levels and counterfactuals.

docs.title: The base class
docs.text:
PyMCModel: authors write build(); the platform fits, predicts and checkpoints (§5).

.. code-block:: python

class Radon(PyMCModel[RadonSettings]):
    id = "demo.radon"
    version = "1.0.0"
    Settings = RadonSettings
    schema_template = {...}
    outputs = {"y": {"dims": ["obs"], "units_of": "y"}}
    expected = {"y": "mu"}             # output -> Deterministic holding E[y]

    def build(self, ds, s, ctx):
        with pm.Model(coords=ctx.coords()) as m:
            floor = ctx.data("floor")
            county = ctx.data("county_idx")
            a = ctx.hier_effect("a", "county")
            b = pm.Normal("b", 0, 1)
            mu = pm.Deterministic("mu", a[county] + b * floor, dims="obs")
            pm.Normal("y", mu, pm.HalfNormal("sigma", 1), observed=ctx.observed("y"),
                      dims="obs")
        return m

fit dispatches to the engine in fit.engine (see :mod:mapi_pymc.engines), adds the opt-in groups (prior/prior_predictive, log_likelihood, a thinned posterior_predictive) and turns r-hat, ESS and divergences into diagnostics.

score rebuilds the model on the canonicalised score data and runs pm.sample_posterior_predictive(..., predictions=True) against the posterior:

  • output.kind = expected returns the Deterministic named in :attr:PyMCModel.expected (no observation noise; counterfactual deltas on it are exact per draw);
  • output.kind = predictive returns draws of the observed variable through icdf(dist, U) with frozen uniforms U seeded by (seed, name, shape). A counterfactual's scenario and baseline therefore share their noise (common random numbers) and the delta's variance is not inflated. Discrete distributions without a symbolic inverse CDF (Poisson, negative binomial, binomial) sample their parameters and push the same frozen uniforms through a numeric inverse CDF (noise = crn_ppf), so a change in one cell's mean never reshuffles the noise of the others. Only distributions with neither fall back to the seeded sampler stream (seeded_stream), whose draws in unchanged cells can still differ between a scenario and its baseline - prefer kind: expected deltas for those.

docs.title: Build context
docs.text:
BuildContext: what a PyMC model's build() uses instead of raw coordinates (plan §5).

build(ds, settings, ctx) runs twice in a model's life: at fit on the training data, and at score on canonicalised score data (fit levels in fit order, then new levels, padded extend dims). The helpers hide the differences so the same build serves both:

  • :meth:BuildContext.coords - the pm.Model(coords=...) mapping; adds <dim>__fit and <dim>__new when the score data holds unseen levels;
  • :meth:BuildContext.data - pm.Data over the current values (rebuild-and-predict);
  • :meth:BuildContext.observed - the target at fit, a shape-only placeholder at score;
  • :meth:BuildContext.hier_effect - a hierarchical effect over a new_levels dim whose new levels are filled according to the dim's strategy (hyperprior draws them from the fitted hyperprior during prediction, with frozen noise so scenario and baseline agree);
  • :meth:BuildContext.position / :attr:BuildContext.anticipated_coords - stable positions along extend dims, so trends and HSGPs see the same axis at fit and at forecast time.

docs.title: hier_effect
docs.text:
hier_effect(
    name: str,
    dim: str,
    *,
    mu: Any = None,
    sigma: Any = None,
    centered: bool = False,
    mu_sigma: float = 1.0,
    sigma_scale: float = 1.0,
) -> TensorVariable

A partially pooled effect over dim: name[dim] ~ Normal(mu, sigma).

Creates name (dims dim) - non-centred by default via name__offset - plus hyperpriors name__mu ~ Normal(0, mu_sigma) and name__sigma ~ HalfNormal (sigma_scale) unless mu/sigma are given (mu may be a scalar or a vector over the full dim). When the score data holds unseen levels, name__new covers them according to the dim's new-level strategy:

  • hyperprior - mu + sigma * z with z frozen standard-normal noise, i.e. a fresh level drawn from the fitted hyperprior for every posterior draw;
  • pooled - the population mean mu;
  • zero - 0;
  • error - raises UNSEEN_LEVELS.

Returns the effect over the full current dim (fit levels, then new levels).

docs.title: Engines
docs.text:
Inference engines for :class:~mapi_pymc.PyMCModel (plan §5).

fit.engine picks one of:

============== ========================================================================== nutpie nutpie NUTS (default when installed). Fast, parallel chains. Not bit-for-bit reproducible from a seed. Checkpoints are snapshots (draws so far): nutpie cannot export its adaptation, so a retry samples again from the start. pymc PyMC NUTS with segmented sampling: tune once, then draw in chunks of fit.checkpoint.every_draws. After each chunk a resumable checkpoint holds the draws, every chain's position and the full sampler state; a retry resumes exactly where the last chunk ended. Chains run in this process one after another (models with discrete variables fall back to pm.sample without segments). numpyro PyMC's external NUTS bridges, when the library is installed. No segments. blackjax map pm.find_MAP - one "draw" (chain 1, draw 1). advi mean-field ADVI; fit.tune is the number of optimisation steps (default 10,000) and fit.draws the number of draws from the approximation. pathfinder pymc-extras' Pathfinder when pymc-extras is installed. ============== ==========================================================================

Every engine reports progress through one callback (fraction, message) where the message names the chain ("chain 2/4: sampling 150/500, 0 divergences").

docs.title: Fast scoring
docs.text:
FrozenPredictor: one compiled PyTensor function for fast posterior predictions (plan §5).

Ported from pymc-model-interactivity/frozen_predictor.py to PyMC 6 / PyTensor 3 and ArviZ 1.x (posteriors are xr.DataTree / xr.Dataset). Given a model, posterior samples, response expressions and the pm.Data inputs to vary, it compiles a single function vectorised over posterior samples and scenarios:

  • only the free random variables that are ancestors of the responses are bound, to constant posterior samples (so compilation stays small);
  • observed random variables upstream of a response are replaced by their observed values when they do not depend on the inputs, and by icdf(dist, U) with frozen uniform quantiles U (one per sample) when they do - common random numbers across scenarios;
  • SpecifyShape constraints on dims that only the inputs use are removed, so inputs may change length (dims shared with other model variables stay fixed).

Inputs may have the data variable's own shape (one scenario) or an extra leading scenario axis. Outputs have shape (sample, [scenario,] *dims) before the optional reducer.

The plan's FrozenPredictorSpec(response_exprs, input_vars, reducer) is the JSON form a plugin declares when capabilities.fast_score is true.

docs.title: Checkpoints
docs.text:
Checkpoints for segmented sampling (plan §5, §8.3).

A long MCMC fit tunes once and then draws in chunks. After each chunk the engine hands a :class:SamplingCheckpoint to a :class:CheckpointSink; a retried run with the same fit key resumes from the last checkpoint instead of starting again.

Two kinds of checkpoint exist:

  • resumable (engine pymc): the draws so far, every chain's current position and the full NUTS sampling state (adapted step size, mass matrix, RNG state). Resuming continues the same chains exactly; the result equals an uninterrupted run with the same seed.
  • snapshot (engine nutpie): the draws so far only. nutpie cannot export or restore its adaptation state, so a snapshot feeds a PARTIAL bundle but a retry starts again.

Nothing here pickles. Sampling states are encoded to JSON by :func:encode_state; arrays travel base64-encoded and dataclasses are rebuilt only from classes defined in an allow-list of PyMC step-method modules (and this package).

docs.title: Supervisor <-> worker channel
docs.text:
The supervisor <-> worker message channel (a socketpair; plan §8.7).

Frames are a 4-byte big-endian length followed by one UTF-8 JSON object. Every message is validated against the models below; the worker is untrusted, so anything malformed, oversized or of an unknown type is a SANDBOX_VIOLATION on the supervisor side.

docs.title: Supervisor
docs.text:
The trusted supervisor (plan §8.1, §8.5, §8.7).

One supervisor runs per execution. It:

  1. reads MAPI_RUN_ID/MAPI_NONCE/MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL, fetches the RunSpec bootstrap object and deletes it before anything else happens;
  2. starts the untrusted worker (python -I -u -m mapi_runner.worker) as a child with a scrubbed environment, a socketpair for messages and pipes for stdout/stderr - as uid 10001 with no-new-privs when it runs as root, in dev mode otherwise;
  3. validates every worker message, turns them and the captured output into HMAC-signed events on its own stdout (the only thing ever written there), enforces the log, event, scratch and output caps, and coalesces progress;
  4. handles SIGTERM and the run deadline (forward to the worker, wait for the checkpoint flush, upload a partial manifest);
  5. uploads outputs with the signed POST policy (streaming, hashing as it goes), writes the signed :class:~mapi_spec.run.OutputManifest with the signed PUT and exits with a :class:~mapi_spec.run.RunnerExit code.

The supervisor never imports plugin code, the SDK, numpy or xarray.

docs.title: Worker isolation
docs.text:
Worker process isolation inside the execution (plan §8.1, §9).

When the supervisor runs as root (Cloud Run gen2 / docker), the worker is started as uid/gid 10001 with no supplementary groups, PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS and no core dumps, and the supervisor makes itself non-dumpable so the worker cannot ptrace it. Anywhere else (macOS, a developer's non-root shell) the uid split is impossible: the run proceeds in dev mode and the supervisor says so in a warning event. Dev mode is never a security boundary.

docs.title: Fit and score
docs.text:
The fit/score harness: the platform side of every run (plan §4.2).

:func:fit_spec implements fit.mode:

  • bind the data, validate it, fit the stateless prefix on all data up to the split stage;
  • split; fit the remaining step states and the model on train (the evaluation fit);
  • evaluate the holdout through the score path (context from train) - never a separate code path - and compute the spec's metrics;
  • evaluate_then_refit: refit states and model on train ∪ holdout so the context tails and terminal state come from the full data; the production bundle links the evaluation bundle and its metrics. train_only keeps the train fit as the result.
  • derived quantities the spec requests (outputs.derived) whose manifest declaration says cache: fit are computed on the production fit by the plugin's derive hook, over the first outputs.ui_draws draws of the thinning index, with ScoreContext.to_original mapping them to the output space.

:func:score_bundle implements scoring: CoordPlan checks, binding, interventions, entry at inputs_stage, context replay, canonical coords, model.score, context removal, selection, inverse transforms to the output space, aggregation, summaries, thinned draws and reverse binding. It returns an xr.DataTree.

score_bundle(

A counterfactual scores the scenario (or the data, when no scenario is given) with the interventions applied against the baseline data; a scenario without baseline data is rejected.
