docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
The preprocessing step contract: Step, StepState and StepContext.

A step is a class with static metadata (id, version, kind, a Pydantic Settings model, an optional State model) and four methods::

fit(ds, settings, ctx) -> State           # learn on train data only
transform(ds, settings, state, ctx) -> ds # never learns; must tolerate an absent target
inverse(ds, settings, state, ctx) -> ds   # invertible VALUE steps only

Rules the contract kit (:mod:mapi_sdk.testing) enforces:

  • transform(train, fit(train)) equals the fit-time output exactly, and transform is deterministic and does not mutate its input;
  • reductions name the dims they reduce over; the state stays labelled by the rest;
  • group-local operations take along/within and declare a :class:ContextNeed;
  • unseen levels go through :meth:StepContext.align_state;
  • the static :class:~mapi_spec.effects.SchemaEffect (effect_template) matches the real output schema.

The static metadata is exported as a :class:~mapi_spec.catalog.StepCatalogEntry, so the control plane validates specs without importing step code.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
The model plugin contract (plan §5).

A plugin turns a model-stage xr.Dataset into a :class:FitOutput and, later, scores a canonicalised dataset into an xr.DataTree whose predictions group holds the declared outputs in the plugin's :class:~mapi_spec.capabilities.Representation::

draws      (chain, draw, *dims)
quantiles  (quantile, *dims)       quantile coords in (0, 1)
interval   (bound, *dims)          bound coords include "lower", "upper" (+ "point")
point      (*dims)
moments    (moment, *dims)         moment coords ["mean", "sd"]

The platform owns everything around that: binding, CoordPlan, context, canonical coords, inverse transforms, reverse binding and summaries. :class:CustomModel is the base class for hand-written plugins; mapi_pymc.PyMCModel and mapi_sklearn.SklearnModel build on the same protocol.

docs.title: Pipelines
docs.text:
The pipeline engine: stages, fitting, score-time replay and the inverse chain (plan §4.2).

A stage is the dataset after a named step (raw is the bound input before any step). :meth:Pipeline.fit fits and transforms a range of stages, recording each step's state and its per-group context tail at the step's input stage. :meth:Pipeline.transform replays stored states over a range of stages, prepending each step's context before it runs (:mod:mapi_sdk.context). :meth:Pipeline.inverse_outputs maps model outputs back through invertible VALUE steps up to the last RESHAPE step and labels the output space.

docs.title: inverse_outputs
docs.text:
inverse_outputs(
    ds: Dataset,
    states: Mapping[str, StepState],
    var_sources: Mapping[str, str],
    *,
    to_stage: str | None = None,
    from_stage: str | None = None,
    representation: Representation = DRAWS,
    retransform: Retransform = "median",
    residuals: Mapping[str, DataArray] | None = None,
    side_tables: Mapping[str, Dataset] | None = None,
    decompositions: Collection[str] = (),
) -> InverseResult

Map output variables back to their output space.

var_sources maps each output variable to the input variable whose transforms it inherits (y_hat -> y). Inversion stops at to_stage (default: the last RESHAPE stage) or at the first non-invertible step that touched the variable. Point outputs through a non-linear inverse are labelled median (plain inverse) or use Duan's smearing over stored model-space residuals; moments use the first-order delta method (g(mu), |g'(mu)| sd with a central difference).

decompositions name additive decompositions (contributions(component, ...)). They are inverted component by component only through additive steps (Step.additive); through any other inverse (expm1, x * sd + mean) the components would no longer sum to the inverted prediction, so inversion stops right after that step and :attr:InverseResult.kept says why.

docs.title: Bundles
docs.text:
Fitted-model bundles: one bundle.zarr.zip DataTree plus JSON sidecars (plan §8.6).

Layout of bundle.zarr.zip::

/                       attrs: format, bundle_id, role
/spec                   attrs: spec (canonical JSON), resolved (ResolvedSpec JSON)
/schema/raw             attrs: json (dataset-named raw DataSchema)
/schema/model           attrs: json (model input schema, effective policies)
/binding                attrs: json
/preprocess/<step_id>   attrs: state (JSON); children: arrays, context
/model                  attrs: manifest, settings, fit_config, learned (JSON)
/model/<group>          ArviZ-named groups (posterior, sample_stats, log_likelihood ...)
/terminal_state         plugin-owned state for sequential models
/native                 uint8 arrays of safe native artifacts (skops, xgb json, ...)
/derived/<name>         derived quantities cached at fit
/fit_coords/<stage>     coordinates of the fitted data at every stage
/side_tables/<name>     pinned side tables used at fit
/residuals              model-space residuals (point models, smearing)
/thin                   the bundle-wide draw thinning index

Sidecars: manifest.json (content hashes of every file: size, CRC32C and MD5 in the GCS base64 form, SHA-256), diagnostics.json, plots.json and metrics.json. An evaluate_then_refit bundle keeps its train-only evaluation bundle under evaluation/. Pickle is never written and is rejected on read.

docs.title: Coordinates
docs.text:
CoordPlan checks, coordinate canonicalisation and horizon coordinates (plan §4.2-4.3).

  • :class:CoordPlan runs the static checks of :func:mapi_spec.validate.validate_score_request against the bundle's fit coordinates and the actual score payload, raising typed errors (UNSEEN_LEVELS, COORD_NOT_ALLOWED, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT, MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE, NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION, ...).
  • :func:canonicalise_coords reorders model-stage score data to the fit order, pads requested subsets to the full fit set, appends unseen levels (flagged by <dim>__is_new) and returns a :class:CanonicalPlan that selects the requested coords back afterwards.
  • :func:horizon_coords / :func:horizon_frame generate future coordinates from a dim's frequency (or integer step).

docs.text:
canonicalise_coords(

    schema: DataSchema | None,
    *,
    pad_extend: bool = True,
    marks: Collection[ContextMark] = (),
    pad_fill: float = 0.0,
) -> tuple[Dataset, CanonicalPlan]

Reindex model-stage score data to the fit coordinate order.

  • fixed dims: labels must be fit labels (UNSEEN_LEVELS); data is reindexed to the full fit set (padding unrequested labels);
  • new_levels dims: fit labels in fit order, then unseen labels appended (the <dim>__is_new coordinate flags them; strategy error raises);
  • extend dims: labels may not start before the fit range (COORD_NOT_ALLOWED), must continue it without gaps (NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION) and may not exceed max_extension (HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT); with pad_extend the full fit range is included so positional models see a contiguous axis.

Padded cells of numeric non-target variables are filled with pad_fill and target variables with NaN; <dim>__requested marks real labels.

docs.title: Summaries
docs.text:
Representation-aware summaries, aggregation and draw thinning (plan §5).

Outputs come in one of five representations (see :mod:mapi_sdk.models). Which summaries and aggregations are valid depends on the representation; the rules live in :data:mapi_spec.capabilities.REPRESENTATION_RULES and are enforced here:

  • draws: every summary; any aggregation (applied per draw);
  • quantiles: median/quantiles/ETI (interpolated on the stored quantile grid, never extrapolated); no aggregation;
  • interval: the interval and its point; no aggregation;
  • point: mean/point; linear aggregation only, flagged;
  • moments: mean/sd and normal ETIs; no aggregation.

Summaries are returned as one variable per output with a leading stat dim whose labels read like mean, hdi_90_lower, hdi_90_upper, q5 ... HDIs are computed in numpy (narrowest window over sorted draws).

In-process executor (isolation NONE) for notebooks, tests and mapi fit on own code.

Implements the :class:mapi_spec.executor.Executor protocol: submit starts the run in a worker thread, status is the source of truth, cancel is cooperative (checked between pipeline phases) and event_source yields :class:~mapi_spec.executor.RunEvent objects. Payloads are JSON only; dataset references are resolved by a resolver.

Supported run kinds: fit (payload spec, data, optional side_tables and raw_schema) and score/evaluate (payload request, bundle - a bundle directory or a key registered with :meth:InprocExecutor.put_bundle - and optional data/scenario/side_tables; otherwise the request's data/scenario refs are used). A counterfactual resolves data as the baseline and scenario as the scenario.

Never use this executor for untrusted code: it runs plugins in the caller's process.

docs.title: Wire formats
docs.text:
Wire formats: XrJSON, single-object zarr v3 zips, DataTree zips, stacking and Arrow IPC.

Encoding rules (plan §3.2), applied by every writer here:

  • any pandas.MultiIndex is reset before persisting (and recorded so readers restore it);
  • string coords and variables are zarr v3 vlen-utf8 (data type string);
  • datetimes are int64 nanoseconds with explicit units and calendar attrs;
  • only the zstd and blosc compressors are written or accepted;
  • :func:stack_rows drops empty rows and records a row mask so :func:unstack_rows restores them.

Pickle (and joblib/cloudpickle) is never used for anything. Readers treat every payload as hostile: zip entries, zarr metadata, codecs, dtypes and sizes are checked before any array is decoded.

docs.text:
stack_rows(
    ds: Dataset,
    dims: Sequence[str],
    new_dim: str = "row",
    *,
    drop: Literal["all", "any", "none"] = "all",
    mask_var: str | None = None,
) -> Dataset

Stack dims into one new_dim and drop empty rows, recording a row mask.

A row is dropped when all (drop="all") or any ("any") of the variables that use every stacked dim are missing there (lower-rank variables, which are broadcast, only decide when no variable is full-rank), or where mask_var is false. The result has no MultiIndex: the component coords are plain coords along new_dim and the boolean <new_dim>__rowmask variable (over the original dims, with their full coords) says which rows were kept, so :func:unstack_rows can restore the dropped rows as missing.

docs.text: scikit-learn and xgboost models: write estimator(), get stacking, safe persistence and uncertainty.

docs.title: Base classes
docs.text:
SklearnModel: scikit-learn and xgboost estimators on labelled data (plan §5).

A plugin author implements only :meth:SklearnModel.estimator, returning an allow-listed estimator (a choice from :data:~mapi_sklearn.estimators.ESTIMATORS, a {kind, params} mapping, or an instance of an allow-listed class). The platform:

  1. stacks the rows dims of the model-stage dataset into samples and builds the design matrix from the selected variables and coordinate features (:mod:mapi_sklearn.design), dropping incomplete rows through the SDK row mask;
  2. fits one or more estimators for the plugin's uncertainty kind;
  3. persists them with skops or xgboost JSON (never pickle);
  4. at score time rebuilds the same columns, handles unseen levels (:mod:mapi_sklearn.levels), predicts and unstacks back to labelled arrays in the plugin's representation:

================= ===================== ========================================== base class representation predictions group ================= ===================== ========================================== SklearnModel point y_hat(*rows) (+ contributions) SklearnQuantile quantiles y_hat(quantile, *rows) SklearnBootstrap draws y_hat(chain, draw, *rows) SklearnConformal interval y_hat(bound=[lower, upper, point], *rows) SklearnClassifier point y_hat(*rows) = P(target == positive) ================= ===================== ==========================================

Forecasting is direct only: future features must be supplied (or produced by the pipeline from coordinates); forecast_strategy: recursive raises RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED.

SklearnQuantileModel()

Bases: SklearnModel[SettingsT]

Conditional quantiles (representation quantiles).

docs.title: SklearnBootstrapModel
docs.text:
SklearnBootstrapModel()

Bases: SklearnModel[SettingsT]

Bootstrap ensemble (representation draws: chain=1, one draw per replicate).

expected outputs are the replicate predictions (uncertainty of the fitted mean); predictive outputs add an out-of-bag residual drawn per cell, approximating the predictive distribution. Draws are joint across cells, so every aggregation is valid.

docs.title: SklearnConformalModel

SklearnConformalModel()

y_hat(bound=[lower, upper, point], ...) with attribute alpha: each interval covers the observed value with probability at least 1 - alpha for data exchangeable with the calibration rows. Intervals have per-cell coverage only and cannot be summed.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Settings of the scikit-learn / xgboost model plugins.

A spec's model.settings for sklearn.* plugins looks like::

estimator: {kind: xgboost.XGBRegressor, params: {n_estimators: 600, max_depth: 6}}
rows: [store, sku, time]               # dims stacked into samples
time_dim: time                         # the row dim that extends at forecast time
columns: {roles: [covariate]}          # which variables become feature columns
coord_features: {store: category, sku: category}
uncertainty: {kind: quantile, quantiles: [0.05, 0.5, 0.95]}
forecast_strategy: direct
retransform: median

The uncertainty kind fixes the output representation, so each kind is its own plugin (sklearn.tabular_quantiles accepts only kind: quantile and so on).

docs.title: Estimator registry
docs.text:
The allow-listed estimator registry.

Plugins never import arbitrary classes. An estimator is chosen by kind from :data:ESTIMATORS, and its hyper-parameters are validated by that kind's Pydantic params model (extra="forbid", bounded values). The platform then builds the estimator with every parameter passed explicitly, so behaviour does not drift when a library changes a default. Parameters the platform owns (seeds, threads, categorical handling and the loss/objective an uncertainty kind needs) are not part of the params models.

In a spec::

estimator: {kind: xgboost.XGBRegressor, params: {n_estimators: 600, max_depth: 6}}

docs.title: Loading and hashing
docs.text:
Strict YAML 1.2 / JSON loading, apiVersion upgrades, canonical JSON and spec hashing.

The loader is safe for hostile input:

  • size ≤ 256 KB, nesting depth ≤ 32, ≤ 10 000 nodes (all configurable via :class:Limits);
  • YAML anchors, aliases, explicit tags (!foo, !!python/...), %TAG directives and multiple documents are rejected;
  • plain scalars are resolved with the YAML 1.2 core schema (yes/on/0777/dates stay strings), NaN/Infinity are rejected, duplicate keys are rejected and every mapping key must be a string;
  • JSON input is parsed with the same limits.

:func:load_document returns a typed document (discriminated on kind) after running the apiVersion upgrade chain (the API accepts N and N-1). :func:canonical_json and :func:spec_hash give a normalised, deterministic serialisation for immutable revisions.

docs.title: Schema effects and stages
docs.text:
Step kinds, SchemaEffects, context needs and static schema propagation.

A :class:SchemaEffect is a data-free description of how a preprocessing step changes a :class:~mapi_spec.schema.DataSchema. Step authors export it as JSON (per image digest); the control plane evaluates it with :func:propagate and never imports step code.

Effects may be templates: strings can reference the step's settings with the :mod:~mapi_spec.template placeholder syntax ("{dim}", "{*vars as v}"). Every referenced setting must be listed in template_params. :func:resolve_effect renders a template with concrete settings into a plain :class:SchemaEffect.

Within one effect, operations apply in this order: renames → drops → transforms_dims → stacks → unstacks → updates → derives → adds.

docs.title: Static validation
docs.text:
Static (JSON-only) validation of ModelSpecs and ScoreRequests.

:func:validate_spec checks a :class:~mapi_spec.spec.ModelSpec against a :class:~mapi_spec.catalog.Catalog and the dataset's raw :class:DataSchema:

  1. binding references exist and do not collide;
  2. every use: resolves to a non-yanked version (semver range);
  3. step and model settings validate against their JSON Schemas;
  4. side-table references exist;
  5. the schema is propagated through every step's SchemaEffect, with per-step input checks;
  6. the split stage is resolved (default: end of the stateless prefix), its dims exist there, and LEAKAGE_RISK is raised if a stateful step precedes it;
  7. the model's schema template is resolved and compared with the final stage; spec dim policies may only tighten the plugin's;
  8. recursive forecasting (a target-dependent lag feeding a longer holdout) is rejected unless the model owns recursion; outputs, plots, metrics and resource class are checked.

:func:validate_score_request runs the static CoordPlan checks for a ScoreRequest from metadata only (resolved spec + fit coordinate summaries + dim policies).

Every finding is an :class:~mapi_spec.errors.Issue with a JSON pointer into the document.

docs.title: Run protocol
docs.text:
See Run protocol for the narrative specification.

The run protocol (plan §8.1, §8.3–§8.7): state machine, bootstrap, events, manifests.

Everything a control plane, an executor and a runner must agree on lives here, as pure Pydantic / stdlib code:

  • :class:RunState, :class:RunTrigger and the transition table :data:TRANSITIONS, with the pure function :func:transition used by the API, dispatcher, events service, reconciler, finalizer and tests;
  • :class:RunSpec — the bootstrap object written to bootstrap/<nonce> before an execution starts (signed URLs, a per-run HMAC key, limits, deadline);
  • :class:~mapi_spec.executor.RunEvent payload models, canonical HMAC-SHA256 signing and verification, and the stdout JSONL wire format ({"mapi_event": {...}} per line);
  • :class:OutputManifest (the runner's claim), metadata-only verification against server-computed hashes, and the platform-signed :class:BundleManifest;
  • the runner invocation contract: environment (:class:RunnerEnv) and exit codes (:class:RunnerExit).

Executor-facing shapes (:class:Isolation, :class:ExecutorCaps, :class:Handle, :class:ExecStatus, :class:RunKind, :class:RunEvent, ...) are defined in :mod:mapi_spec.executor and re-exported here unchanged, so both import paths name the same classes.

docs.title: Job payloads
docs.text:
See Job payloads and object names.

Run job payloads: what RunSpec.spec holds for each run kind, plus the input and output object names shared by the control plane (which writes RunSpecs and reads outputs) and the runner (which reads RunSpecs and writes outputs).

========== ============================================ ====================================== kind RunSpec.spec inputs (RunSpec.inputs names) ========== ============================================ ====================================== ingest :class:IngestJob (a bare IngestMapping upload (the raw file; dataset is also accepted) is accepted as a fallback) describe :class:DescribeJob none validate a ModelSpec document dataset, optional schema, side.<name> fit a ModelSpec document dataset, optional schema, side.<name> score a ScoreRequest document, or bundle, optional :class:ScoreJob bundle.manifest, dataset (the request's data), scenario, side.<name> evaluate :class:EvaluateJob bundle, dataset, ... derive :class:DeriveJob bundle, dataset, side.<name> render :class:RenderJob plots (a plots.json) ========== ============================================ ======================================

Datasets are single-object *.zarr.zip files. A dataset's raw schema comes from the schema input, else the zarr root attribute mapi_schema (written by ingest), else it is inferred. bundle is the bundle.zarr.zip of a fit and bundle.manifest the SDK bundle manifest that the fit uploaded as bundle.manifest.json.

This module is pure Pydantic (no numpy/xarray): the control plane imports it.

docs.title: Object storage
docs.text:
Object storage contracts (plan §8.6): metadata, the ObjectStore protocol, signed URLs, integrity hashes and the bucket/key naming scheme.

The control plane talks to object storage only through :class:ObjectStore. Two implementations exist outside this package: ShimObjectStore (the local GCS emulator in mapi_gcs_shim) and GcsObjectStore (google-cloud-storage). Both expose GCS semantics:

  • every write creates a new generation; if_generation_match=0 means "only if the object does not exist" (write-once);
  • the server computes CRC32C (base64 of the big-endian 4-byte value) and MD5 (base64 of the 16-byte digest) — uploader-supplied hashes are never evidence;
  • signed GET URLs are pinned to a generation and honour HTTP Range; signed PUT URLs and V4 POST policies (key prefix + content-length-range) are how sandboxes write, so the executor never holds storage credentials.

Object keys are always built server-side from validated IDs with the helpers at the bottom of this module (never from user-supplied paths).

docs.title: ObjectStore
docs.text:
Bases: Protocol

Async object-store driver used by the control plane (GCS semantics).

Conventions shared by every method:

  • generation pins the source generation to read (None = live generation);
  • if_generation_match is a precondition on the target: 0 means "must not exist", n means "live generation must be n"; a failed precondition raises :class:PreconditionFailed;
  • missing buckets/objects raise :class:NotFound; denied operations raise :class:AccessDenied.

docs.title: SignedGet
docs.text:
Bases: StrictModel

A generation-pinned signed GET URL plus the server-computed facts about its object.

The URL honours HTTP Range, so zarr zip readers can range-read one object. A reader verifies size/crc32c after a full download (corruption check only — integrity is enforced by the control plane).

docs.title: SignedPut
docs.text:
Bases: StrictModel

A signed PUT URL for exactly one object name.

headers must be sent verbatim (they are part of the signature): typically content-type, x-goog-if-generation-match: 0 (write-once) and x-goog-content-length-range: 0,<max_bytes>.

docs.title: PostPolicy
docs.text:
Bases: StrictModel

A V4 POST policy: multipart form uploads of any key under prefix.

The uploader posts multipart/form-data to url with every entry of fields, then key (which must start with prefix), then the file part last. The storage service rejects bodies outside content_length_range and keys outside the prefix.

A create_only policy cannot replace an existing object (its signed conditions carry x-goog-if-generation-match: 0), so the holder can neither overwrite the write-once manifest nor swap an output after it was written.

docs.title: REST DTOs
docs.text:
See HTTP API (v1) for the endpoint table and conventions.

REST DTOs for the M1 HTTP API (/v1; plan §8.2 subset).

Conventions shared by every endpoint (see docs/reference/http-api.md):

  • Requests reject unknown fields (extra="forbid"); responses ignore unknown fields when parsed by a client, so older clients keep working when the server adds fields.
  • Every resource carries tenant_id and project_id. M1 is single-tenant: both are :data:DEFAULT_TENANT_ID / :data:DEFAULT_PROJECT_ID, but the identity is in every row and key so M2 can add row-level security without migrations churn.
  • Lists return :class:Page (items + opaque next_cursor); errors are RFC 7807 :class:~mapi_spec.errors.Problem documents with stable codes.
  • Timestamps are timezone-aware RFC 3339 strings in UTC.

:data:M1_ENDPOINTS is the machine-readable endpoint table; the server's route table and the reference docs are tested against it.

docs.title: mapi_steps
docs.text:
The built-in core.* steps. For every step's settings, see the generated steps catalog.

Built-in preprocessing steps for modeling-api (core.*).

Every step implements the :class:mapi_sdk.steps.Step contract and exports static JSON (settings schema, templated :class:~mapi_spec.effects.SchemaEffect, context need) so the control plane can validate specs without importing this package. Steps are discovered through the mapi.steps entry point (:func:builtin_steps); :func:registry returns a ready :class:~mapi_sdk.registry.Registry, and python -m mapi_steps.catalog prints the catalog JSON.

docs.title: Catalog export

Static catalog export: python -m mapi_steps.catalog [--splits] [--out FILE].

Prints the :class:mapi_spec.catalog.Catalog JSON of every built-in step (settings JSON Schema, templated SchemaEffect, context need, kind, flags). Runner images generate it at build time; the control plane loads it to validate specs without importing step code. --splits adds the split catalog under a separate splits key (not part of Catalog). The same JSON ships with the package as mapi_steps/catalog.json.

docs.title: Splits
docs.text:
The five built-in train/holdout splits (plan §4.1 "Split" group).

Splits are not pipeline steps: a spec chooses one in data.split and the harness applies it at the split stage (:func:mapi_sdk.split.split_dataset), after the stateless prefix. This module gives each split kind a catalog identity (core.<kind>@1.0.0) with its settings schema and plain-language summaries for pickers and docs, plus a direct :meth:SplitStrategy.split for notebooks and tests.

======================== ==================================================================== core.time_holdout hold out the last last periods / a fraction / after a label core.as_of train up to and including as_of; optional gap periods core.leave_group_out hold out whole groups (explicit groups or n random ones) core.last_per_group last last rows of each group with at least min_len rows core.mask_block random blocks over dims covering fraction of the cells ======================== ====================================================================

docs.title: mapi
docs.text:
Usage: mapi [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  The modeling-api command line.

  Local commands (new, check, fit, score, catalog, plugin, spec) need no server. Remote commands
  (runs, datasets, --remote) use the API from --url, MAPI_URL or a profile in
  ~/.config/mapi/config.toml, with --token or MAPI_TOKEN. --json prints machine-readable output
  on stdout.

Options:
  --url <str>           API base URL (default: MAPI_URL, profile, local)
  --token <str>         Bearer token (default: MAPI_TOKEN, profile)
  --profile <str>       Config profile (default: MAPI_PROFILE)
  --json                Machine-readable JSON on stdout
  --version             Show the version
  --install-completion  Install completion for the current shell.
  --show-completion     Show completion for the current shell, to copy it or customize the
                        installation.
  -h, --help            Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  new       Scaffold a ModelSpec YAML from a template (geo-mmm, forecast, tabular, glm).
  check     Statically validate a spec (exit status 1 when it has errors).
  fit       Fit a spec locally (in-process) or on the API (--remote).
  score     Score a fitted bundle locally, or a model version on the API (--remote).
  catalog   Show the catalog of the locally installed plugins (or the API's with --remote).
  serve     Start the local development stack (API, embedded Postgres, GCS shim).
  runs      Inspect and control runs on the API.
  datasets  Datasets on the API.
  plugin    Plugin authoring: scaffold and test model plugins.
  spec      Spec document tools.
  config    Client configuration (~/.config/mapi/config.toml).

docs.title: Error codes
docs.text: Every error is a MapiError with one of these stable codes. Over HTTP it becomes an RFC 7807 problem document (application/problem+json) whose type ends in the code. Anything your data or a plugin said is returned separately, as untrusted_text.

docs.title: Spec and static validation
docs.text: Code HTTP Meaning Retryable SCHEMA_INVALID 422 The document does not match its schema – SPEC_PARSE_ERROR 400 The document could not be parsed – PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE 413 The document exceeds a size limit – UNSUPPORTED_API_VERSION 422 Unsupported apiVersion – REF_UNRESOLVED 422 A reference could not be resolved – SETTINGS_INVALID 422 Settings do not match their schema – BINDING_INVALID 422 The data binding is invalid – SPLIT_INVALID 422 The train/holdout split is invalid – LEAKAGE_RISK 422 A stateful step runs before the split – DIM_POLICY_LOOSENED 422 A dim policy may only be tightened – SCHEMA_DYNAMIC 422 Schema needs a dry-run to resolve – SIDE_TABLE_COVERAGE 422 A side table is not available – PLOT_UNSAFE 422 The plot spec violates the plot safety policy –

docs.title: Score-time coordinate checks (CoordPlan)
docs.text: Code HTTP Meaning Retryable UNSEEN_LEVELS 422 Unseen levels on a dim that forbids them – COORD_NOT_ALLOWED 422 Coordinates not allowed by dim policy – HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT 409 Horizon exceeds the fitted range – MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE 422 A future covariate is missing – NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION 422 Extension is not contiguous – CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED 422 The model lacks this capability – RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED 422 Recursive forecasting unsupported –

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text: Code HTTP Meaning Retryable MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED 422 Score mode not supported –

docs.title: Quotas
docs.text: Code HTTP Meaning Retryable QUOTA_EXCEEDED 429 Quota exceeded – RATE_LIMITED 429 Too many requests yes

docs.title: API
docs.text: Code HTTP Meaning Retryable UNAUTHENTICATED 401 Authentication required – FORBIDDEN 403 Not allowed – NOT_FOUND 404 Not found – CONFLICT 409 Conflict – IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT 409 Idempotency key reused – PRECONDITION_FAILED 412 Precondition failed –

docs.title: Run failures
docs.text: Code HTTP Meaning Retryable USER_CODE_ERROR 422 User or plugin code failed – RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED 507 Run exhausted its resources – INFRA_ERROR 503 Infrastructure error yes INTEGRITY_FAILURE 500 Output integrity check failed – TIMEOUT 504 Run timed out – SANDBOX_VIOLATION 422 Sandbox policy violated – CANCELLED 409 Run was cancelled –

docs.title: Internal
docs.text: Code HTTP Meaning Retryable INTERNAL_ERROR 500 Internal error yes

docs.title: mmm.hierarchical_geo
docs.text:
Hierarchical geo marketing-mix model: geometric/delayed adstock over a lag tensor, logistic or Hill saturation, channel effects partially pooled across geos, new geos drawn from the hyperprior, additive contributions, response curves and marginal costs in original units, and a budget objective for optimisation.

Version 1.3.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes counterfactual, evaluate, forecast, predict, simulate Contributions additive Decision objective yes Fast scoring yes Owns – LOO valid Default plots core.ppc_fan, core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, mmm.decomposition, mmm.response_curves, mmm.marginal_cost Resources class M (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description y_hat (geo, time) of y Expected (or predictive) target contributions (component, geo, time) of y Additive contribution of each channel, the baseline and each control; sums to y_hat

Derived quantities (outputs.derived)

Name Dims Units Cached Description contributions (sample, channel, geo, time) target fit Channel, baseline and control contributions over the fit window per thinned draw, in original units response_curves (sample, channel, multiplier, geo) target fit Total contribution per spend multiplier, channel and geo per thinned draw (Guided-mode slider grids) marginal_cost (sample, channel, geo) spend per target fit Extra spend per extra unit of the target at current spend

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description pooling partial or complete or none partial basic How channel effects are shared across geos: partial pooling (default), one effect for all geos, or independent geos (no new geos at score time) centred boolean false advanced Centred parameterisation of the geo-level effects (non-centred samples better with few geos or little data per geo) adstock AdstockSettings {"kind": "geometric", "l_max": null, "normalize": true} basic saturation SaturationSettings {"kind": "logistic"} basic priors Priors {"intercept": null, "intercept_sigma": null, "beta_channel"… advanced Prior overrides by parameter (pymc-marketing Prior dict form) controls list of string (optional) null advanced Control variables (default: every other numeric variable along time) lag_dim string lag advanced Lag dim of the spend tensor grid GridSettings {"max_multiplier": 2.0, "points": 21, "marginal_step": 0.01} advanced Nested settings types Input data contract (schema template) 
{
  "params": {
    "lag_dim": {
      "type": "string",
      "default": "lag"
    },
    "pooling": {
      "type": "string",
      "path": "pooling",
      "enum": [
        "partial",
        "complete",
        "none"
      ],
      "default": "partial"
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "geo": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "new_levels",
        "new_level_strategy": "hyperprior"
      },
      "channel": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "fixed"
      },
      "time": {
        "kind": "time",
        "policy": "extend"
      },
      "{lag_dim}": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "y": {
        "dims": [
          "geo",
          "time"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target"
      },
      "spend": {
        "dims": [
          "geo",
          "channel",
          "time",
          "{lag_dim}"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "spend"
      }
    }
  },
  "cases": [
    {
      "when": {
        "pooling": "none"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "geo": {
            "policy": "fixed",
            "new_level_strategy": "error"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: AdstockSettings
docs.text:
Carry-over of spend into later periods.

Field Type Default Description kind geometric or delayed geometric geometric: decays from the spend period; delayed: peaks after theta periods l_max integer (optional) null Number of lags (must equal the pipeline's lag_tensor l_max; default: taken from the data) normalize boolean true Normalise the lag weights to sum to one (steady-state adstock = spend)

docs.title: GridSettings
docs.text:
Response-curve grids cached per thinned draw for Guided-mode sliders.

Field Type Default Description max_multiplier number 2.0 Largest spend multiplier on the grid (1 = spend over the fit window) (> 0, ≤ 20) points integer 21 Grid points from 0 to max_multiplier (≥ 3, ≤ 201) marginal_step number 0.01 Relative spend change used for marginal cost (central difference) (> 0, ≤ 0.25)

docs.title: PositiveChannelPrior
docs.text:
A positive prior, optionally one per channel (dims: [channel]).

Field Type Default Description distribution HalfNormal or HalfStudentT or HalfCauchy or Exponential or Gamma or InverseGamma or LogNormal or Weibull or Beta or Uniform or TruncatedNormal required PyMC distribution name dims list of channel – max items 1

docs.title: PositiveScalarPrior
docs.text:
A positive prior shared by every label (no dims).

Field Type Default Description distribution HalfNormal or HalfStudentT or HalfCauchy or Exponential or Gamma or InverseGamma or LogNormal or Weibull or Beta or Uniform or TruncatedNormal required PyMC distribution name dims list of string – max items 0

docs.title: Priors
docs.text:
Prior overrides by model parameter; unset parameters keep their defaults. Each parameter accepts only distributions with the right support (a media effect is positive, an adstock decay lies in (0, 1)) and only the dims it may vary over, so the control plane rejects a wrong prior from the JSON Schema alone.

Field Type Default Description intercept RealScalarPrior (optional) null Population mean of the geo intercepts (model units: the target is mean-scaled) intercept_sigma PositiveScalarPrior (optional) null Spread of the geo intercepts around their population mean beta_channel PositiveChannelPrior (optional) null Typical (median across geos) effect of each channel at full saturation beta_sigma PositiveChannelPrior (optional) null Log-scale spread of a channel's effect across geos (partial pooling) alpha UnitChannelPrior (optional) null Adstock decay per period theta PositiveChannelPrior (optional) null Delayed adstock: periods until the peak effect lam PositiveChannelPrior (optional) null Logistic saturation rate (per unit of scaled spend) slope PositiveChannelPrior (optional) null Hill saturation slope half PositiveChannelPrior (optional) null Hill half-saturation point (scaled spend) gamma_control RealScalarPrior (optional) null Coefficient of each control feature (seasonality, holidays, ...) sigma PositiveScalarPrior (optional) null Observation noise (model units)

docs.title: RealScalarPrior
docs.text:
A real-valued prior shared by every label (no dims).

Field Type Default Description distribution Normal or StudentT or Laplace or HalfNormal or HalfStudentT or HalfCauchy or Exponential or Gamma or InverseGamma or LogNormal or Weibull or Beta or Uniform or TruncatedNormal required PyMC distribution name dims list of string – max items 0

docs.title: SaturationSettings
docs.text:
Diminishing returns of (adstocked) spend.

Field Type Default Description kind logistic or hill or none logistic logistic or hill curves; none for a linear response

docs.title: UnitChannelPrior
docs.text:
A prior on (0, 1), optionally one per channel (dims: [channel]).

Field Type Default Description distribution Beta or Uniform or TruncatedNormal required PyMC distribution name dims list of channel – max items 1

docs.title: mmm.pymc_marketing
docs.text:
pymc-marketing's MMM (geometric adstock, logistic/Hill saturation, controls and yearly seasonality) behind the platform contract; it owns scaling, carry-over and the inverse to original units.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes counterfactual, evaluate, forecast, predict Contributions additive Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns carryover, inverse_units, scaling LOO valid Default plots core.ppc_fan, core.convergence, core.counterfactual Resources class M (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description y_hat (time) of y Expected (or predictive) target in original units, over the panel dims and time contributions (component, time) of y Channels, baseline, controls and seasonality in original units; they sum to y_hat

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description dims list of string [] basic Extra panel dims besides time and channel (e.g. [geo]) (max items 4) adstock AdstockSettings {"kind": "geometric", "l_max": 4, "normalize": true} basic saturation SaturationSettings {"kind": "logistic"} basic controls list of string [] advanced Control variables over (*dims, time) (max items 64) yearly_seasonality integer (optional) null basic Fourier order of yearly seasonality adstock_first boolean true advanced Nested settings types Input data contract (schema template) 
{
  "params": {
    "dims": {
      "type": "string_list",
      "default": []
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "time": {
        "kind": "time",
        "policy": "extend"
      },
      "channel": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "fixed"
      },
      "{*dims as d}": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "fixed"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "y": {
        "dims": [
          "{*dims}",
          "time"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target"
      },
      "spend": {
        "dims": [
          "{*dims}",
          "channel",
          "time"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "spend"
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: sklearn.tabular_bootstrap
docs.text:
Tabular regression with a bootstrap ensemble: one joint draw per replicate, so any aggregation is valid.

Version 1.0.0 Inference bootstrap Representation draws Score modes counterfactual, evaluate, forecast, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO invalid: scikit-learn and xgboost estimators provide no pointwise log-likelihood Default plots – Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description y_hat (chain, draw) – Bootstrap draws of the prediction over the row dims contributions (chain, draw, component) – Per-replicate feature contributions, in model space

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description estimator LinearRegressionChoice or RidgeChoice or LassoChoice or ElasticNetChoice or QuantileRegressorChoice or LogisticRegressionChoice or RandomForestRegressorChoice or RandomForestClassifierChoice or GradientBoostingRegressorChoice or HistGradientBoostingRegressorChoice or XGBRegressorChoice or XGBClassifierChoice required – target string y – rows list of string required – min items 1, max items 8 time_dim string time – time_kind time or integer or index or none time – columns ColumnsSettings – – coord_features map of category or onehot or ordinal or numeric – – new_levels pooled or zero or error pooled – pooled_max_levels integer 256 – ≥ 1, ≤ 10000 weight string (optional) null – mask string (optional) null – forecast_strategy direct or recursive direct – retransform median or smearing median – n_jobs integer 1 – ≥ 1, ≤ 64 uncertainty BootstrapUncertainty – – contributions none or auto or exact or zeroing auto – Nested settings types Input data contract (schema template) 
{
  "params": {
    "target": {
      "type": "string",
      "default": "y"
    },
    "rows": {
      "type": "string_list",
      "required": true
    },
    "time_dim": {
      "type": "string",
      "default": "time"
    },
    "time_kind": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "time",
        "integer",
        "index",
        "none"
      ],
      "default": "time"
    },
    "new_levels": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "pooled",
        "zero",
        "error"
      ],
      "default": "pooled"
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "{*rows as d}": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "new_levels",
        "new_level_strategy": "{new_levels}"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "{target}": {
        "dims": "{rows}",
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "missing": "allow"
      }
    }
  },
  "cases": [
    {
      "when": {
        "time_kind": "time"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "{time_dim}": {
            "kind": "time",
            "policy": "extend",
            "new_level_strategy": "error"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    {

Split-conformal prediction intervals (representation interval, never draws). A calibration fraction of the training rows is held out (the most recent periods of time_dim for calibration_by: last, a seeded random subset for random); the interval is point ± q where q is the ceil((n+1)(1-alpha))-th smallest absolute calibration residual. refit refits the point model on all rows afterwards (sharper, but the finite-sample guarantee then only holds approximately).

docs.title: tabular.hierarchical_glm
docs.text:
A hierarchical generalised linear model in long layout: group intercepts (and optional slopes) partially pooled towards a population mean that may depend on group-level covariates. Unseen groups are drawn from the fitted hyperprior.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes counterfactual, evaluate, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO valid Default plots core.ppc, core.convergence, core.posterior_forest Resources class S (min S)

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description group_dim string county – The grouping dim (index var: _idx) family normal or student_t or poisson or bernoulli normal – Likelihood family (its canonical link) covariates list of string [] – Observation-level predictors over obs (max items 256) varying_slopes list of string [] – Covariates whose slope varies by group (max items 32) group_covariates list of string [] – Group-level predictors of the group intercept (max items 64) centered boolean false – Centred group effects (non-centred default) intercept_sigma number 2.0 – Prior sd of the population intercept (> 0) group_sigma_scale number 1.0 – Half-normal scale of group sds (> 0) beta_sigma number 1.0 – Prior sd of the population slopes (> 0) noise_sigma number 1.0 – Half-normal scale of the noise sd (> 0) Input data contract (schema template)

docs.title: tabular.regressor
docs.text:
Tabular quantile regression for panels such as store x sku x week demand: rows are stacked from labelled dims, coordinates become categorical features, new levels are pooled and forecasts are direct. Quantiles are per cell and never aggregated.

Version 1.0.0 Inference custom Representation quantiles Score modes counterfactual, evaluate, forecast, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO invalid: scikit-learn and xgboost estimators provide no pointwise log-likelihood Default plots core.fit_vs_actual, core.residuals_over_time, ml.feature_importance Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description y_hat (quantile) – Conditional quantiles of the target over the row dims

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description estimator XGBRegressorChoice or HistGradientBoostingRegressorChoice or GradientBoostingRegressorChoice or QuantileRegressorChoice {"kind": "xgboost.XGBRegressor", "params": {"colsample_byle… – A quantile-capable estimator from the allow-listed registry target string y – rows list of string required – min items 1, max items 8 time_dim string time – time_kind time or integer or index or none time – columns ColumnsSettings – – coord_features map of category or onehot or ordinal or numeric – – new_levels pooled or zero or error pooled – pooled_max_levels integer 256 – ≥ 1, ≤ 10000 weight string (optional) null – mask string (optional) null – forecast_strategy direct or recursive direct – retransform median or smearing median – n_jobs integer 1 – ≥ 1, ≤ 64 uncertainty QuantileUncertainty {"kind": "quantile", "quantiles": [0.1, 0.5, 0.9], "rearran… – Quantile levels (the default gives an 80% band around the median) Nested settings types Input data contract (schema template) 
{
  "params": {
    "target": {
      "type": "string",
      "default": "y"
    },
    "rows": {
      "type": "string_list",
      "required": true
    },
    "time_dim": {
      "type": "string",
      "default": "time"
    },
    "time_kind": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "time",
        "integer",
        "index",
        "none"
      ],
      "default": "time"
    },
    "new_levels": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "pooled",
        "zero",
        "error"
      ],
      "default": "pooled"
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "{*rows as d}": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "new_levels",
        "new_level_strategy": "{new_levels}"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "{target}": {
        "dims": "{rows}",
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "missing": "allow"
      }
    }
  },
  "cases": [
    {
      "when": {
        "time_kind": "time"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "{time_dim}": {
            "kind": "time",
            "policy": "extend",
            "new_level_strategy": "error"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "when": {
        "time_kind": "integer"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "{time_dim}": {
            "kind": "integer",
            "policy": "extend",
            "new_level_strategy": "error"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "when": {
        "time_kind": "index"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "{time_dim}": {
            "kind": "index",
            "policy": "extend",
            "new_level_strategy": "error"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: ts.gaussian_hmm
docs.text:
A K-state Gaussian hidden Markov model over padded sequences (e.g. animal tracks). Hidden states are marginalised with the forward algorithm; forecasts and filters start from the stored terminal state.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes evaluate, filter, forecast, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO invalid: the HMM likelihood is a potential over whole sequences; steps within a sequence are dependent, so pointwise leave-one-out is not defined Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description y_hat (animal, step) of y One-step-ahead expected value or predictive draw of y state_prob (animal, step, state) probability Hidden-state probabilities (predicted, or filtered in filter mode)

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description n_states integer 2 – Number of hidden states K (≥ 2, ≤ 8) mu_center number 0.0 – Prior mean of the state means mu_sigma number 2.0 – Prior sd of the state means (> 0) sigma_scale number 1.0 – Half-normal scale of the emission sds (> 0) stickiness number 2.0 – Extra Dirichlet weight on staying in the same state (≥ 0, ≤ 1000) pi_concentration number 1.0 – Dirichlet weight of pi (> 0) identification relabel or ordered relabel – relabel: sort states by mean after sampling; ordered: ordered prior Input data contract (schema template)

        "policy": "extend"

docs.title: ts.hsgp_trend
docs.text:
A smooth Hilbert-space GP trend with optional linear drift and Fourier seasonality for one regular time series (Mauna-Loa style). Forecasts reach at most max_extension periods past the fit; further horizons need a refit.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes evaluate, forecast, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO valid Default plots core.ppc_fan, core.convergence, core.posterior_forest Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description y_hat (t) of y The series: expected value (trend + seasonality) or a predictive draw trend (t) of y The long-term component (intercept + drift + GP), no seasonality

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description max_extension integer 24 – Periods a forecast may reach past the fitted range without a refit; sizes the HSGP domain (x-ui-level: basic) (≥ 1, ≤ 10000) kernel expquad or matern52 or matern32 expquad – Covariance kernel of the smooth trend m integer 30 – Number of HSGP basis functions (≥ 4, ≤ 400) c number 1.5 – Boundary factor (L = c on the scaled axis) (> 1.0, ≤ 5.0) lengthscale_mu number 0.4 – Median of the lengthscale prior on the scaled axis [-1, 1] (> 0) lengthscale_sigma number 0.5 – Log-scale sd of the lengthscale (> 0) eta_sigma number 1.0 – Half-normal scale of the GP amplitude (> 0) linear_trend boolean true – intercept_sigma number 1.0 – > 0 slope_sigma number 1.0 – > 0 season_period number (optional) 12.0 – Seasonal period in periods of t (12 for monthly data) season_order integer 3 – Fourier order of the seasonality (≥ 0, ≤ 20) season_sigma number 0.5 – > 0 noise_sigma number 0.5 – > 0 Input data contract (schema template) 
{
  "params": {
    "max_extension": {
      "type": "integer",
      "default": 24
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {

        "kind": "time",
        "policy": "extend",
        "max_extension": "{max_extension}"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "y": {
        "dims": [
          "t"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "missing": "allow"
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: The authorization rules of the platform, generated from mapi_spec.tenancy and mapi_spec.tokens by scripts/gen_docs_platform.py. Every component (the API, the web app through OpenAPI, the tests) checks the same table. The Administration guide explains how to use it.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Roles are ordered viewer < editor < runner < admin; each includes the one before it. tenant-wide means only a tenant-wide membership grants it; otherwise the effective role in the project counts (the higher of the tenant-wide and the project grant). A pair that is not listed is denied to everyone.

docs.title: Operators
docs.text: Platform operators (verified e-mails in MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS, signed in; never through an API token) hold exactly these permissions, on every tenant: audit read, billing read, catalog read, executor read, executor update, kill_switch read, kill_switch update, member read, project read, quota delete, quota read, quota update, run read, tenant_deletion manage, tenant_deletion read, tenant_member read, tenant create, tenant delete, tenant manage, tenant read, token read, usage read. None of them reads tenant content: datasets, specs, models or plots.

docs.title: Token scopes
docs.text:
A token acts as its owner, narrowed by its scopes: both the owner's role and a scope must allow an action. admin covers everything the owner's role allows; score:<alias> covers one endpoint (score:* every endpoint of the project).

docs.title: Server settings
docs.text:
Every setting of mapi-server (api, worker, migrate, dev), generated from mapi_server.settings.Settings by scripts/gen_docs_reference.py. Each field reads the environment variable MAPI_<FIELD>; .env files are not read. The configuration reference explains them by task and lists the variables of the other components.

Variable Type Default Description MAPI_ENV str local Selects bucket names mapi-{env}-* MAPI_PROFILE single-tenant | multi-tenant single-tenant MAPI_TENANT_ID str default MAPI_PROJECT_ID str default MAPI_DEBUG bool False Include tracebacks in problem.untrusted_text MAPI_API_HOST str 127.0.0.1 MAPI_API_PORT int 8000 MAPI_API_URL str http://127.0.0.1:8000 MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN str http://127.0.0.1:5173 MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN str http://127.0.0.1:5174 MAPI_DATA_DIR Path .local MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS list (computed) Host header values the API answers (comma-separated in the environment; '*' turns the check off). The host of api_url is always allowed. The API is unauthenticated in M1, so this is what stops DNS-rebinding pages from using it. MAPI_DATABASE_URL or DATABASE_URL str \| None unset postgresql:// URL; unset = embedded pgserver under data_dir/pg MAPI_DB_POOL_SIZE int 10 MAPI_DB_ECHO bool False MAPI_OBJECT_STORE shim | memory shim MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT str http://127.0.0.1:4443 MAPI_GCS_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT str \| None unset Base URL put into signed URLs when executions/browsers reach the shim under another host name (default: gcs_endpoint) MAPI_GCS_ROOT Path \| None unset The GCS shim's state directory (default: data_dir/gcs) MAPI_GCS_KEY_FILE Path \| None unset Key file of the shim's control principal (default: gcs_root/_shim/keys/control.json) MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN str \| None unset Bearer token of the shim's exec principal (local executors only; default: read from gcs_root/_shim/keys/exec.json) MAPI_EXECUTOR local-process | docker | docker-gvisor local-process MAPI_RUNNER_COMMAND list (computed) argv of the supervisor (shell-quoted string in the environment) MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGE str mapi/base-bayes:0.2.0 Runner image for runs without a mapped plugin (ingest, describe, ...) MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGES dict (computed) Plugin namespace → runner image (JSON in the environment) MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK str none Network of run containers: 'container:' (share the shim's namespace, so 127.0.0.1:4443 works) or an internal network holding only the shim. 'none' is refused while the bootstrap URL is HTTP (nothing would be reachable). The declarative modelling file.

Field Type Default Description after_step string (optional) null Stage the split happens at (a step id or 'raw'); default: end of the stateless prefix allow_leakage boolean false Downgrade LEAKAGE_RISK to a warning (acknowledged) kind as_of required dim string required as_of string or integer or number or boolean required gap integer 0 ≥ 0

docs.title: Binding
docs.text:
Canonical name → dataset name, for dims and variables (geo: market). Names that are not bound keep their dataset name. The binding is stored in the bundle and reversed on every output by default.

docs.title: Built-in steps catalog
docs.text:
Generated from the mapi-steps catalog export (python -m mapi_steps.catalog): the same static JSON the control plane uses to validate specs without importing step code. For how the steps behave together, read Built-in steps.

Step Kind Learns state Invertible Looks back Summary core.calendar feature – – – Calendar features (day of week, month, ISO week, ...) core.encode_levels feature yes – – Integer codes for categorical levels core.formula feature – – – Derived variable from an arithmetic expression core.fourier feature yes – – Fourier seasonality features core.holidays feature – – – Holiday indicators per period from a side table core.lag feature – – yes Lagged copies of variables within groups core.lag_tensor feature – – yes Lag tensor (lags 0 .. l_max-1) for in-model carry-over core.missing_indicator feature – – – Indicators of missing values core.one_hot feature yes – – One-hot indicators of categorical variables core.trend feature yes – – Polynomial time trend core.count_events reshape – – – Count events per period on a dense grid core.filter_coords reshape – – – Select labels of a dim core.resample reshape – – – Aggregate a time dim to a coarser frequency core.stack reshape – – – Stack dims into one core.to_long reshape – – – Padded ragged data to long form core.to_padded reshape – – – Long ragged data to padded form with a mask core.unstack reshape – – – Unstack a dim into several core.adstock value – – yes Adstock (carry-over) with fixed parameters core.clip value – – – Clip values to bounds core.fx_convert value – yes – Currency conversion with per-period rates from a side table core.impute value yes – – Fill missing values (mean, median, constant or forward fill) core.log1p value – yes – log(1 + x) of the named variables core.logit value – yes – Logit of proportions core.max_abs_scale value yes yes – Divide by the maximum absolute value over the named dims core.mean_scale value yes yes – Divide by the mean absolute value over the named dims core.replace_sentinel value – – – Turn sentinel codes into missing values core.saturation value – – – Saturation curve with fixed parameters core.standardize value yes yes – Standardise to zero mean and unit variance over the named dims

docs.text: Metric Type Labels Meaning mapi_runs_total counter kind, state Runs that reached a terminal state, by kind and terminal state. mapi_runs_active gauge state Runs currently in a non-terminal state (sampled each reconcile pass). mapi_run_transitions_total counter state Run state transitions, by target state (every edge, terminal or not). mapi_dispatch_latency_seconds histogram — Seconds from a run entering QUEUED to the executor accepting its submission. mapi_time_to_running_seconds histogram — Seconds from a run entering QUEUED to its first event (RUNNING). mapi_event_ingestion_lag_seconds histogram — Seconds between a run event's timestamp and its ingestion. mapi_events_ingested_total counter result Run events seen by the ingestor, by result (accepted, duplicate, bad_hmac, ...). mapi_finalize_outcomes_total counter kind, outcome Finalize attempts, by outcome (succeeded, partial, integrity, infra, retry). mapi_integrity_failures_total counter tenant_id Output-integrity verification failures at FINALIZING (a security signal). mapi_sandbox_violations_total counter reason Sandbox violations observed by the control plane, by reason. mapi_quota_rejections_total counter scope, code Requests denied by a quota or rate limit, by scope and error code. mapi_cost_micros_total counter tenant_id Billed compute cost in currency micros, by tenant (cost ledger). mapi_global_spend_micros gauge — Current spend against the global cap, in currency micros (0 until set). mapi_global_spend_cap_micros gauge — The configured global spend cap, in currency micros (0 = no cap set). mapi_sse_clients gauge — Live Server-Sent-Events subscribers connected to this process. mapi_executor_submit_throttled_total counter executor 429 answers from an executor backend to a submission (Cloud Run jobs.run), each one, retried or not. Not the API's own 429s to tenants. mapi_executor_running_executions gauge executor Runs holding a live execution on this executor (fleet-wide, from the run table; each orchestrator reports the same value, so aggregate with max). mapi_http_requests_total counter method, route, status HTTP requests handled by the API, by method, route template and status. mapi_http_request_duration_seconds histogram method, route HTTP request handling time, by method and route template. mapi_endpoint_promotions_total counter outcome Endpoint promotion and rollback decisions, by outcome (allowed, overridden, needs_override, blocked, forbidden, rollback). mapi_endpoint_score_requests_total counter result, inline POST /v1/endpoints/{alias}/score calls, by result (accepted, replayed, invalid) and whether the payload was inline XrJSON. mapi_webhook_events_total counter type Webhook events written to the outbox, by event type. mapi_webhook_deliveries_total counter status Webhook delivery tries, by resulting status (succeeded, retrying, failed, blocked). mapi_webhook_delivery_duration_seconds histogram — Time of one webhook delivery try (resolution, connection, answer). mapi_webhook_ssrf_blocked_total counter stage Webhook URLs refused by the SSRF policy, by stage (create, update, replay, delivery). mapi_webhooks_disabled_total counter reason Webhooks the platform disabled, by reason (failures, gone).

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
modeling-api ships as three products, in this order: a typed modelling runtime, a job platform around it, and a hosted multi-user platform. The rules that make the last one safe (no pickle, JSON-only contracts, static validation, sanitized plots, sandboxed runs whose outputs are verified) are in the code from the first release.

timeline
    title Releases
    v0.1 · M0 · contract layer : SDK, specs and schemas : 28 steps, PyMC and sklearn base classes : 11 built-in models, plots, sanitizer : conformance corpus
    v0.2 · M1 · local platform (now) : HTTP API, queue, sandboxed runner : GCS shim, signed bundles : Expert web app, CLI, Python client : make dev and Docker Compose
    v0.3 · M2 · cloud and multi-tenant : Cloud Run Jobs executor : tenants, OIDC, tokens, RLS : quotas, cost ledger, observability : private beta
    v0.4 · M3 · Guided mode and integrations : templates and question flow : business priors, scorecard, what-if sliders : endpoints, webhooks, embeds : public launch of specs and built-ins
Release Milestone Theme Status v0.1 M0 The contract layer: specs, the xarray runtime, steps, models, plots, the conformance corpus, all in your own Python process available v0.2 M1 The local platform: the same work as API calls and sandboxed runs, with the Expert web app, on a laptop or one Docker host this release v0.3 M2 Cloud and multi-tenant core: one fresh sandbox per run on Cloud Run, tenants, tokens, quotas; a private beta next v0.4 M3 Guided mode and integrations: analysts from CSV to report and scenario; endpoints for other apps; first public launch planned

docs.title: What v0.2 contains
docs.text:
• The /v1 HTTP API: datasets, specs with synchronous static validation, runs, model versions, scoring with Prefer: wait, plots; OpenAPI 3.1, RFC 7807 errors, idempotency keys, cursor pagination, server-sent events with Last-Event-ID resume
  • An orchestrator on PostgreSQL: dispatcher with intent rows, a level-triggered reconciler (executor status is the liveness truth, orphan adoption, stalled as a warning), a metadata-only finalizer with server-side copy and signed bundle manifests
  • local-process, docker and docker-gvisor executors
  • mapi-runner: a trusted supervisor and an untrusted worker per run, a one-time bootstrap object, HMAC-signed events, capped logs and outputs, checkpoints and partial runs; ingest, describe, validate, fit, score, evaluate, derive, render
  • mapi-gcs-shim: a local Cloud Storage with generations, server-computed CRC32C and MD5, signed URLs and POST policies, per-principal permissions and write-once buckets
  • The Expert web app and an origin-isolated plot sandbox
  • The mapi CLI and the typed Python client
  • make dev without Docker, six container images and a Docker Compose stack
  • End-to-end suites: the E33 geo MMM fitted, inspected and scored through the API and through the browser

docs.title: v0.3 · M2: cloud and multi-tenant core
docs.text: Runs move to Cloud Run Jobs, one fresh microVM per run, in an execution project with deny-all egress (DNS included) and VPC Service Controls; a fixed inventory of about a dozen Jobs (base image × resource class) with tenant code arriving later as hash-pinned overlays. The control plane gains tenants and projects with PostgreSQL row-level security, OIDC sign-in, scoped API tokens with budgets, quotas in vCPU-seconds, interactive and batch priority classes, a per-run cost ledger shown in the UI, Cloud KMS signatures, checkpoint and resume across infrastructure failures, Terraform for every project, and an observability stack. Exit criteria include 100 concurrent fits without loss, chaos and executor-conformance suites, a nightly security suite and a p95 time-to-running under 90 seconds. More.

docs.title: v0.4 · M3: Guided mode and integrations
docs.text: Analysts get Guided mode: templates, a question flow instead of a column mapper, sandboxed CSV, Parquet and MFF ingest, business priors and lift-test input, the sanity scorecard and what-if sliders over response curves precomputed per posterior draw, and forecast and counterfactual screens. Other applications get endpoints and aliases promoted on the scorecard, the Python client's Atlas RemoteModel, generated snippets, signed webhooks, static plot rendering and embed links. The exit criterion: five non-technical testers go from upload to report to scenario unaided in under 30 minutes. It is the first public launch: declarative specs and built-in models (untrusted data, trusted code). More.

docs.title: After v0.4
docs.text:
Further out, in the order they are planned: uploading your own plugins to the hosted platform (first for allow-listed teams, built into hash-pinned overlays and checked by the contract kit on upload), then public code upload behind a stricter sandbox and abuse controls, then scale features (warm scorers, GPU executors, other clouds, model composition) when real usage asks for them.

Dates

Releases are cut when their exit criteria pass, not on a calendar. Follow the changelog for what has landed.

docs.title: Cloud and multi-tenant core coming in v0.3
docs.text:
Status: next (milestone M2)

v0.3 runs fits and scores in the cloud, one fresh sandbox per run, and makes the platform multi-tenant for a private beta. The run protocol it uses (bootstrap object, signed events, verified outputs, signed bundle manifests) already runs locally in v0.2; v0.3 replaces the local pieces with their cloud counterparts.

docs.title: One sandbox per run
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    subgraph SB["Fresh sandbox (one per run)"]
        direction LR
        SUP["Supervisor<br/><i>trusted · holds credentials</i>"] -->|"inputs"| W["Worker<br/><i>separate uid · runs the plugin</i>"]
        W -->|"outputs (claims)"| SUP
    end
    SUP -->|"signed upload"| OBJ[("Object store")]
    SUP -->|"HMAC-signed events"| EV["Events service"]
    OBJ -->|"server-computed hashes"| FIN["Finalizer<br/>verifies, then publishes"]
  • Isolation. Each run gets a fresh micro-VM sandbox (Cloud Run Jobs, gen2). A trusted supervisor holds the run's short-lived credentials; an untrusted worker runs the harness and the plugin under a different user, with no credentials and no network.
  • No egress. Sandboxes cannot reach the internet, including DNS. Data comes in and results go out only through object-scoped signed URLs.
  • Outputs are claims. The finalizer checks every artifact against the hashes and object generation the store computed itself, then copies it somewhere the sandbox cannot write. A manifest that does not match is rejected as INTEGRITY_FAILURE.
  • Progress you can trust. Only the supervisor writes events, each line HMAC-signed and sequence-numbered; the executor's own status decides whether a run is alive.
  • Resumable long fits. Segmented PyMC sampling checkpoints to the run's prefix, so a preempted fit resumes where it stopped. (Checkpoints, partial runs and resume already work locally in v0.2.)
Local in v0.2 In the cloud in v0.3 local-process / docker executor Cloud Run Jobs, a fixed inventory of base image × resource class Worker as your user (DEV_MODE_ISOLATION) Worker under its own uid, no_new_privs, in a microVM GCS shim with emulated principals Cloud Storage with IAM, VPC Service Controls Events from the supervisor's stdout pipe Cloud Logging → Pub/Sub push → POST /internal/events EC P-256 key in .local/keys/ Cloud KMS asymmetric signatures, same bytes No authentication, 127.0.0.1 only OIDC for people, scoped tokens for programs

docs.title: Multi-tenant core
docs.text:
• Tenants and projects with role-based access; row-level security in Postgres on every table (every row and storage key already carries tenant_id and project_id in v0.2).
  • Scoped API tokens with their own budgets; per-tenant quotas in vCPU-seconds; interactive and batch priority classes so one big sweep cannot starve everyone's scoring.
  • A per-run cost ledger shown in the UI.
  • Other backends plug in through the same Executor protocol, each gated by an executor conformance suite.

docs.title: What it means for plugins
docs.text: Nothing changes in your code. The contract kit already checks the properties the cloud relies on: no pickle, deterministic bundles, typed errors, evaluate path equals score path. A plugin that passes check_model today is ready for sandboxed execution.

docs.title: Guided UI and integrations coming in v0.4
docs.text:
Status: planned (milestone M3)

v0.4 lets analysts go from a CSV to a trustworthy report and a what-if scenario without writing YAML, and lets other applications call fitted models through stable endpoints. It is the first public launch: declarative specs and built-in models.

docs.title: Guided mode: organised around tasks
docs.text:
One app, two modes over the same ModelSpec. A header toggle switches between Guided and Expert; every Guided screen has "View as YAML", and Expert edits round-trip back.

journey
    title An analyst's first marketing-mix model
    section Set up
      Choose "Geo marketing mix": 5: Analyst
      Upload a CSV, answer "which column is revenue?": 4: Analyst
      Enter beliefs as ROI ranges per channel: 4: Analyst
    section Run
      Watch plain-language progress, with an ETA: 5: Analyst
    section Decide
      Read the report and the sanity scorecard: 5: Analyst
      Drag what-if sliders, see bands update instantly: 5: Analyst
      Share a link or connect a spreadsheet: 4: Analyst
  1. Templates. "What do you want to learn?": geo marketing mix, weekly forecast, demand by store, customer choice.
  2. A question flow instead of a column mapper. Answers fill in dims, roles and the binding.
  3. Business priors. Beliefs entered as ROI ranges or contribution shares, converted to model priors, with a prior-predictive preview in business units. Lift-test results can be entered as calibration data.
  4. A report with a sanity scorecard. Convergence, holdout error and plausibility checks, each with a plain-language message and a suggested action.
  5. Instant what-if sliders. Sliders interpolate response curves precomputed per posterior draw at fit time, so the uncertainty bands stay joint and honest. "Run exact" submits a real score run.

docs.title: Already in place
docs.text:
The pieces Guided mode is built on already ship, most since v0.1, the rest in the v0.2 web app:

Guided feature Built on (available now) Forms that show only the basics x-ui-level (basic or advanced) on every model setting Plain-language plot captions caption_plain and persona on every plot recipe Scorecard items Diagnostic with expert and plain messages and a suggested action Data problems in words validate_dataset ("2 markets are missing 2 days of revenue in March 2026") What-if sliders response_curves derived quantity of mmm.hierarchical_geo, per thinned draw Role-based plot templates tmpl.* templates bound to roles and dims, not variable names One app, two modes The v0.2 web app's Guided / Expert switch and the Guided task preview The scorecard in the UI The v0.2 model page's scorecard, with plain messages and suggested actions Column mapping The v0.2 upload panel's CSV preview and dim/role mapping

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
• Endpoints and aliases (endpoint://growth/eu-geo-mmm-prod) with promotion gated on the scorecard.
  • The Python client (available in v0.2) gains endpoints and the Atlas RemoteModel adapter; ready-to-paste snippets (Python, TypeScript, curl, R) are prefilled from an endpoint's schema.
  • Webhooks with signed, timestamped payloads and a delivery log.
  • Static plot rendering (PNG, SVG, PDF) and read-only embed links for BI tools and docs.
  • An MCP server with a curated set of tools (list_models, describe_model, score, get_run, get_plot), where every string that came from a user or plugin is returned as clearly delimited untrusted text.

docs.title: The local platform v0.2
docs.text:
Status: available in v0.2 (milestone M1)

The documents the platform accepts (ModelSpec, ScoreRequest), the error codes it returns and the executor protocol it drives were defined in v0.1. v0.2 puts an HTTP API, a job queue, a sandboxed runner, a local object store and the Expert web app around them, and runs it all on one machine. Start with the quickstart.

docs.title: What changed for you
docs.text:
Everything you do in a notebook is also an API call, and the work runs in a sandbox instead of your process:

In your process (v0.1) On the platform (v0.2) validate_spec(spec, catalog, schema) POST /v1/specs:validate, every problem at once with JSON pointers, and the editor's live squiggles fit_spec(spec, data, ...) POST /v1/runs with kind: fit; progress streamed as server-sent events score_bundle(bundle, request, data) POST /v1/models/{id}/versions/{v}:score with Prefer: wait A bundle directory A model version in a registry, with lineage, metrics, a scorecard, plots and a signed manifest InprocExecutor local-process and docker executors behind the same protocol 
flowchart LR
    C["Web app · CLI ·<br/>Python client · curl"] -->|"/v1 JSON"| API["API<br/>(validates from static JSON)"]
    API --> Q[("PostgreSQL<br/>runs · queue · events")]
    Q --> D["Dispatcher"]
    D --> X["Executor<br/>(local process / Docker)"]
    X --> R["Runner<br/>supervisor + worker"]
    R -->|"outputs + manifest"| S[("GCS shim")]
    R -->|"signed events"| API

docs.title: Design commitments, kept
docs.text:
• The API never imports plugin code and never decodes your arrays. It validates specs and score requests from the exported catalog JSON and stored metadata. An import-linter contract keeps numpy, xarray and every plugin out of the server, and the server image build checks it against the installed packages.
  • Runs are idempotent and observable. Submissions carry idempotency keys; the executor's status is the source of truth; events drive progress bars, never liveness decisions.
  • Errors are RFC 7807 problems with the same stable codes you see in Python.
  • OpenAPI 3.1 describes every endpoint, and the generated clients are checked for drift in CI.
  • Outputs are verified. A run's outputs are checked against the object store's own checksums and generations, copied where runs cannot write, and signed.
